# I. Introduction
*(The framing of the present paper, stated up front.)* The dual-content development across all sections of this paper is an extended articulation of the **McGucken Duality** — the pattern by which physics admits two parallel articulations of dx₄/dt = ic, with **The McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel** as the algebraic-symmetry face (operator algebras, Stone–von Neumann uniqueness, Wigner classification, Noether currents, Lovelock uniqueness) and **The McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel** as the geometric-propagation face (McGucken Sphere wavefront propagation, Huygens construction, Compton-coupling channel contentD, Bekenstein–Hawking area law, the McGucken-Wick rotation τ = x₄/c). The seven levels of description developed in this paper, the 47-theorem dual-channel architecture of [3], and the convergent-overdetermination convergences of Theorems IX.15.5, IX.15.7, and IX.15.9 are all instances of the McGucken Duality celebrating dx₄/dt = ic's two faces, and the empirical existence of the Duality is itself evidence for dx₄/dt = ic as the principle from which both channels descend (Corollary IX.28.2).

## I.1 The McGucken Principle as Active Expansion, Not Coordinate Convention

The McGucken Principle is the physical–geometric statement

$$\boxed{\;\frac{dx_{4}}{dt} \;=\; ic \;}$$

read as follows. The universe possesses a fourth dimension perpendicular to the three spatial dimensions $x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}$. From every event $p_{0} = (x_{0}, t_{0})$ in spacetime, this fourth dimension expands at the velocity of light c, in a manner spherically symmetric in the three-dimensional spatial subspace orthogonal to its advance. The imaginary unit i in dx₄/dt = ic is the **perpendicularity marker** that encodes the geometric orthogonality of x₄ to $x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}$ — the unique element of ℂ that satisfies i² = −1 and that, by the Frobenius theorem ([Frobenius 1878]; modern treatment [Lounesto 2001, §3.5]), is forced as the algebraic generator of x₄-advance over the reals.

The physics of the McGucken Principle: x₄ is a spherically symmetric wavefront with wavelength, frequency, phase, and therefore action. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is more than the abstract statement that "the fourth dimension expands" with the geometry left to subsequent derivation. The physics is that **x₄ expands as a spherically symmetric wavefront at velocity c, and the wavefront carries wavelength, frequency, phase, and therefore action.** The expansion at velocity c is a wave expansion in the wave-equation sense: it has a definite wavelength $\lambda$, a definite frequency $\nu$, a definite phase content $\phi$, and a definite action content $S$ accumulating per cycle of the advance. From this physics, the consequences are immediate and constitutive — they are directly properties of the principle as it sits, written down here at the position:

**(I.1.S.1) c and ℏ are twin properties of the one advance.** The velocity of light c is the rate at which x₄'s wavefront advances. The reduced Planck constant ℏ is the action quantum that accumulates per cycle of the wavefront's phase advance. The two constants are two articulations of the one advance — c articulates the spatial-velocity property of x₄'s wavefront expansion, ℏ articulates the per-cycle action property of the same wavefront. The dimensional identity $c = \ell_{P}/t_{P}$ with $\ell_{P} = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^{3}}$ and $t_{P} = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^{5}}$ is the numerical signature of this twin-property fact: c is the velocity dimension of x₄'s advance, ℏ is the action dimension of the same advance, and the Planck units relate the two through the constitutive identity. The 125-year-old question of what ℏ physically IS (since Planck 1900, who introduced ℏ as an empirical constant of unknown physics) receives its answer here: ℏ is the per-cycle action quantum of the wavefront advance of x₄ at velocity c, with the per-cycle accumulation being the algebraic structureC of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic-spectral reading.

**(I.1.S.2) The spinor lives on a wavefront that already has the Compton frequency.** The Compton angular frequency $\omega_{C}(m) = mc^{2}/\hbar$ for a particle of rest mass m is the beat note between the particle's rest mass m and the universal wavefront-advance rate of x₄ at velocity c. The spinor ψ that carries the quantum mechanics of the particle is a complex-valued amplitude on the wavefront, with the wavefront already supplying the Compton-frequency oscillation that ψ inherits. The spinor's $4\pi$-periodicity under spatial rotation, the Dirac equation's first-order Lorentz-covariant content, and the Pauli-Schrödinger ladder of mass and spin invariants all derive from the spinor's residence on a wavefront that already has the Compton frequency built in. The wavefront supplies the wave-mechanical content as a property of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic.

**(I.1.S.3) The dynamics were in the premise.** The Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\,\partial_{t}\psi = \hat{H}\psi$, the Dirac equation $(i\gamma^{\mu}\partial_{\mu} - m)\psi = 0$, the Klein-Gordon equation $(\Box + m^{2}c^{2}/\hbar^{2})\psi = 0$, Maxwell's wave equation $\Box A^{\mu} = 0$, the Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^{4})T_{\mu\nu}$, and the Friedmann equations $H^{2} = (8\pi G/3)\rho + \Lambda c^{2}/3$ are the wavefront of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic read at six distinct tiers — quantum-mechanical (Schrödinger), relativistic-quantum (Dirac), scalar-field (Klein-Gordon), electromagnetic (Maxwell), gravitational-tier (Einstein), cosmological-tier (Friedmann). The dynamics are properties of the wavefront expansion that the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic already specifies. The dynamics were in the premise. Once dx₄/dt = ic is recognized as the wavefront advance at c with wavelength-frequency-phase-action content, every dynamical law of foundational physics descends as wavefront. The 47-theorem dual-channel architecture of [3], the seven McGucken Dualities of [1], and the overdetermination Bayesian likelihood ratio $\geq 10^{141}$ of Theorem IX.26.11 are the consolidated documentation that the dynamics are in the premise; the physics of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic as a wavefront-advance is what makes this consolidation possible.

**(I.1.S.4) the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel reads the wavefront's algebraic-spectral content; the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel reads the wavefront's geometric-propagation.** The McGucken Duality (§I, Movement II) is the architectural consequence of the physics of dx₄/dt = ic as a wavefront-advance. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel reads the wavefront's algebraic-spectral content — the action quantum ℏ accumulating per cycle, the Stone-theorem unitary group $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat{H}t/\hbar)$ generated by the x₄-translation continuous symmetry, the canonical commutator $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ resolving individual action quanta, the Wigner classification of unitary irreducible representations of $\widetilde{\mathrm{ISO}}(1,3)$ on the mass-shell content. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel reads the wavefront's geometric-propagation — the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ as the spatial-cross-section of the wavefront at retarded time $t - t_{p}$, Huygens' Principle as the iterated-Sphere reconstruction of the wavefront from secondary wavelets, the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy as the count of wavefront modes on the horizon Sphere, the Friedmann equations as the cosmological-scale wavefront propagation. Both readings are theorems of the physics — the wavefront is the physical primitive, and both channels are two readings.

The **integrated form** x₄ = ict is the mere coordinate shadow of this active expansion. Differentiation of the active expansion with respect to coordinate time yields the integrated form as a tautology:
$$\int_{0}^{t} \frac{dx_{4}}{dt'} \, dt' \;=\; \int_{0}^{t} ic \, dt' \;\Longrightarrow\; x_{4}(t) \;=\; ict + x_{4}(0).$$
With the convention $x_{4}(0) = 0$ for an event at $t = 0$, x₄ = ict. The coordinate label is the integrated shadow of the active expansion. This distinction — the difference between dx₄/dt = ic (dynamical) and x₄ = ict (static convention) — is the central conceptual move of the McGucken framework, the move that all of the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel derives from. Minkowski 1908 [Minkowski 1909], Pauli 1921 [Pauli 1921], Sommerfeld, Weyl, and the entire textbook tradition since the 1920s did not make this move.

Before proceeding to the four-fold ontology, I want the reader to see how quickly the foundations of physics drop out of dx₄/dt = ic. The Lorentzian spacetime metric drops out in two lines. Square the differential of the active expansion to get $dx_{4}^{2} = (ic\,dt)^{2} = -c^{2}\,dt^{2}$, so the squared spacetime interval — built as the sum of squared differentials over all four dimensions — becomes
$$ds^{2} \;=\; dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} + dx_{4}^{2} \;=\; dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} - c^{2}\,dt^{2}.$$
The Minkowski signature $(+, +, +, -)$ is drops out automatically because the imaginary unit in dx₄/dt = ic squares to $-1$. Special relativity, the entire kinematics of Einstein 1905, is contained in this two-line derivation; the Lorentz transformations, time dilation, length contraction, simultaneity relativity, mass-energy equivalence, and the invariance of c are immediate corollaries of the Minkowski metric just derived.

The Schrödinger equation drops out via either channel in three lines. **The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel route**: dx₄/dt = ic identifies $x_{4}$-translation as a continuous symmetry of physics; Stone's theorem ([Stone 1932], modern treatment [Reed–Simon 1980, Theorem VIII.7]) extracts from this continuous symmetry a strongly continuous unitary one-parameter group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar}$ on the Hilbert space of states, with a self-adjoint generator $\hat H$; differentiating $U(t)\psi$ with respect to $t$ at $t = 0$ yields
$$i\hbar\,\partial_{t}\psi \;=\; \hat H\,\psi.$$
**The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel route**: every event $p \in \mathcal M_{G}$ emits a Huygens wavefront — the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ — expanding at velocity c; the wavefunction of a massive particle is the iterated-Sphere secondary-wavelet sum on this expanding wavefront, with Compton phase $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar$ accumulating per cycle of $x_{4}$-advance; the iterated sum coincides with the Feynman path integral $\int \mathcal D\gamma\, e^{iS[\gamma]/\hbar}$ by the Trotter formula, and the non-relativistic limit of the path integral is the same Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\,\partial_{t}\psi = \hat H\psi$. The two routes share no intermediate machinery. Stone's theorem is signature-locked to Lorentzian metric and operator-algebra, whereas Huygens' Principle is signature-flexible and geometric-propagation, yet both converge on the same Schrödinger equation. This is the **convergent-overdetermination signature** that establishes dx₄/dt = ic as the source of quantum dynamics.

The Born rule drops out via both channels, with the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel route being more natural and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel route operating on starting data that descends from upstream Geometric-Channel content. **The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel route** (geometric overlap on the McGucken Sphere, *physical mechanism*): the Born density $P = \psi^{*}\psi$ at an event $B$ is the geometric overlap, at $B$, of the forward x₄-expansion (carrying phase from $x_{4} = ict$, the integrated form of dx₄/dt = ic) and the conjugate x₄*-expansion (carrying phase from $x_{4}^{*} = -ict$) emanating from the source; the squared modulus is the incidence amplitude of the two McGucken-Sphere expansions arriving at $B$ ([70, Theorem 7.4]). The Malus correspondence of [70, Proposition 7.5] supplies the squared-modulus reading: the Born rule is to x₄-projection what Malus's 1809 law is to spatial projection — the squared cosine of the angle between the polarization direction (the x₄-direction along which the state advances) and the projection axis (the spatial slicing of the measurement) gives the transmitted intensity. The Geometric route delivers a physical mechanism — two real Sphere expansions, oppositely oriented in x₄, overlap at the measurement event, and the overlap density is the squared modulus. The +ic orientation enters : the forward expansion has $dx_{4}/dt = +ic$, the conjugate has $dx_{4}^{*}/dt = -ic$, and the head-on collision at the measurement event is directional. **The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel route** (uniqueness theorem on the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing inherited from upstream Geometry): the rank-2 character of $\eta^{\mu\nu}$ — itself the integrated form of $dx_{4}^{2} = -c^{2}\,dt^{2}$ from squaring $dx_{4} = ic\,dt$, which is the McGucken Sphere expansion principle of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel — admits a unique-up-to-scalar natural bilinear pairing of forward and conjugate complex amplitudes (the bilinearity lemma of [70, §7.4]). The unique non-negative density on this pairing satisfying the four requirements (R1)–(R4) — (R1) normalization, (R2) non-negativity, (R3) phase invariance (descending from the universality of x₄-expansion: a universal x₄-shift is unobservable), (R4) bilinearity in $(\psi, \psi^{*})$ (descending from the rank-2 character of the Minkowski metric, itself the integrated shadow of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic) — is $P(\mathbf x) = |\psi(\mathbf x)|^{2}$ ([70, Theorem 7.2]). All four requirements are downstream consequences of dx₄/dt = ic; the crucial one is (R4), with bilinearity inherited from the rank-2 metric. The Algebraic route delivers a uniqueness theorem operating on starting data — the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing, the complex amplitudes encoding Compton-phase oscillation on the McGucken Sphere — that is downstream Geometric-Channel content. The +ic orientation does not enter : the rank-2 pairing and its uniqueness theorem are time-symmetric algebraic structures, sign-blind on the +ic orientation that the Geometric mechanism carries as a primitive. This is the content-asymmetry theorem (Theorem IX.30.C.3) instantiated at the Born-rule level: constructive independence with asymmetric content. The Hilbert space itself is a Algebraic structureU: it arises as the Cauchy completion (via Riesz–Fischer) of the pre-Hilbert space carrying the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing on complex amplitudes over the Lorentzian spacetime $M_{1,3}$, co-generated with the Born rule from the common parent of the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing, with the four-level cascade dx₄/dt = ic $\to$ $\mathcal M_{G}$ $\to$ $M_{1,3}$ $\to$ ($\mathcal V$, rank-2 sesquilinear pairing) $\to$ (Hilbert space, Born rule) as siblings ([70, §10.1; Theorem 6.1]; [76, Theorem 3.4]). Gleason's 1957 theorem, the canonical prior derivation of the Born rule's form, *presupposed the Hilbert space* and derived the rule from non-contextuality on projection lattices ([70, §7.1.2] supplies the McGucken diagnostic of Gleason). The McGucken framework operates one level upstream, deriving the Hilbert space and the Born rule together from the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, with the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel supplying the physical mechanism that produces both.

The Born rule is more natural in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel — the geometric-overlap physical mechanism delivers the rule from a directional collision of two real Sphere expansions — but the rule was historically developed almost exclusively through the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel. Born 1926 [Born 1926a, Born 1926b] *postulated* the rule within the post-Schrödinger algebraic formalism without derivation; Gleason 1957 [Gleason 1957] derived the rule's form as a uniqueness theorem on projection lattices in a postulated Hilbert space; Everett 1957 [Everett 1957] supplied a branching-interpretation derivation within unitary Hilbert-space evolution; Hartle 1968 [Hartle 1968] supplied a frequency-operator derivation within Hilbert space; Deutsch 1999 [Deutsch 1999], Wallace 2003 / 2010 / 2012 [Wallace 2003, 2010, 2012], and Saunders 2021 [Saunders 2021] supplied decision-theoretic derivations within Hilbert space; Zurek 2003 / 2005 [Zurek 2003, 2005] supplied an envariance derivation within Hilbert space; Sebens–Carroll 2018 [Sebens-Carroll 2018] supplied a self-locating-uncertainty derivation within Hilbert space; Masanes–Galley–Müller 2019 [Masanes-Galley-Müller 2019] supplied operational-axiom derivations within generalized probabilistic theories (algebraic generalization); QBism (Caves–Fuchs–Schack 2002, Fuchs 2010) [Caves-Fuchs-Schack 2002, Fuchs 2010] supplied subjective-probability derivations within Hilbert space; Goyal 2010 [Goyal 2010] supplied information-theoretic axiomatic derivations; Hardy 2001 [Hardy 2001] supplied generalized-probabilistic-theory axiomatic derivations; Schlosshauer–Fine 2005 [Schlosshauer-Fine 2005] supplied decoherence derivations within Hilbert space; Chiribella–D'Ariano–Perinotti 2010s supplied categorical-operational derivations; Ichikawa 2018 supplied measurement-theoretic derivations within Hilbert space. **Every single major historical derivation of the Born rule operates within the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic apparatus** — within a postulated complex Hilbert space, operator algebra, or algebraic-axiomatic generalization thereof. ## I.1.A The McGucken Duality at the Level of the Principle: dx₄/dt = ic as Four-Vector (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel) and as Spherically-Symmetric Wavefront (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel)

Before cataloguing how each of the seven dualities of foundational physics descends from dx₄/dt = ic through both channels (Master Table I.1 in §I.5), I establish the McGucken Duality at the McGucken Principle. The Principle dx₄/dt = ic admits two distinct readings of the equation, each generating a complete derivational chain through disjoint mathematics. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel reads dx₄/dt = ic as a **four-vector statement** on the tangent space at every event of $\mathcal M_{G}$; the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel reads the same equation as a **spherically-symmetric wavefront statement** generated at every event. The two readings describe the same null structure of spacetime through disjoint machinery and converge on the same McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ as their shared geometric object.

### I.1.A.1 the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel reads dx₄/dt = ic as a four-vector

In the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel, the McGucken Principle is a one-dimensional algebraic condition on the four-velocity $u^{\mu} = dx^{\mu}/d\tau$ at every event $p \in \mathcal M_{G}$: the fourth component of the four-velocity is fixed at $u^{4} = dx_{4}/dt = ic$. Combined with the spatial three-components, this generates the four-velocity-budget identity $u^{\mu} u_{\mu} = -c^{2}$ (Minkowski 1908; Theorem 10 of [3]) — every massive object in spacetime moves at exactly $c$ through spacetime along the signed Lorentzian norm — with the equivalent bounded partition $v^{2} + (c\,d\tau/dt)^{2} = c^{2}$ holding along every worldline of $\mathcal M_{G}$ (timelike and null), where $v = |d\mathbf x/dt|$ is the coordinate spatial speed and $c\,d\tau/dt$ is the standard time-dilation factor ($= c/\gamma$ on massive worldlines). The bounded partition is exception-free: at $v = 0$ (spatial rest), $c\,d\tau/dt = c$; at $v = c$ (null worldline), $c\,d\tau/dt = 0$ with $d\tau = 0$ pointwise. Notational conventions for the three quantities $\{dx_{4}/dt,\; c\,d\tau/dt,\; \tau[\gamma]\}$ that appear along a worldline are collected at Appendix N. The four-vector reading generates the algebraic apparatus of foundational physics through a definite chain.

The Lorentzian metric drops out of vector substitution. Squaring the McGucken Principle $dx_{4} = ic\,dt$ yields $dx_{4}^{2} = -c^{2}\,dt^{2}$, with the negative sign produced by $i^{2} = -1$. Substituting into the four-coordinate Euclidean line element $ds^{2} = dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} + dx_{4}^{2}$ pulls back to the Lorentzian line element $ds^{2} = dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} - c^{2}\,dt^{2}$ on the real spacetime. The Minkowski signature $(-, +, +, +)$ is forced by the imaginary unit in dx₄/dt = ic with no separate postulate about signature required. This is the algebraic substitution at the level of vectors — taking the squared norm of a four-vector with the McGucken-forced fourth component substituted in.

The Lorentz and Poincaré groups act as preservation machinery. The Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^{+}(1, 3)$ is defined as the connected component of the linear transformations preserving the indefinite quadratic form $\eta_{\mu\nu}\xi^{\mu}\xi^{\nu}$; the Poincaré group $\mathrm{ISO}(1, 3) = \mathbb R^{1, 3} \rtimes \mathrm{SO}^{+}(1, 3)$ extends Lorentz by spacetime translations. The Lorentz algebra brackets $[J^{\mu\nu}, J^{\rho\sigma}] = i(\eta^{\mu\rho}J^{\nu\sigma} - \eta^{\nu\rho}J^{\mu\sigma} - \eta^{\mu\sigma}J^{\nu\rho} + \eta^{\nu\sigma}J^{\mu\rho})$ carry the same imaginary unit $i$ that appears in dx₄/dt = ic, by the Frobenius theorem applied to the real Clifford structure of $\mathbb R^{1, 3}$: the minimal real associative finite-dimensional division algebra extending $\mathbb R$ with a perpendicular axis generated by an element squaring to $-1$ is $\mathbb C$, with generator $i$ (Frobenius 1878; Theorem 4 of [3]; §XI of present paper). The $i$ in dx₄/dt = ic, the $i$ in the Lorentz algebra brackets, the $i$ in the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, and the $i$ in the unitary one-parameter group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar}$ are the *same* $i$ — the algebraic record of x₄-perpendicularity to the spatial three (Theorem IX.11.1; the three-mechanism classification of i-insertions, Theorem IX.13.5).

Null vectors carry the algebra of nonlocality. A four-vector $r^{\mu}$ satisfying $\eta_{\mu\nu}r^{\mu}r^{\nu} = 0$ is a *null vector* — a vector of zero Lorentzian length under the Minkowski inner product. The locus of null vectors from a source event $p_{0}$ is the future light cone of $p_{0}$, with the radii from $p_{0}$ to every point of the cone being null vectors of zero spacetime length. The term "null" was chosen carefully by Minkowski 1908: it is not "zero in the colloquial sense of nonexistence" but "zero under the spacetime inner product." Two events connected by a null vector are, in the Lorentz-invariant sense, *at zero spacetime distance* from each other along that null direction; events on the future null cone of $p_{0}$ are at zero null-interval from $p_{0}$ along every radial null geodesic. **This is the algebra of nonlocality in the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel**, available in the null-vector formalism from Minkowski 1908 onward, before any quantum mechanics enters the picture.

The canonical commutator generates unitary evolution. ## I.3 The Central Question of the Present Paper

The seven dualities of physics. Hamiltonian/Lagrangian, Noether/Second-Law, Heisenberg/Schrödinger, particle/wave, locality/nonlocality, rest-mass/spatial-energy, time/space — are, in the standard literature, treated as seven separate facts:

- **Wave/particle duality** is accepted since Bohr's 1927 Como lecture [Bohr 1928] as a complementarity principle without geometric source.
- **Hamiltonian/Lagrangian duality** is treated as a mathematical equivalence (Dirac 1933 [Dirac 1933], Feynman 1948 [Feynman 1948], Stone 1932 [Stone 1932], von Neumann 1931 [von Neumann 1931]) of two formalisms.
- **Noether conservation laws** (Noether 1918 [Noether 1918]) and **the Second Law** (Boltzmann 1872 [Boltzmann 1872], Loschmidt 1876 [Loschmidt 1876]) are treated as two facts of physics whose coexistence is mathematically permitted but physically unexplained — the Loschmidt reversibility objection has stood as an unresolved tension for 150 years.
- **Heisenberg/Schrödinger pictures** are treated as two mathematically equivalent representations of unitary evolution.
- **Local microcausality** (Wightman 1956, Haag–Kastler 1964) and **nonlocal Bell correlations** (Bell 1964 [Bell 1964], Aspect 1982 [Aspect 1982], Weihs–Jennewein–Zeilinger 1998 [Weihs 1998], Hensen 2015 [Hensen 2015]) are treated as two facts of quantum mechanics whose coexistence has been called "spooky" [EPR 1935] and "uncomfortable" but has not been given a geometric source.
- **Rest mass and spatial-motion energy** are treated as two terms of the relativistic dispersion $E^{2} = (pc)^{2} + (mc^{2})^{2}$.
- **Time and space** are treated as two dimensional categories joined by the Minkowski metric (Minkowski 1908 [Minkowski 1909]).

The central question of the present paper is: **why do exactly these seven dualities exist, why are they parallel, and what physical principle generates them all?**

The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is wholly constituted by the active expansion. The forward light cone (Proposition V.3) is the integrated three-dimensional cross-section of x₄'s spherical expansion at rate c; without the expansion there is no light cone as a geometric object, only the metric sign $-c^{2} dt^{2}$ as an algebraic relation. # II. The Foundational Duality: Hamiltonian and Lagrangian Formulations of Quantum Mechanics (Level 1)
*(McGucken Duality framing for Level 1.)* The Hamiltonian and Lagrangian routes to $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ developed in this section are the **Level 1 instance of the McGucken Duality** — celebrating dx₄/dt = ic's **The McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel** face (the Hamiltonian route through Stone's theorem, Stone–von Neumann uniqueness, and the time-translation invariance of x₄-expansion, supplying the algebraic-symmetry of the commutator) and dx₄/dt = ic's **The McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel** face (the Lagrangian route through Huygens-wavefront propagation on the iterated McGucken Sphere, Compton-phase accumulation at $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$, and the Feynman path integral, supplying the geometric-propagation of the commutator). Both routes converge on the same identity $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ through disjoint intermediate machinery — the convergent-overdetermination signature of the McGucken Duality (Theorem IX.15.7 of the present paper).

Level 1 is the level. The Hamiltonian operator formulation and the Lagrangian path integral are, in the standard literature [Dirac 1933, Feynman 1948, Stone 1932, von Neumann 1931], two mathematically equivalent formulations of non-relativistic quantum mechanics whose equivalence rests on Stone–von Neumann uniqueness and Feynman's 1948 derivation of the Schrödinger equation from the path integral. The McGucken framework supplies the geometric source of both: each is a derived theorem of dx₄/dt = ic through a disjoint intermediate chain, and the two chains close at the same identity $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ from distinct sides. This section presents both chains at PhD rigor. Full development of the fifteen-framework completeness argument (the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel coverage in five frameworks, the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel coverage in six, intermediate structures disjoint in fourteen of fifteen positions) is in [2]; here I summarize at proof-grade rigor.

## II.1 The Hamiltonian Route: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel in Five Propositions

I derive $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ via the Algebraic-Channel account of dx₄/dt = ic: algebraic-symmetry, Stone's theorem, the Minkowski metric as the integrated shadow of the active expansion, and the position-momentum representation. Five propositions follow. The propositions of this subsection are referred to elsewhere in the paper interchangeably as **Proposition II.1–II.5** (by section-number convention) or as **Proposition H.1–H.5** (by Hamiltonian-route mnemonic); both names refer to the same statements.

**assumptions for §II.1:**
*A1*: The configuration space of a single non-relativistic particle is ℝ (one-dimensional, for clarity; the three-dimensional generalization is immediate).
*A2*: Quantum states are vectors in a complex separable Hilbert space $\mathcal H$.
*A3*: Symmetries are represented by strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups on $\mathcal H$, as is forced by Wigner's theorem [Wigner 1931] for invertible symmetry maps preserving transition probabilities.

**Proposition II.1 (H.1: Minkowski metric as integrated shadow of the active expansion).** *Let dx₄/dt = ic be the active expansion. Then the four-dimensional Euclidean line element $d\ell^{2} = dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} + dx_{4}^{2}$, evaluated with $dx_{4} = ic\,dt$ (the differential form of the active expansion), produces the Minkowski line element*
$$ds^{2} \;=\; dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} - c^{2} dt^{2}.$$
*The minus sign on $c^{2} dt^{2}$ is the algebraic shadow of i² = −1, i.e., of the perpendicularity marker that x₄ supplies through the active expansion.*

*Proof.* Substitute $dx_{4} = ic\,dt$ into $d\ell^{2}$:
$$d\ell^{2} \;=\; dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} + (ic\,dt)^{2} \;=\; dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} + i^{2} c^{2} dt^{2}.$$
Since i² = −1 (definition of ℂ over ℝ, equivalently the Frobenius-theorem characterization of the unique two-dimensional real division algebra extending ℝ [Frobenius 1878]), and since the integrated form $x_{4} = ict$ descends from the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, the right side equals $dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} - c^{2} dt^{2}$, which is the Minkowski line element of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ in the convention used throughout this paper. Identifying $d\ell^{2}|_{x_4 = ict} = ds^{2}$ as the physical four-dimensional line element gives the result. ∎

**Remark II.1.** The Minkowski metric is the integrated shadow of the active expansion. Minkowski 1908 [Minkowski 1909] observed the form x₄ = ict as a coordinate convention without dynamics; Pauli 1921 [Pauli 1921] adopted it in the Encyklopädie article without modification; the textbook tradition (Møller 1952, Misner–Thorne–Wheeler 1973, Weinberg 1972) abandoned the imaginary fourth coordinate in favor of the real Lorentzian signature. The McGucken framework restores the imaginary coordinate as the integrated shadow of the active dynamical expansion. The signature is forced; the i is forced; the dynamics survives the integration. Full priority record for the dynamical reading: [14]; [55]; [56]; [67].

**Proposition II.2 (H.2: Momentum operator as the Stone-theorem generator of spatial translation).** *Spatial translation by $a \in \mathbb{R}$, $T(a): \psi(q) \mapsto \psi(q - a)$, is represented on $\mathcal H = L^{2}(\mathbb{R})$ by a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group $U(a) = T(a)$. By Stone's theorem [Stone 1932], there exists a unique self-adjoint operator $\hat p$ such that $U(a) = \exp(-ia\hat p / \hbar)$. The minus sign and the factor ℏ are conventional; the factor i is forced as the perpendicularity marker that x₄ supplies through Proposition II.1's Minkowski signature.*

*Proof.* Strong continuity of $U(a)$ in $a$ is a direct verification on dense subdomains: for $\psi \in C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})$, $\|U(a)\psi - \psi\|^{2} = \int |\psi(q - a) - \psi(q)|^{2} dq \to 0$ as $a \to 0$ by uniform continuity. The group property $U(a + b) = U(a) U(b)$ is immediate: $T(a)T(b)\psi(q) = \psi(q - a - b) = T(a + b)\psi(q)$. Unitarity follows from translation invariance of Lebesgue measure: $\|T(a)\psi\|^{2} = \int |\psi(q - a)|^{2} dq = \int |\psi(q')|^{2} dq' = \|\psi\|^{2}$. Hence U is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group. By the converse direction of Stone's theorem [Stone 1932; modern treatment Reed–Simon 1980, vol. I, Theorem VIII.7] — inherited as functional-analytic background per §III.1 and [69] — there exists a unique self-adjoint generator $\hat p$ with $U(a) = \exp(-ia\hat p/\hbar)$.

The factor i in the exponent is forced by the Stone theorem: for $U(a)$ unitary, $U^{*}(a) = U(a)^{-1} = U(-a)$, and writing $U(a) = \exp(-iaX)$ for self-adjoint X gives $U^{*}(a) = \exp(+iaX) = U(-a)$ as required. A real generator $\exp(-aY)$ would produce a non-unitary semigroup. The i is therefore inherited as the perpendicularity marker that the Minkowski-signature integration of dx₄/dt = ic supplies (Proposition II.1). The ℏ enters by dimensional consistency, and its value is fixed by [16] as the action per x₄-cycle at the Planck frequency; I treat ℏ here as a dimensional convention and refer to [16] for the geometric derivation. ∎

**Remark II.2.** Stone's theorem in the form used here — the converse direction extracting the self-adjoint generator from the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group — is inherited functional-analytic background per §III.1 and [69]. The *physics* of the application (the unitary group itself, its strong continuity, its unitarity, the carrier Hilbert space, the action quantum ℏ, the interior position of i) is McGucken-internal at every component per [69]. Calling Stone's theorem "the bridge from the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic structure to the self-adjoint generator" is accurate at the *mathematical-closing-argument* level but should not be read as a claim that Stone's theorem itself is a McGucken theorem — only that the physical instance of its application to QM time evolution is McGucken-internal. The bridge to the algebraic-symmetry of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the McGucken source-pair $(\mathcal M_G, D_M)$ co-generated by dx₄/dt = ic (§IX.0.A); Stone's theorem closes the mathematics of that bridge as inherited background. Full the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel coverage of the Stone-theorem use in the McGucken framework: [2].

**Proposition II.3 (H.3: Momentum operator in the Schrödinger representation).** *Let $U(a)\psi(q) = \psi(q - a)$. Then in the Schrödinger representation, $\hat p = -i\hbar \, d/dq$ on the domain of absolutely continuous functions with square-integrable derivative.*

*Proof.* By Stone's theorem (Proposition II.2), $\hat p$ is the strong limit of $i\hbar\, dU(a)/da|_{a=0}$ on a dense domain. For $\psi \in C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})$,
$$\hat p \psi(q) \;=\; i\hbar \frac{d}{da}\bigg|_{a = 0} \psi(q - a) \;=\; i\hbar \cdot (-\psi'(q)) \;=\; -i\hbar \psi'(q) \;=\; -i\hbar \frac{d\psi}{dq}.$$
The self-adjoint extension to absolutely continuous square-integrable-derivative functions is the standard Reed–Simon construction. ∎

**Proposition II.4 (H.4: Canonical commutation relation, Hamiltonian route).** *Let $\hat q$ be the position operator $(\hat q \psi)(q) = q \psi(q)$ and $\hat p = -i\hbar\, d/dq$. Then $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar \, \mathbb{1}$ on the common domain $C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})$.*

*Proof.* On $C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})$:
$$\hat q (\hat p \psi)(q) = q \cdot (-i\hbar)\psi'(q) = -i\hbar q \psi'(q),$$
$$\hat p (\hat q \psi)(q) = -i\hbar \frac{d}{dq}\big[q \psi(q)\big] = -i\hbar\big[\psi(q) + q \psi'(q)\big] = -i\hbar \psi(q) - i\hbar q \psi'(q).$$
Therefore
$$[\hat q, \hat p]\psi(q) = \hat q(\hat p\psi)(q) - \hat p(\hat q\psi)(q) = -i\hbar q \psi'(q) - \big(-i\hbar \psi(q) - i\hbar q \psi'(q)\big) = i\hbar \psi(q).$$
Hence $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar \mathbb 1$ on $C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})$. The extension to the full Schwartz domain $\mathcal S(\mathbb{R})$ is standard. ∎

**Proposition II.5 (H.5: Stone–von Neumann uniqueness, closing the Hamiltonian route).** *Up to unitary equivalence, the irreducible representation of the canonical commutation relation $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar \mathbb 1$ on a separable complex Hilbert space, with $\hat q$ and $\hat p$ self-adjoint and the Weyl form $U(a) V(b) = e^{iab/\hbar} V(b) U(a)$ exponentiating the commutator, is unique and is the Schrödinger representation [von Neumann 1931].*

*Proof.* This is von Neumann's 1931 theorem [von Neumann 1931]; I cite it. A modern self-contained proof appears in Reed–Simon 1980 (vol. I, Theorem VIII.14). The import: once $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ is forced by the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel (Propositions II.1–II.4), the entire kinematics of non-relativistic quantum mechanics is determined up to unitary equivalence. The Hamiltonian route closes. ∎

This concludes the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel derivation of $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$. The chain is:
$$\begin{aligned} dx_{4}/dt = ic \;&\xrightarrow{\text{II.1}}\; \text{Minkowski signature} \;\xrightarrow{\text{II.2}}\; U(a) = e^{-ia\hat p/\hbar} \;\xrightarrow{\text{II.3}}\; \hat p = -i\hbar\, d/dq \\ &\xrightarrow{\text{II.4}}\; [\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar \;\xrightarrow{\text{II.5}}\; \text{Schrödinger uniqueness}. \end{aligned}$$
The intermediate structures are: Minkowski metric, Stone's theorem, Schrödinger differentiation, direct commutator computation, Stone–von Neumann uniqueness. All five are the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel (algebraic-symmetry). The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is not invoked at any step of this chain.

## II.2 The Lagrangian Route: the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel in Six Propositions

I now derive the same identity $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ via the Geometric-Channel account: geometric-propagation, Huygens' principle as a theorem of the active spherical expansion, iterated Huygens generating Feynman paths, x₄-phase accumulation generating the path-integral weight, Gaussian integration of the kernel against an initial wavefunction generating the Schrödinger equation, and identification of the resulting kinetic operator as $\hat p^{2}/2m$ with $\hat p = -i\hbar\, d/dq$. Six propositions follow. The full development is in [17] and [18]. The propositions of this subsection are referred to elsewhere in the paper interchangeably as **Proposition II.6–II.11** (by section-number convention) or as **Proposition L.1–L.6** (by Lagrangian-route mnemonic); both names refer to the same statements.

**assumptions for §II.2:**
*B1*: A single non-relativistic particle has rest mass $m > 0$ and Compton frequency $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar$.
*B2*: The non-relativistic limit $|v|/c \ll 1$ allows expansion $\gamma^{-1} = 1 - v^{2}/(2c^{2}) + O((v/c)^{4})$ to order $(v/c)^{2}$.
*B3*: Path-integral convergence is via the Trotter–Lie product formula [Trotter 1959] applied to the short-time kernel.

**Proposition II.6 (L.1: Huygens' principle from x₄-spherical expansion).** *Let $p_{0} = (\mathbf x_{0}, t_{0}, x_{4,0})$ be a spacetime event. The active expansion dx₄/dt = ic emanates from $p_{0}$ spherically symmetrically at rate c in the spatial subspace $\mathbb R^{3}$ orthogonal to x₄. The three-dimensional cross-section at observer coordinate time t is the McGucken Sphere*
$$\Sigma_{+}(p_{0}) \;=\; \{\mathbf x \in \mathbb R^{3} : |\mathbf x - \mathbf x_{0}| = c(t - t_{0})\}.$$
*This sphere is geometrically the forward light cone restricted to time t, and Huygens' secondary wavelet [Huygens 1690]. The retarded Green's function $G_{+}(\mathbf x - \mathbf x', t - t')$ of the wave equation $\Box \phi = 0$ in four-dimensional spacetime has support exactly on $\Sigma_{+}(\mathbf x', t')$ for every emission event $(\mathbf x', t')$.*

*Proof.* The active expansion dx₄/dt = ic asserts that the fourth dimension expands at rate ic from $p_{0}$. The spatial cross-section at observer time t is the set of points reachable from $p_{0}$ at proper distance $c(t - t_{0})$ in the spatial subspace, which is the sphere $\Sigma_{+}(p_{0})$ of radius $c(t - t_{0})$ centered at $\mathbf x_{0}$. This sphere is the forward light cone at time t from emission event $(\mathbf x_{0}, t_{0})$, the surface on which the d'Alembertian Green's function $G_{+}$ has its (singular) support in four-dimensional spacetime (odd spatial dimension equal to three, where the **strong Huygens principle** holds — see Hadamard 1932; modern treatment Friedlander 1975, §6.3). Identification with Huygens' secondary wavelet is the standard account: every point on a wavefront is a new center of a secondary wavelet of radius $c\, d\tau$ after time $d\tau$ (Huygens 1690, *Traité de la Lumière*, Chapter III). The active expansion supplies this geometry: every event is the center of a McGucken Sphere expanding at rate c. Full development as Theorem 1 of [18]. ∎

**Remark II.6.** Huygens' principle is a theorem of the active expansion. The retarded Green's function $G_{+}$ is the analytical encoding of the McGucken Sphere as a geometric object. The strong-Huygens condition (sharp localization on the cone, no tail) holds in dimension $3 + 1$ because the expansion is spherically symmetric and the spatial subspace is three-dimensional, with three an odd number — the algebraic feature of odd spatial dimension is the algebraic shadow of the geometric feature of the McGucken Sphere having codimension 1 in the four-dimensional spacetime. This is the same geometry read two ways.

**Proposition II.7 (L.2: Iterated Huygens generates all continuous paths).** *Let $q_{i}$ at $t_{i}$ and $q_{f}$ at $t_{f}$ be the initial and final configurations of a particle. Divide $[t_{i}, t_{f}]$ into N subintervals of length $\varepsilon = (t_{f} - t_{i})/N$. Applying Huygens' principle (Proposition II.6) at each subdivision $t_{k} = t_{i} + k\varepsilon$, $k = 0, 1, \dots, N$, with the secondary wavelet emanating from $(q_{k}, t_{k})$, the limit $N \to \infty$ generates all continuous paths $q(t)$ from $q_{i}$ to $q_{f}$. Equivalently, the Feynman sum over paths is the limit of the sum over chains of McGucken Spheres.*

*Proof.* Each McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{+}(q_{k}, t_{k})$ at time $t_{k+1} = t_{k} + \varepsilon$ is the sphere of radius $c\varepsilon$ centered at $q_{k}$. In the non-relativistic limit (B2), the particle's spatial displacement is $\Delta q_{k} = q_{k+1} - q_{k}$ with $|\Delta q_{k}| \ll c\varepsilon$. The set of accessible $(q_{k+1}, t_{k+1})$ as $q_{k+1}$ varies over $\Sigma_{+}(q_{k}, t_{k})$ projected to the line (or to $\mathbb R^{3}$ in three dimensions) is the entire spatial range at radius $\leq c\varepsilon$. Concatenating N such Huygens steps and taking $N \to \infty$ with $\varepsilon \to 0$, $N\varepsilon = t_{f} - t_{i}$ fixed, generates all continuous paths $q: [t_{i}, t_{f}] \to \mathbb R$ with $q(t_{i}) = q_{i}$, $q(t_{f}) = q_{f}$. This is the geometry of the Feynman sum over paths [Feynman 1948] read as a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel object: the path integral is the integral over chains of McGucken Spheres. Full development in [17]. ∎

**Proposition II.8 (L.3: Accumulated x₄-phase gives the Feynman weight).** *Each particle of rest mass $m > 0$ has Compton frequency $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar$ (B1). The active expansion at rate ic produces a phase rotation of the particle's internal x₄-oscillator at frequency $\omega_{C}$ per unit coordinate time. Over a subinterval ε, the accumulated x₄-phase is*
$$\Delta \phi_{k} \;=\; \omega_{C} \gamma^{-1} \varepsilon \;=\; \frac{mc^{2}}{\hbar}\big(1 - v_{k}^{2}/(2c^{2})\big)\varepsilon + O(v_{k}^{4}/c^{4})$$
*to order $(v/c)^{2}$ (B2). The expansion gives $\omega_{C}\gamma^{-1}\varepsilon = (mc^{2}/\hbar)\varepsilon - (mv^{2}/(2\hbar))\varepsilon = (mc^{2}\varepsilon - \tfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}\varepsilon)/\hbar$. The first term is the rest-mass contribution (a global phase common to all paths between fixed endpoints). The second term is the kinetic-energy contribution per subinterval, identified with $T\varepsilon$ where $T = \tfrac{1}{2}m v^{2}$. Including a potential $V(q)$, the on-shell short-interval phase is*
$$\exp\!\Big(\frac{i\varepsilon}{\hbar}\big(T - V\big)\Big) \;=\; \exp\!\Big(\frac{i\varepsilon}{\hbar} L_{\text{cl}}\Big),$$
*where $L_{\text{cl}} = T - V$ is the classical Lagrangian. Integrating over the path,*
$$\text{phase}(\text{path}) \;=\; \prod_{k=0}^{N-1} \exp\!\Big(\frac{i\varepsilon}{\hbar}L_{\text{cl},k}\Big) \;\xrightarrow{N\to\infty}\; \exp\!\Big(\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_{t_i}^{t_f} L_{\text{cl}}(q, \dot q, t)\, dt\Big) \;=\; \exp\!\big(iS[\text{path}]/\hbar\big),$$
*where $S[\text{path}] = \int L_{\text{cl}}\, dt$ is the classical action.*

*Proof.* The Compton-frequency identification $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar$ is the de Broglie relation for the rest-mass wave [de Broglie 1924], derived as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic in [2]: the x₄-oscillator runs at the Compton rate because the active expansion supplies frequency $\omega_{C}$ to a particle whose four-velocity points entirely into x₄ at rest. Time dilation: along a worldline with three-velocity $v_{k}$, the proper time per coordinate time ε is $\gamma^{-1}\varepsilon = (1 - v_{k}^{2}/c^{2})^{1/2}\varepsilon$. Hence the accumulated x₄-phase per subinterval is $\omega_{C}\gamma^{-1}\varepsilon$. Expansion to order $(v/c)^{2}$ using (B2) gives the displayed expression. The rest-mass term $(mc^{2}/\hbar)\varepsilon$ is common to all paths between fixed endpoints (it depends only on $N\varepsilon = t_{f} - t_{i}$) and absorbs as a global multiplicative phase that does not affect the kernel ratio. The kinetic-energy term $(mv_{k}^{2}/(2\hbar))\varepsilon$ is path-dependent. Including a potential V as a position-dependent x₄-phase shift, the short-interval phase weight is $\exp(i\varepsilon (T - V)/\hbar) = \exp(i\varepsilon L_{\text{cl}}/\hbar)$. The product over N subintervals and the limit $N \to \infty$ give the standard Feynman weight $\exp(iS/\hbar)$. Detailed treatment of the sign and factor-of-two conventions in [17]. ∎

**Proposition II.9 (L.4: The Feynman path integral as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic).** *Composing Propositions II.7 and II.8 and taking $N \to \infty$ with $\varepsilon \to 0$, $N\varepsilon = t_{f} - t_{i}$ fixed, the propagator kernel from $(q_{i}, t_{i})$ to $(q_{f}, t_{f})$ is*
$$K(q_{f}, t_{f}; q_{i}, t_{i}) \;=\; \int_{q(t_{i}) = q_{i}}^{q(t_{f}) = q_{f}} \mathcal D x(t) \; \exp\!\Big(\frac{i}{\hbar} S[x(t)]\Big),$$
*where $\mathcal D x(t)$ is the formal path-integral measure of [Feynman 1948]. The Feynman path integral is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic.*

*Proof.* Direct composition of Propositions II.7 (iterated Huygens generates paths) and II.8 (x₄-phase generates the Feynman weight), with the standard normalization $\prod_{k}\sqrt{m/(2\pi i\hbar\varepsilon)}$ that converges (in the sense of Trotter [Trotter 1959]) to the Feynman measure. Convergence is technical; the geometry is what I have established: every path is a chain of McGucken Spheres, and every weight is the x₄-phase accumulation along the chain. ∎

**Proposition II.10 (L.5: Schrödinger equation from short-time kernel).** *Apply $K_{\varepsilon}(q, q')$ at short time ε to an initial wavefunction $\psi(q', t)$ and expand to first order in ε. The short-time kernel is*
$$K_{\varepsilon}(q, q') \;=\; \sqrt{\frac{m}{2\pi i\hbar\varepsilon}}\, \exp\!\Big(\frac{i\varepsilon}{\hbar}\Big[\frac{m(q - q')^{2}}{2\varepsilon^{2}} - V(q)\Big]\Big).$$
*Gaussian integration of $K_{\varepsilon}(q, q') \psi(q', t)$ over $q'$ to first order in ε yields*
$$i\hbar \frac{\partial \psi}{\partial t} \;=\; -\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m} \frac{\partial^{2}\psi}{\partial q^{2}} + V(q)\psi(q, t).$$
*This is the time-dependent Schrödinger equation [Schrödinger 1926].*

*Proof.* Standard Feynman derivation [Feynman 1948; modern treatment Feynman–Hibbs 1965, §4.1, or Schulman 1981, §1.2]. The Gaussian integral $\int e^{i m (q - q')^{2}/(2\hbar\varepsilon)} \cdot \psi(q', t)\, dq'$, expanded around $q' = q$ via stationary phase, produces $\psi(q, t) + (i\hbar\varepsilon)/(2m) \partial^{2}_{q}\psi(q, t) + O(\varepsilon^{2})$ after Gaussian completion. Multiplication by $e^{-i\varepsilon V/\hbar} = 1 - i\varepsilon V/\hbar + O(\varepsilon^{2})$ and identification $\psi(q, t + \varepsilon) - \psi(q, t) = \varepsilon \partial_{t}\psi$ yields the Schrödinger equation upon dividing by ε. ∎

**Proposition II.11 (L.6: Canonical commutation relation, Lagrangian route, closing).** *Identifying the kinetic operator $-(\hbar^{2}/2m) \partial^{2}/\partial q^{2}$ of Proposition II.10 with $\hat p^{2}/(2m)$ forces $\hat p = -i\hbar\, \partial/\partial q$. Direct computation, identical to Proposition II.4, then yields $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar \mathbb 1$.*

*Proof.* From Proposition II.10, the Schrödinger equation reads $i\hbar \partial_{t}\psi = (\hat p^{2}/2m + V(\hat q))\psi$. Identifying $\hat p^{2}/2m = -\hbar^{2}\partial_{q}^{2}/(2m)$ forces $\hat p^{2} = -\hbar^{2}\partial_{q}^{2}$. The square root, picking the sign consistent with $\hat p$ self-adjoint and the Stone-theorem generator orientation, is $\hat p = -i\hbar\, \partial/\partial q$. Then by Proposition II.4 (the calculation is identical), $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar \mathbb 1$. The Lagrangian route closes at the same identity through disjoint intermediate structures. ∎

This concludes the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel derivation of $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$. The chain is:
$$\text{dx}_{4}/\text{dt} = \text{ic} \;\xrightarrow{\text{II.6}}\; \text{Huygens} \;\xrightarrow{\text{II.7}}\; \text{iterated Huygens / paths} \;\xrightarrow{\text{II.8}}\; \text{x}_{4}\text{-phase} = \exp(iS/\hbar) \;\xrightarrow{\text{II.9}}\; \text{Feynman kernel}$$
$$\;\xrightarrow{\text{II.10}}\; \text{Schrödinger equation} \;\xrightarrow{\text{II.11}}\; \hat p = -i\hbar\,\partial_{q}, \;\; [\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar.$$
The intermediate structures are: Huygens' principle, iterated Huygens, Compton-frequency x₄-phase, Feynman kernel, Gaussian integration, identification of kinetic term. All six are the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel (geometric-propagation). The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is not invoked at any step of this chain except in the final identification of $\hat p^{2}/2m$ with the kinetic term, which is a *kinematic* identification (the same self-adjoint operator on $L^{2}$, indexed by the *spectral* Lebesgue measure), not a derivational input.

## III.1 the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel: The Noether Catalog

Noether's theorem (1918) is a downstream consequence of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic via the Father Symmetry priority. The Father Symmetry paper [1] establishes that dx₄/dt = ic is prior to Noether's theorem: under the McGucken Principle, the existence of a smooth one-parameter Lie group of symmetries of the active-expansion-induced action functional, together with the integrated-shadow Algebraic structureH of dx₄/dt = ic, generates Noether's theorem itself as a theorem of the framework. When I invoke "Noether's theorem" in the propositions below, I am therefore citing a derived theorem of dx₄/dt = ic —, the Father-Symmetry-Theorem F1 of [1] — not an external mathematical framework. The historical name "Noether's theorem (1918)" is retained for pedagogical familiarity, with the understanding that the priority order is **dx₄/dt = ic ⇒ Father Symmetry ⇒ Noether's theorem ⇒ conserved currents**, not "Noether's theorem applied to dx₄/dt = ic gives conserved currents." Every invocation of Noether's theorem in the propositions below should be read as a corpus-internal citation to the Father-Symmetry chain, not as the importation of an external mathematical theorem.

Stone's theorem on one-parameter unitary groups (Stone 1932) occupies a *different* position in the McGucken framework than Noether's theorem does, and the difference is central. I state this carefully because conflating the two would overstate the McGucken claim.

The McGucken Symmetry paper [1] establishes Noether's theorem itself — the statement that every smooth one-parameter symmetry of an action functional generates a conserved current — as a derived theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via the Father Symmetry priority. The Father Symmetry chain produces both the symmetry-group structure and the conservation-law content from the McGucken Principle, so Noether's theorem is McGucken-internal.

For Stone's theorem, the McGucken corpus claims a **scope-restricted** result, not the analogous downstream-of-McGucken claim. The Father Symmetry paper's Theorem 34 (the analogue of Theorem 30 for the unitary-group sector) — restated and elaborated in the recent dedicated paper [69] — establishes that the *physics* of Stone's theorem applied to quantum-mechanical time evolution is McGucken-internal: (i) the carrier Hilbert space ℋ on which the theorem is applied is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic; (ii) the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group U(t) of physical time evolution is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic; (iii) the unitarity of U(t) is conservation of x₄-flux through the McGucken Sphere; (iv) the strong continuity of U(t) is the continuity of the dx₄/dt = ic flow at constant rate; (v) the action quantum ℏ in U(t) = exp(−iĤt/ℏ) is the McGucken Planck-scale oscillation action quantum; (vi) the interior position of i in U(t) is the σ-image of x₄'s perpendicularity to the spatial three-slice; (vii) the self-adjointness of the McGucken Hamiltonian Ĥ is a downstream consequence of unitarity and the McGucken construction of ℏ.

What the corpus does **not** claim, and what would overstate the framework if claimed — is that the *mathematical converse direction* of Stone's theorem (every strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group on a complex separable Hilbert space arises from a unique densely defined self-adjoint generator) is a McGucken theorem. The converse direction holds on Hilbert spaces with no x₄ interpretation (the Hardy space H²(D), the Hilbert space ℓ²(ℤ) with the bilateral shift, the Bargmann-Fock space, the L²-space of any complex vector bundle), so it cannot be a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic — the converse direction would have to fail when dx₄/dt = ic does not hold, but it does not fail on those x₄-free Hilbert spaces. The converse direction is therefore inherited functional-analytic background, established by von Neumann's 1929 spectral theorem and Stone's 1932 Cayley-transform analysis, on the same epistemological footing as Cauchy–Schwarz (used in Robertson uncertainty closure), Riesz–Fischer (used in L² completion), and Frobenius's theorem on real division algebras (used confirmingly in the determination that ℂ is the scalar field of quantum mechanics). [69] states this boundary explicitly. The McGucken Category synthesis [46] follows the same careful boundary by citing Stone's theorem at [Stone 1932] as a standard reference (their reference [74]), not as a derived theorem of the McGucken corpus.

In every invocation of Stone's theorem in the propositions below, the *physics* of the application to QM time evolution is McGucken-internal per [69], while the *mathematical converse direction* is inherited functional-analytic background per [69]. This is the same template applied throughout the corpus: physical instance is McGucken-internal, functional-analytic closing argument is inherited background. This is the standard pattern of mathematical physics. Newton with calculus, Maxwell with vector analysis, Einstein with tensor calculus, and does not weaken the McGucken claim; it sharpens it.

The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel reads the active expansion through its algebraic-symmetry. Each symmetry of dx₄/dt = ic generates, by Noether's theorem (Father-Symmetry-Theorem F1 of [1]), a conserved current. The full Noether catalog has twelve conservation laws: ten Poincaré charges, two internal-gauge structures (U(1) electric, with SU(2)_L and SU(3)_c as Clifford-algebraic extensions), and one diffeomorphism-covariant stress-energy. I present three propositions covering the catalog.

**assumptions for §III.1:**
*A4*: The active expansion is invariant under the Poincaré group $ISO(1, 3) = \mathbb R^{1,3} \rtimes SO^{+}(1, 3)$ acting on Minkowski spacetime.
*A5*: The action functional $S[\phi] = \int \mathcal L\, d^{4}x$ for any field theory built on the Minkowski background inherits the Poincaré invariance.

**Proposition III.1 (Ten Poincaré charges).** *The Poincaré invariance (A4–A5) of the active expansion's integrated form implies, by Noether's first theorem, ten conserved currents:*

*(i) Temporal uniformity (time-translation invariance) ⇒ $dE/dt = 0$ (one conservation law).*
*(ii) Spatial homogeneity (three-translation invariance) ⇒ $d\mathbf P/dt = 0$ (three conservation laws).*
*(iii) Spherical isotropy (rotation invariance) ⇒ $d J_{ij}/dt = 0$, $i, j \in \{1, 2, 3\}$, $i < j$ (three conservation laws).*
*(iv) Lorentz boost covariance ⇒ $d K_{i}/dt = 0$ on-shell (three conservation laws on the center-of-energy three-vector).*

*Total: ten Poincaré charges. Each conservation law is time-symmetric: the Poincaré group includes time-symmetry as one of its discrete generators (in the full $O(1,3)$ extension), and the continuous Noether currents are invariant under the time-reversal transformation.*

*Proof.* Noether's first theorem [Noether 1918; modern self-contained proof Goldstein–Poole–Safko 2002, §13.7] asserts: for an action functional invariant under a smooth one-parameter Lie group of transformations with generator X, there exists a conserved current $j^{\mu}$ with $\partial_{\mu}j^{\mu} = 0$ on solutions. Apply to:

(i) Time translation $t \to t + s$, generator $\partial/\partial t$: the conserved charge is the Hamiltonian density integrated over space, $E = \int T^{00}\, d^{3}\mathbf x$, with $dE/dt = 0$.

(ii) Spatial translation $\mathbf x \to \mathbf x + \mathbf a$, generator $\partial/\partial \mathbf x$: the conserved currents are $T^{0i}$ for $i = 1, 2, 3$, with $\mathbf P = \int T^{0i}\, d^{3}\mathbf x$ and $d\mathbf P/dt = 0$.

(iii) Spatial rotation in the $ij$-plane, generator $L_{ij} = x_{i}\partial_{j} - x_{j}\partial_{i}$: the conserved charges are angular-momentum components $J_{ij} = \int (x_{i} T^{0j} - x_{j} T^{0i})\, d^{3}\mathbf x$, with $dJ_{ij}/dt = 0$ for $i < j$, giving three conservation laws.

(iv) Lorentz boost in the $0i$-plane, generator $M_{0i} = t \partial_{i} + x_{i} \partial_{t}/c^{2}$ (appropriately normalized): the conserved on-shell quantity is $K_{i} = \int (x_{i} T^{00}/c^{2} - t T^{0i})\, d^{3}\mathbf x$ (center-of-energy first moment), with $d K_{i}/dt = 0$ on shell. Detailed treatment in Weinberg 1995, §7.4.

time-symmetry: each generator is even or appropriately covariant under $t \to -t$; the conserved charges transform as scalars, vectors, or tensors under T, preserving conservation. The ten Poincaré charges are time-symmetric. ∎

**Proposition III.2 (Three internal-gauge charges and four-component fermion structure).** *Local U(1) gauge invariance on the x₄-phase (A6) generates Maxwell's equations and conservation of electric charge $dQ_{\text{EM}}/dt = 0$. The matter orientation condition (M), only even-grade multivectors propagate as matter, selects the Dirac equation $(i\gamma^{\mu}\partial_{\mu} - m)\psi = 0$ as the unique first-order Lorentz-covariant equation of motion. The SU(2)_L weak isospin emerges as the doublet structure on left-handed Weyl spinors; SU(3)_c emerges from the triplet structure on three-color quark sub-multiplets in the relevant Clifford sub-algebra. Conservation: weak-isospin and color conservation follow by Noether's theorem applied to the SU(2)_L and SU(3)_c gauge symmetries, with covariantly-conserved currents $D_{\mu}j^{a, \mu} = 0$. ∎

**Proposition III.3 (Diffeomorphism invariance and stress-energy conservation).** *Coordinate-independence of x₄'s advance on the smooth four-manifold implies diffeomorphism invariance of the action. By Noether's second theorem [Noether 1918, §II], this is a local gauge symmetry whose conserved current is the stress-energy tensor $T^{\mu\nu}$, with covariant conservation $\nabla_{\mu}T^{\mu\nu} = 0$.*

*Proof.* Diffeomorphism invariance of the action under $x^{\mu} \to x^{\mu} + \xi^{\mu}(x)$ for arbitrary $\xi^{\mu}$ is a local gauge symmetry (infinite-dimensional). ## III.2 the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel: The Second Law

The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel reads the active expansion through its geometric-propagation. The spherical symmetry of x₄'s expansion produces an isotropic random walk in three-space; the Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of an ensemble undergoing this walk grows strictly monotonically; the Shannon entropy of a photon riding the expanding McGucken Sphere grows strictly monotonically. The Second Law is a theorem of the active expansion.

**assumptions for §III.2:**
*B4*: The matter–expansion coupling is the Compton-frequency coupling of [21], i.e., a particle of rest mass $m$ experiences an effective oscillatory contribution to its x₄-advance at frequency $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar$ with small amplitude $\varepsilon \ll 1$.
*B5*: The coarse-graining scale for entropy is the spatial-displacement scale of the iterated isotropic random walk (Proposition III.4 below).

**Proposition III.4 (Spherical isotropic random walk from x₄-spherical expansion).** *The spherical symmetry of x₄'s expansion contains no preferred spatial direction. The spatial projection of each particle's x₄-driven displacement is a vector of magnitude $r = c \Delta t / \gamma$ uniformly distributed over $S^{2}$. Iterated N times, the mean-square displacement is*
$$\langle |\mathbf x_{N} - \mathbf x_{0}|^{2} \rangle \;=\; N r^{2} \;=\; D t,$$
*where $D = c^{2}\Delta t / \gamma^{2}$ is the diffusion constant of the spherical isotropic walk and $t = N\Delta t$.*

*Proof.* By the spherical symmetry of the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{+}(\mathbf x_{n}, t_{n})$ (Proposition II.6), the displacement $\Delta \mathbf x_{n} = \mathbf x_{n+1} - \mathbf x_{n}$ is a vector of magnitude $r = c\Delta t / \gamma$ (the proper spatial advance per coordinate-time step, accounting for the time-dilation factor $\gamma^{-1}$ if the particle is moving with three-velocity $v$) and direction uniform on $S^{2}$. Hence $\langle \Delta \mathbf x_{n} \rangle = 0$ (vanishing first moment) and $\langle |\Delta \mathbf x_{n}|^{2} \rangle = r^{2}$. By statistical independence of steps (a consequence of the spherical isotropy at each step),
$$\langle |\mathbf x_{N} - \mathbf x_{0}|^{2} \rangle \;=\; \langle \big| \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} \Delta \mathbf x_{n}\big|^{2} \rangle \;=\; \sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\langle |\Delta\mathbf x_{n}|^{2}\rangle \;=\; N r^{2}.$$
Setting $t = N\Delta t$ and $D = r^{2}/\Delta t = c^{2}\Delta t/\gamma^{2}$ gives $\langle |\mathbf x_{N} - \mathbf x_{0}|^{2}\rangle = Dt$. ∎

**Proposition III.5 (Central limit theorem: Gaussian distribution at large N).** *Under the conditions of Proposition III.4, the displacement $\mathbf x_{N} - \mathbf x_{0}$ converges (in distribution, as $N \to \infty$ with $N\Delta t = t$ fixed) to a Gaussian random variable of mean zero and variance $Dt$ per dimension.*

*Proof.* Standard application of the multivariate central limit theorem [Feller 1971, vol. II, §VIII.4] to the sum of i.i.d. Random vectors with finite mean and covariance. The mean is zero, the per-dimension variance is $r^{2}/3$ (since $\langle (\Delta x_{n}^{(i)})^{2}\rangle = r^{2}/3$ for each $i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ by isotropy), and the sum's per-dimension variance is $Nr^{2}/3 = Dt/3$. Identifying the per-dimension diffusion constant as $D/3$ in the convention where D is the trace of the diffusion tensor (the standard convention), the limiting density is
$$\rho(\mathbf x, t) \;=\; \frac{1}{(4\pi Dt/3)^{3/2}}\, \exp\!\Big(-\frac{|\mathbf x - \mathbf x_{0}|^{2}}{4 D t/3}\Big).$$
A convention-cleaned form, more commonly written with D as the per-dimension diffusion constant, is $\rho(\mathbf x, t) = (4\pi D' t)^{-3/2}\exp(-|\mathbf x|^{2}/(4 D' t))$ with $D' = D/3$. I use the per-dimension convention henceforth and write D for $D'$ (so $\langle |\mathbf x|^{2}\rangle = 3Dt$, consistent with the sum of three independent per-dimension Gaussians of variance $2Dt$ — the factor of 2 from the standard $\langle x^{2}\rangle_{\text{Gauss}} = 2Dt$ in one dimension for the diffusion equation $\partial_{t}\rho = D \partial_{x}^{2}\rho$). ∎

**Proposition III.6 (Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of a Gaussian).** *For the Gaussian density of Proposition III.5, the Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy is*
$$S_{\text{BG}}(t) \;=\; -k_{B} \int \rho \ln \rho\, d^{3}\mathbf x \;=\; \frac{3}{2} k_{B} \ln(4\pi e D t) + \text{const}.$$

*Proof.* Direct computation. For a Gaussian density $\rho(\mathbf x, t) = (4\pi D t)^{-3/2}\exp(-|\mathbf x|^{2}/(4 D t))$ (per-dimension convention),
$$-\ln\rho(\mathbf x, t) \;=\; \frac{3}{2}\ln(4\pi D t) + \frac{|\mathbf x|^{2}}{4 D t}.$$
The entropy is $S_{\text{BG}}/k_{B} = \langle -\ln\rho\rangle = (3/2)\ln(4\pi D t) + (3/2)$ (using $\langle |\mathbf x|^{2}\rangle = 6 D t$ from the three-dimensional sum with $\langle x_{i}^{2}\rangle = 2Dt$ for each Cartesian component, and $\langle |\mathbf x|^{2}\rangle/(4Dt) = 3/2$). Hence $S_{\text{BG}} = (3/2) k_{B} \ln(4\pi e D t) + \text{const}$, with the constant absorbing the $\hbar^{3}$ phase-space cell from the underlying quantum kinematics. ∎

**Proposition III.7 (Strict positivity of entropy production).** *The Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of Proposition III.6 satisfies*
$$\frac{dS_{\text{BG}}}{dt} \;=\; \frac{3 k_{B}}{2 t} \;>\; 0 \qquad \text{for all }t > 0.$$
*The entropy production is strictly positive: absolutely, at every event, not merely on average or statistically. Entropy cannot decrease because x₄ cannot retreat.*

*Proof.* Direct differentiation of Proposition III.6: $dS_{\text{BG}}/dt = (3 k_{B}/2)(d/dt)\ln(4\pi e D t) = (3 k_{B}/2)(1/t) = 3 k_{B}/(2t)$, which is positive for all $t > 0$. The reason this is strict (rather than merely statistical, as in Boltzmann's 1872 H-theorem with the Stosszahlansatz [Boltzmann 1872]) is geometric: the spherical expansion of x₄ at rate c produces, at every time $t > 0$, a wider Gaussian than at any earlier time $t' < t$, and the Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of a wider Gaussian is greater. There is no probabilistic averaging required; the entropy is a deterministic function of the variance of the underlying Gaussian, and the variance is a deterministic function of t via $\langle |\mathbf x|^{2}\rangle = 6 Dt$. The "x₄ cannot retreat" assertion is the geometry of dx₄/dt = ic: x₄ advances at rate c, monotonically, with no provision for retreat. ∎

**Remark III.7.** This strict positivity is *the* key result that resolves the Loschmidt objection. I elaborate in §III.4.

**Proposition III.8 (Shannon entropy on the McGucken Sphere grows because the Sphere grows).** *For a photon emitted isotropically from $p_{0} = (\mathbf x_{0}, t_{0})$, the photon rides the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{+}(p_{0})$ of radius $R = c(t - t_{0})$ with uniform distribution. The Shannon entropy of this distribution is*
$$S_{\text{Sh}}(t) \;=\; k_{B}\ln\big(4\pi (c(t - t_{0}))^{2}\big) + \text{const},$$
*with*
$$\frac{dS_{\text{Sh}}}{dt} \;=\; \frac{2 k_{B}}{t - t_{0}} \;>\; 0 \qquad \text{for all }t > t_{0}.$$

*Proof.* The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{+}(p_{0})$ at observer time t has area $A(t) = 4\pi(c(t - t_{0}))^{2}$ (the standard area formula for a sphere of radius $R$). The uniform distribution on $\Sigma_{+}(p_{0})$ has Shannon entropy equal to the logarithm of the area (with appropriate dimensional factors): $S_{\text{Sh}} = k_{B}\ln A(t) + \text{const}$. Differentiating, $dS_{\text{Sh}}/dt = k_{B}(d/dt)\ln(4\pi c^{2}(t - t_{0})^{2}) = 2 k_{B}/(t - t_{0})$, which is positive for $t > t_{0}$. The entropy grows because the sphere grows; the sphere grows because x₄ advances at rate c. ∎

The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel at Level 2 summarises as follows. Two entropy theorems (Boltzmann–Gibbs for massive particles, Shannon for photons), each strictly positive for all $t > 0$, each traced to a geometry: the active expansion of x₄ at rate c. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is the geometric-propagation / advance face of the active expansion.

## III.3 The Five Arrows of Time

All five classical arrows of time trace to the single geometry that x₄ advances monotonically at rate c:

**(1) Thermodynamic arrow.** The direction of dS/dt > 0 (Propositions III.7 and III.8). The arrow points in the direction of increasing entropy, which is the direction of x₄-advance.

**(2) Radiative arrow.** The direction of the outgoing retarded Green's function $G_{+}$ of the wave equation. Advanced solutions $G_{-}$ are mathematically permitted but not physically realized because they would require x₄-retreat (their support is the past light cone, which is the retreating McGucken Sphere). The radiative arrow is therefore the +ic direction of the active expansion.

**(3) Causal arrow.** The direction of propagation into the forward light cone. Since the forward light cone is the McGucken Sphere advancing at rate c, the causal arrow is the +ic direction.

**(4) Cosmological arrow.** The direction of cosmological expansion (Hubble flow), which is the macroscopic expression of every particle's forced advance through x₄ at rate c. The cosmological arrow is identified empirically with the CMB-frame absolute motion (item (4) in the four-fold ontology of §I.2).

**(5) Psychological arrow.** Memory encodes events in the past light cone; the causal arrow instantiated in neural systems. The psychological arrow is the causal arrow read by an observer with finite memory.

Reichenbach 1956 [Reichenbach 1956] unified the thermodynamic and causal arrows. Penrose 1989 [Penrose 1989] grounded the thermodynamic arrow in cosmological boundary conditions (the Weyl curvature hypothesis). **The McGucken Principle unifies all five as parallel consequences of dx₄/dt = ic**, with no boundary-condition input and no statistical input. The arrows of time are the arrows of x₄-advance, read at five levels of description.

## III.4 Dissolution of the Loschmidt Reversibility Objection

Loschmidt 1876 [Loschmidt 1876] observed that if microscopic dynamics are time-reversal symmetric, the strict H-theorem cannot follow rigorously: any entropy-increasing trajectory is matched by a time-reversed entropy-decreasing trajectory of equal statistical weight. Boltzmann's 1877 response resolved the tension statistically (by appeal to the overwhelmingly greater volume of macrostates compatible with high entropy) but not absolutely, and required the Past Hypothesis (the initial state has low entropy) as auxiliary input.

The tension presupposes that the time-symmetric conservation laws (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel) and the time-asymmetric Second Law (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel) have a common origin that must itself be either time-symmetric or time-asymmetric. The McGucken framework supplies a common origin — dx₄/dt = ic, but they descend through two logically distinct channels:

- **The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel reads the active expansion's algebraic-symmetry**, which is time-symmetric (the Poincaré group includes T as a discrete symmetry, and the continuous Noether currents are time-symmetric). This produces time-symmetric conservation laws (Proposition III.1).

- **The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel reads the active expansion's geometric-propagation**, which is time-asymmetric (x₄ advances at +ic monotonically, with no provision for retreat). This produces the time-asymmetric Second Law (Propositions III.7, III.8).

Both readings are simultaneously valid. They are simultaneous readings of the McGucken Principle's two informational contents. **This is the same move that wave/particle duality makes** (Level 4, §V): a photon traversing a double-slit apparatus is has both readings simultaneously. The dynamics of the universe is has both dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel (symmetric) and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel (asymmetric) content simultaneously.

A referee who accepts wave/particle duality without objection cannot consistently reject the conservation-law/Second-Law duality on "which reading is privileged" grounds: the logic is identical. This is the central rhetorical point of the dual-channel framework, and it is (not philosophical): the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel/the Geometric-Channel account is the same Kleinian split (§IX) at the two levels.

The Loschmidt objection is dissolved: it is a misreading of one principle through its two informational contents.

## III.5 Derivation of the Past Hypothesis as a Theorem

For a system whose entropy increases through the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel, the lowest-entropy moment is by construction the moment when x₄'s expansion begins from the initial configuration. The lowest-entropy moment is the geometric starting point of the advance. For the universe as a whole, this moment is identified with the hot Big Bang.

Penrose 1989 [Penrose 1989] computed the improbability of the initial state, under a uniform prior over microstates compatible with the macroscopic initial conditions, as approximately $10^{-10^{123}}$. This computation assumes a *uniform prior*. Under the McGucken framework, the prior is not uniform: **the geometric structure of x₄'s expansion selects the lowest-entropy moment as its starting point.** The Past Hypothesis is derived from the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. The 10^{-10^{123}} "fine-tuning" is the integrated improbability under an incorrect prior; under the correct (geometric) prior, the initial state has probability 1, because it is the starting point.

**Theorem III.A (Past Hypothesis as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic).** *Under the active expansion at rate ic from a starting event $p_{0} = (\mathbf x_{0}, t_{0})$, the entropy of any ensemble of particles confined to a finite spatial region at $t_{0}$ has a strict lower bound at $t = t_{0}^{+}$, achieved by the configuration in which all particles are at $p_{0}$. The entropy strictly increases for $t > t_{0}$ (Proposition III.7). The Past Hypothesis, that the initial state has low entropy — is therefore a theorem of the McGucken Principle.*

*Proof.* The Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of a delta-function distribution at $p_{0}$ at $t = t_{0}^{+}$ is, in the regularized form, $S_{\text{BG}} \to -\infty$ (the most negative possible value), or, with a UV cutoff at the de Broglie length, $S_{\text{BG}} = (3/2)k_{B}\ln(4\pi e D \epsilon) + \text{const}$ for an infinitesimal ε, which is bounded below for any finite D. As t increases from $t_{0}^{+}$, the Gaussian widens (Proposition III.5) and the entropy strictly increases (Proposition III.7). The minimum entropy moment is $t = t_{0}^{+}$, the starting point of the active expansion. ∎

The Penrose Past Hypothesis is dissolved: the initial state is the lowest-entropy state because it is the *starting point*, not a fine-tuned configuration. The "fine-tuning" was the integrated improbability under a uniform prior; the correct prior is geometric (active-expansion-based).

I again anticipate §IX. At Level 2, the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel are the algebra-and-geometry split of the Poincaré-group action on the spacetime manifold:

### III.A.2 Five-arrow synthesis

**Theorem III.A.1.** *Let $\mathcal{M}_{G}$ be the McGucken four-manifold governed by dx₄/dt = ic. Then the following five arrows of time are one and the same arrow — namely the +ic orientation of the active expansion of x₄ — read at five distinct levels of description:*

3. *Causal arrow: the direction of propagation of physical influence into the forward light cone of every event.*
4. *Cosmological arrow: the direction of the Hubble flow, i.e., the macroscopic expression of every event's x₄-advance.*
5. *Psychological arrow: the direction in which memory encodes events in the past light cone of an observer.*

*Proof.* By Primitive 1, the Lorentzian interval on $\mathcal{M}_{G}$ admits a temporal orientation. By the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, that orientation is fixed at +ic (rather than −ic): the differential equation dx₄/dt = ic carries the sign $+i$ on its right-hand side, not $-i$, and this sign is a geometric primitive of the McGucken framework — the active expansion of x₄ is *outward*, not inward. (The choice +ic is determined empirically by the observed thermodynamic arrow and the Generalized Second Law of black-hole thermodynamics, [3].)

I now show each arrow is the +ic-orientation of the active expansion, read at its respective level.

*Arrow 1 (Thermodynamic).* Proposition III.7 of the present paper establishes that the Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of a Gaussian ensemble on $\mathcal{M}_{G}$ undergoing the spherical expansion forced by dx₄/dt = ic satisfies $dS/dt = 3k_{B}/(2t) > 0$ for all $t > 0$. The strict positivity is geometric, not statistical: it follows from the variance $\langle |\mathbf{x}|^{2}\rangle = 6Dt$ of the Gaussian density (Proposition III.5) which is forced by the spherical-expansion-induced isotropic random walk in three-space. Reversing the orientation of the active expansion from +ic to −ic would reverse the sign of D in the Gaussian width and hence reverse $dS/dt$; the +ic orientation forces dS/dt > 0. The thermodynamic arrow is the +ic-orientation.

*Arrow 2 (Radiative).* The wave equation $\Box \phi = 0$ on $\mathcal{M}_{G}$ admits two distributional Green's functions $G_{\pm}$ supported on the forward and past light cones respectively. By Primitive 2, the forward light cone is the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{+}(p_{0})$ expanding outward from the source event $p_{0}$ as $R(t) = c(t-t_{0})$ for $t > t_{0}$. The advanced Green's function $G_{-}$ would require a contracting McGucken Sphere with $R$ decreasing as t increases past $t_{0}$, i.e. A sphere contracting at velocity $-c$, which would require dx₄/dt = −ic. By the +ic-orientation fixed above, $G_{-}$ is geometrically excluded; only $G_{+}$ is physical. The radiative arrow is the +ic-orientation.

*Arrow 3 (Causal).* Physical influence propagates along worldlines that are timelike or null with respect to the Lorentzian metric of Primitive 1, and lies within the forward light cone of the source event by Primitive 2. By the argument of Arrow 2, the forward light cone is the outward-expanding McGucken Sphere, which is the +ic-direction. The causal arrow is the +ic-orientation.

*Arrow 4 (Cosmological).* On the McGucken framework's cosmological extension [5], URL https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2026/05/19/the-mcgucken-cosmology-dx%e2%82%84-dt-ic-and-the-fourth-dimension-is-expanding-at-the-velocity-of-light-take-first-place-on-twelve-tests-of-the-twelve-tests-with-zero-free-dark-sector-3/, the Hubble flow $H(t) = \dot{a}/a$ of the FLRW metric is derived as a direct consequence of dx₄/dt = ic via the Friedmann equation as the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Sphere-expansion (Theorem 28 of [3]). The $\dot{a} > 0$ requirement of the empirical Hubble expansion forces the +ic orientation; reversing the orientation to −ic would yield $\dot{a} < 0$ (contraction), contradicting observation. The cosmological arrow is the +ic-orientation.

*Arrow 5 (Psychological).* An observer with finite memory at event $p_{\text{obs}} \in \mathcal{M}_{G}$ encodes events from the past light cone $J^{-}(p_{\text{obs}})$, not the future light cone $J^{+}(p_{\text{obs}})$, because the past light cone consists of events whose forward-McGucken-Spheres have already reached $p_{\text{obs}}$ (these are the events from which causal influence has arrived) while the future light cone consists of events whose forward-McGucken-Spheres have not yet reached $p_{\text{obs}}$ (no causal influence has yet arrived). The asymmetry of memory is the asymmetry of the past versus future light cones, which is the +ic-orientation by Arrows 2 and 3. The psychological arrow is the +ic-orientation.

All five arrows reduce to the single +ic-orientation of dx₄/dt = ic. ∎
