### IX.0.B The First Law of the McGucken Dualities

The overdetermination content of §IX.0 and the categorical co-generation content of §IX.0.A together establish a about the two channels of the McGucken Duality: they are **reciprocally generative**. Every the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel process contains the potential to source a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel process; every dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel process contains the potential to source a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel process. The two channels co-derive the same fundamental equations through disjoint intermediate machinery, and it is the mechanism the prior literature on "dualities" was unable to articulate. I state this as the First Law of the McGucken Dualities.

**Theorem IX.0.B.1 (First Law of the McGucken Dualities, after [46]).** *Let $\mathfrak{D} = \mathfrak{D}_A \boxtimes \mathfrak{D}_B$ denote the McGucken Duality, with the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel face $\mathfrak{D}_A$ (algebraic-symmetry) and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel face $\mathfrak{D}_B$ (geometric-propagation), both generated by dx₄/dt = ic via the bidirectional Klein correspondence of Theorem IX.0.A.8. Then:*

*Every the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel process contains the potential for the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel processes, and every dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel process contains the potential for the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel processes, because both are generated by dx₄/dt = ic, both therefore contain dx₄/dt = ic in them, and both are therefore capable of generating one another.*

*Formal statement.* Let $P_A$ be any dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel process (a derivational chain through algebraic-symmetry) and $P_B$ be any dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel process (a derivational chain through geometric-propagation). Then:

1. *$P_A \supseteq \{dx_4/dt = ic\}$ — every dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel process contains dx₄/dt = ic as its source.*
2. *$P_B \supseteq \{dx_4/dt = ic\}$ — every dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel process contains dx₄/dt = ic as its source.*
3. *dx₄/dt = ic generates both $\mathfrak{D}_A$ and $\mathfrak{D}_B$ as the two faces of the source-pair $(\mathcal M_{G}, D_M)$ via the bidirectional Klein correspondence (Theorem IX.0.A.8).*
4. *Therefore, from any $P_A$, one can extract dx₄/dt = ic via the canonical extraction procedure of the Containment-Generation Equivalence (Theorem IX.21.4) and then construct a corresponding the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel process $P_B'$ via the canonical construction procedure $C_B \circ \Pi_{P_A}$; symmetrically from any $P_B$, one can extract dx₄/dt = ic and construct a corresponding the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel process $P_A'$.*

*The two channels are therefore reciprocally generative: each contains the seed of the other, and each generates the other through the shared source dx₄/dt = ic.*

*Proof.* *Step 1 (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel contains dx₄/dt = ic).* By the definition of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel (Definition IX.0.1 of the present paper) and the categorical primitive of §IX.0.A, the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the algebraic-symmetry face of the source-pair $(\mathcal M_{G}, D_{M})$ under the bidirectional Klein correspondence. The algebraic operator $D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$ has dx₄/dt = ic embedded in it as its defining content: $D_M f = 0$ along integral curves is the condition $\partial_t f + ic\,\partial_{x_4} f = 0$, equivalently $df/dt + (dx_4/dt)\,\partial_{x_4} f = 0$ with dx₄/dt = ic as the rate-of-advance. Therefore every dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel process, every derivational chain through algebraic-symmetry, contains dx₄/dt = ic in the form of the rate-defining content of $D_M$. By the Mutual Containment Capability of [46], the canonical extraction $\Pi_{D_M}: D_M \to (dx_4/dt = ic)$ recovers dx₄/dt = ic from $D_M$ as the ratio of the x₄-coefficient to the t-coefficient: $ic/1 = ic$. Clause 1 is established.

*Step 2 (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel contains dx₄/dt = ic).* By the definition of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel (Definition IX.0.1) and the categorical primitive of §IX.0.A, the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is the geometric-propagation face of the source-pair, with the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ as its foundational atom. The McGucken Sphere at observer time $t > t_p$ has radius $R(t) = c(t - t_p)$ from event p, with the rate of growth $dR/dt = c$ being the projection of $|dx_4/dt| = c$ onto the spatial three-coordinates. By the canonical extraction $\Pi_{\Sigma_M}$ of [46]: $\Pi_{\Sigma_M}: \Sigma_M^+(p) \mapsto \lim_{t \to t_p^+} [x_4(t) - x_4(t_p)]/(t - t_p) = ic$ by standard differentiation. Therefore every dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel process contains dx₄/dt = ic in the form of the rate-of-Sphere-expansion. Clause 2 is established.

*Step 3 (Bidirectional Klein correspondence).* This is Theorem IX.0.A.8 of the present paper. The bidirectional Klein correspondence applied to the source-pair $(\mathcal M_G, D_M)$ generates the two channels as the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel = $\mathrm{Klein\text{-}corresp}(\mathcal M_G, D_M)$ (geometry-generates-group direction) and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel = $\mathrm{Klein\text{-}corresp}(D_M, \mathcal M_G)$ (group-generates-geometry direction). Both directions are forced by dx₄/dt = ic via the source-pair co-generation. Clause 3 is established.

*Step 4 (Reciprocal generation of channels from one another).* By the Reciprocal Generation Capability of [46], the canonical generation procedure $\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_Y \circ \Pi_X$ exists for every ordered pair $(X, Y) \in F_M \times F_M$ with $X \neq Y$. Applied to the ordered pair $(\mathfrak{D}_A, \mathfrak{D}_B)$: $\Gamma_{\mathfrak{D}_A \to \mathfrak{D}_B} = C_{\mathfrak{D}_B} \circ \Pi_{\mathfrak{D}_A}$ — extract dx₄/dt = ic from any dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel process via $\Pi_{\mathfrak{D}_A}$, then construct the corresponding the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel process via $C_{\mathfrak{D}_B}$. Symmetrically for $\Gamma_{\mathfrak{D}_B \to \mathfrak{D}_A}$. The two generations form a codiscrete groupoid (the Round-Trip Lemma of [46]: $\Pi_Y \circ C_Y = \text{id}_{\text{axiom}}$). Clause 4 is established.

*The four clauses are jointly forced by the Mutual Containment Capability, the Reciprocal Generation Capability, and the Containment-Generation Equivalence of [46], all derived from dx₄/dt = ic. The two channels are reciprocally generative under the McGucken Duality.* ∎

The First Law of the McGucken Dualities is the claim that the prior literature on dualities. Stone–von Neumann, Atiyah–Segal, Connes' spectral triples, Penrose–Witten twistor / amplituhedron, Maldacena AdS/CFT, T-duality, S-duality, mirror symmetry — was unable to articulate. This is the physics the prior literature could not see because none of those frameworks identified dx₄/dt = ic as the physical-geometric principle in both channels.

The First Law has direct empirical consequence: it predicts that **any physical phenomenon derivable through the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is also derivable through the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel, and vice versa.** This is the dual-channel overdetermination phenomenon of the 47-theorem architecture of [3]: every one of the 47 fundamental theorems of GR and QM has been derived through both channels independently, with no exceptions. The empirical signature of the First Law is therefore the dual-channel convergent-overdetermination of the experimental record — the same claimor that produces the $\geq 10^{141}$ Bayesian likelihood ratio in favor of the McGucken Principle (Theorem IX.26.11 of the present paper).

§IX.0 has established the McGucken Duality as the identity whereby every fundamental equation of foundational physics admits two and exactly two mathematically disjoint derivations from dx₄/dt = ic. **Theorem IX.0.B.2 (Empty cells would falsify the character of dx₄/dt = ic).** *Suppose for contradiction that dx₄/dt = ic generated content for some cells of $\mathcal M_{2 \times N}$ but not others. consider four failure modes:*

The position-of-i is what distinguishes the two encodings, and the moving character of the perpendicular dimension (the *dx₄/dt = ic* dynamics rather than the *x₄ = ict* static-coordinate content) is what supplies the boost-character signature (Theorem IX.13.14.7) of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's encoding and the wavefront-propagation signature of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's encoding. The uniformity across subjects is therefore the uniformity of perpendicularity-of-a-moving-dimension across physics. ∎

**Theorem IX.0.B.4 (Self-generation of the arena reinforces the 2×N completeness).** *The arena on which both channels operate for every subject — namely, the constraint surface $M_{1,3}$ where dx₄/dt = ic holds locally at every event — is self-generated by the principle (Theorem IX.22.6.C.6). Each cell of the 2×N matrix is therefore a derivation that runs on a self-generated arena. This is stronger than what general relativity alone supplies: in GR, the Einstein field equations operate on a manifold whose structure is independent of the equations; in the McGucken framework, dx₄/dt = ic is both the dynamical law and the constitutive law of the arena, with every point of the arena instantiating the principle locally (Definition IX.22.6.C.5).*

*The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel / the Geometric-Channel account of self-generation is that both channels operate on the same self-generated arena, each reading the arena's structure through its own lens. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's Lorentz group $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)$ is the isometry group of the self-generated Lorentzian metric; the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ at every event is the local instantiation of the principle as the x₄-expansion wavefront. Both channels see the same arena; they encode it differently. The 2×N matrix being fully populated is therefore about how the principle generates the very arena in which the derivations happen.*

*Proof.* I establish that the constraint surface $M_{1,3}$ is self-generated by dx₄/dt = ic, that both channels operate on this same self-generated arena, and that the strength of the McGucken framework over GR alone follows from the self-generation property.

*Step 1 (Constraint-surface self-generation of $M_{1,3}$).* By Theorem 2.4 of [70] and the constraint-surface construction of [70, §2] (also reproduced as Theorem IX.0.B.3 of the present paper), the constraint surface $M_{1,3}$ is the level set $\{(\mathbf x, t, x_4) : x_4 = ict\}$ inside the four-coordinate carrier $E_4 = \mathbb R^3 \times \mathbb C$. The level-set construction is uniquely determined by dx₄/dt = ic itself: integrating the principle along worldlines from any initial event $p_0$ produces $x_4 = ic\,t + \kappa$ (Convention $\kappa$ on the integration constant set to zero per Definition 1 of [1]), and the union of all such worldlines is $M_{1,3}$. The arena is therefore self-generated by the principle: there is no input beyond dx₄/dt = ic required to specify $M_{1,3}$ as the constraint surface. Every event $p \in M_{1,3}$ is a point at which dx₄/dt = ic holds locally (the self-generation property of Theorem IX.0.C.3). ✓

*Step 2 (The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel operates on the self-generated arena).* The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's operator algebra acts on the Hilbert space $\mathcal H \cong L^2(\Sigma, d^3\mathbf x)$ derived from the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing on $M_{1,3}$ amplitudes ([70, Theorem 6.1]; Theorem IV.6(ii) of the present paper). The Hilbert space is the Cauchy completion of complex-amplitude solutions of $\Box_M\psi = 0$ on $M_{1,3}$ (the self-generated arena). The operator algebra $B(\mathcal H)$ is the algebra of bounded linear maps on this Hilbert space. Both the Hilbert space and the operator algebra are therefore derived structures, with the arena being $M_{1,3}$ itself (self-generated by dx₄/dt = ic in Step 1). The Algebraic Channel's operator-algebra runs entirely on the self-generated arena. ✓

*Step 3 (The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel operates on the same self-generated arena).* The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's iterated Huygens-Sphere path integral (Theorem IX.10.1 the Universal Geometric Channel) operates on the iterated McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ at every event $p \in M_{1,3}$ ([3, §IV]). Each Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ is the local wavefront at retarded time $t - t_p$ from the event $p$, generated by the active expansion at rate $ic$ from $p$. The collection of Spheres $\{\Sigma_M^+(p) : p \in M_{1,3}\}$ is the geometry of dx₄/dt = ic at every event of the self-generated arena. The Geometric Channel's wavefront-propagation runs entirely on the same self-generated arena $M_{1,3}$. ✓

*Step 4 (strength over GR-alone via self-generation).* In general relativity, the Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4)T_{\mu\nu}$ operate on a Lorentzian manifold $(M, g)$ whose differential-geometric structure is *independent* of the equations: any smooth four-manifold with Lorentzian metric admits the operation of the Einstein equations as a constraint on the metric, with the manifold structure given as external input. In the McGucken framework, dx₄/dt = ic is both the dynamical law (the differential relation that the active expansion satisfies at every event) and the constitutive law of the arena (the principle that generates $M_{1,3}$ via the integrated-shadow constraint $x_4 = ict$). Every point of the arena instantiates dx₄/dt = ic locally (Definition IX.22.6.C.5; the self-generation property of Theorem IX.0.C.3). The McGucken framework is therefore stronger than GR alone: the arena and the dynamics are both generated by the same single physical principle, rather than the dynamics being imposed on an externally-specified arena. ✓

*Step 5 (2×N matrix fully populated on self-generated arena).* By Steps 2–3, both channels run on the same self-generated arena $M_{1,3}$. Each cell of the 2×N matrix of Theorem IX.0.B.1 is therefore a derivation that runs on a self-generated arena. The full population of the matrix (every (channel, subject) cell admitting a derivation from dx₄/dt = ic) is about how the principle generates the very arena in which the derivations happen — not just about which subjects admit dual-channel derivations. The self-generation property reinforces the 2×N completeness because it shows that the framework's foundational reach is total: the principle generates both the dynamics and the arena on which the dynamics operates, with every subject's derivations being instances of the same principle acting on its own self-generated content. ∎

**Theorem IX.0.B.5 (The dual-formulation pattern of the history of physics as the signature of the McGucken framework's character).** *The universal observation that every successful theory in the history of physics has admitted two dual formulations. Hamiltonian (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel precursor) versus Lagrangian (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel precursor) for classical mechanics (Lagrange 1788 / Hamilton 1833); Heisenberg picture versus Schrödinger picture for non-relativistic quantum mechanics (Heisenberg 1925 / Schrödinger 1926); canonical quantization versus path-integral quantization for quantum field theory (Schwinger / Tomonaga versus Feynman, equivalence proven by [Dyson 1949]); Einstein 1915's variational derivation versus [Jacobson 1995]'s thermodynamic derivation of general relativity; lattice formulation versus perturbative formulation of quantum chromodynamics; bulk gravitational physics versus boundary CFT in holographic duality ([Maldacena 1997; Witten 1998]) — is, in the McGucken framework, the fingerprint of physics descending from a principle with the position-of-i 2-fold structure.*

*The conventional historical account treats the universality of the dual-formulation pattern as a coincidence of mathematical sophistication: "physicists have, over two centuries, developed both formulations because both turned out to be useful." The McGucken-framework account is sharper: **the dual-formulation pattern is universal because physics descends from a principle whose derivational structure is inherently 2-fold**, with the two formulations being the two channel-readings of the same principle. Hamilton and Lagrange both succeeded because there was something 2-fold to find. Heisenberg and Schrödinger both succeeded for the same reason. Schwinger/Tomonaga and Feynman both succeeded; canonical-quantization and path-integral QFT both succeeded; Einstein 1915 and Jacobson 1995 both succeeded — every dual-formulation pair is a manifestation of the same underlying the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel / the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel architecture, with the architecture itself descending from dx₄/dt = ic via the position-of-i diagnosis.*

*Proof.* I establish the -signature claim by showing that each of the six historical dual-formulation pairs instantiates the (The Geometric Channel, the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel) structure via the position-of-i diagnosis, and that the universality of the pattern is forced by the 2-fold position-of-i structure of dx₄/dt = ic.

*Step 1 (Position-of-i diagnostic recapitulated).* By Theorems IX.13.14.2 and IX.13.14.3 of the present paper, every dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel object has $i$ *interior* to its algebraic definition (interior to the operator algebra, the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, the Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat H\psi$, the Stone-theorem unitary $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$), with $i$ functioning as the perpendicularity-marker for x₄'s orthogonality to the spatial three-slice. Every dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel object has $i$ *exterior* as a phase weight on real geometry (the Compton-phase weight $e^{i\omega_C\tau}$ on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront, the path-integral weight $\exp(iS/\hbar)$ on real spatial paths, the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ that exteriorizes the $i$ onto the coordinate axis), with the same $i$ as perpendicularity-marker. The two positions of $i$ — interior to the algebra vs exterior as a phase weight — are exhaustive and mutually exclusive: every theorem of foundational physics descended from dx₄/dt = ic is read through exactly one position-of-i. ✓

*Step 2 (Hamilton/Lagrange 1788–1833 instantiates (Geometric, Algebraic)).* Hamilton's 1833 formulation operates on phase space $(q, p)$ with the Hamiltonian operator on phase space and the algebraic structureY $\{q, p\} = 1$ — the algebraic-symmetry of the dual-formulation pair. *Step 3 (Heisenberg/Schrödinger 1925–26 instantiates (Algebraic, Geometric)).* Heisenberg's 1925 matrix mechanics operates on the operator algebra of matrix-valued observables the (dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel; Proposition IV.4 of the present paper). Schrödinger's 1926 wave mechanics operates on the configuration space $\mathbb R^3$ with wave equation $i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat H\psi$ the (dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel; Proposition IV.5). *Step 5 (Einstein 1915 / Jacobson 1995 instantiates (Algebraic, Geometric)).* Einstein's 1915 variational derivation of GR operates on the action functional $S_H = \int R\sqrt{-g}\,d^4x$ with Lovelock 1971 uniqueness fixing the form of $G_{\mu\nu}$ the (dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel: variational/operators). 't Hooft 1973's perturbative QCD formulation operates on the operator algebra of quark and gluon field operators with Feynman-diagram expansion the (dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel: operator-algebra). The universality of the pattern is *forced* by the 2-fold structure of dx₄/dt = ic itself: the principle's position-of-i admits exactly two encodings (interior to algebra, exterior as phase weight), and every theorem of foundational physics descended from dx₄/dt = ic is read through exactly one of these encodings. Heisenberg and Schrödinger both succeeded for the same reason. Schwinger/Tomonaga and Feynman both succeeded. Einstein and Jacobson both succeeded. Wilson and 't Hooft both succeeded. Maldacena and Witten both succeeded — every dual-formulation pair is a manifestation of the same underlying the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel / the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel architecture, with the architecture itself being a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic. ∎

**Theorem IX.0.B.6 (Distinction from alternative foundational proposals).** *The McGucken framework's property — generating two channels natively for every subject of physics, on an arena self-generated by the principle, with both channels descending from one principle and disjoint — distinguishes the framework from every prior foundational proposal in mathematical physics. Five alternative foundational proposals fail to exhibit the 2×N full-population property for distinct reasons (Table IX.0.B.A below).*

*Proof.* By examination of each foundational proposal against the five properties (The Algebraic Channel from upstream, the Geometric Channel from upstream, both from one principle, self-generated arena, disjoint channels).

*Mathematical foundationalism* (Russell–Whitehead *Principia Mathematica* 1910–1913, Hilbert's program 1899–1934): attempted to derive physics from logic and axioms. This program generates the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic-symmetry (formal-axiomatic structures can supply the operator-algebra of QM after appropriate axiomatization) but cannot generate the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometric-propagation from logic alone — the McGucken Sphere as the x₄-expansion wavefront is a *physical-geometric* object that requires a physical principle (dx₄/dt = ic) for its origin, not a logical axiom. The position-of-i is also absent: formal logic does not supply the perpendicularity-marker reading of i.

*Hilbert-space foundationalism* ([von Neumann 1932], [Mackey 1957], [Piron 1964], [Solèr 1995]): postulates the complex separable Hilbert space as the arena and derives the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's content from operator-algebraic axioms internal to the Hilbert space. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel has to be added separately: Feynman's 1948 path integral and the equivalence proof of [Dyson 1949] are required to glue the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel onto the Hilbert-space arena. The two channels are postulated separately and matched empirically.

*Operational foundationalism* ([Hardy 2001], [Chiribella–D'Ariano–Perinotti 2010s], [Masanes–Galley–Müller 2019]): postulates operational axioms about probability distributions and finite-parameter measurement structures, derives the complex Hilbert-space arena from these axioms. Generates the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's -operational content but blind to the geometric-propagation of perpendicularity: the McGucken Sphere has no operational counterpart in this program, and the wavefront-propagation account of perpendicularity is not articulated.

*Information-theoretic foundationalism* ([Wheeler 1989] "it from bit"; [Fuchs et al. 2010s] QBism; [Bell-Information-Reconstruction tradition 2000s]): postulates information-theoretic primitives (bits, correlations, agent degrees of belief) and derives the operational structure of QM from informational axioms. Blind to both encodings of perpendicularity: the algebraic encoding (i as perpendicularity-marker for x₄) is not articulated as physical perpendicularity, and the geometric encoding (the McGucken Sphere as x₄-wavefront) is not articulated at all.

*Holographic foundationalism* ([Maldacena 1997]; [Witten 1998]; [Susskind 1995]; [ER=EPR 2013]): postulates a bulk-boundary duality between gravitational physics in the bulk and conformal field theory on the boundary, with each side admitting independent development and the duality being matched calculationally. The bulk side is a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel-style geometric-propagation theory; the boundary side is a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel-style operator-algebra CFT. The two channels are present, but they are developed independently and matched via the duality dictionary rather than generated from a single principle. The principle whose 2-fold type would unify them in the McGucken-framework sense is absent.

*Stochastic-quantum foundationalism* ([Barandes 2023, 2024] stochastic-quantum correspondence): postulates a stochastic dynamics on a configuration space and derives QM as the stochastic-quantum correspondent. Generates a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel-style geometry (the stochastic process on configurations) but the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's operator-algebra is recovered through the correspondence rather than generated independently. The two channels are not generated by one principle; one is generated and the other recovered.

**Remark IX.0.B.7 (The one-sentence summary).** The 2×2 (or 2×N) structure tells us that physics is at root a theory of how a perpendicular *moving* fourth dimension relates to three spatial dimensions; that dx₄/dt = ic is that perpendicularity-of-a-moving-dimension made dynamical; that the principle's single i admits exactly two encodings (interior to operator algebra, exterior as geometric phase weight); that the moving character of the perpendicular dimension is what supplies the boost-character signature of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's encoding (Theorem IX.13.14.7) and the wavefront-propagation signature of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's encoding; that every subject of physics inherits both encodings because every subject is at root a theory of the same perpendicularity-of-a-moving-dimension; that the algebraic structureE is the principle's fingerprint; that the subject-uniformity is the principle's derivational reach; and that the 2×N matrix being fully populated is the test that the principle is foundational rather than merely sufficient. The framework's distinction from alternative foundational proposals is therefore one of type, not degree of mathematical sophistication: dx₄/dt = ic is the unique principle in foundational physics that generates two channels natively for every subject, on an arena self-generated by the principle, with both channels descending from one source.

*Proof of Theorem IX.0.B.6.* I establish the distinction by exhibition: for each of the six alternative foundational proposals catalogued above, I verify the failure mode on each of the five properties — (1) the Algebraic Channel from upstream, (2) the Geometric Channel from upstream, (3) both from one principle, (4) self-generated arena, (5) disjoint channels — with the failure modes summarised in Table IX.0.B.A.

*Step 1 (Mathematical foundationalism fails on properties 2 and 4).* Russell–Whitehead 1910–1913 *Principia Mathematica* and Hilbert's 1899–1934 axiomatic programme attempt to derive physics from logic and axioms. Formal-axiomatic structures supply the Algebraic Channel content (operator-algebraic axioms can be developed within set theory) but cannot supply the Geometric Channel content from logic alone: the McGucken Sphere as the x₄-expansion wavefront is a *physical-geometric* object that requires a physical principle (dx₄/dt = ic) for its origin, not a logical axiom. The arena is also postulated as the natural-number lattice plus set-theoretic operations. Failure on properties (2) and (4); the position-of-i is also absent because formal logic does not supply the perpendicularity-marker reading of i.

*Step 2 (Hilbert-space foundationalism fails on properties 3 and 4).* von Neumann 1932, Mackey 1957, Piron 1964, Solèr 1995 postulate the complex separable Hilbert space as the arena (not self-generated, failure on property 4) and derive the Algebraic Channel content from operator-algebraic axioms internal to the Hilbert space. The Geometric Channel must be added separately: Feynman's 1948 path integral and Dyson 1949's equivalence proof are required to glue the Geometric Channel onto the Hilbert-space arena. The two channels are therefore postulated separately and matched empirically rather than generated from one principle; failure on property (3).

*Step 3 (Operational foundationalism fails on properties 2, 3, and 4).* Hardy 2001, Chiribella–D'Ariano–Perinotti 2010s, Masanes–Galley–Müller 2019 postulate operational axioms about probability distributions and finite-parameter measurement structures. The Algebraic Channel content is reconstructed from operational axioms (passes property 1 with caveats); but the Geometric Channel has no operational counterpart in the programme — the McGucken Sphere is invisible to operational primitives, failure on property (2). Both channels are not from one principle (operational axioms supply only one channel), failure on property (3). The arena (the operational lattice) is postulated, failure on property (4).

*Step 4 (Information-theoretic foundationalism fails on properties 2, 3, and 4).* Wheeler 1989 "it from bit", Fuchs et al. 2010s QBism, the Bell-information-reconstruction tradition postulate information-theoretic primitives (bits, correlations, agent degrees of belief) and derive operational structure of QM from informational axioms. The programme is blind to both encodings of perpendicularity: the algebraic encoding (i as perpendicularity-marker for x₄) is not articulated as physical perpendicularity, and the geometric encoding (the McGucken Sphere as x₄-wavefront) is not articulated at all. Failure on properties (2), (3), and (4) simultaneously.

*Step 5 (Holographic foundationalism fails on properties 3, 4, and 5).* Maldacena 1997, Witten 1998, Susskind 1995, ER=EPR 2013 postulate a bulk-boundary duality. The bulk side supplies a Geometric Channel-style geometric-propagation theory; the boundary side supplies an Algebraic Channel-style operator-algebra CFT. Both channels are therefore present (passes properties 1 and 2). But the two channels are developed *independently* and matched via the duality dictionary rather than generated from a single physical principle (failure on property 3); the arena (AdS background) is postulated (failure on property 4); and the disjointness is only partial — the duality dictionary supplies a matching, not a derivational disjointness in the Definition IX.26.2 sense (failure on property 5).

*Step 6 (Stochastic-quantum foundationalism fails on properties 1 and 3).* Barandes 2023, 2024 postulates a stochastic dynamics on a configuration space (The Geometric Channel-style content) and derives QM as the stochastic-quantum correspondent. The Algebraic Channel content (operator algebra) is recovered through the correspondence rather than generated independently (partial failure on property 1: recovered via correspondence). The two channels are not generated by one principle (failure on property 3): one is generated, the other recovered.

*Step 7 (The McGucken framework passes all five properties).* By Theorem IX.18.2 (the source-pair $(\mathcal M_G, D_M)$ is co-generated by dx₄/dt = ic), property (3) holds: both channels descend from one principle. By Theorem IX.0.B.4 (Step 1 of its proof: constraint-surface self-generation of $M_{1,3}$), property (4) holds: the arena $M_{1,3}$ is self-generated by the principle. By Theorem IX.0.B.1 (the 2×N matrix's full population), both channels supply each subject's derivation from upstream physics, properties (1) and (2) hold. By Definition IX.26.2 (Dual-Channel Disjointness Predicate) and Theorem IX.26.3 (dual-channel disjointness across 47 theorems), property (5) holds: the two channels are disjoint in the formal sense. All five properties are jointly satisfied.

*Step 8 (Tabulation in Tables IX.0.B.A, IX.0.B.B, IX.0.B.C).* The -property comparison is summarised in Table IX.0.B.A (six proposals × five properties); the 2×N matrix's full population by the McGucken framework is summarised in Table IX.0.B.B (seven subjects × two channels with derivational machinery indicated); the position-of-i encoding across the matrix is summarised in Table IX.0.B.C (seven subjects × two encodings of perpendicularity). The three tables jointly establish the distinction: only the McGucken framework satisfies all five properties simultaneously.

*Conclusion.* By Steps 1–7, the McGucken framework's type — both channels supplied from upstream physics, both channels descending from one principle, arena self-generated by the principle, and derivational disjointness in the formal sense — is unique among foundational proposals in mathematical physics. The 2×N matrix being fully populated is the test that distinguishes a principle from a postulate that happens to be sufficient. ∎

The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel, the algebraic-symmetry, draws its tools from what mathematicians from the mid-nineteenth century onward have called *algebra* in the broadest sense:

Group theory and Lie theory enter here. Temporal uniformity is invariance under the time-translation group $(\mathbb R, +)$. Spatial homogeneity is invariance under the three-dimensional translation group $\mathbb R^{3}$. Spherical isotropy is invariance under the rotation group $SO(3)$. Lorentz covariance is invariance under $SO^{+}(1, 3)$, the group of proper orthochronous Lorentz transformations. Assembled together these form the Poincaré group $ISO(1, 3) = \mathbb R^{1,3} \rtimes SO^{+}(1, 3)$, the full symmetry group of Minkowski spacetime. Each of these groups is a Lie group, and each has an associated Lie algebra of infinitesimal generators whose commutation relations encode the algebraic structureQ of the group.

Complex algebra and Clifford algebra enter here. The perpendicularity marker i for x₄ is the defining element of the field of complex numbers ℂ, the algebraic object satisfying i² = −1. The Minkowski signature $(-, +, +, +)$ that descends, through the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic and its integrated form x₄ = ict, from Proposition II.1 is the real-form shadow of this complex structure. In the spin sector, i extends to the Clifford algebra $C\ell(1, 3)$, whose generators $\{\gamma^{\mu}\}$ satisfy $\{\gamma^{\mu}, \gamma^{\nu}\} = 2\eta^{\mu\nu}$; here the perpendicularity marker acquires a matrix-algebraic realization that carries through the Dirac equation into the fermionic matter (Proposition III.2).

Invariant theory and Noether's theorem enter here. The bridge from "invariance under a group action" to "conserved quantity under the dynamics" is Noether's 1918 theorem [Noether 1918], a result in the calculus of variations: if the action functional is invariant under a smooth one-parameter group, there exists a corresponding conserved Noether current. The ten conserved charges of the Poincaré group, the gauge charges of $U(1) \times SU(2)_{L} \times SU(3)_{c}$, and the covariantly-conserved stress-energy from diffeomorphism invariance are all instances of this one theorem applied to successively larger invariance groups.

**The common feature of all of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's tools is that they describe *sameness*:** what does not change, what transforms covariantly, what is preserved. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is algebra in the sense of Klein, Noether, Cartan, and the twentieth-century invariant-theoretic tradition.

The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel, the geometric-propagation, draws its tools from what mathematicians have called *geometry* and *analysis*:

Differential geometry and Lorentzian geometry enter here. The forward light cone at any event p is the set of future-directed null vectors $\{v \in T_{p}M : \eta(v, v) = 0, v^{0} > 0\}$ — a three-dimensional null hypersurface in four-dimensional spacetime, embedded as the boundary of the future causal cone $J^{+}(p)$. Its differential-geometric structure (null generators, affine parameter, orientation) is the subject of Lorentzian geometry in the tradition of Penrose, Hawking, and Ellis [Hawking–Ellis 1973].

Partial differential equations and Green's functions enter here. Huygens' wavefront propagation is the geometry of the retarded Green's function of the d'Alembertian,
$$G_{\text{ret}}(x, x') \;=\; \theta(t - t') \cdot \frac{\delta\big((t - t')^{2} - |x - x'|^{2}/c^{2}\big)}{2\pi}.$$
In four-dimensional spacetime (odd spatial dimension equal to three), the support of this Green's function is exactly the forward light cone — the strong Huygens principle holds. Every wavefront is a light cone, and every forward light cone is a wavefront; the distinction is nominal, not geometric.

Measure theory and dynamical-systems theory enter here. The monotonic arrow of time is a statement about a measure (Boltzmann–Gibbs phase-space volume, or equivalently the geometric-dispersal measure of x₄'s expansion) that increases monotonically along a flow. The Fokker–Planck description of the spatial random walk driven by x₄'s isotropic expansion (§III.2), the strict positivity dS/dt > 0 of the coarse-grained entropy for all $t > 0$ (Proposition III.7), and the identification of the Past Hypothesis as a theorem at the geometric origin of x₄'s advance (Theorem III.A) are all results in the measure-theoretic study of dispersive flows.

Topology and orientation enter here. The word *forward* in "forward light cone" presupposes a time-orientation — a continuous choice of the +-sheet of the null cone at every spacetime event. This is a topological statement about the existence of a global non-vanishing timelike vector field, equivalent to the triviality of a certain $\mathbb Z/2$-bundle over spacetime.

**The common feature of all of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's tools is that they describe *propagation* and *flow*:** where things go, how they spread, which way they advance. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is geometry and analysis in the sense of Riemann, Huygens, Poincaré, and the twentieth-century differential-geometric and PDE tradition.

## IX.0.C The Three Generation Properties of dx₄/dt = ic: Self-Generation, Co-Generation, Reciprocal Generation, and the Cross-Generation of Mathematics and Physics

The 2×N completeness established in §IX.0.B has a deeper source. The reason dx₄/dt = ic populates every (channel, subject) cell of the 2×N matrix, and the reason the populations are are organised by a single generative architecture — is that dx₄/dt = ic exhibits three distinct generation properties at the categorical primitive of the McGucken source-pair $(\mathcal M_{G}, D_{M})$: it is *self-generative*, *co-generative*, and *reciprocally generative*. These three properties, established in [7 = McGuckenReciprocalGeneration2026] as Theorems 22, 25, 27, and 41, supply the mechanism by which the 2×N matrix is fully populated. They also extend in a fourth, cross-cutting direction: the *cross-generation* of mathematics and physics, whereby the McGucken Pair $(\mathcal M_{G}, D_{M})$ as a mathematical object and the Lorentzian spacetime with its derived physical theorems mutually generate each other ad infinitum via the greater Huygens' Principle embodied in dx₄/dt = ic.

I now develop the four properties, with explicit identification of how each reinforces the 2×N completeness, how each connects to the position-of-i diagnosis of §IX.13.14, and how the four properties together establish the character of dx₄/dt = ic in a sense stronger than what alternative foundational proposals achieve.

**Definition IX.0.C.1 (The McGucken source-pair as the categorical primitive).** *The McGucken source-pair $(\mathcal M_{G}, D_{M})$ is the categorical primitive on which the McGucken Duality is exhibited (Definition IX.0.1) and on which the 2×N matrix is populated (Theorem IX.0.B.1). The pair has two faces:*

*(i) **The geometric face** $\mathcal M_{G}$: the McGucken source space, a real four-dimensional manifold with associated structure $(E_{4}, \Phi_{M}, D_{M}, \Sigma_{M})$ specified by [70, Theorem 2.4]. The geometric face is the carrier of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometric-propagation (the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ at every event $p \in \mathcal M_{G}$, the Huygens iteration, the iterated-Sphere path space, the Compton phase accumulation, the horizon-thermodynamic structures).*

*(ii) **The algebraic face** $D_{M}$: the McGucken Operator, the differential-operator specification of dx₄/dt = ic at each point of $\mathcal M_{G}$. The algebraic face is the carrier of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic-symmetry (the operator algebra, the unitary representations, the canonical commutation relations, the spectral decompositions, the Stone–von Neumann content).*

*The McGucken Duality (Definition IX.0.1) is the bidirectional Klein-correspondence account of the source-pair: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the geometry-generates-group direction $\mathrm{Klein\text{-}corresp}(\mathcal M_{G}, D_{M})$; the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is the group-generates-geometry direction $\mathrm{Klein\text{-}corresp}(D_{M}, \mathcal M_{G})$. The two channels are the two readings of the same source-pair, not two independent derivational pathways.*

**Theorem IX.0.C.2 (Co-Generation of $(\mathcal M_{G}, D_{M})$ by dx₄/dt = ic, after [70, Theorem 2.4]).** *The McGucken source-pair $(\mathcal M_{G}, D_{M})$ is co-generated by dx₄/dt = ic in the strict sense of [70, §10.2]: a single relation simultaneously generates both the geometric face $\mathcal M_{G}$ and the algebraic face $D_{M}$, with neither face foundationally prior to the other within the generation step. Specifically:*

*(i) The principle dx₄/dt = ic specifies the geometric face $\mathcal M_{G}$ as the constraint surface where dx₄/dt = ic holds locally at every event ($M_{1,3}$ as the integrated coordinate shadow of dx₄/dt = ic, with the spherically-symmetric x₄-expansion at velocity c being the algebraic structureQ of the principle at every event of $\mathcal M_{G}$).*

*(ii) The principle dx₄/dt = ic specifies the algebraic face $D_{M}$ as the differential-operator implementation of dx₄/dt = ic acting on functions over $\mathcal M_{G}$: $D_{M} = \partial/\partial t - ic\, \partial/\partial x_{4}$ (the differential identity that vanishes on solutions of dx₄/dt = ic), with the chain-rule identity $\partial/\partial t = ic\, \partial/\partial x_{4}$ on the constraint surface specifying how $D_{M}$ acts.*

*(iii) The two specifications are simultaneous and jointly forced: $\mathcal M_{G}$ is the manifold of points where $D_{M}$ acts; $D_{M}$ is the operator that specifies the algebraic structureQ of $\mathcal M_{G}$ at every point; neither is derivable from the other without invoking dx₄/dt = ic, and dx₄/dt = ic generates both.*

*Proof.* The constraint-surface construction of [70, §2] establishes that the integrated form $x_{4} = ict$ specifies a 3-dimensional submanifold of $E_{4} = \{(t, x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, x_{4})\}$ as the surface where dx₄/dt = ic holds, with the Lorentzian metric on this submanifold ($ds^{2} = dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} - c^{2}dt^{2}$) inherited from squaring the differential of x₄ = ict (Theorem IX.0.B.3). The operator $D_{M} = \partial/\partial t - ic\, \partial/\partial x_{4}$ vanishes identically on solutions of dx₄/dt = ic, and acts non-on functions over the constraint surface as the implementation of the principle as a differential equation. The space and the operator are therefore generated by the same single relation. Neither is derivable from the other without dx₄/dt = ic: the manifold without the operator is just a generic 4-manifold; the operator without the manifold is just a generic first-order differential expression. The pair is co-generated. ∎

**Theorem IX.0.C.3 (Self-Generation: every point of $\mathcal M_{G}$ is itself a generative operator, after [7, Theorem 22]).** *Every point $p \in \mathcal M_{G}$ is itself a generator of a local McGucken Operator $D_{M}^{(p)}$, the pointwise restriction of $D_{M}$ at $p$. The local operator $D_{M}^{(p)}$ specifies the algebraic structureQ of dx₄/dt = ic at the point $p$: the principle holds at $p$ with the spherically-symmetric x₄-expansion at velocity c emanating from $p$ as the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$. The self-generation is therefore not a metaphorical statement but a precise fact: the manifold $\mathcal M_{G}$ is constituted by points each of which is a local instance of the principle, with the local operator $D_{M}^{(p)}$ being the principle's expression at $p$.*

*Self-generation at the cellular level of the 2×N matrix.* The self-generative property extends to every cell $(C, S)$ of the 2×N matrix. The derivation of the fundamental theorems of subject $S$ through channel $C$ ultimately reduces to pointwise applications of dx₄/dt = ic at events of $\mathcal M_{G}$: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's operator-algebraic derivations act through the operator $D_{M}$ on the Hilbert space derived from amplitudes on $\mathcal M_{G}$, with the operator's local action at each point being $D_{M}^{(p)}$; the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometric-propagation derivations act through the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ at every point, with the Sphere being the local x₄-expansion at $p$. Every cell of the 2×N matrix is therefore populated by derivations that ultimately reduce to local pointwise instances of dx₄/dt = ic — the self-generative property *propagates* through the cascade and through the matrix.

*Comparison with general relativity.* In general relativity, the Einstein field equations operate on a manifold whose structure is independent of the equations: the manifold is the arena, and the equations are the dynamical law. The principle in the McGucken framework is stronger: dx₄/dt = ic is simultaneously the constitutive law of the arena (every point of $\mathcal M_{G}$ is a local instance of the principle) and the dynamical law on the arena. This is a foundational property no prior framework has supplied: von Neumann's Hilbert space is just an axiom (the arena postulated, with no derivation from upstream physics); Mackey's lattice is a restriction (the lattice axioms postulated); Hardy's operational axioms are external constraints on agents (the axioms postulated as operational principles); none of these has the self-generative character at the level.

*Proof.* From the constraint-surface construction (Theorem IX.0.C.2(i)), every point $p \in \mathcal M_{G}$ is a point at which dx₄/dt = ic holds. The pointwise restriction of $D_{M}$ at $p$ — call it $D_{M}^{(p)}$ — specifies the principle's algebraic structureQ at $p$: $D_{M}^{(p)}\psi(p) = (\partial_{t} - ic\, \partial_{x_{4}})\psi(p) = 0$ for solutions $\psi$ of dx₄/dt = ic. The local operator therefore *is* dx₄/dt = ic evaluated at $p$, because the operator's vanishing on solutions encodes the principle's algebraic structureQ. The pointwise generation of the local operator at every point of the manifold is the self-generative property. ∎

**Theorem IX.0.C.4 (Reciprocal Generation Property: the family of pointwise operators reciprocally generates the space, after [7, Theorems 25 and 27]).** *The family $\{D_{M}^{(p)} : p \in \mathcal M_{G}\}$ of pointwise McGucken Operators reciprocally generates the McGucken Space $\mathcal M_{G}$ as a whole. The reciprocal generation has three components:*

*(i) **Forward direction (point-to-operator).** Every point $p \in \mathcal M_{G}$ generates the local operator $D_{M}^{(p)}$ via the self-generative property of Theorem IX.0.C.3.*

*(ii) **Backward direction (operator-family-to-space).** The family $\{D_{M}^{(p)} : p \in \mathcal M_{G}\}$ of pointwise operators reciprocally generates the space $\mathcal M_{G}$: the manifold structure of $\mathcal M_{G}$ — its topology, its differential structure, its Lorentzian metric, its causal structure — is fully recoverable from the family of pointwise operators, with the metric reconstructible from the operator's principal-symbol structure, the causal structure from the operator's hyperbolicity, and the topology from the constraint surface where the operator vanishes on solutions ([7, Theorem 25] supplies the explicit reconstruction).*

*(iii) **Simultaneity and joint forcing.** The two generations (point-to-operator and operator-family-to-space) are simultaneous, reciprocal, and jointly forced by the single relation dx₄/dt = ic. Neither direction is derivationally prior to the other; both are facets of the single co-generative act of dx₄/dt = ic on the source-pair ([7, Theorem 27]).*

*The reciprocal generation property is the mechanism by which the 2×N matrix is organised: every cell of the matrix is a derivation through one channel of one subject, and every derivation acts on the source-pair through a combination of the forward direction (using local pointwise operators at every event) and the backward direction (using the operator-family structure to access the space's global content). The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel reads the source-pair through the operator-family structure (the algebra of $\{D_{M}^{(p)}\}$ acting on a Hilbert space derived from amplitudes on $\mathcal M_{G}$); the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel reads the source-pair through the manifold-and-Sphere structure (the geometry of $\mathcal M_{G}$ with the local McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ at every point). Both readings are valid because the reciprocal generation property establishes both directions of recovery between point and operator-family.*

*Proof.* I establish each of the three components (i)–(iii), anchored in the McGucken framework — the source-pair structure (Theorem IX.0.A.4), the pointwise operator $D_M^{(p)}$ (Theorem IX.0.C.3 self-generation), and the chain-rule identity $\partial_t = ic\,\partial_{x_4}$ inherited from dx₄/dt = ic.

*Step 1 (Verification of (i): forward direction, point-to-operator).* By Theorem IX.0.C.3 (Self-Generation Property), every point $p \in \mathcal M_G$ generates its local pointwise McGucken Operator $D_M^{(p)} = (\partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4})|_p$ via the local restriction of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic at $p$. The operator's defining content is the local chain-rule identity: $D_M^{(p)}\psi(p) = 0$ for any function $\psi$ that respects the McGucken Principle at $p$ (equivalently, any solution of $dx_4/dt = ic$ at $p$). The forward direction is therefore established by the self-generative content of Theorem IX.0.C.3: each point generates its own local operator. ✓

*Step 2 (Verification of (ii): backward direction, operator-family-to-space).* The family $\{D_M^{(p)} : p \in \mathcal M_G\}$ recovers the manifold structure of $\mathcal M_G$ through four reconstruction steps, each established at [7, Theorem 25] and reproduced here:

*(R-metric) Metric reconstruction.* The principal symbol $\sigma(D_M^{(p)}) = \tau + ic\,\xi_4$ at $p$ (with $\tau, \xi_4$ the cotangent coordinates dual to $t, x_4$) determines the local Lorentzian metric structure at $p$ via the squaring operation: $|\sigma(D_M^{(p)})|^2 = \tau^2 + c^2\xi_4^2 \to -c^2 dt^2 + c^2 dx_4^2$, giving the rank-2 Minkowski metric $g_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-1, +1, +1, +1)$ (Lemma IX.23.4) on the tangent space at $p$. Repeating at every event $p$ yields the global Lorentzian metric on $\mathcal M_G$.

*(R-causal) Causal structure reconstruction.* The hyperbolicity of $D_M^{(p)}$ — equivalently the indefinite-signature character of its principal symbol — determines the local null cone at $p$: vectors $v \in T_p\mathcal M_G$ satisfying $g(v, v) = 0$ are null, those with $g(v, v) < 0$ are timelike, those with $g(v, v) > 0$ are spacelike. The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ at retarded time $t - t_p$ is the spacelike-slice cross-section of the null cone at $p$, recovered as the geometry of the operator's hyperbolicity.

*(R-topology) Manifold topology reconstruction.* The operator-domain structure on the family $\{D_M^{(p)}\}$ supplies the manifold topology of $\mathcal M_G$: two points $p, q$ are close iff $D_M^{(p)}$ and $D_M^{(q)}$ act continuously on a common dense domain of smooth functions on a common neighborhood (the standard differential-operator topology, Hörmander 1983 Vol. I).

*(R-constraint) Constraint-surface reconstruction.* The zero set $\{(p, \psi_p) : D_M^{(p)}\psi_p = 0\}$ specifies the constraint surface on which the McGucken Principle holds at every event. By Theorem IX.0.B.3, this constraint surface is identified with $\mathcal M_G$ via the integrated-shadow embedding $x_4 = ict$.

The four reconstructions (R-metric), (R-causal), (R-topology), (R-constraint) together recover the manifold $\mathcal M_G$ from the operator family $\{D_M^{(p)}\}$, with no additional input beyond the dx₄/dt = ic structure of the pointwise operators. ✓

*Step 3 (Verification of (iii): simultaneity and joint forcing).* By Theorem IX.0.A.4 (Reciprocal Generation Property at the source-pair level), the manifold $\mathcal M_G$ and the operator $D_M$ are co-generated by dx₄/dt = ic via the single integration with Convention $\kappa$ (Step 1 of Theorem IX.0.A.4): fixing an initial event $p_0$ and integrating dx₄/dt = ic along worldlines emanating from $p_0$ produces the manifold $\mathcal M_G$ and adjoins the operator $D_M$ as the differential structure simultaneously. Neither face is foundationally prior; both are facets of the single co-generative act. The pointwise version of this — that at every event $p \in \mathcal M_G$, the local operator $D_M^{(p)}$ and the local manifold-neighborhood at $p$ are co-generated by the local restriction of dx₄/dt = ic — is the per-event instantiation of the source-pair co-generation, with the family of pointwise instantiations giving the global manifold-operator-family pair. The simultaneity is : the integration of dx₄/dt = ic at $p$ produces both the local operators and the local manifold-neighborhood content in one step. ✓

*Step 4 (Conclusion: the reciprocal generation is jointly forced by dx₄/dt = ic).* By Steps 1–3, the forward direction (Step 1, point-to-operator via Theorem IX.0.C.3), the backward direction (Step 2, operator-family-to-space via the four reconstructions), and the simultaneity (Step 3, joint forcing by the integration of dx₄/dt = ic at every event) are jointly established. The family $\{D_M^{(p)} : p \in \mathcal M_G\}$ reciprocally generates the McGucken Space $\mathcal M_G$ via the single relation dx₄/dt = ic. ∎

**Theorem IX.0.C.5 (Huygens-Equals-Reciprocal-Generation Identity, after [7, Theorem 41]).** *The Reciprocal Generation Property of $(\mathcal M_{G}, D_{M})$ is identical to Huygens' 1690 Principle. Huygens' Principle states that every point on an advancing wavefront is itself a source of secondary spherical wavelets, with the envelope of the secondary wavelets being the next advancing wavefront. the claim has five clauses:*

*(H1) **Geometry.** Every point on the wavefront is a source of a secondary spherical wavelet — equivalently, every point $p \in \mathcal M_{G}$ supports a McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ emanating from it as the local x₄-expansion.*

*(H2) **Operator content.** The advancing wavefront is the envelope of the secondary wavelets — equivalently, the family $\{D_{M}^{(p)}\}$ of pointwise operators generates the global manifold structure of $\mathcal M_{G}$, with the wavefront-envelope content corresponding to the operator-family-to-space generation.*

*(H3) **Equivalence to the Kirchhoff integral.** The mathematics of Huygens' Principle is expressed by the Kirchhoff integral formula for the wave-equation Green's function in 4-dimensional spacetime (odd spatial dimension 3 supports the strong Huygens principle), with the integral kernel being supported exactly on the forward light cone — the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$.*

*(H4) **Elevation from heuristic to theorem.** The reciprocal generation property elevates Huygens' Principle from a heuristic construction (Huygens 1690 framed it as a construction technique for advancing wavefronts) to a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic: every point of $\mathcal M_{G}$ is a generative operator, and the family of pointwise operators generates the space, with both directions descending from the single physical principle dx₄/dt = ic.*

## IX.0.D The Containment-Generation Equivalence Keystone: The Categorical Identity of Being and Becoming, and the Reading of the Equals Sign in dx₄/dt = ic

§IX.0.C established the four generation properties (self-generation, co-generation, reciprocal generation, cross-generation) as the mechanism by which the 2×N matrix is forced to be fully populated. The McGucken Category $\text{McG}_{6}$ paper [76] sharpens this analysis at the categorical level: the three categorical theorems characterizing $\text{McG}_{6}$. The Mutual Containment Capability (Generalized Mutual Containment), the Reciprocal Generation Capability (Reciprocal Generation Capability), the Containment-Generation Equivalence (Containment-Generation Equivalence) — together establish that the equality sign in dx₄/dt = ic is a *identity*, not a contingent equation between *being* (the invariant content ic on the right-hand side) and *becoming* (the differential content dx₄/dt on the left-hand side). This identity lifts at the categorical level to the biconditional the Containment-Generation Equivalence: the Mutual Containment Capability ⇔ the Reciprocal Generation Capability, with mutual containment (the being aspect of each member of $\text{McG}_{6}$) being equivalent to reciprocal generation (the becoming aspect of each member). The **the Containment-Generation Equivalence keystone** is the McGucken framework: the "=" of the axiom IS the "⇔" of the Containment-Generation Equivalence at the categorical level, with the being-becoming duality propagating through every level of organization in a self-similar fashion. This subsection develops the keystone content, with explicit identification of how the keystone broadens and deepens §IX.0.C's four generation properties through the categorical-equivalence reading.

I formalise this through eight numbered statements (Theorem IX.0.D.1 through Remark IX.0.D.8), with two detailed left-justified 10pt tables (Tables IX.0.D.A and IX.0.D.B) summarizing respectively the four-level self-similar structure of the being-becoming identity and the guarantees the Containment-Generation Equivalence supplies. The §IX.21 treatment of $\text{McG}_{6}$ remains the central rigorous treatment of the six-object category; the present subsection develops the philosophy of the keystone in the context of the 2×N matrix (§IX.0.B) and the four generation properties (§IX.0.C).

**Theorem IX.0.D.1 (The being-becoming algebraic structureU of the axiom dx₄/dt = ic, after [76, §5.1]).** *The McGucken axiom $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ has, at the level of its symbol-structure, two halves separated by an equation sign, each carrying a distinct content:*

*(i) **The left-hand side $dx_{4}/dt$**: the differential expression — the rate of change, the active mathematics. This is the **becoming aspect** of the axiom: $dx_{4}/dt$ tells us how something is changing, what flow is occurring, what the dynamics is. The left-hand side is therefore the algebraic representative of *change*, *flow*, *advance*, *generation*.*

*(ii) **The right-hand side $ic$**: the invariant expression — the fixed value, the definite mathematical object. This is the **being aspect** of the axiom: $ic$ tells us what something *is*, what the static value of the rate is, what invariant the dynamics equals. The right-hand side is therefore the algebraic representative of *invariance*, *fixed-value*, *what-is-the-case*.*

*(iii) **The equation sign $=$**: not a contingent equation but a identity. The equation sign asserts that the becoming aspect (the differential $dx_{4}/dt$) and the being aspect (the invariant $ic$) are *the same claim*: $dx_{4}/dt$ IS $ic$. The becoming is the being. The axiom is therefore a identity statement, not a derivation or a conditional or a relation between two distinct quantities. The two halves of the axiom are two ways of saying the same thing: that the rate of x₄-advance equals the invariant $ic$, where the rate IS the invariant, and the invariant IS the rate.*

*The being-becoming algebraic structureU of the axiom is the symbol-level expression of the deeper Algebraic structureI that will be lifted at the McGucken Category level (Theorem IX.0.D.2): the static face of the principle (what each member of $\text{McG}_{6}$ is, the being aspect) and the dynamic face (what each member does, the becoming aspect) are bound by the Containment-Generation Equivalence as the same claim at the categorical level, exactly as the two halves of the axiom are bound by the equation sign at the symbol level.*

*Proof.* Inspection of the symbol structure of $dx_{4}/dt = ic$. The left-hand side $dx_{4}/dt$ is a differential, expressing rate-of-change content of $x_{4}$ with respect to $t$; the right-hand side $ic$ is an invariant complex number $i \cdot c$ where $i$ is the imaginary unit and $c$ is the speed of light. The equation sign asserts equality of the two quantities. The identity reading is supplied by that the equation is the axiom of the framework, standing at the level below which no more fundamental statement exists: it is therefore the constitutive statement of the framework, with the equality sign carrying the identity that the two halves are two faces of one principle. The being-becoming algebraic structureU is therefore the symbol-level expression of the identity of the axiom. ∎

**Theorem IX.0.D.2 (The categorical lifting: the Containment-Generation Equivalence as the keystone biconditional the Mutual Containment Capability ⇔ the Reciprocal Generation Capability, after [76, §5.1] and [76, Theorem 4.3]).** *The three categorical theorems characterizing $\text{McG}_{6}$ (the McGucken six-object category established at §IX.21) lift the being-becoming algebraic structureU of the axiom to the categorical level:*

*(i) **the Mutual Containment Capability. Generalized Mutual Containment** (Theorem IX.21.2 of the present paper, from [76, §4.1]). The Mutual Containment Capability asserts that every object $X \in F_{M}$ (the McGucken source-tuple) contains the axiom $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ in full, with a canonical extraction procedure $\Pi_{X}$ recovering the axiom from $X$. The Mutual Containment Capability is **unary**: it is a containment-bearing property of each individual object, expressing what each member of $\text{McG}_{6}$ *is*. The Mutual Containment Capability is therefore the **being aspect at the categorical level** — the categorical statement of the static, axiom-containment content of each member.*

*(ii) **the Reciprocal Generation Capability. Reciprocal Generation Capability** (Theorem IX.21.3 of the present paper, from [76, §4.2]). The Reciprocal Generation Capability asserts that for every ordered pair $(X, Y) \in F_{M} \times F_{M}$ with $X \neq Y$, there exists a canonical generation procedure $\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_{Y} \circ \Pi_{X}$ taking the axiom-content of $X$ to the $Y$. The Reciprocal Generation Capability is **binary**: it is a generation-bearing property of each ordered pair of objects, expressing what each member of $\text{McG}_{6}$ *does* to every other. The Reciprocal Generation Capability is therefore the **becoming aspect at the categorical level** — the categorical statement of the dynamic, generative content of each member.*

*(iii) **the Containment-Generation Equivalence. Containment-Generation Equivalence** (Theorem IX.21.4 of the present paper, from [76, §4.3]). The Containment-Generation Equivalence asserts the biconditional*

$$\forall X \in F_{M}: \quad \big[X \text{ contains } dx_{4}/dt = ic \text{ in full}\big] \;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\; \big[X \text{ generates every other member of } F_{M}\big]$$

*— equivalently, the Mutual Containment Capability ⇔ the Reciprocal Generation Capability. The Containment-Generation Equivalence binds the being aspect (the Mutual Containment Capability: each member contains the axiom) to the becoming aspect (the Reciprocal Generation Capability: each member generates the others), establishing them as the same claim. The Containment-Generation Equivalence is therefore the **categorical identity of being and becoming** — the categorical-level analogue of the equation sign in the axiom.*

*The identity statement is: the "=" of the axiom $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ and the "⇔" of the Containment-Generation Equivalence: the Mutual Containment Capability ⇔ the Reciprocal Generation Capability are the **same identity** at two levels — symbol level and categorical level. At the symbol level, the equation sign asserts that the differential (becoming) and the invariant (being) are the same claim. At the categorical level, the Containment-Generation Equivalence asserts that mutual containment (being) and reciprocal generation (becoming) are the same claim. The two-level statement of identity is the central content of the keystone.*

*Proof.* By [76, Theorem 4.3] and the corresponding Theorem IX.21.4 of the present paper, the Containment-Generation Equivalence is established as a theorem of $\text{McG}_{6}$ with explicit forward and backward implications: the Mutual Containment Capability ⇒ the Reciprocal Generation Capability (if every object contains the axiom in full, then every object generates every other via the canonical generation procedure $\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_{Y} \circ \Pi_{X}$), and the Reciprocal Generation Capability ⇒ the Mutual Containment Capability (if every ordered pair admits a canonical generation procedure, then every object contains the axiom-content from which the generation procedures extract). The biconditional is therefore established as a categorical theorem. The identity reading of the Containment-Generation Equivalence as the categorical analogue of the axiom's equation sign is [76, §5.1]: the two halves of the axiom (differential and invariant) are bound by "=" as the same claim; the two aspects of $\text{McG}_{6}$ (the Mutual Containment Capability as containment, the Reciprocal Generation Capability as generation) are bound by "⇔" as the same claim; the two binding relations ("=" and "⇔") are the same identity at different levels of articulation. ∎

**Theorem IX.0.D.3 (Why the Containment-Generation Equivalence is the keystone. The Mutual Containment Capability alone is inert, the Reciprocal Generation Capability alone is ad hoc, after [76, §5.2]).** *the Containment-Generation Equivalence is the **keystone** of the McGucken Category $\text{McG}_{6}$, not the Mutual Containment Capability alone or the Reciprocal Generation Capability alone, because either property taken alone yields a weaker framework that fails to deliver the foundations of the McGucken Duality:*

*(i) **the Mutual Containment Capability alone is inert.** If we assert only that each member of $F_{M}$ contains the axiom $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ in full — without asserting that the containment has generative consequences — the containment could be *inert*. The axiom-content sits inside each member as a recoverable substructure, but the members might not be related to one another in any generative way. The framework would be a collection of axiom-bearing objects without the interconnection that makes the source-tuple a category in the sense.*

*(ii) **the Reciprocal Generation Capability alone is ad hoc.** If we assert only that each ordered pair of objects admits a generation procedure — without asserting that the generation is grounded in the axiom-content of the source object — the generation could be *ad hoc*. The generation procedures would exist as functorial mappings between objects but would not have a source: they would be relations that happen to exist among the objects, without the principled source that makes them theorems of the axiom rather than independent postulates.*

*(iii) **the Containment-Generation Equivalence asserts that containment and generation are the same claim**, so that:*

*- Containment is not inert (every containment of the axiom generates the others, by the Reciprocal Generation Capability part of the Containment-Generation Equivalence).*

*- Generation is not ad hoc (every generation procedure is grounded in axiom-containment, by the Mutual Containment Capability part of the Containment-Generation Equivalence).*

*- The framework cannot be one without the other: weakening to the Mutual Containment Capability alone breaks the generation aspect; weakening to the Reciprocal Generation Capability alone breaks the containment aspect; both are forced jointly by the Containment-Generation Equivalence.*

*The keystone reading is therefore: the Containment-Generation Equivalence is the rigidity of the framework. Removing the Containment-Generation Equivalence would leave the framework with either inert containment or ad hoc generation, neither of which would supply the character that the McGucken framework requires.*

*Proof.* Direct from the definitions of the Mutual Containment Capability and the Reciprocal Generation Capability and the biconditional content of the Containment-Generation Equivalence. The -rigidity content is established at [76, §5.2 and §5.4] and at the present paper's §IX.21 (the central rigorous treatment of $\text{McG}_{6}$). The keystone reading is consistent with the standard -engineering vocabulary of "keystone": the -essential element whose removal breaks the integrity of the whole. The Containment-Generation Equivalence is the keystone of $\text{McG}_{6}$ in this sense — without it, the framework's integrity is broken at either the containment or the generation aspect. ∎

**Theorem IX.0.D.4 (Self-similar structure: the being-becoming identity propagates across four levels of organization, after [76, §5.3]).** *The McGucken framework exhibits the same becoming-equals-being identity at four levels of organization, with the identity being the same at every level but the articulation being level-specific:*

*(i) **Level 1. The axiom level.** Becoming aspect: $dx_{4}/dt$ (the differential). Being aspect: $ic$ (the invariant). Identity that binds them: "=" (the equation sign). The axiom-level statement is Theorem IX.0.D.1.*

*(ii) **Level 2. The category $\text{McG}_{6}$ level.** Becoming aspect: the Reciprocal Generation Capability (generation among objects). Being aspect: the Mutual Containment Capability (containment of the axiom in each object). Identity that binds them: the Containment-Generation Equivalence (the biconditional the Mutual Containment Capability ⇔ the Reciprocal Generation Capability). The category-level statement is Theorem IX.0.D.2.*

*(iii) **Level 3. The McGucken Sphere level.** Becoming aspect: Sphere-generation at every point (every point $p \in \mathcal M_{G}$ emits the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ as the local x₄-expansion wavefront). Being aspect: axiom-containment at every point (every point $p$ instantiates dx₄/dt = ic locally via the pointwise restriction $D_{M}^{(p)}$). Identity that binds them: the recursive structure of the atom — the Sphere is generated by the point because the point contains the axiom, and the point contains the axiom because it generates the Sphere. The Sphere-level statement is the Huygens-Equals-Reciprocal-Generation Identity of Theorem IX.0.C.5.*

*(iv) **Level 4. The Σ_M-descent level.** Becoming aspect: the descent chain Sphere → CP³ (Penrose twistor space) → Z_a (momentum twistors) → G_+(k,n) (positive Grassmannian) → 𝒜_{n,k} (amplituhedron) → loop amplituhedron → Feynman diagrams (each stage generates the next). Being aspect: each stage contains $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ in full (each stage admits the canonical extraction $\Pi_{X}$ recovering the axiom). Identity that binds them: Theorems 6–23 of [76] (the explicit Σ_M-descent theorems). The descent-level statement is the categorical equivalence of the six descents.*

*The self-similar structure is therefore not a metaphor but a : the same becoming-equals-being identity is realized at four levels of organization, with each level being a distinct expression of the same identity. The four-level self-similar structure is summarized in Table IX.0.D.A.*

*Proof of Theorem IX.0.D.4.* *Proof.* I verify the same becoming-equals-being identity at each of the four levels of organization, with each verification establishing the level-specific binding relation.

*Level 1 verification (axiom-level identity).* By Theorem IX.0.D.1, the axiom $dx_4/dt = ic$ has the becoming aspect $dx_4/dt$ (differential, rate-of-change) and the being aspect $ic$ (invariant complex value), with the equation sign "=" binding them as the same claim. The Level 1 identity is established by symbol-level inspection of the axiom. ✓

*Level 2 verification (categorical-level identity).* By Theorem IX.0.D.2, the McGucken Category $\text{McG}_6$ has the becoming aspect (the Reciprocal Generation Capability: every ordered pair $X, Y \in F_M$ admits a canonical generation procedure $\Gamma_{X \to Y}$) and the being aspect (the Mutual Containment Capability: every $X \in F_M$ contains $dx_4/dt = ic$ in full with canonical extraction $\Pi_X$), with the Containment-Generation Equivalence binding them as the biconditional the Mutual Containment Capability ⇔ the Reciprocal Generation Capability ([76, Theorem 4.3]). The Level 2 identity is established as a categorical theorem of $\text{McG}_6$. ✓

*Level 3 verification (Sphere-level identity).* By Theorem IX.0.C.5 (Huygens-Equals-Reciprocal-Generation Identity), the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ at every event $p \in \mathcal M_G$ has the becoming aspect (Sphere-generation at $p$: the active expansion at rate $ic$ generates the local Sphere as wavefront emanating from $p$) and the being aspect (axiom-containment at $p$: every point $p$ instantiates dx₄/dt = ic locally via the pointwise restriction $D_M^{(p)}$). The binding relation is the recursive structure of the atom: the Sphere is generated by the point because the point contains the axiom, and the point contains the axiom because it generates the Sphere — a closed loop establishing the two aspects as the same claim. The Level 3 identity is established by the Huygens-Reciprocal-Generation identity. ✓

*Level 4 verification ($\Sigma_M$-descent-level identity).* By [76, Theorems 6–23], the $\Sigma_M$-descent operates through six descent stages — $\Sigma_M$ → $\mathbb{CP}^3$ (Penrose twistor space) → $Z_a$ (momentum twistors) → $G_+(k,n)$ (positive Grassmannian) → $\mathcal A_{n,k}$ (amplituhedron) → loop amplituhedron → Feynman diagrams as canonical forms on positive geometries. The becoming aspect (each stage generates the next via explicit functors and natural isomorphisms) and the being aspect (each stage contains $dx_4/dt = ic$ in full via canonical extraction $\Pi_X$) are bound by the categorical-equivalence theorems of the descent. The categorical-equivalence content is mathematical-rigorous (not analogous): the six descent stages are categorically equivalent under explicit functorial mappings, with the binding relation being the categorical-equivalence-of-stages content of [76, Theorems 6–23]. The Level 4 identity is established by the categorical-equivalence of the $\Sigma_M$-descent. ✓

*Self-similar structure.* Levels 1–4 each instantiate the same identity (becoming = being) at four distinct organizational levels, with the binding relations being level-specific articulations of the same identity: symbol-level (equation sign), categorical-level (the Containment-Generation Equivalence), Sphere-level (recursive structure of the atom), descent-level (categorical equivalence). The self-similarity is mathematical, not metaphorical: the same identity is realized at every level by a level-specific binding relation that establishes the becoming and being aspects as the same claim within that level's vocabulary. ∎

**Theorem IX.0.D.5 (Five guarantees from the Containment-Generation Equivalence, after [76, §5.4]).** *The keystone the Containment-Generation Equivalence supplies five physical guarantees, each of which has mathematical consequences for the McGucken framework:*

*(G1) **Codiscrete groupoid structure on the 30 generation procedures.** The 30 generation procedures $\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_{Y} \circ \Pi_{X}$ on the six objects of $F_{M}$ (there are $6 \times 5 = 30$ ordered pairs $X \neq Y$) form a codiscrete groupoid: every ordered pair admits exactly one canonical generation procedure, and the procedures compose consistently. Corollary 5.15 of [76]; cf. Theorem IX.21.4 of the present paper.*

*(G2) **Path-Independence Theorem.** Any two generation routes in the network of 30 procedures, connecting the same pair of objects through different intermediates, produce equivalent generations. Theorem 5.14 of [76]; this is the categorical analogue of the Stokes-theorem path-independence of conservative vector fields.*

*(G3) **Initial-object status in the Physical Foundations category.** The McGucken source-tuple $F_{M}$ is initial in the Physical Foundations category, the category of six-object physical foundations satisfying the Containment-Generation Equivalence-type conditions. Theorem 7.27 of [76]. Initiality means every the Containment-Generation Equivalence-bearing six-object physical foundation admits a unique morphism FROM $F_{M}$: $F_{M}$ is the source of which other the Containment-Generation Equivalence-bearing foundations are downstream specializations.*

*(G4) **Terminal-object status in the Physical Foundations category^prim.** $F_{M}$ is terminal in the Physical Foundations category^prim, the category of six-object primitive foundations. Main Theorem of [76, §7]. Terminality means every six-object primitive physical foundation admits a unique morphism INTO $F_{M}$: $F_{M}$ is the target of which other primitive foundations are upstream generators.*

*(G5) **Non-fragmentability of the framework.** Removing any object from $F_{M}$ breaks the Reciprocal Generation Capability (the removed object cannot be generated by the others, so generation is incomplete); by the Containment-Generation Equivalence, this breaks the Mutual Containment Capability (containment of the axiom is incomplete, since one container is missing); by Theorem 5.7 of [76], the framework is forced to re-include the removed object to restore both properties. The framework is therefore non-fragmentable in the sense: any attempt to weaken it by removing an object collapses back to the full six-object structure.*

*Together, the five guarantees establish that $\text{McG}_{6}$ has the type of an initial-and-terminal six-object category in the Physical Foundations category universe, with rigidity (non-fragmentability) and path-independent generation as physical mathematical consequences of the Containment-Generation Equivalence. The five guarantees are summarized in Table IX.0.D.B.*
