Both produce the same entropy $S_{BH} = k_B A/(4\ell_p^2)$, and the cross-channel agreement is the overdetermination content of the McGucken Duality at the gravitational tier (Theorem IX.15.5 Signature-Bridging Theorem of the present paper). The QM analogue is the agreement between (i) the Heisenberg-picture canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ in its Lorentzian form, (ii) its transformed-A2 counterpart in the Euclidean Heisenberg group $[\hat q, \hat p_E] = \hbar$, and (iii) the Feynman path-integral derivation in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel; the three readings agree on the underlying commutator structure with appropriate signature conventions, and the agreement is the overdetermination content of the McGucken Duality at the quantum-mechanical tier (Theorem IX.15.7 Heisenberg–Feynman Equivalence of the present paper).*

**Remark IX.13.23 (reconciliation with the channels-are-connected-by-the-rotation framing of §IX.10).** *The differential-response framing of §IX.13.13. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is destroyed by the rotation, the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is transported by it — might appear to contradict the Universal the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Theorem of §IX.10 and the bi-conditional diagnostic of §IX.12, both of which state that dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel are connected by the McGucken-Wick rotation. The two framings are complementary, not contradictory, and address different levels of the McGucken Duality:*

*(i) **Origin level (§§IX.10, IX.12).** At the level of derivation, both channels descend from the same physical principle dx₄/dt = ic, and the McGucken-Wick rotation τ = x₄/c is internal to the principle — it is the coordinate identification on the real four-manifold $\mathcal M_G$ that bridges the two signature-readings of the same active expansion. At this level, the channels are connected by the rotation, with the connection being the source-pair $(\mathcal M_G, D_M)$ co-generated by dx₄/dt = ic.*

*(ii) **Response level (§IX.13.13).** At the level of transformation behaviour, the channels respond asymmetrically to the McGucken-Wick rotation. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is destroyed at its signature-specific content; the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is transported with its geometric-propagation preserved. At this level, the rotation acts as a diagnostic applied to each channel separately, not as a transformation that carries the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel into the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel.*

*Both framings are correct, and both are required for a complete account of the dual-channel architecture. The origin-level framing identifies dx₄/dt = ic as the common source of both channels and the McGucken-Wick rotation as the coordinate-identification bridge between them. The response-level framing establishes that the two channels remain disjoint derivations of the same equation, with the overdetermination content of the McGucken Duality (Heisenberg–Feynman equivalence, Hilbert–Jacobson agreement, particle-level/horizon-level Second-Law agreement) preserved because the channels are not collapsible to one derivation in two notations. The McGucken-Wick rotation is therefore both* the bridge between the two signature-readings of the same principle *(origin level) and* the diagnostic test that confirms the two channels are disjoint *(response level). The dual role of the rotation, as bridge and as diagnostic, is itself a feature of the McGucken framework that the orthodox treatment of Wick rotation as a formal device cannot accommodate.*

#### IX.13.13.4 Reading: The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel / the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Distinction Is the Descartes Algebra/Geometry Split

The differential-response framing of §§IX.13.13.1–IX.13.13.3 admits a deeper reading that consolidates the entire dual-channel architecture into a single mathematical-historical-physical statement. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel / the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel distinction is,, the **Descartes split of 1637** — the unification-via-distinction between *algebra* (the symbolic-equational mathematics of components on coordinate axes) and *geometry* (the shape-based mathematics of forms invariant under coordinate transformations) — read at the level of physics rather than mathematical description. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic admits two readings because Descartes' analytic geometry recognized that algebra and geometry are two faces of the *same* mathematics; the McGucken framework recognizes that they are also two faces of the same *physical* content when dx₄/dt = ic supplies the geometric primitive on which both readings operate.

I develop this in three identifications: the channel distinction is the Descartes split (§IX.13.13.4.A); the Wick rotation tests which side of the split a derivation operates on (§IX.13.13.4.B); the channel distinction is therefore physical, historical, and mathematical simultaneously, structured as one consequence with three faces (§IX.13.13.4.C).

##### IX.13.13.4.A The Channel Distinction as the Algebra/Geometry Split

**Theorem IX.13.24 (The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel / the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel distinction as the Descartes algebra/geometry split).** *The McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel and the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel distinguish the algebraic and geometric readings of dx₄/dt = ic in the sense of Descartes' 1637 analytic-geometry unification:*

*(i) **The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the algebraic reading.** the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel operates on the symbolic-equational face of physics: components on Cartesian axes with specific signature labels, operators acting on Hilbert-space vectors with imaginary commutators, symmetry-group representations acting on tensor and spinor components. Each content of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is articulated in coordinates: the Lorentz signature $\eta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-, +, +, +)$ is signature labels on Cartesian axes; the master equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ is a Cartesian-component identity; the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ is an algebraic identity on Cartesian configuration-momentum operators; the unitary representation $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$ is an exponential of an operator in a Cartesian Hilbert-space basis; Stone's theorem, Wigner classification, Stone–von Neumann uniqueness are theorems about operators on Hilbert spaces whose Cartesian-basis representations are the central objects of study. The position of i in the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is interior to the algebraic structure (Proposition IX.12.1) — it sits inside the operator, inside the commutator, inside the signature label, as the algebraic record of x₄'s perpendicularity to the spatial axes.*

*(ii) **The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is the geometric account.** the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel operates on the shape-based face of physics: the McGucken Sphere as a real geometric object whose definition is invariant under rotations and signature changes, the wavefront propagation on iterated Spheres as a foliation-independent geometric flow, the horizon area as a coordinate-invariant scalar, the Clausius integration on local Rindler horizons as a thermodynamic-geometric identity. Each content of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is articulated as shape: the Sphere is a Sphere in both signatures; the area law $S = k_B A/(4\ell_p^2)$ is signature-invariant; the Compton-coupling rate $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ on x₄ is an oscillation-frequency on a geometric axis; the path-integral weight $\exp(iS/\hbar)$ has it in the action S (a geometric-Lagrangian integral over a path) with the i exteriorisable to the coordinate axis (Proposition IX.12.2). The position of i in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is exteriorisable from the geometric structure — the shape persists when the i moves to the coordinate.*

*(iii) **The Wick rotation is the test for which side of the split.** The McGucken-Wick rotation τ = x₄/c is a signature change on the four-coordinate ambient space. Algebra (components on signature-bearing axes) is destroyed by the signature change: components transform, signature labels flip, the imaginary commitments of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's content dissolve into real form. Geometry (shape-invariant structure) is transported by the signature change: the Sphere is still a Sphere, the area law is still the area law, the propagation rate is still c. The Wick rotation is therefore the* signature-change test for axis-locked-versus-shape-invariant content *— a test that maps directly onto the Descartes split.*

*Proof.* Each clause is established by direct examination of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel already enumerated in the present paper. For (i), the algebraic-symbolic character of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is established by Propositions H.1–H.5 of §II.1 (Hamiltonian route to $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$), Theorem IX.25.4 (Hilbert variational derivation of $G_{\mu\nu}$ — operating on the metric *tensor* via tensor algebra, with the action $\int R\sqrt{-g}\,d^4 x$ being an integral of an algebraic-tensor scalar over Cartesian-like coordinate patches), Theorem IX.13.19 (the failures of unitarity, group structure, Wigner classification, and Heisenberg commutator under Wick rotation — each failure is a component-level algebraic failure). For (ii), the geometric-shape character of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is established by Propositions L.1–L.6 of §II.2 (Huygens-wavefront propagation on the iterated McGucken Sphere — a shape-based geometric flow), Theorem IX.10.3 (Jacobson Clausius integration on local Rindler horizons — a geometric-thermodynamic identity), Theorems IX.13.20 (the transports of the Sphere, the area law, the Unruh temperature, and the Clausius relation under Wick rotation — each transport is a shape-level geometric invariance). For (iii), the Wick rotation as the test is established by Theorems IX.13.19 and IX.13.20 of the present paper, with the differential response operating exactly along the Descartes split. ∎

##### IX.13.13.4.B Historical Anchoring: The Algebra/Geometry Tension in the History of Mathematical Physics

The Descartes-split reading of the channel distinction admits a sharp historical anchoring. The dual-channel architecture of physics is *not* an artifact of twentieth-century formalism; it is the continuation, at the physical level, of a tension between two great mathematical traditions that Descartes' 1637 analytic-geometry program unified at the mathematical level but did not — *could not*. Resolve at the physical level.

Tradition 1 (Greek classical-geometric): the shape-based tradition. Euclid 300 BCE, Apollonius 200 BCE, Archimedes 250 BCE, and the Greek tradition through Pappus 320 CE operated on shape-content: constructions with compass and straightedge, classification of conic sections by their geometric definition (the locus of points satisfying a focal-directrix condition rather than the solution set of a polynomial equation), proofs by direct geometric reasoning (Euclid's *Elements* contains no algebraic notation). The tradition treats geometry as primitive — shapes are the fundamental objects, and properties of shapes are read from the shapes themselves.

Tradition 2 (Babylonian–Arabic–medieval algebraic): the symbol-based tradition. Al-Khwārizmī 825 CE (whose *al-Jabr* gave the field its name), Cardano 1545, Bombelli 1572, Viète 1591, Stevin 1585, and the medieval-Renaissance European tradition through Descartes 1637 operated on symbolic content: the manipulation of symbols representing unknowns, the solution of polynomial equations by algebraic transformations, the development of notation for variables, exponents, and operations. The tradition treats symbolic content as primitive — equations are the fundamental objects, and properties of equations are read from the equations themselves via algebraic manipulation.

Descartes 1637 unified analytic geometry at the mathematical level. *La Géométrie* (the appendix to *Discours de la méthode*) supplied the Cartesian coordinate system — the bijective correspondence between points in geometric space and ordered pairs of real numbers, and thereby made shape-content and symbol-content two faces of one algebraic structureM. A curve is both a geometric shape (the locus of points satisfying a geometric condition) and an algebraic equation (the solution set of a polynomial in coordinate variables). The unification was foundational: by the eighteenth century, Euler's analytic methods, Lagrange's *Mécanique analytique* 1788 (which famously declared "*on ne trouvera point de figures dans cet ouvrage*"), and the algebraic-analytical tradition of continental mathematics had developed the algebraic face into the dominant mode of mathematical physics; Newton's *Principia* 1687, by contrast, was written in deliberately classical-geometric style with proofs by Euclidean-geometric construction.

The tension persists in twentieth-century physics. The Descartes unification was complete at the mathematical level — algebra and geometry are two readings of the same, but the *physical* tradition of theoretical physics inherited the algebra/geometry split as a *methodological tension* that persists to the present:

— *Einstein 1915 chose geometry.* General relativity is constructed on the geometric face of Descartes' synthesis: the metric tensor as a geometric object, the Christoffel symbols as connection coefficients on a manifold, the Riemann tensor as the geometric measure of curvature, Schwarzschild's solution as the geometry of a black hole. Einstein's letters to Hilbert in 1915 emphasize the geometry; the Einstein–Grossmann collaboration on the *Entwurf* 1913 was a geometric construction.

— *Heisenberg 1925 chose algebra.* Matrix mechanics is constructed on the algebraic face of Descartes' synthesis: observables as matrices, commutators as algebraic identities, the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ as the central algebra. Heisenberg's 1925 paper "Über quantentheoretische Umdeutung kinematischer und mechanischer Beziehungen" is explicitly algebraic — kinematic relations re-read as relations between operator components.

— *Schrödinger 1926 chose geometry.* Wave mechanics is constructed on the geometric face: the wavefunction as a geometric field on configuration space, the Schrödinger equation as a wave equation with the Laplacian as the central geometry, the path integral (Feynman 1948) as a sum over geometric paths in configuration space.

— *Dirac 1930 chose algebra.* Dirac's *Principles of Quantum Mechanics* developed the algebraic-bra-ket formalism as the unifying language; the wave-mechanical content of Schrödinger was reinterpreted as the position-representation of an underlying algebraic state in Hilbert space.

— *Feynman 1948 returned to geometry.* The path integral re-introduced geometry as foundational: paths as geometric objects, the action functional as a geometric integral, the path sum as a geometric superposition. Feynman's diagrams 1949 are explicitly geometric: lines and vertices as combinatorial-geometric objects representing physical processes.

— *Penrose 1967, Witten 1986: geometry.* Twistor theory and topological quantum field theory pushed the geometric face into the level of QFT, with twistors as geometric primitives that algebraicize as a *consequence* rather than as a starting point.

— *Connes 1985, Voiculescu 1990s: algebra.* Non-commutative geometry pushed the algebraic face into the level of geometry itself, with operator algebras as the primitive content and "geometry" as a derived consequence of the algebra's Algebraic structureS.

The tension between the algebraic-Heisenberg-Dirac-Connes lineage and the geometric-Einstein-Schrödinger-Feynman-Penrose lineage is *not* a tension between two competing physical theories; it is the methodological mark of the Descartes split — the same physics can be read algebraically (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel) or geometrically (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel), and the two readings are *historically* developed by different traditions that emphasize different faces of the underlying physics. **The McGucken framework is the first theory that recognizes the Descartes split as a feature of physics rather than as a methodological choice between competing traditions**, and supplies, through dx₄/dt = ic, the geometric primitive on which both faces operate simultaneously.

##### IX.13.13.4.C The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel / the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Distinction Is Physical, Historical, and Mathematical Simultaneously

**Corollary IX.13.25 (the channel distinction is physical, historical, and mathematical as one consequence with three faces).** *The McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel / the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel distinction is not a distinction in any single sense — physical only, or historical only, or mathematical only, but a single distinction with three faces, each face being a true reading of the same:*

*(i) **Mathematical face — the Descartes algebra/geometry split (1637).** At the mathematical level, the distinction is the Descartes split of analytic geometry: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the algebraic-symbolic face (components on Cartesian axes, operators, signature-bearing equations); the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is the geometric-shape face (the McGucken Sphere, foliation-independent wavefronts, signature-invariant areas and rates). The two faces were unified by Descartes 1637 as mathematical descriptions of the same; the McGucken framework recognizes that they are also two distinct readings of dx₄/dt = ic at the physical level.*

*(ii) **Historical face — the algebra-geometry tradition split (300 BCE–2026).** At the historical level, the distinction maps onto two mathematical-physical traditions: the Greek-classical-geometric tradition (Euclid, Apollonius, Archimedes, Newton's Principia, Einstein's geometric GR, Schrödinger's wave mechanics, Feynman's path integral, Penrose twistors) and the Babylonian-Arabic-medieval-algebraic tradition (al-Khwārizmī, Cardano, Viète, Lagrange's analytic mechanics, Heisenberg matrix mechanics, Dirac's algebraic QM, Connes non-commutative geometry). The traditions have alternated as the dominant mode of foundational physics over the past century, with each generation choosing one face and treating the other as "merely formal" or "computationally convenient." The McGucken framework is the first theory to recognize the alternation as a symptom of the underlying dual-channel architecture rather than as a methodological choice.*

*(iii) **Physical face — the differential-response diagnostic (the present paper).** At the physical level, the distinction is operationalised by the McGucken-Wick rotation as a differential diagnostic: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's signature-specific algebra is destroyed by the rotation (the Cartesian-axis-locked content fails the signature-change test); the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's shape-content is transported by the rotation (the geometric-shape-invariant content passes the signature-change test). The two channels remain disjoint derivations of the same equation, with the overdetermination content of the McGucken Duality (Heisenberg–Feynman equivalence, Hilbert–Jacobson agreement, particle-level/horizon-level Second-Law agreement) preserved because the two faces, algebraic and geometric, supply distinct derivations that happen to converge on the same physics.*

*The three faces are three views of the same : physics admits an algebraic-symbolic reading (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel) and a geometric-shape reading (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel) because the principle dx₄/dt = ic admits two readings — one operating on components on axes (the algebraic-symmetry account, transmitted through Stone, Wigner, Noether) and one operating on shape (the geometric-propagation account, transmitted through Huygens, Feynman, Jacobson). The distinction is mathematical (the Descartes split), historical (the algebra-geometry tradition alternation), and physical (the differential-response diagnostic) simultaneously, because the same claim has three readings at three levels of description.*

*Proof.* I establish each of the three faces with the corresponding anchor, then verify they are three readings of the same.

*Step 1 (Mathematical face — Descartes split).* By Theorem IX.13.24 (the channel distinction as Descartes algebra/geometry split), the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel articulates physics as components on Cartesian axes (operators, signature-bearing equations, commutator structure), and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel articulates physics as shape (McGucken Sphere, foliation-independent wavefronts, signature-invariant areas and rates). Descartes 1637 *Discours de la méthode* established that algebra and geometry are two mathematical descriptions of the same; the McGucken framework recognizes that the same split operates at the *physical* level for dx₄/dt = ic. The mathematical face is therefore the Descartes split applied to physics.

*Step 2 (Historical face — algebra-geometry tradition alternation).* By the historical record of foundational physics: the Greek-classical-geometric tradition (Euclid 300 BCE → Apollonius → Archimedes → Newton *Principia* → Einstein GR → Schrödinger wave mechanics → Feynman path integral → Penrose twistors) and the Babylonian-Arabic-medieval-algebraic tradition (al-Khwārizmī 820 → Cardano → Viète → Lagrange analytic mechanics → Heisenberg matrix mechanics → Dirac algebraic QM → Connes non-commutative geometry) have alternated as the dominant foundational mode in physics. Each generation has chosen one face and treated the other as "merely formal" or "computationally convenient" (the cultural-suppression record at §IX.13.13.4.E catalogues twentieth-century instances). The McGucken framework is the first to recognize the alternation as a symptom of the underlying dual-channel architecture rather than as a contingent methodological choice (Theorem IX.0.B.5 the dual-formulation pattern as signature).

*Step 3 (Physical face — differential-response diagnostic).* By Corollary IX.13.18 (channel-membership diagnostic via Wick-rotation response): the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's signature-specific algebra is destroyed by the McGucken-Wick rotation (Theorem IX.13.19 for QM; Theorem IX.13.20 for GR), while the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's shape-content is transported (Step 4 of the proof of Theorem IX.10.1). The differential-response diagnostic is therefore a physical operationalization of the channel distinction. By Theorem IX.26.3 (Dual-Channel Disjointness across 47 theorems), the two channels remain disjoint derivations of the same equation, preserving the overdetermination content (Heisenberg-Feynman, Hilbert-Jacobson, Heisenberg-Feynman of Theorem IX.15.7).

*Step 4 (The three faces as views of one ).* Steps 1-3 establish three distinct faces of the same distinction. The unification: each face anchors the same — dx₄/dt = ic admits two readings, one through components on axes (The Algebraic Channel) and one through shape (The Geometric Channel) — at a different level of description. The mathematical face (Step 1) is at the level of the descriptive vocabulary (algebra vs. geometry). The historical face (Step 2) is at the level of the intellectual tradition that develops each vocabulary. The physical face (Step 3) is at the operational diagnostic that distinguishes them. The three faces are necessarily co-present because the same dual-channel architecture surfaces at all three levels: in mathematics through the Descartes split, in history through the alternating-tradition record, in physics through the differential-response diagnostic. The corollary therefore holds. ∎

**Remark IX.13.26 (the reading: the McGucken Sphere as the unified geometric primitive across both fields).** *The light-cone-as-McGucken-Sphere-null-surface identification (where the GR light cone is the integrated trace of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront emanating from each event), the QM nonlocal-source 2-sphere identification (where the quantum-mechanical source-detection nonlocality is the McGucken-Sphere wavefront viewed at fixed time), and the area-law content of the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy (where the horizon entropy is the McGucken-Sphere mode count at the horizon) are three aspects of one geometric object, the iterated McGucken Sphere, appearing in three apparent contexts (GR causal structure, QM nonlocality, gravitational entropy) but supplying the same dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content in all three. The orthodox tradition has these as three primitively separate structures in three subfields of physics, with no foundational principle linking them. The McGucken framework recognizes them as three views of the same geometric primitive — the McGucken Sphere expanding at rate c from every spacetime event — viewed under different foliations and at different scales. The unification across the three contexts is the McGucken Sphere being the same geometric object in all three contexts. The Wick rotation transports the Sphere in all three contexts because the Sphere is the geometric-shape face of physics — the Descartes-geometric primitive, and the rotation operates on signature, not on shape.*

**Remark IX.13.27 (the appropriateness of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel being described first by a rotationally symmetric Sphere).** *The McGucken Sphere is rotationally symmetric on its spatial three-slice by construction: it is the surface of constant x₄-advance from a given event E, and the spatial component of that advance is spherically symmetric in $x_1 x_2 x_3$ (the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic supplies an active expansion that is, by hypothesis, spherically symmetric — every direction in the spatial three-slice is treated equally). It is therefore appropriate that dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometric primitive is rotationally symmetric: the geometric-shape face of physics is the face that survives coordinate rotations and signature changes (the differential-response diagnostic of §§IX.13.13.1–IX.13.13.3), and the Sphere — the maximally-symmetric three-dimensional surface under spatial rotation — is the natural geometric primitive for the shape-invariant content of physics. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel, by contrast, is naturally described by Cartesian axis-locked content (signature labels, operator components, commutator structure) because the algebraic-symbolic face of physics depends on the choice of axes for it. The -appropriateness reading is therefore: the geometric primitive of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is rotationally symmetric because the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is the rotation-invariant face of physics, and the algebra of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel depends on the axis structure because the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the axis-bearing face of physics. The Wick rotation, as a signature change on the four-coordinate ambient space, is the operation that distinguishes axis-bearing content from rotation-invariant content, and it operates as a diagnostic along the Descartes split.*

##### IX.13.13.4.D Observational and Experimental Methods Driving the Differential Development of Channels Across the History of Physics

The Descartes-split reading of the channel distinction admits a further that consolidates the explanation of why specific subfields of physics developed predominantly along the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel or the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel lines: **the observational and experimental methods of each era, together with the popular mathematical models available to physicists of that era, determined which channel was available for the account of a given physical phenomenon.** I trace the development field by field, with the reading that each subfield's predominant channel-of-development was selected by the contingent availability of observational methods and mathematical models in the era when the subfield was foundationally articulated.

Steam-engine thermodynamics (Carnot 1824, Clausius 1850, Kelvin 1851) developed as Geometric-Channel content. The observational methods of the 19th-century thermodynamics tradition were heat-engine measurements: indicator-diagram measurements of work output per cycle, calorimetric measurements of heat input and rejection, temperature measurements via mercury thermometers calibrated to the steam-water-ice triple points. These methods supplied access to *bulk thermodynamics*. The geometric-propagation face of thermal physics: entropy as a state function on a thermodynamic-phase manifold, the Second Law as a monotonicity statement on a geometric trajectory through state space, the Clausius integration $\delta Q = T\,dS$ as a thermodynamic-geometric identity. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel face of thermodynamics — statistical-mechanical operator algebras, Boltzmann transport equations, the quantum-statistical $-i\hbar\,\partial_t$ formalism — was not yet developed in 1850; the Cartesian-algebraic reading of thermodynamics had to wait for Boltzmann's 1872 H-theorem (still partially the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel), Gibbs's 1902 statistical-ensemble approach (transitional), and von Neumann's 1932 quantum-statistical operator formalism (mature the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel). The 19th-century thermodynamic tradition is *the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel by historical accident*. The observational methods of the era supplied geometric-thermodynamics, and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel algebra was not yet articulable in form.

Electromagnetism (Faraday 1831, Maxwell 1865) developed as Geometric-Channel content. Faraday's observational methods were geometric-field measurements: iron-filing patterns visualising magnetic field lines, compass-needle orientations mapping field directions in space, current-carrying conductors and their force-on-conductor interactions. Each measurement supplied *shape-content of the electromagnetic field*. A the Geometric-Channel account of the field as a geometric structure on three-dimensional space, with field lines as the geometric primitive. Maxwell's 1865 unification "A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field" articulated the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content as field equations on a geometric continuum: the four equations as constraint equations on the algebraic structureI of the electromagnetic wavefront. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel face of electromagnetism — gauge-field representation theory, the $U(1)$-gauge group's unitary representations on Hilbert space, the photon as the irreducible representation of the Poincaré group with spin 1 — had to wait for the development of group-theoretic methods (Wigner 1939) and the operator-quantization of the electromagnetic field (Dirac 1927, Jordan–Pauli 1928). The 19th-century electromagnetic tradition is *the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel by historical accident*. The observational methods of Faraday and the mathematical models available to Maxwell supplied geometric-field content, and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel representation-theoretic content had to wait three-quarters of a century for the algebraic-group-theoretic tradition to develop the apparatus.

Maxwell 1865 and Hertz 1888 further developed the Geometric Channel via the light-as-electromagnetic-wave identification. Maxwell's 1865 calculation that the speed of electromagnetic wave propagation $1/\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}$ matches the measured speed of light supplied a geometric-propagation identification: light *is* the geometric propagation of the electromagnetic field at a universal rate. Hertz's 1888 experimental confirmation supplied direct empirical evidence for the geometric account. The identification *light = electromagnetic wave at speed c* is a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content statement — geometric propagation at a universal rate, and was developed in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel tradition. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic-Channel account of light — light as a unitary representation of $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)$ with mass zero and helicity $\pm 1$ — was not articulable until Wigner 1939 supplied the group-representation apparatus.

The constancy of the speed of light (Michelson–Morley 1887, Lorentz 1895, Einstein 1905) drove a transition to the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel. The Michelson–Morley null result for the aether wind, combined with Lorentz's 1895 reading of the result as length-contraction and time-dilation in the moving frame, and Einstein's 1905 derivation of special relativity from the constancy of c together with the relativity principle, introduced the Lorentz transformations as the central algebraic-symmetry of relativistic kinematics. The Lorentz transformations are a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel object: they are algebraic-symmetry transformations on Cartesian space-time components, with c entering as a coupling constant in the transformation matrix rather than as a geometric-propagation rate on a real four-manifold. The 1905 development of relativity was therefore *the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel by methodological choice*. Einstein's 1905 derivation operates on the Lorentz-transformation invariance of physical laws (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel: algebraic-symmetry), not on the geometric-propagation of the electromagnetic wavefront at rate c (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel: shape content). The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric-Channel account was available. Maxwell 1865 had supplied it 40 years earlier, but the account of special relativity chose the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel. Minkowski's 1908 four-vector formalism, with x₄ = ict as the time coordinate, was the algebraic-spacetime articulation of the Algebraic-Channel account.

Minkowski's spherically-expansive geometric account was suppressed for over a century. Minkowski's 1908 "Raum und Zeit" introduced four-vectors with x₄ = ict, but the *geometry* of x₄, that the fourth coordinate corresponds to an actual physical direction, with the imaginary unit i encoding its perpendicularity to the spatial three-axes, and that the integrated form x₄ = ict reflects an underlying dynamical principle dx₄/dt = ic supplying spherically symmetric expansion at rate c — was not articulated. Minkowski treated x₄ = ict as an algebraic-notational identity that made the four-coordinate quadratic form algebraically convenient: $ds^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 - c^2\,dt^2$ on substitution. The geometric account, that x₄ corresponds to an active fourth dimension expanding spherically at rate c from every spacetime event, generating the McGucken Sphere as a real geometric object on a real four-manifold — was not on Minkowski's map, and was not on the map of the subsequent twentieth-century relativistic tradition (§XI.5 Poincaré–Minkowski thought experiment of the present paper). The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content of x₄ was *available* at 1908 but *culturally suppressed* by the algebraic-formalist reading of Minkowski and the subsequent the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel development of special relativity by Sommerfeld, Klein, Einstein–Grossmann, and the differential-geometric tradition of curved-spacetime relativity.

Quantum spectra (Balmer 1885, Rydberg 1888, Bohr 1913) developed as Algebraic-Channel content. The observational methods of 19th-century atomic spectroscopy were emission-line measurements: hydrogen-line wavelengths recorded by photographic plate, classified by Balmer 1885 and Rydberg 1888 according to algebraic formulas relating wavelength to integer quantum numbers. Each spectral line corresponds to a *discrete algebra*. A transition between discrete-quantum-number states with energy differences related by algebraic identities. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel face of atomic physics — quantum states as Hilbert-space vectors, the spectrum of the Hamiltonian as the algebra of atomic-energy quantization, transition matrix elements as algebraic-operator quantities — was the natural mathematical framework for the spectroscopic content. Bohr's 1913 quantization condition $L = n\hbar$ is an algebraic identity on the angular momentum operator; the subsequent development of matrix mechanics by Heisenberg 1925, the wave mechanics by Schrödinger 1926 (transitional — wave-mechanical equation has the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel form, but the canonical-commutator formalism was the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel), and the Dirac–Jordan transformation theory 1927–1930 articulated the Algebraic-Channel account of atomic physics. The 20th-century atomic-physics tradition is *the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel by historical accident*. The observational methods of spectroscopy supplied discrete-algebra, and the geometric-propagation the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content of atomic physics (the de Broglie wavefront on the Bohr orbit, the Schrödinger wavefunction as a Huygens-wavefront propagation on the spatial three-slice) had to be re-discovered later in the path-integral tradition.

Planck's 1900 quantum emerged from the blackbody filament problem. The observational methods of late-19th-century blackbody radiation measurements supplied the spectrum of a heated filament as a function of frequency: Wien's law $u(\nu, T) = (\nu^3) f(\nu/T)$ at high frequency, Rayleigh–Jeans $u(\nu, T) = 8\pi\nu^2 k_B T/c^3$ at low frequency, with the experimental curves falling between the two extremes and failing to match either at the full frequency range (the "ultraviolet catastrophe" of Rayleigh–Jeans at high ν). Planck's 1900 derivation supplied the interpolating curve $u(\nu, T) = (8\pi h\nu^3/c^3)(e^{h\nu/k_B T} - 1)^{-1}$ by introducing the energy quantum $E = h\nu$ as the discretization of the oscillator's energy states. The quantum $h$ was introduced *as a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel object*. An algebraic discretization of energy spectra — to solve a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel problem (the algebraic-spectral content of blackbody radiation). The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content of $h$, that $h$ is the action quantum of one Planck-frequency oscillation of x₄, with $\hbar = h/2\pi$ entering the Compton angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ that supplies the geometric-propagation rate of x₄ on its iterated Sphere — was not available to Planck in 1900 because dx₄/dt = ic was not an option for 1900-era physics. Planck's $h$ is the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel by the historical contingency of how it was introduced; the McGucken framework re-identifies it as a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel / dual-channel quantity supplied by the Compton-coupling rate of x₄ ([16]; Theorem 5.2 of [69]).

Einstein 1905 established universal $h$, carrying the unrealised Geometric-Channel content of the Schrödinger equation. ##### IX.13.13.4.E The Cultural Suppression of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel: The MTW 1973 Banishment of x₄ = ict and the Tragic Wrong of the Geometric-Dynamics Lineage

The historical-developmental analysis of §IX.13.13.4.D supplies the reason why specific subfields developed predominantly along the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel or the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel lines. The — the **cultural suppression of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel by the very lineage that should have championed it** — admits a sharp documentary anchor in the textbook of relativistic gravitational physics, *Gravitation* by Misner, Thorne, and Wheeler (MTW 1973). The MTW passage that performs the suppression is worth quoting in full, since it is the precise textbook moment at which the geometric account of x₄ was *banished from general relativity by the very lineage of John Archibald Wheeler that, twenty years later in 1989–1990, would produce dx₄/dt = ic as the answer to the question Poincaré and Minkowski had posed in 1905–1908*.

In *Gravitation* §2.2 (the introduction of the spacetime interval in flat geometry, p. 51 of [Misner–Thorne–Wheeler 1973]), MTW write (verbatim):

> *"In a region where spacetime is flat, one can hide this from view by writing $(\Delta s)^2 = (\Delta x^1)^2 + (\Delta x^2)^2 + (\Delta x^3)^2 + (\Delta x^4)^2$, with $x^4 = ict$, no one has discovered a way to make an imaginary coordinate work in the general curved spacetime manifold. If '$x^4 = ict$' cannot be used there, it will not be used here. In this chapter and hereafter, as throughout the literature of general relativity, a real time coordinate is used, $x^0 = t = ct_{\text{conv}}$ (superscript 0 rather than 4 to avoid any possibility of confusion with the imaginary time coordinate)."*

This is the textbook moment of the cultural suppression of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel in general relativity. MTW articulate three commitments simultaneously:

*(i) The geometry of x₄ = ict (which descends from the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic as its integrated shadow on the Lorentzian four-manifold) is dismissed as a notational device that "hides" the underlying real-coordinate structure rather than as an algebraic articulation of a geometry about x₄'s perpendicularity to the spatial three-slice.*

*(iii) The disciplinary commitment of "the literature of general relativity" is invoked as a normative standard — "as throughout the literature of general relativity, a real time coordinate is used" — establishing the suppression as a community-wide convention rather than as an individual choice.*

The consequence of the MTW banishment is severe: it commits the geometric-dynamics lineage of Wheeler — the lineage that emphasised geometry as the primitive content of gravity, that championed Misner–Thorne–Wheeler's *geometrodynamics* program, and that produced the textbook on which two generations of relativists were trained — to the *Cartesian-algebraic* reading of time, *against* the Greek-geometric account of x₄ as a real four-coordinate axis with an algebraic-imaginary marker for perpendicularity. *Step 1 (Null-vector content of relativity: Minkowski 1908).* The standard Minkowski formalism of relativity defines the inner product $\eta(v, w) = -v^0 w^0 c^2 + v^1 w^1 + v^2 w^2 + v^3 w^3$ on the tangent space $T_p \mathcal M_G$ at every event $p \in \mathcal M_G$.
