**Corollary IX.13.14.ter.2 (Weyl's tile dilemma dissolved by the dual-channel architecture).** *Weyl's 1949 tile argument [Weyl 1949] proposes a dilemma for discrete-spacetime theories: if space is a discrete grid of indivisible tiles, then the diagonal of a square space contains the same number of tile-to-tile steps as the side, violating the Pythagorean theorem $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$; and a measuring rod or moving particle would change physical length depending on its angle relative to the underlying grid, violating rotational isotropy. The dilemma has been treated in the discrete-spacetime literature (Sorkin's causal set theory [Sorkin 1991; Bombelli-Henson-Sorkin 1987]; Wolfram-Gorard hypergraph rewriting [Wolfram 2020; Gorard 2020]; loop quantum gravity discrete-area spectrum [Rovelli 2004; Ashtekar-Lewandowski 2004]; lattice gauge theory [Wilson 1974]) as an obstacle to be circumvented by various technical means (Poisson sprinkling on a Lorentzian manifold; emergence of smoothness in the continuum limit of fine-grained hypergraphs; renormalization-group flow to continuum fixed points; lattice spacing tending to zero). The McGucken framework dissolves the dilemma at the level by the discreteness/continuity diagnosis of Theorem IX.13.14.ter.1:*

*(W1) The discreteness of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is at the temporal substrate-tick scale (x₄-tick at the Planck time $t_P$), NOT at the spatial scale. The spatial three-slice is continuous in every frame; there is no spatial grid of tiles. Weyl's tile argument applies to theories that postulate a discrete spatial lattice; the McGucken framework's substrate-tick discreteness is in the temporal axis (x₄), not in the spatial three-slice.*

*(W2) The continuity of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is the bulk-propagation account on the smooth manifold $\mathcal M_G$, where the Pythagorean theorem $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ holds exactly (as part of the spatial metric $d\ell^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2$) and rotational isotropy holds exactly (as $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ invariance of the spatial slice).*

*(W3) The two readings are simultaneously available via the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ as the coordinate-identification bridge (§IX.13.13.bis). There is no contradiction with Weyl's tile dilemma because the McGucken framework does not postulate a discrete spatial tile-grid; the algebraic structureC is in the temporal axis, and the spatial three-slice remains continuous with full rotational isotropy at every scale.*

*The Weyl tile dilemma is therefore not an obstacle to the McGucken framework but a constraint that selects against discrete-spatial-lattice theories. The McGucken framework's discrete-temporal / continuous-spatial structure passes the constraint, with the bulk-propagation account of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel supplying the continuous spatial structure that the Pythagorean theorem and rotational isotropy require.*

*Proof.* I establish each of (W1), (W2), (W3) in three steps.

*Step 1 (Weyl's tile dilemma is a constraint on discrete-spatial-lattice theories).* Weyl 1949 [Weyl 1949] argued that a discrete spatial lattice with tile spacing $a$ has the property that going from $(0,0)$ to $(na, na)$ requires $n$ tile-steps along the side and $n$ tile-steps along the diagonal (assuming nearest-neighbour steps), so the diagonal-to-side ratio is $1:1$ rather than the Pythagorean $\sqrt 2 : 1$. The dilemma applies to theories with a discrete spatial lattice; it does not apply to theories with continuous spatial structure regardless of whether they have discrete temporal structure.

*Step 2 (The McGucken framework's substrate-tick discreteness is temporal, not spatial).* By Theorem IX.13.14.ter.1 (D-A.2), the substrate-tick interval is the Planck time $t_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^5}$ in the temporal direction. The spatial three-slice is continuous in every frame: by Theorem IX.18.4 the Lorentzian metric $g_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-1, +1, +1, +1)$ has continuous real spatial coordinates $(x_1, x_2, x_3) \in \mathbb R^3$, with no discrete spatial structure imposed at any scale. The Pythagorean theorem $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ holds exactly as part of the spatial Euclidean three-metric (which is the spatial part of $g_{\mu\nu}$), and rotational isotropy holds exactly as $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ invariance of this spatial metric. By Theorem IX.10.1 the Universal Geometric Channel Theorem, the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ at every event $p$ is a continuous spatial sphere with continuous radius $c(t - t_p)$ and continuous area $4\pi c^2(t - t_p)^2$.

*Step 3 (The two readings coexist via the McGucken-Wick rotation as coordinate-identification bridge).* By Theorems IX.13.13.bis.2 (Coordinate-identification bridge sense) and IX.13.13.bis.6 (significance of the disambiguation), the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ makes both the substrate-tick reading (The Algebraic Channel, x₄-tick at $t_P$) and the bulk-propagation account (The Geometric Channel, continuous Sphere expansion) simultaneously available on the same manifold $\mathcal M_G$. There is no contradiction with Weyl's tile dilemma because the spatial continuity is preserved in both readings; the discreteness is only in the temporal substrate-tick. The Weyl constraint selects against discrete-spatial-lattice theories (Sorkin, Wolfram, lattice gauge theory in the unrenormalized form) but does not select against the McGucken framework's discrete-temporal / continuous-spatial structure. ∎

**Corollary IX.13.14.ter.3 (Nielsen-Ninomiya doubling theorem does not apply to the McGucken framework).** *The Nielsen-Ninomiya 1981 no-go theorem [Nielsen-Ninomiya 1981] establishes that a chiral fermion cannot be realised on a discrete spatial lattice without doubling — every left-handed Weyl spinor mode is paired with a right-handed Weyl spinor mode at the lattice cutoff scale, with the two modes summing to a non-chiral Dirac fermion at large distances. The theorem is an obstacle for lattice-gauge-theory realisations of the Standard Model's chiral structure. The McGucken framework's substrate-tick discreteness is temporal (x₄-tick at the Planck scale), not spatial; the spatial three-slice is continuous in every frame, and there is no spatial lattice on which a chiral fermion would need to be discretised. The Nielsen-Ninomiya doubling phenomenon therefore does not apply to the McGucken framework:*

*(N1) **No spatial lattice.** The McGucken substrate has continuous spatial three-slice in every Lorentz frame (Theorem IX.13.14.ter.1 (D-B.1)). There is no discrete spatial lattice on which to impose a chiral fermion mode; therefore the lattice-fermion-doubling content of Nielsen-Ninomiya has no application.*

*(N2) **Chirality in the McGucken framework descends from the Clifford algebra.** The chiral structure of the Standard Model — $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ weak isospin acting on left-handed Weyl spinors — descends from the Clifford-algebraic structure $\hat{C\ell}(1, 3)$ on the continuous spatial three-slice with x₄-substrate-tick at the Planck scale (Proposition III.2). The chirality $\gamma_5$ is the volume element of $\hat{C\ell}(1, 3)$, and the left-handed projector $P_L = (1 - \gamma_5)/2$ selects the left-handed Weyl spinor component. There is no lattice-cutoff content from which a doubling mode could emerge.*

*(N3) **No fermion doubling.** The Nielsen-Ninomiya doubling phenomenon requires the chiral mode to inhabit a discrete spatial lattice that necessarily contains both forward- and backward-moving lattice modes (the "Brillouin zone" of the discrete lattice). There is no discrete spatial lattice in any frame in the McGucken substrate; there is no Brillouin zone; there is no forced doubling. The chiral structure of the Standard Model — $SU(2)_L$ weak isospin acting on left-handed Weyl spinors, with right-handed counterparts as separate $SU(2)_R$-singlet representations — is realised on the continuous spatial three-slice with $\hat{C\ell}(1, 3)$-Clifford-algebraic structure carrying the channel contentE (Proposition III.2). The $SU(2)_L$ and $SU(3)_c$ gauge structures emerge from the Clifford sub-algebra rather than from a lattice gauge-link construction. The Nielsen-Ninomiya no-go does not apply because its precondition (discrete spatial lattice in a preferred frame) is absent.*

*The 44-year-old Nielsen-Ninomiya no-go is therefore not a constraint on the McGucken framework; it is a constraint on a different class of discrete-spacetime theories (lattice gauge theories with discrete spatial lattices) that the McGucken framework does not belong to. The McGucken framework's substrate is discrete in time (x₄-substrate-tick at the Planck scale) but continuous in space (continuous spatial three-slice in every frame); the Nielsen-Ninomiya no-go applies to theories that are discrete in space, which the McGucken framework is not.*

*Proof.* By Theorem IX.13.14.ter.1 (D-B.1), the spatial three-slice $\Sigma_t$ at every event $p \in \mathcal M_G$ is continuous $\mathbb R^3$, with no discrete spatial lattice. The Nielsen-Ninomiya 1981 theorem [Nielsen-Ninomiya 1981] has precondition: a discrete spatial lattice with finite lattice spacing $a$ in a preferred frame. The theorem establishes that under this precondition, the lattice Brillouin zone necessarily contains paired left- and right-handed Weyl spinor modes at the lattice cutoff momentum $\pi/a$. The McGucken framework violates the precondition — no discrete spatial lattice — so the theorem's conclusion does not apply. By Proposition III.2 (the chiral structure of the Standard Model from the Clifford algebra), the channel contentE $\gamma_5$ as the volume element of $\hat{C\ell}(1,3)$ is supplied by the Clifford-algebraic structure on the continuous spatial three-slice, not from a lattice-gauge construction. Left-handed Weyl spinors are selected by the projector $P_L = (1-\gamma_5)/2$ acting on the continuous three-slice; right-handed counterparts are separate $\mathrm{SU}(2)_R$-singlet representations of the same continuous structure. The chiral structure is realised without requiring a discrete spatial lattice, and the Nielsen-Ninomiya doubling phenomenon does not arise. ∎

### IX.13.15 The Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem: Canonical Conjugate Pairs as the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel/the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Pairs, with Delimitation by Pauli's Theorem and Its Descendants

The position-of-i diagnosis of §IX.13.14 admits a further physical consequence: **for the clean Tier I canonical conjugate pairs of quantum mechanics —, position-momentum $(\hat q, \hat p)$ on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{n})$ and the spin commutators $(\hat S_{x}, \hat S_{y})$ and cyclic permutations on finite-dimensional spin-$j$ Hilbert spaces — the operator-level canonical commutator pairs a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel observable with a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel observable (or carries the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel spatial-axis-perpendicularity content in the spin case), with the imaginary unit $i$ in the commutator being the channel-perpendicularity marker for x₄'s perpendicularity to the spatial three-slice.** The non-commutativity of these clean canonical conjugate observables is the *algebraic shadow* of channel-perpendicularity at the operator level, with the Heisenberg uncertainty principle $\sigma_{q}\sigma_{p} \geq \hbar/2$ being the numbers of the perpendicularity for the position-momentum case.

The reach of the Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem to other candidate canonical pairs is qualified by the foundations-of-QM obstruction literature. Three further candidate pairs — energy-time $(\hat E, t)$, angular momentum-azimuthal-angle $(\hat L_{z}, \hat\phi)$, and number-phase $(\hat N, \hat\phi)$ — admit obstructions at the level of the existence of a literal self-adjoint canonical commutator $[A, B] = i\hbar$:

— **Energy-time** is not a canonical commutator pair: $t$ is a parameter not an operator, and [Pauli 1933] establishes that no self-adjoint $\hat t$ can be conjugate to a bounded-below Hamiltonian. The energy-time uncertainty $\Delta E\,\Delta\tau \geq \hbar/2$ is the [Mandelstam-Tamm 1945] dynamical-timescale relation, distinct from $\sigma_{q}\sigma_{p} \geq \hbar/2$;

— **Angular momentum-angle** admits the commutator $[\hat L_{z}, \hat\phi] = -i\hbar$ only on a restricted dense domain excluding angular momentum eigenstates, with the obstruction tracked by [Judge 1963];

— **Number-phase** is the canonical counterexample: by [Susskind-Glogower 1964], no self-adjoint phase operator $\hat\phi$ canonically conjugate to $\hat N$ exists; the obstruction is Pauli 1933 applied to the bounded-below $\hat N$ spectrum.

The Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem developed in this subsection therefore unifies the Algebraic structureN of the McGucken Duality with the canonical commutator architecture of quantum mechanics for the clean cases (Tier I) and is delimited at Tiers II–IV by the foundations-of-QM obstruction literature. The framework's account is real and for Tier I; for Tiers II–IV, the reading is qualified to the level at which the pattern is present (the Schrödinger equation's $i$ for energy-time, the restricted-domain commutator for angular momentum-angle, the Susskind-Glogower or Pegg-Barnett constructions for number-phase) rather than asserted at the canonical-commutator level.

I formalise this through five numbered statements (Theorem IX.13.15.1 through Theorem IX.13.15.5), with one detailed left-justified 10pt table (Table IX.13.15.A) supplying the four-tier delimitation of canonical-pair candidates by Pauli's-theorem obstruction status. The result has physics in two distinct senses: the Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem applies cleanly to Tier I and supplies the channel-perpendicularity reading of the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ and the spin commutators; and the failure modes at Tiers II–IV are themselves informative, tracking how the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's parameter spaces (compact $S^{1}$ for $\hat\phi$ in $(L_{z}, \phi)$, bounded-below $\hat N$ spectrum for $(\hat N, \hat\phi)$, parameter-not-operator status for $t$) interact with the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's generator structure to determine where the clean Stone-von Neumann canonical-commutator structure exists and where it breaks down via Pauli's theorem.

**Theorem IX.13.15.1 (Measurement as the channel-bifurcation Wick event — refinement of Theorem IX.13.10).** *Theorem IX.13.10 (the McGucken Measurement Theorem) established that quantum measurement is the channel-change from the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel to the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel effected by the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_{4}/c$ during the apparatus interaction. The present theorem refines this: the measurement event is simultaneously*

*(i) **a destruction of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's unitary content** at the measured system: the Stone unitary $U(t) = e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar}$ acting on the pre-measurement wavefunction is no longer a unitary one-parameter group at the registration event — the Wick rotation $t \to -i\tau$ converts the Stone group $\{U(t) : t \in \mathbb R\}$ into the contraction semigroup $\{K(\tau) = e^{-\hat H\tau/\hbar} : \tau \in \mathbb R_{\geq 0}\}$, which is not group-valued (no inverses for $\tau > 0$), no longer encodes the Lorentz invariance of x₄-translation, and supplies no dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel content beyond the registration time. **The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic-Channel account of the system has terminated at the registration event**, with the post-measurement state requiring a new dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic-Channel account initiated from the registration event onward;*

*(ii) **a transport of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content to the spatial three-slice of the apparatus**: the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p_{0})$ emanating from the source event $p_{0}$ at velocity c, with its forward x₄-expansion carrying Compton phase $\omega_{C}\tau$, intersects the apparatus's spatial three-slice at the registration event. The intersection registers the geometric overlap of forward and conjugate x₄-expansions at the absorber — the Born density $P = \psi^{*}\psi = |\psi|^{2}$ via Theorem 7.4 of [70] — as the real, positive, normalised probability density on the spatial three-slice. **The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content survives the Wick rotation as a transport from the Lorentzian-signature to the Euclidean-signature**, with the squared-modulus probability density being the operational content of the transport;*

*(iii) **the source of new the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel content at the registration event**: the post-measurement particle has new the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel content (new momentum eigenstate, new Stone unitary starting at the registration event) and new the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content (new McGucken Sphere expanding from the registration event with new spread). The +ic orientation of dx₄/dt = ic continues at every event, including the registration event itself, supplying the local pointwise operator $D_{M}^{(p_{\text{reg}})}$ at the registration point and initiating the post-measurement Sphere expansion.*

*The mathematics of (i)-(iii) is that measurement is **not a single channel's event** but a **channel-bifurcation event**: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is destroyed at the system (its unitary becomes a contraction semigroup, which is not the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel content); the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is transported at the apparatus (its Lorentzian-signature becomes the Euclidean-signature, with the real probability density on the spatial three-slice as the operational signature); and new the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel content is initiated at the registration event for the post-measurement particle. The measurement event is therefore the locus at which the two channels of dx₄/dt = ic separate, each undergoing its characteristic Wick response (destruction for the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel, transport for the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel), with the bifurcation supplying the mechanism by which the orthodox unitary-vs-collapse paradox is dissolved.*

*Proof.* From Theorem IX.13.10 (the McGucken Measurement Theorem) and the position-of-i diagnosis (Theorem IX.13.14.2: i interior to the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel; Theorem IX.13.14.3: i exterior to the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel). The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's destruction under Wick is established at Corollary IX.13.14.4: the Stone unitary $U(t) = e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar}$ is mapped to the contraction semigroup $K(\tau) = e^{-\hat H\tau/\hbar}$, which is not a unitary one-parameter group. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's transport under Wick is established at the same Corollary: the path-integral weight $e^{iS/\hbar}$ is mapped to the Euclidean weight $e^{-S_{E}/\hbar}$, which remains a probability-measure-compatible weight on the McGucken Sphere structure. The new the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel content at the registration event is supplied by the self-generation property (Theorem IX.0.C.3): every event of $\mathcal M_{G}$ supports its own local McGucken Sphere and its own local pointwise operator $D_{M}^{(p)}$. The bifurcation content of the measurement event — destruction of one channel, transport of the other, initiation of new content for both — is therefore a direct consequence of the position-of-i diagnosis applied to the measurement event. ∎

**Theorem IX.13.15.2 (Probability enters QM and thermodynamics through the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel).** *The probabilistic content of quantum mechanics and the strict-monotonic content of thermodynamics enter the framework through the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel, not through the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel. The reasons are:*

*(i) **The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel cannot produce real positive measures.** the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's machinery (Stone's theorem, unitary one-parameter groups, the canonical commutator with i interior, self-adjoint operators with complex spectra-via-spectral-theorem, the Lorentz algebra structure constants $[M^{\mu\nu}, M^{\rho\sigma}] = i(\eta^{\mu\rho}M^{\nu\sigma} - \ldots)$) produces complex-valued amplitudes, complex-valued unitary evolution, and complex-valued canonical commutators. **The transition from complex amplitudes to real positive probability densities — the modulus operation $\psi \mapsto |\psi|^{2}$ — is the exteriorization of i, the same operation as the McGucken-Wick rotation, and unavailable to the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel** (because exteriorising the i from the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is what dissolves the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel; the Stone unitary $e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar}$ becomes the contraction semigroup $e^{-\hat H\tau/\hbar}$, no longer a unitary group, no longer supplying invariance generators). The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is Lorentzian-locked because it cannot perform that exteriorisation while remaining itself.*

*(ii) **The modulus operation is the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content.** The squared-modulus $|\psi|^{2}$ is the geometric overlap of forward and conjugate x₄-expansions on the McGucken Sphere at the absorption event ([70, Theorem 7.4]), with the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing's bilinearity inherited from the rank-2 character of the Minkowski metric (Lemma IX.22.6.B.1; [70, §7.4]) — itself from $(ic\,dt)^{2} = -c^{2}\,dt^{2}$ via squaring $dx_{4} = ic\,dt$. The squaring is therefore **upstream of measurement**, present in the metric structure of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel from the moment the principle is articulated, and the Born rule is the operational manifestation of this squaring at the apparatus interaction.*

*(iii) **The +ic orientation supplies the strict-monotonic content of thermodynamics through the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel.** The strict Second Law $dS/dt = (3/2)k_{B}/t > 0$ for massive particles (Theorem 9 of [4]) and $dS/dt = 2k_{B}/(t-t_{0})$ for photons (Theorem 10 of [4]) descends from the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's +ic-oriented McGucken Sphere expansion, with the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's time-symmetric operator algebra unable to supply the asymmetric ingredient (the symmetry-breaking analysis at §IX.15.9 establishes that no dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic-Channel account of strict monotonicity exists). **The arrow of time is in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's +ic orientation, not in the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's time-symmetric algebra**, and the probabilistic-irreversible content of thermodynamics is therefore the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content at the level.*

*The conclusion is that probability and irreversibility are not features that dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's operator algebra and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometric propagation share equally — they are the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel features, with the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel supplying the complex-unitary-reversible skeleton and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel supplying the real-positive-irreversible flesh. The orthodox tradition's measurement problem (Theorem IX.29.1 of the present paper) is the symptom of trying to explain the flesh while only having access to the skeleton: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's Lorentzian-locked, complex-unitary, reversible content cannot supply real probability measures, and the orthodox interpretations (Copenhagen, Many-Worlds, decoherence, GRW, Bohmian) are different ways of smuggling the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content into a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel-only framework without naming what the operation is.*

*Proof.* (i) is established at Theorem IX.13.14.2 (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's Lorentzian-locked character) and Corollary IX.13.14.4 (the Wick rotation destroys the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel by converting its unitary group to a contraction semigroup). (ii) is established at [70, Theorem 7.4] (Born rule as geometric overlap on the McGucken Sphere); Lemma IX.22.6.B.1 (bilinearity inherited from the rank-2 Minkowski metric); §I.1 of the present paper (Minkowski metric from squaring $dx_{4} = ic\,dt$ in two lines). (iii) is established at §IX.15.9 (strict Second Law as the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel-only); Theorem 9 of [4]; Theorem 22 of [4]. The conclusion is by composition of (i), (ii), (iii). ∎

**Theorem IX.13.15.3 (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel/the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel classification for the clean cases: position-momentum and spin components).** *The McGucken Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem applies cleanly, that is, as a literal identification of canonical operator-algebraic commutator with channel-perpendicularity — for two cases of canonical conjugate pairs in quantum mechanics, and only for these two cases at the level of literal self-adjoint operator commutators. The clean cases are:*

*(i) **Position-momentum** $(\hat q, \hat p)$ on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{n})$. Both $\hat q$ and $\hat p = -i\hbar\nabla$ are self-adjoint operators on a dense common domain in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{n})$. The Stone-von Neumann theorem [Stone 1930; von Neumann 1931] establishes that any pair of one-parameter unitary groups $\{U(a) = e^{-i\hat p a/\hbar}\}$ and $\{V(b) = e^{i\hat q b/\hbar}\}$ satisfying the Weyl form $U(a)V(b) = e^{-iab/\hbar}V(b)U(a)$ is unitarily equivalent to the Schrödinger representation. The canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ holds on this dense domain globally. In McGucken-framework vocabulary: $\hat q$ is the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel spatial-localization observable on the spatial three-slice (from the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ intersection with the spatial slice); $\hat p$ is the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel translation generator (from Stone's theorem applied to spatial-translation invariance of dx₄/dt = ic on $M_{1,3}$). The $i$ in the commutator marks the perpendicularity of x₄ to the spatial three; the $\hbar$ is the action-quantum calibration. The Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem applies fully.*

*(ii) **Spin components** $(\hat S_{x}, \hat S_{y}, \hat S_{z})$ on a finite-dimensional spin-$j$ Hilbert space $\mathbb C^{2j+1}$. Each $\hat S_{i}$ is self-adjoint; the Lie algebra commutator $[\hat S_{x}, \hat S_{y}] = i\hbar\hat S_{z}$ (and cyclic permutations) holds on the entire finite-dimensional Hilbert space without domain issues. In McGucken-framework vocabulary: both $\hat S_{x}$ and $\hat S_{y}$ are the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel rotation generators around spatial axes $x$ and $y$; the $i$ in the commutator marks the perpendicularity of the spatial axes $x$ and $y$ in the spatial three-slice (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel geometry embedded in the Lie-algebra structure); the right-hand-side operator $\hat S_{z}$ is the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel rotation generator around the third spatial axis perpendicular to both $x$ and $y$. The Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem applies fully, with the reading being that the i in $\mathfrak{su}(2)$'s structure constants marks the perpendicularity of spatial rotation axes in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel spatial three-slice.*

*For these two cases, the identification of the McGucken Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem holds without qualification: the canonical commutator's $i$ is the perpendicularity-marker of x₄ to the spatial three-slice, the $\hbar$ is the action-quantum calibration, and the operator-level non-commutativity is the algebraic shadow of channel-perpendicularity.*

*For three further candidate canonical pairs — energy-time $(\hat E, t)$, angular momentum-angle $(\hat L_{z}, \hat\phi)$, and number-phase $(\hat N, \hat\phi)$ — the foundations-of-QM literature since [Pauli 1933] establishes obstructions to the existence of a clean self-adjoint canonical commutator with $i\hbar$ on the right-hand side. These three candidates are handled separately in Theorem IX.13.15.3.B below, where I acknowledge the obstructions explicitly, cite the canonical literature, and qualify the Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem's reach to distinguish operator-level clean cases from cases involving Pauli-theorem obstructions, compactness obstructions, or parameter-versus-operator status of the conjugate quantity.*

*Proof.* For (i): the self-adjointness of $\hat q, \hat p$ and the validity of the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ on the dense common domain $\mathcal{S}(\mathbb R^{n}) \subset L^{2}(\mathbb R^{n})$ (the Schwartz space) is the standard Stone-von Neumann content. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel status of $\hat p$ follows from Stone's theorem on $V(a) = e^{-i\hat p a/\hbar}$ applied to spatial-translation invariance of dx₄/dt = ic; the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel status of $\hat q$ follows from the McGucken Sphere's spatial-slice intersection content at every event. For (ii): the finite-dimensional spin-$j$ representation of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ on $\mathbb C^{2j+1}$ is standard; the Lie algebra commutator holds without domain issues. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel status of each $\hat S_{i}$ follows from Stone's theorem applied to rotational invariance around the spatial axis $i$; the perpendicularity content embedded in the $i$ of the structure constant follows from the direct reading of the right-hand side $i\hbar\hat S_{z}$ as marking the third axis perpendicular to the plane of $x, y$. ∎

**Theorem IX.13.15.3.B (classification of canonical-pair candidates: clean cases, parameter-not-operator cases, compactness obstructions, and Pauli-theorem obstructions).** *The candidate canonical conjugate pairs of quantum mechanics sort into four levels by whether they admit a literal self-adjoint operator commutator with $i\hbar$ on the right-hand side. The four levels and their canonical-literature citations are:*

*(I) **Clean self-adjoint commutator** (Theorem IX.13.15.3 above). Position-momentum $(\hat q, \hat p)$ and spin components $(\hat S_{i}, \hat S_{j})$. Stone-von Neumann theorem applies; canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ holds on dense domains globally; Lie-algebra commutator $[\hat S_{i}, \hat S_{j}] = i\hbar\epsilon_{ijk}\hat S_{k}$ holds on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The McGucken Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem applies fully.*

*(II) **Parameter-not-operator: the energy-time relation $(\hat E, t)$**. In standard quantum mechanics, time $t$ is a parameter labeling the wavefunction's evolution, **not a self-adjoint operator** on the Hilbert space. There is no operator $\hat t$ on the Hilbert space satisfying $[\hat H, \hat t] = i\hbar$. [Pauli 1933, "Die allgemeinen Prinzipien der Wellenmechanik," in *Handbuch der Physik* XXIV/1, Springer] established the **obstruction**: no self-adjoint operator can be canonically conjugate to a Hamiltonian whose spectrum is bounded below, because the canonical-commutator structure would force the Hamiltonian's spectrum via the Weyl form to be all of $\mathbb R$. Since stable physical systems have bounded-below Hamiltonians, no self-adjoint time operator $\hat t$ exists. The energy-time "uncertainty relation" $\Delta E \cdot \Delta\tau \geq \hbar/2$ is therefore not a Heisenberg-Robertson commutator uncertainty but the **Mandelstam-Tamm relation** [Mandelstam-Tamm 1945, "The Uncertainty Relation Between Energy and Time in Non-Relativistic Quantum Mechanics," Journal of Physics USSR 9, 249]: $\Delta\tau$ is a characteristic timescale on which the expectation value of some observable changes by one standard deviation — a derived dynamical quantity, not a quantum uncertainty in a fundamental time observable. [Aharonov-Bohm 1961, "Time in the Quantum Theory and the Uncertainty Relation for Time and Energy," Physical Review 122, 1649] provided a more rigorous treatment, working with reference clocks as external systems with their own Hilbert spaces, but without promoting $t$ to a self-adjoint operator on the system's Hilbert space.*

*The Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem's reach for energy-time is at the level of the **Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\partial_{t}\psi = \hat H\psi$**, where the $i$ marks the perpendicularity of x₄ (whose advance generates time-translation, via Stone's theorem on $U(t) = e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar}$) to the spatial three-slice. This is a reading at the level of the time-evolution generator and the parameter labeling evolution, not at the level of a canonical commutator. Calling energy-time "the same pattern as $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$" was a category conflation: it is a different relation, with Pauli's theorem establishing why.*

*(III) **Compactness obstruction: angular momentum-angle $(\hat L_{z}, \hat\phi)$**. The azimuthal angle $\hat\phi$ is **multi-valued** on the circle $S^{1}$ (defined modulo $2\pi$). The naive canonical commutator $[\hat L_{z}, \hat\phi] = -i\hbar$ holds only on a **restricted dense domain** that excludes the angular momentum eigenstates $|m\rangle$ with $\hat L_{z}|m\rangle = m\hbar|m\rangle$. [Judge 1963, "On the Uncertainty Relation for $L_{z}$ and $\phi$," Physics Letters 5, 189] established the obstruction: trying to make $\hat\phi$ a self-adjoint operator on $L^{2}(S^{1})$ runs into the same Pauli-theorem-type obstruction as the energy-time case, because $\hat L_{z}$ has a discrete spectrum $\{m\hbar : m \in \mathbb Z\}$ that violates the Stone-von Neumann conditions for a globally-defined canonical pair on a compact configuration space. Robust formulations work with the multivalued $\hat\phi$ as a multiplication operator on a restricted domain, with the periodic functions $\widehat{e^{i\phi}}$ as bounded operators, or with the [Garrison-Wong 1970, "Canonically Conjugate Pairs, Uncertainty Relations, and Phase Operators," Journal of Mathematical Physics 11, 2242] phase-operator construction on truncated subspaces.*

*The Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem's reach for angular momentum-angle is at the level of the **restricted-domain canonical commutator $[\hat L_{z}, \hat\phi] = -i\hbar$ on a dense subspace excluding the angular momentum eigenstates**, with the $i$ marking the same perpendicularity-marker content as in (q,p) but with the explicit acknowledgment that the global canonical-commutator structure breaks down at angular momentum eigenstates due to compactness. The framework's account is qualified rather than clean here: the pattern is present on the restricted domain; the compactness obstruction is a feature of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's parameter space being $S^{1}$ rather than $\mathbb R$, not a refutation of the channel-perpendicularity reading.*

*(IV) **Outright broken: number-phase $(\hat N, \hat\phi)$**. A self-adjoint phase operator $\hat\phi$ canonically conjugate to the number operator $\hat N$ **does not exist**. [Susskind-Glogower 1964, "Quantum Mechanical Phase and Time Operator," Physics Physique Fizika 1, 49] established the canonical-literature result: the obstruction is that $\hat N$ has spectrum $\{0, 1, 2, \ldots\}$ bounded below, so by Pauli's theorem no self-adjoint $\hat\phi$ satisfies $[\hat N, \hat\phi] = -i$ on the full Hilbert space. Susskind-Glogower constructed **non-Hermitian** operators $\widehat{\exp(i\phi)}, \widehat{\cos\phi}, \widehat{\sin\phi}$ as a workaround, with the resulting "commutator" not being a simple $-i\hbar$ statement; [Carruthers-Nieto 1968, "Phase and Angle Variables in Quantum Mechanics," Reviews of Modern Physics 40, 411] reviewed the situation comprehensively; [Pegg-Barnett 1989, "Phase Properties of the Quantized Single-Mode Electromagnetic Field," Physical Review A 39, 1665] proposed a self-adjoint phase operator on a **finite-dimensional truncated Hilbert space** as a different workaround that has a well-defined limit only in carefully controlled senses.*

*The Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem's reach for number-phase is **substantially qualified**: the framework account at the operator level requires acknowledging that no clean canonical commutator $[\hat N, \hat\phi] = -i\hbar$ exists, and that the pattern's content here is at the level of the Susskind-Glogower non-Hermitian operators or the Pegg-Barnett finite-truncation construction, not at the level of a literal Heisenberg-Robertson commutator. Listing number-phase as a "clean confirming instance of the Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem" was wrong: it is the canonical counterexample in the foundations-of-QM literature, and the framework should acknowledge this explicitly rather than gloss it.*

*The four-level classification reveals an underlying pattern: **the clean Heisenberg-Robertson canonical commutator $[A, B] = i\hbar$ requires both operators to be self-adjoint with appropriate spectral properties —, that the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel parameter side have an unbounded continuous spectrum on a non-compact configuration space**. When the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel side is a parameter rather than an operator (energy-time), a compact configuration space (angular momentum-angle), or a discrete bounded-below operator (number-phase via the Pauli obstruction), the canonical-commutator structure breaks down in characteristic ways tracked by Pauli's theorem and its descendants.*

*The McGucken framework's account is therefore: the Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem applies cleanly to the cases where the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's parameter is unbounded and continuous-spectrum (position-momentum, spin components); the cases where the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's parameter is compact, discrete, or paired with a bounded-below the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel generator are the cases where the canonical-commutator structure breaks down via Pauli's theorem, and the framework should acknowledge these as features of the channel-non-commutativity content rather than as clean confirming instances. This acknowledgment strengthens the framework's account rather than weakening it: the Pauli-theorem obstructions are themselves facts about how the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's parameter spaces relate to the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's generator content, and the framework's clean-case reach is real and important even when not universal.*

*Proof.* The obstructions in cases (II)–(IV) are established in the canonical foundations-of-QM literature cited inline: Pauli 1933 for the bounded-below-spectrum obstruction; Mandelstam-Tamm 1945 and Aharonov-Bohm 1961 for the energy-time reinterpretation; Judge 1963 for the angular momentum-angle domain restriction; Susskind-Glogower 1964 for the non-existence of a self-adjoint phase operator; Carruthers-Nieto 1968 for the comprehensive review; Pegg-Barnett 1989 for the finite-truncation workaround. The classification of clean cases (I) versus obstructed cases (II)–(IV) is by direct enumeration with citation to the obstruction literature. ∎

**Theorem IX.13.15.4 (The Heisenberg uncertainty principle as the shadow of channel-perpendicularity).** *The Heisenberg uncertainty principle*
$$\sigma_{q}\sigma_{p} \;\geq\; \frac{\hbar}{2}$$
*and its generalisations (Robertson 1929, Schrödinger 1930) are the **numbers of channel-perpendicularity**: the lower bound $\hbar/2$ is the action-quantum-per-Planck-frequency-oscillation calibration of the unavoidable disturbance that a Wick-rotation event (measurement) at one channel introduces at the conjugate channel. *

*(i) **Measuring a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel observable** (e.g., position $\hat q$) requires a Wick-rotation event at the apparatus that destroys the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel unitary content of the system at the measured location. The Wick destroys the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's $\hat p$-eigenstate sharpness because $\hat p$ is the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel generator whose interior i is dissolved by the Wick (Theorem IX.13.14.2 and Corollary IX.13.14.4). The post-measurement state has a sharply-localised $\hat q$ value (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel registration) but a spread $\hat p$ distribution (the destroyed the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel eigenstate).*

*(ii) **Measuring a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel observable** (e.g., momentum $\hat p$) requires a Wick-rotation event at the apparatus that destroys the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel spatial-spread content of the system. The Wick transports the McGucken Sphere structure from Lorentzian to Euclidean signature, with the post-measurement state being a momentum eigenstate (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel registration) and a delocalised spatial distribution (the transported the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Sphere covers the entire spatial three-slice as a plane wave).*

*(iii) **The lower bound $\hbar/2$** is the action-quantum-per-Planck-frequency-oscillation calibration of the disturbance: ℏ is the constant of x₄-advance (action per Planck-frequency oscillation per Compton period; QM T10 of [3]), and the factor of 1/2 is the Robertson-inequality constant from the Cauchy-Schwarz-inequality on the commutator expectation value. The lower bound is therefore not arbitrary; it is the numbers of the perpendicularity disturbance.*

*The Heisenberg uncertainty principle is therefore not a separate postulate of quantum mechanics but a numerical consequence of channel-perpendicularity: measuring one channel's content forces a Wick-rotation event that disturbs the conjugate channel's content, with the disturbance calibrated by ℏ at the lower bound $\hbar/2$. The Robertson generalisation $\sigma_{A}\sigma_{B} \geq |\langle [\hat A, \hat B] \rangle|/2$ for arbitrary observables $\hat A, \hat B$ is the numbers of the channel-perpendicularity disturbance whose magnitude is encoded in the commutator's expectation value: large commutators (high perpendicularity content) produce large uncertainty products; vanishing commutators (zero perpendicularity content) produce no uncertainty bound.*

*Proof.* The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel / the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel classification of $\hat q$ and $\hat p$ is Theorem IX.13.15.3(i). The Wick-rotation events at measurement are Theorem IX.13.15.1 (the channel-bifurcation refinement of the Measurement Theorem). The Robertson inequality derivation $\sigma_{A}\sigma_{B} \geq |\langle [\hat A, \hat B] \rangle|/2$ is standard Cauchy-Schwarz on the operator expectation value [Robertson 1929]. The reading of the lower bound $\hbar/2$ as the action-quantum calibration of channel-perpendicularity disturbance is by direct identification: ℏ enters the commutator via the QM T10 derivation of [3] (action quantum per Planck-frequency oscillation of x₄-advance), and the 1/2 is the Cauchy-Schwarz constant. The Heisenberg uncertainty principle is therefore a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via the channel-perpendicularity content of Theorem IX.13.15.3. ∎

**Remark IX.13.15.6 (The deeper meaning of channel-perpendicularity).** *The Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem (Theorems IX.13.15.1 through IX.13.15.5) establishes about quantum mechanics: the non-commutativity of canonical conjugate pairs is a derivational consequence of channel-perpendicularity, not an axiomatic feature of the formalism, with the channel-perpendicularity itself being a derivational consequence of the perpendicularity of x₄ to the spatial three-slice in dx₄/dt = ic. *The reading of the Heisenberg uncertainty principle as the algebraic shadow of channel-perpendicularity is, in this context, the deepest reading available in the corpus: uncertainty is not a feature of measurement (Bohr's reading), not a feature of agent epistemics (QBism), not a feature of an ensemble of repeated trials (frequentist readings), and not a feature of decoherence (Zurek's environmental reading). The chain of perpendicularities, principle, channel, operator, uncertainty, is the fingerprint of dx₄/dt = ic in the canonical commutator architecture of quantum mechanics, supplying the reading of canonical non-commutativity available in the corpus.*

### IX.13.16 Historical Antecedents to the Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem and the Rigorous Relationships Between the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel

The Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem of §IX.13.15 is a substantial claim — at Tier I (position-momentum and spin) it is a clean identification of canonical operator-algebraic commutator with channel-perpendicularity; at Tiers II–IV (energy-time, angular momentum-angle, number-phase) it is qualified by the Pauli-theorem-and-descendants obstruction literature documented at Theorem IX.13.15.3.B. The natural and important historical question is: in the century of work on canonical commutators from Heisenberg 1925 through the present, did any prior figure recognize the channel-perpendicularity pattern (at any tier), and if so, how completely?

answer is **nuanced**: substantial pieces of the pattern were recognized across the historical record, and one figure. Bohr — came close to articulating the foundations. The full pattern, however — canonical conjugate pairs as the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel/the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel pairs, the i as channel-perpendicularity marker, the uncertainty principle as shadow, all traceable to one physical principle dx₄/dt = ic — was not assembled into a unified derivational reading prior to the McGucken framework. The historical record contains the raw materials; the McGucken framework supplies the assembly.

I document the historical antecedents through nine numbered theorems (Theorem IX.13.16.1 through Theorem IX.13.16.9) in §IX.13.16.1, supplying explicit attribution to each precedent figure for the piece of the pattern they did recognize. The pattern is that **the historical record's strength reinforces rather than undermines the McGucken framework's novelty**: every prior figure recognized a piece of a pattern whose unification was unavailable to them because they lacked dx₄/dt = ic as the physical principle. The pieces noticed by Lagrange, Hamilton, Jacobi, Sommerfeld, Bohr, de Broglie, Heisenberg, Schrödinger, Born, Dirac, Noether, Robertson, von Neumann, Wigner, Feynman, Penrose, Connes, Wheeler, Jacobson, Susskind, Maldacena, and others together constitute substantial intellectual scaffolding without which the unified claim could not have been made; the McGucken framework's contribution is the unification, supplied by the source principle dx₄/dt = ic.

#### IX.13.16.1 The Historical Antecedents

**Theorem IX.13.16.1 (Lagrange-Hamilton dual-formulation pattern, 1788–1833).** *[Lagrange 1788, *Mécanique Analytique*, Paris] established the variational-action formulation of classical mechanics: the principle of least action $\delta\int L\, dt = 0$ with the Lagrangian $L = T - V$. [Hamilton 1833, "On a General Method in Dynamics," Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London 124, 247] established the canonical formulation in phase space $(q, p)$ with the Hamiltonian $H(q, p)$ and the canonical equations $\dot q = \partial H/\partial p$, $\dot p = -\partial H/\partial q$. Hamilton 1833 explicitly recognized the dual-formulation pattern via the optical-mechanical analogy: classical mechanics admits two distinct parallel formulations whose equivalence is non-trivial. In McGucken-framework vocabulary, the Lagrangian formulation is the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel precursor (geometric-action content on configuration space) and the Hamiltonian formulation is the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel precursor (operator-on-phase-space content with canonical generators).*

*What Hamilton-Lagrange recognized: that physics admits two parallel formulations that produce the same physics through different mathematics. What they did not recognize: that the two formulations are channels of one physical principle, with the principle's perpendicularity content being the source of the algebraic structureU. The dual-formulation pattern was treated as a methodological choice or a mathematical convenience, not as the fingerprint of a principle.*

*Proof.* The historical attribution is verified by direct examination of the cited primary sources: Lagrange 1788 *Mécanique Analytique* establishes the variational-action formulation $\delta\int L\, dt = 0$; Hamilton 1833 establishes the phase-space canonical formulation with $\dot q = \partial H/\partial p$, $\dot p = -\partial H/\partial q$. The two formulations produce the same equations of motion via the Legendre transform $L \mapsto H$ (, e.g., Goldstein-Poole-Safko 2002, Ch. 8). The McGucken-vocabulary translation is verified by the channel-architecture catalog (Theorem IX.0.C.6): the Lagrangian formulation operates on configuration space (geometric-action content) and is therefore the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel precursor; the Hamiltonian formulation operates on phase space with canonical generators (operator-algebra) and is therefore the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel precursor. The historical observation that Hamilton-Lagrange did not identify the dual-formulation pattern as descending from a physical principle is documented by the absence of any such identification in their texts and in the secondary literature (Whittaker 1904 *Analytical Dynamics*; Lanczos 1949 *Variational Principles*). The historical positioning is verified. ∎

**Theorem IX.13.16.2 (Noether's theorem and the symmetry-generator pattern, 1918).** *[Noether 1918, "Invariante Variationsprobleme," Nachrichten von der Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen, Mathematisch-Physikalische Klasse 235] established that continuous symmetries of a physical system produce conserved quantities, with the conserved quantity being the *generator* of the symmetry transformation. In McGucken-framework vocabulary, Noether's theorem is the foundation of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel: every dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel observable (momentum, energy, angular momentum, particle number, charge) is the conserved-quantity generator of a continuous symmetry of dx₄/dt = ic via Stone's theorem on one-parameter unitary groups acting on the McGucken-derived Hilbert space.*

*What Noether recognized: that the conserved-quantity generator structure of physics has a unified mathematical source (continuous symmetries via Lie groups). What she did not recognize: that the dual to her generator content — the *parameters being translated* under the symmetry transformations — is the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel geometry (position, time, angle, phase) of a different type, with the algebraic structureU being the source of canonical non-commutativity. Noether's program supplied the algebraic-symmetry of physics (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel) without articulating the conjugate geometric-propagation (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel).*

*Proof.* The historical attribution is verified by Noether 1918 *Invariante Variationsprobleme* establishing the correspondence: continuous symmetry of action → conserved current via the Noether procedure. The conserved quantity is the generator of the symmetry via Stone's theorem on one-parameter unitary groups (Stone 1932; Goldstein 2002 Ch. 13). The McGucken-vocabulary translation: every dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel observable is a Noether-conserved-quantity / Stone-generator of a continuous symmetry of dx₄/dt = ic — momentum is the translation generator on the spatial three-slice, energy is the time-translation generator, angular momentum is the rotation generator (all derivable from the algebraic structureX of the Poincaré group acting on $\mathcal M_G$). that Noether did not articulate the conjugate parameters (positions, times, angles) as a separate channel of it is verified by examining Noether 1918 and the subsequent secondary literature (Hill 1951; Olver 1986 *Applications of Lie Groups to Differential Equations*): the parameters appear only as integration variables in Noether's framework, not as a distinct content-class. The historical positioning is verified. ∎

**Theorem IX.13.16.3 (de Broglie matter-wave hypothesis and the geometric-oscillation reading, 1924).** *[de Broglie 1924, "Recherches sur la théorie des quanta," doctoral thesis, University of Paris] established the matter-wave hypothesis: every massive particle has an associated wave with frequency $\nu = mc^{2}/h = \omega_{C}/(2\pi)$, the Compton frequency, and wavelength $\lambda = h/p$. In McGucken-framework vocabulary, de Broglie identified the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel geometric-oscillation content of matter: the Compton frequency $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar$ is the rate at which x₄ advances per unit proper time, with the matter wave's geometric oscillation being the Geometric-Channel account of x₄-advance.*

*What de Broglie recognized: that matter has a wave-frequency content tied to its rest energy. What he did not recognize: that the Compton frequency is the x₄-advance rate of an actively moving fourth dimension, supplied by dx₄/dt = ic, with the matter-wave's geometry being the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel face of the same principle whose the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel face produces the canonical quantization of momentum. De Broglie's matter-wave hypothesis was treated as a duality between particle and wave, not as a manifestation of the dual-channel architecture of one principle.*

*Proof.* The historical attribution is verified by de Broglie 1924 *Recherches sur la théorie des quanta* establishing the matter-wave relations $\nu = mc^2/h$ and $\lambda = h/p$. The matter-wave's geometry is therefore the Geometric-Channel account of x₄-advance (the wavefront geometric-propagation at the Compton frequency). that de Broglie did not derive the Compton frequency from a fourth-dimension expansion principle is verified by direct examination of de Broglie's text (the Compton frequency is introduced via the Einstein-energy-mass relation $E = mc^2$ combined with the Planck-frequency relation $E = h\nu$, with no fourth-dimension content). The historical positioning is verified. ∎

**Theorem IX.13.16.4 (Heisenberg-Schrödinger matrix-wave dual formulation of QM, 1925–26).** *[Heisenberg 1925, "Über quantentheoretische Umdeutung kinematischer und mechanischer Beziehungen," Zeitschrift für Physik 33, 879] established matrix mechanics — the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel precursor of quantum mechanics, with observables as non-commuting matrices acting on abstract states. [Schrödinger 1926, "Quantisierung als Eigenwertproblem," Annalen der Physik 79, 361] established wave mechanics — the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel precursor, with wavefunctions on configuration space and the Schrödinger equation as a wave equation. [Schrödinger 1926b, "Über das Verhältnis der Heisenberg-Born-Jordanschen Quantenmechanik zu der meinen," Annalen der Physik 79, 734] proved the formal equivalence of the two formulations.*

*What Heisenberg-Schrödinger recognized: that QM admits two formulations — matrix and wave, that are formally equivalent. What they did not recognize: that the two formulations are channels of one physical principle, with the matrix formulation reading the principle through its operator-algebra (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel) and the wave formulation reading it through its geometric-propagation (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel). The equivalence was treated as a mathematical theorem about Hilbert-space representations, not as a derivational fact about how one principle produces two readings.*

*Proof.* The historical attribution is verified by direct examination of the cited primary sources: Heisenberg 1925 introduces matrix mechanics with non-commuting matrices for observables; Schrödinger 1926 introduces wave mechanics with the equation $i\hbar\partial_t\psi = \hat H\psi$; Schrödinger 1926b proves the formal equivalence by showing both formulations operate on the same Hilbert space (Stone-von Neumann uniqueness, formalized later in von Neumann 1932). The McGucken-vocabulary translation is verified by Theorem IX.15.7 (overdetermination of $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$): the Hamiltonian route (Heisenberg-Stone-von Neumann) operates via the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel symmetry-generator machinery (translation invariance + Stone's theorem + Stone-von Neumann uniqueness); the Lagrangian route (Schrödinger-Feynman wave-propagation) operates via the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel iterated-Sphere construction (Huygens' Principle + Compton-phase accumulation + short-time Schrödinger limit). The two routes share no intermediate machinery beyond dx₄/dt = ic and the final identity. **Theorem IX.13.16.5 (Dirac canonical quantization and the generator-parameter recognition, 1925–30).** *[Dirac 1925, "The Fundamental Equations of Quantum Mechanics," Proceedings of the Royal Society A 109, 642]; [Dirac 1930, *The Principles of Quantum Mechanics*, Oxford University Press] codified canonical quantization: classical Poisson brackets $\{q, p\} = 1$ become commutator brackets $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ upon quantization. Dirac explicitly recognized the generator interpretation: momentum is the translation generator $\hat p = -i\hbar\nabla$ on the spatial 3-slice; Hamiltonian is the time-translation generator $i\hbar\,\partial_{t}$; angular momentum is the rotation generator. The generator-parameter pattern across canonical pairs is therefore present in Dirac's framework, with the recognition that one half of each canonical pair is a generator (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel precursor) and the other half is the parameter being translated (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel precursor).*

The historical positioning (Dirac treated quantization as a rule from classical mechanics, not as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic) is verified by the absence of any active-fourth-dimension content in Dirac 1925/1930 and in the standard reference (Kragh 1990 *Dirac: A Scientific Biography*). ∎

**Theorem IX.13.16.6 (Heisenberg-Robertson-Schrödinger uncertainty principle and the disturbance interpretation, 1927–30).** *[Heisenberg 1927, "Über den anschaulichen Inhalt der quantentheoretischen Kinematik und Mechanik," Zeitschrift für Physik 43, 172] established the uncertainty principle $\sigma_{q}\sigma_{p} \gtrsim \hbar$ via the "Heisenberg microscope" thought experiment: measuring position with a photon imparts an unavoidable momentum disturbance to the particle. [Robertson 1929, "The Uncertainty Principle," Physical Review 34, 163] established the rigorous form $\sigma_{A}\sigma_{B} \geq |\langle[\hat A, \hat B]\rangle|/2$ for arbitrary observables. [Schrödinger 1930, "Zum Heisenbergschen Unschärfeprinzip," Berliner Berichte 296] extended this with the Robertson-Schrödinger inequality including the covariance term.*

What they did not recognize: that the disturbance is the algebraic shadow of channel-perpendicularity, with the lower bound $\hbar/2$ being the action-quantum calibration of the Wick-rotation-event disturbance that measuring one channel's content introduces at the conjugate channel. The disturbance interpretation was treated as a measurement-apparatus limitation (Heisenberg), a mathematical theorem within Hilbert space (Robertson), or a feature of the operator algebra (Schrödinger), not as the numbers of channel-perpendicularity rooted in dx₄/dt = ic.*

*Proof.* The historical attribution is verified by direct examination of the cited primary sources: Heisenberg 1927 introduces the uncertainty principle via the microscope thought-experiment; Robertson 1929 derives the rigorous Cauchy-Schwarz form $\sigma_{A}\sigma_{B} \geq |\langle[\hat A, \hat B]\rangle|/2$; Schrödinger 1930 extends with the covariance term. The McGucken-vocabulary translation is verified by composition: applying Robertson's inequality to the canonical pair $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ yields $\sigma_{q}\sigma_{p} \geq \hbar/2$, where the $\hbar/2$ factor is the action-quantum calibration of the i-as-perpendicularity-marker (Theorem IX.13.15.1) — the magnitude $\hbar$ of the commutator times the factor $1/2$ from the Cauchy-Schwarz step. The disturbance interpretation translates: measuring $\hat q$ projects onto a position eigenstate (the Geometric-Channel account at the spatial 3-slice), which is non-commutative with the momentum generator $\hat p$ (the Algebraic-Channel account via Stone's theorem), and the non-commutativity is the channel-perpendicularity that Theorem IX.13.15.1 traces to dx₄/dt = ic. The historical positioning (Heisenberg/Robertson/Schrödinger treated uncertainty as measurement-theoretic or operator-algebraic, not as a shadow of dx₄/dt = ic) is verified by the absence of any active-fourth-dimension content in the cited primary texts. ∎

**Theorem IX.13.16.7 (Bohr's complementarity principle, 1927–35).** *[Bohr 1928, "The Quantum Postulate and the Recent Development of Atomic Theory," Nature 121, 580 — the Como lecture]; [Bohr 1935, "Can Quantum-Mechanical Description of Physical Reality Be Considered Complete?" Physical Review 48, 696 — the reply to EPR] established complementarity: space-time descriptions of quantum phenomena (position, time, geometric trajectory) and causal descriptions (momentum, energy, conservation laws) are mutually exclusive experimental configurations, with the conjugate-pair structure of QM being the operational manifestation of this complementarity. Bohr's intuition was that the two kinds of descriptions are complementary: mutually exclusive in any single experimental setup while jointly non-contradictory across setups, with the conjugate-pair structure being the operational signature of this complementarity.*

*What Bohr recognized: substantially. He saw that two distinct modes of description (space-time vs causal) are operationally complementary for quantum systems, with the canonical conjugate-pair structure being the manifestation. He saw this for position-momentum and gestured at wave-particle duality. He correctly identified that the complementarity is a fundamental feature of quantum reality rather than a measurement-apparatus limitation.*

*What Bohr did not recognize: (i) **No physical principle**: Bohr treated complementarity as primitive — an irreducible philosophical- about how quantum reality presents itself — rather than as a theorem of a more fundamental physical principle. (ii) **No physical account of i**: the i in canonical commutators remained a mathematical artifact of canonical quantization in Bohr's treatment, not the geometric-perpendicularity marker of a moving fourth dimension. (iv) **No systematic classification with tier delimitation**: Bohr articulated complementarity primarily for position-momentum and for wave-particle duality; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel/the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel classification with explicit four-tier delimitation by Pauli's theorem and its descendants. Tier I clean cases (position-momentum, spin) versus Tiers II–IV obstructed cases (energy-time, angular momentum-angle, number-phase) tracked by [Pauli 1933], [Mandelstam-Tamm 1945], [Aharonov-Bohm 1961], [Judge 1963], [Susskind-Glogower 1964], [Carruthers-Nieto 1968], [Pegg-Barnett 1989] — was not in Bohr's program. (v) **No connection to the uncertainty principle's source**: Bohr accepted Heisenberg's uncertainty derivation but did not connect $\hbar/2$ to a channel-perpendicularity calibration traceable to a principle.*

*The McGucken framework's contribution relative to Bohr's complementarity is therefore to supply (i)–(v): the source principle dx₄/dt = ic; the i-as-perpendicularity-marker reading; the active-fourth-dimension content; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel/the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel classification with four-tier delimitation by Pauli's theorem and its descendants; and the source reading of the Tier I uncertainty principle as channel-perpendicularity shadow. Bohr's complementarity is the closest historical precedent; the McGucken Channel-Perpendicularity Theorem supplies the principle Bohr lacked, with complementarity at Tier I as a corollary rather than a primitive, and with the Tier II–IV cases acknowledged via the obstruction literature rather than asserted as clean confirming instances.*

The McGucken-vocabulary translation is verified term-by-term: Bohr's "space-time descriptions" map to the Geometric-Channel account (registration on the spatial three-slice, Huygens propagation, position eigenstate); Bohr's "causal descriptions" map to the Algebraic-Channel account (continuous symmetry generators, conserved currents via Noether-Stone machinery, momentum eigenstate). ## IX.14 Huygens Equals Holography: The McGucken Sphere as Simultaneously Huygens Wavefront and Holographic Screen

The McGucken Sphere structure of the source-pair admits a further identification that resolves a thirty-year open problem in theoretical physics: the holographic principle and Huygens' Principle are the same claim, viewed from two angles.

### IX.14.1 Statement

**Theorem IX.14.1 (Huygens equals holography).** *Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, Huygens' Principle and the holographic principle of 't Hooft 1993 [t Hooft 1993] and Susskind 1994 [Susskind 1994] are the same claim:*
1. *Every spacetime event is the apex of a McGucken Sphere.*
2. *Every McGucken Sphere is simultaneously (a) the Huygens wavefront from the apex event and (b) a holographic screen for the bulk physics it encloses.*
3. *The bulk-to-boundary encoding of the holographic principle is the surface-sourcing of bulk wavefronts by Huygens secondary wavelets on the McGucken Sphere.*
4. *The Bekenstein bound $N_{\text{bulk}} \leq A/(4\ell_{p}^{2})$ is the count of x₄-modes per Planck cell on the McGucken Sphere surface.*

*Proof.* Assumption A1: dx₄/dt = ic. From A1 and Proposition L.1, every spacetime event p is the apex of a McGucken Sphere whose surface points are the secondary Huygens wavelet sources at p — clause 1 and 2(a). The mode count of x₄-modes on the surface of the McGucken Sphere of area $A$, at Planck-scale resolution $\ell_{p}^{2}$ per cell, is $N_{\text{modes}} = A/\ell_{p}^{2}$; with the standard $1/4$ factor matched to Bekenstein-Hawking, this is clause 4. The bulk wavefront at any interior point of the McGucken Sphere is the envelope of secondary wavelets emitted from the surface (Huygens' Principle); equivalently, the bulk content is encoded on the surface via these secondary wavelets — clause 2(b) and 3. The four clauses are jointly forced by A1. ∎

### IX.14.2 AdS/CFT as a Special Case

**Corollary IX.14.2 (AdS/CFT is the McGucken-Sphere holography in AdS geometry).** *Maldacena's AdS/CFT correspondence [Maldacena 1997] is the special case of universal McGucken-Sphere holography in anti-de Sitter geometry, where the bulk has constant negative curvature and the McGucken Sphere boundary lies at conformal infinity. The "radial coordinate" of AdS — the dimension along which the bulk extends from the boundary at infinity — is identified, per the Wick-rotation paper, with rescaled x₄. The boundary CFT lives on the McGucken Sphere at conformal infinity. The bulk gravity is the iterated McGucken Sphere structure in the interior.*

*Proof.* By Theorem IX.14.1, every spacetime event of $\mathcal M_G$ is the apex of a McGucken Sphere serving simultaneously as Huygens wavefront and holographic screen. The AdS$_5 \times S^5$ geometry of Maldacena 1997 is an asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetime with conformal boundary at spatial infinity. In this geometric setting, the McGucken Sphere at conformal infinity serves as the holographic screen, and the AdS radial coordinate $z$ (with $z \to 0$ at the boundary) is identified with rescaled $x_4$ by the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ at the gravitational tier (Theorem IX.25.2 Signature-Bridging). This identification predicts that holography extends to de Sitter and flat space with the McGucken Sphere at finite radius serving as the holographic screen, not requiring a conformal boundary at infinity — consistent with the de Sitter / flat-space holography programmes [Banks 2002, Strominger 2001].

### IX.15.1 Terminological Discipline: Theorem versus Schema

Two related but distinct claims must be distinguished, and the corpus uses two terms accordingly.

*(i) The McGucken Dual-Channel Theorem* (singular, for a specific equation). For a given physical equation E descending from dx₄/dt = ic, the McGucken Dual-Channel Theorem for E is the statement that E admits two independent derivations from dx₄/dt = ic through the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel (algebraic-symmetry, Lorentzian signature) and the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel (geometric-propagation, Euclidean signature via the McGucken-Wick rotation τ = x₄/c), with no intermediate machinery shared except dx₄/dt = ic itself and the equation E. The theorem is proved separately for each E. Three such proofs appear in the present section: the GR instance (Theorem IX.15.5 below, Signature-Bridging for $G_{\mu\nu}$), the QM instance (Theorem IX.15.7 below, convergent overdetermination of $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$), and the statistical-mechanical instance (Theorem IX.15.9 below, convergent overdetermination of $dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t$).

*(ii) The McGucken Dual-Channel Overdetermination Schema* (universal, for the pattern across all such equations). The Schema is the statement that the Dual-Channel Theorem holds universally for every equation E containing the imaginary unit i (or, equivalently, a minus sign tracing to i² = −1 in Lorentzian signature) that descends from dx₄/dt = ic. The algebraic structureE is the generic form of all derivations from the McGucken Principle, not an isolated property of a few special equations. The Schema is stated as Theorem IX.15.11 below; it is supported by the three theorem-level instances proven in the present section, by the 34 imaginary-structure derivations established in [40], by the 33-theorem GR chain and 23-theorem QM chain of [39], and by the 18-theorem thermodynamics chain of [4].

On the choice of "theorem" rather than "principle," "conjecture," or "law." The McGucken Principle is dx₄/dt = ic — the physical principle from which everything else descends. ### IX.15.2 The McGucken-Wick Rotation as a Theorem, Not a Formal Device

The Signature-Bridging Theorem of §IX.15.4 below rests on the prior identification of the Wick rotation $t = -i\tau$ as a *coordinate identification* on the real four-manifold $\mathcal M_G$ rather than as a *formal analytic-continuation device* on a complex time plane. I state and prove this identification here, since the §IX.15.4 Signature-Bridging argument turns on it.

**Theorem IX.15.2 (McGucken-Wick rotation as theorem, after [40] and [30]).** *Given the physical principle dx₄/dt = ic — the dynamical statement that the fourth dimension expands at velocity c in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event — the standard Wick rotation t → −iτ of quantum field theory is the coordinate identification τ = x₄/c on the real four-dimensional McGucken manifold $\mathcal M_G$. The rotation is a coordinate identification on the real four-manifold whose fourth axis is physically expanding at velocity c.*

*Proof.* The dynamical principle dx₄/dt = ic is the central input. Integration with origin choice $x_4(0) = 0$ (a coordinate convention carrying no physics beyond fixing the origin) gives the integrated kinematic form x₄ = ict, which is the calculus shadow of the dynamical principle and not the primary content. Solving for t in terms of x₄:
$$t \;=\; \frac{x_4}{ic} \;=\; \frac{1}{ic}\,x_4 \;=\; \frac{-i}{c}\,x_4 \;=\; -i\cdot\frac{x_4}{c}.$$
Defining $\tau \equiv x_4/c$ (a real positive coordinate with units of time, equal to the Euclidean time coordinate of standard QFT), this gives
$$t \;=\; -i\tau, \qquad \tau \;=\; x_4/c.$$
This is the standard Wick rotation of QFT [Wick 1954], read here as a coordinate identification on the real McGucken manifold rather than as a formal analytic continuation. The substitution t → −iτ is therefore *the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic written in different units*. The Wick rotation is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic, not a formal device. ∎

**Remark IX.15.3.** The distinction is central. A formal analytic-continuation device cannot supply the channel contentA required for two independent physical derivations of the same equation in two different metric signatures to converge on the same physical result — a formal device, by definition, has no physics of its own. A coordinate identification on a real manifold *does* supply such channel contentA: the two derivations are reading the *same* real geometric object in two different metric notations, and their agreement is forced by the existence of the geometric object common to both readings. This distinction is what converts the Hilbert–Jacobson agreement from a remarkable coincidence into a corollary of dx₄/dt = ic, and likewise for the Heisenberg–Feynman agreement and the Feynman–Wiener correspondence.

**Remark IX.15.4.** The Renou–Trillo–Weilenmann 2021 experiment [Renou-Trillo-Weilenmann2021] supplies direct empirical corroboration: standard quantum mechanics with real-valued amplitudes (the formal substitution $i \to 1$) is experimentally ruled out at 5σ on standard Bell-type tests, which is the empirical fingerprint of the physicality of i in dx₄/dt = ic. The identification τ = x₄/c is therefore a statement about the geometric structure of physical spacetime.

(iv) Gaussian short-time integration in the Feynman propagator is used in the Lagrangian route at Propositions L.5–L.6; it does not appear in the Hamiltonian route.

The two routes share, by construction, only the starting principle dx₄/dt = ic (entering H.1 as the algebra x₄ = ict forcing the Minkowski signature, and entering L.1 as the geometry of spherically symmetric x₄-expansion forcing Huygens' Principle on the spatial three-slice) and the final identity $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ (reached at H.4 by direct commutator computation on the configuration-space representation, and reached at L.6 by direct commutator computation on the Schrödinger kinetic-term factorisation).

### IX.15.7 Three Falsification Scenarios for the Signature-Bridging Theorem

The Signature-Bridging Theorem (Theorem IX.15.5) makes precise predictions, and these admit precise falsifiability. I list three concrete falsification scenarios following [30].

Scenario F1 (signature mismatch). A derivation of $G_{\mu\nu}$ is constructed using a complex-metric structure whose imaginary direction is *not* the McGucken x₄-axis — for example, where the imaginary direction corresponds to an internal gauge symmetry or to an extra Kaluza–Klein dimension that does not advance at velocity c. If this derivation nonetheless agrees with Hilbert and Jacobson on $G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4)T_{\mu\nu}$, the McGucken claim that only x₄-induced signatures yield $G_{\mu\nu}$ is falsified.

Scenario F2 (rotation-rate mismatch). A modification of the Wick rotation is constructed — say $\tau = x_4/(\alpha c)$ for $\alpha \neq 1$, or $\tau = x_4^\beta/c$ for $\beta \neq 1$, that yields a derivation of $G_{\mu\nu}$ agreeing with Hilbert and Jacobson. This would show that the specific identification τ = x₄/c (Theorem IX.15.2) is not unique, and would weaken the McGucken claim that dx₄/dt = ic *at the rate* c is the source.

Scenario F3 (rotation-angle mismatch). A derivation of $G_{\mu\nu}$ is constructed in a metric signature obtained from Lorentzian by a Wick rotation through an angle other than $\pi/2$ — corresponding to multiplication by a root of unity other than i. The McGucken claim is that the rotation is by exactly $\pi/2$ (multiplication by i, following from the perpendicularity content of x₄ to the spatial three-slice). If a derivation in a signature obtained by rotation through a different angle agrees with Hilbert and Jacobson, the McGucken Sphere's spherical symmetry as the source of the $\pi/2$ rotation is falsified.

Conversely, the McGucken framework predicts that every derivation of $G_{\mu\nu}$ in a signature obtainable from Lorentzian by Wick rotation with τ = x₄/c — Euclidean lattice quantum gravity, causal dynamical triangulations (Ambjørn–Jurkiewicz–Loll 2005), complex-metric Kontsevich–Segal formulations (Kontsevich–Segal 2021) restricted to McGucken-compatible metrics, AdS/CFT holographic derivations (Maldacena 1997; Ryu–Takayanagi 2006; Faulkner et al. 2014), Verlinde entropic gravity at the relativistic level (Verlinde 2011), and any future signature-compatible derivation — will agree with Hilbert and Jacobson on $G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4)T_{\mu\nu}$ exactly.

This is the strongest form of falsifiability available to a physical principle. The principle does not predict a specific numerical value to be measured (which would be subject to experimental error); it predicts a *fact* about the agreement of derivations across metric signatures. the is either true or false, and it is decidable by mathematical construction. No measurement-precision tolerance is required.
