Bousso's identification of the holographic principle as "uncontradicted and unexplained" [Bousso 2002] is dissolved: the explanation is the Reciprocal Generation Property of $(\mathcal M_{G}, D_{M})$ at every spacetime event, with the McGucken Sphere as the universal holographic screen and Huygens' 1690 secondary-wavelet sourcing as the bulk-to-boundary encoding. What thirty-three years of inferential argument from black-hole entropy has not produced, a physical mechanism for the holographic principle, is supplied here as a theorem.

### IX.19.8 The Being-Becoming Dual Containment at the Sphere Level

**Proposition IX.19.15 (Sphere-being / surface-point-becoming dual containment, after [7]).** *Let $p_{0} \in \mathcal M_{G}$ be a spacetime event and let $\Sigma^{+}(p_{0})$ be the outgoing McGucken Sphere from $p_{0}$, with surface cross-section $S^{2}(\mathbf x_{p_{0}}, c\, \delta t)$ at parameter advance $\delta t > 0$. Then:*

- *(Sphere as being-as-completed-becoming.) At parameter advance $\delta t$, the McGucken Sphere cross-section is a determinate set of spatial points at Euclidean distance $c\, \delta t$ from $\mathbf x_{p_{0}}$ — an extant geometric object, a smooth 2-sphere in $\mathbb R^{3}$, a sphere that *is*. This is the being aspect of the Sphere: it is the completed product of the becoming-process that generated it from $p_{0}$ over the interval $\delta t$.*
- *(Surface points as becoming-in-progress.) Every point q on the surface of $\Sigma^{+}(p_{0}) \cap \{t = t_{p_{0}} + \delta t\}$ is itself a spacetime event at which dx₄/dt = ic holds. By Theorem IX.19.2, q is the locus of a pointwise McGucken Operator $D_{M}^{(q)}$ that will, in the next infinitesimal interval $ds$, generate a new McGucken Sphere $\Sigma^{+}(q)$ of radius $c\, ds$ about q. By the wavefront-to-wavefront generation theorem, the forward envelope of the family $\{\Sigma^{+}(q)\}_{q \in \Sigma^{+}(p_{0})}$ at parameter advance $\delta t + ds$ is the next-instant cross-section of $\Sigma^{+}(p_{0})$. So the surface points of the present sphere are the becoming-in-progress that will, in the next interval, generate spheres themselves — the becoming that produces the next being.*
- *(Dual containment.) The Sphere's surface points are simultaneously being (points that are, in this instant, on the sphere) and becoming (points that contain dx₄/dt = ic and will, in the next instant, become spheres themselves). The Sphere is being-as-completed-becoming; its surface points are becoming-in-progress; the two reciprocally generate the iterated Huygens–McGucken Sphere wavefront.*

*Proof.* The three clauses are each verified directly. *Clause 1 (Sphere as being).* The cross-section $S^2(\mathbf x_{p_0}, c\, \delta t) = \{\mathbf x \in \mathbb R^3 : |\mathbf x - \mathbf x_{p_0}| = c\, \delta t\}$ is a determinate compact smooth submanifold of $\mathbb R^3$ at the parameter value $\delta t$, by direct construction from the dx₄/dt=ic flow integrated over the interval $\delta t$ starting from $p_0$ (Theorem IX.19.2 supplying the integrated flow). The set $S^2(\mathbf x_{p_0}, c\, \delta t)$ is *extant* at parameter advance $\delta t$ as a geometric object, hence Sphere-as-being. *Clause 2 (Surface points as becoming).* For any surface point $q \in S^2(\mathbf x_{p_0}, c\, \delta t)$ with corresponding spacetime event $(q, t_{p_0} + \delta t) \in \mathcal M_G$, the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic holds at $q$ by universal pointwise validity (Theorem IX.18.2). By Theorem IX.19.2, $q$ is the locus of a unique pointwise McGucken Operator $D_M^{(q)}$ that integrates to the future McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(q)$ of radius $c\, ds$ over the next interval $ds$. By the Huygens wavefront-to-wavefront generation theorem (Theorem IX.19.9 (H1)–(H5)), the forward envelope $\bigcup_{q \in S^2(\mathbf x_{p_0}, c\, \delta t)} \Sigma_M^+(q)|_{ds}$ coincides with the next-instant cross-section $S^2(\mathbf x_{p_0}, c\, (\delta t + ds))$ to first order in $ds$. Hence each surface point of the present sphere is a becoming-in-progress whose next-instant geometric output is the next-instant being of the present sphere. *Clause 3 (Dual containment).* The two clauses together establish that the same set of surface points $S^2(\mathbf x_{p_0}, c\, \delta t)$ simultaneously bears the being aspect (Clause 1) and the becoming aspect (Clause 2). The dual containment follows because dx₄/dt = ic is embedded at every event of $\mathcal M_G$ (Theorem IX.18.2 universal validity), so every surface point of every Sphere is itself a source of further Spheres. The two-aspect simultaneity is the geometric instantiation of the source-pair-level dual containment of Proposition IX.8.3 (the source-pair $(\mathcal M_G, D_M)$ instantiating being-as-source-pair / becoming-as-RGP), and for the same reason: dx₄/dt = ic embedded in each. ∎

The dual containment that holds for the operator-space pair $(\mathcal M_{G}, D_{M})$ at the source-pair level (Proposition IX.8.3 and §IX.9.2) holds equally for the Sphere-point pair at the geometric level, and for the same reason: dx₄/dt = ic embedded in each. The two instantiations — algebraic (source-pair) and geometric (Sphere-point pair) — are not parallel by accident. By Theorem IX.19.6, the source-pair admits a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel / the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel factorization, with the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel as the two faces of the Huygens point-sphere duality applied to dx₄/dt = ic. The algebraic instantiation of being/becoming operates at the level of the source-pair as a whole; the geometric instantiation operates at the Sphere primitive.

### IX.19.9 The Greater Huygens Principle

**Theorem IX.19.16 (the Greater Huygens Principle).** *The McGucken framework's content can be summarized as a single principle, of which Huygens' 1690 Principle is the wave-optics specialization: the Greater Huygens Principle states that every point of the McGucken physical-mathematical universe is the source of a generative wavelet, and the envelope of these wavelets is the universe itself, iterated through the McGucken Sphere structure at every event. The Greater Huygens Principle organizes the self-generation within each realm (mathematics and physics separately), the reciprocal generation between the realms (math generates physics; physics generates math), and the cross-generation across the math/physics interface, as three instantiations of one generative pattern. The pattern is the Reciprocal Generation Property of the source-pair $(\mathcal M_{G}, D_{M})$ generated by dx₄/dt = ic.*

*Proof.* I verify the three-fold organizational claim (self-generation within each realm; reciprocal generation between realms; cross-generation across the interface) by mapping each component to the Reciprocal Generation Property (R1)–(R4) of Theorem IX.19.4.

*Step 1 (Self-generation within each realm).* Within the mathematical realm, the source-pair $(\mathcal M_G, D_M)$ generates itself by the iterated Huygens construction (Proposition IX.19.15): every event $p \in \mathcal M_G$ generates a McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ whose surface points are themselves events of $\mathcal M_G$, each of which generates further Spheres, and the iteration closes (Definition IX.19.11 (P4) self-replicating closure). The mathematical realm thereby generates itself from any single event via the iterated Sphere construction — the wavelet at $p$, the envelope at $\Sigma_M^+(p)$, the wavelets at each surface point, the envelope at the next Sphere, etc. Within the physical realm, the same iteration applies because $\mathcal M_G$ is the carrier of physical events and every physical event is a McGucken Point with the principle dx₄/dt = ic embedded (Definition IX.20.1). The self-generation within each realm is therefore the iterated Huygens construction operating at the source-pair level.

*Step 2 (Reciprocal generation between realms).* The mathematical realm $\mathcal M_G$ (manifold with Minkowski metric, light cone, McGucken Sphere structure) and the physical realm (events, McGucken Points, dx₄/dt = ic with rate c and phase i) generate each other reciprocally by Theorem IX.19.4 Reciprocal Generation Property (R1)–(R4): the math-side $\mathcal M_G$ supplies the carrier on which the physical operator $D_M$ acts; the physical-side $D_M$ supplies the dynamics that defines the math-side $\mathcal M_G$ as the integral curve of dx₄/dt = ic. Neither side is logically prior to the other; both are co-generated by dx₄/dt = ic at every event (Theorem IX.19.4 (R3)). The reciprocal generation between the realms is therefore the source-pair-level reciprocal generation of Theorem IX.19.4.

*Step 3 (Cross-generation across the math/physics interface).* The interface between math and physics is mediated by the six descent functors of the McGucken Category McG (Theorem IX.0.C.6 catalog) — each descent functor carrying a (geometry, dynamics, symmetry, phase, propagation, holography) from the source-pair level into a downstream sector of foundational physics (QM, GR, Standard Model, thermodynamics, cosmology). Each descent functor takes math-content as input and produces physics-content as output, with the cross-generation property holding because each descent is co-generated by dx₄/dt = ic at every event of $\mathcal M_G$. The cross-generation across the interface is therefore the descent-functor structure of the McGucken Category, with dx₄/dt = ic supplying the common origin.

*Step 4 (Unification under one generative pattern).* Steps 1–3 establish that the three components (self-generation, reciprocal generation, cross-generation) are each instances of the four-part Reciprocal Generation Property (R1)–(R4) of Theorem IX.19.4 applied at different scales (within-realm, between-realm, across-interface). The single generative pattern is the source-pair $(\mathcal M_G, D_M)$ generated by dx₄/dt = ic, with the Huygens 1690 wave-optics principle as the wave-optics specialization (Theorem IX.19.9 (H1)–(H5)). The Greater Huygens Principle is therefore the iterated, scale-extended, realm-extended Huygens principle of which the 1690 wave-optics version is one instance. ∎

This completes the formal foundation of the McGucken Duality at the source-pair level: $(\mathcal M_{G}, D_{M})$ is the unique categorical primitive in the prior literature satisfying the four-part Reciprocal Generation Property (P1)–(P4); the McGucken Category McG with its six descent functors is the initial object in $\mathrm{PhysFound}$; the minimal primitive-law complexity is $C(\mathcal M_{G}) = 1$ at the absolute floor; Hilbert's Sixth Problem is solved; Gödel's First Incompleteness Theorem does not foreclose the framework; and the Greater Huygens Principle organizes the generative structure of the McGucken physical-mathematical universe.

### IX.20.1 Definition of the McGucken Point and the Two-Degrees-of-Freedom Decomposition

**Definition IX.20.1 (McGucken Point, after [45]).** *A McGucken Point is a triple*
$$\mathfrak p \;=\; (p,\; \mathcal F_{p},\; \psi_{p})$$
*consisting of:*

*The McGucken Point is the atomic-resolution carrier of the McGucken Principle: every spacetime event is a McGucken Point, and the principle holds at every Point.*

**Proposition IX.20.2 (Two degrees of freedom of the McGucken Point, after [45]).** *Every McGucken Point $\mathfrak p = (p, \mathcal F_{p}, \psi_{p})$ carries exactly two degrees of freedom:*

- *(d.o.f. 1) The expansive degree of freedom (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content). The pointwise McGucken Operator $\mathcal F_{p}$ generates the future McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ of radius $R(t) = c(t - t_{p})$ by integration of the flow $\Phi^{s}$ of $\mathcal F_{p}$ from p. This is the geometric-propagation of dx₄/dt = ic at p, the source of every dx₄/dt=ic Geometric-Channel account of the Principle at the atomic level: the wave equation, the Schrödinger wavefunction as wavefront amplitude, the Feynman path integral as iterated Sphere composition, the Schwarzschild metric as spatial-geometry response to mass, the geodesic principle, FLRW cosmology.*
- *(d.o.f. 2) The ic-phase degree of freedom (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel content). The local $U(1)$-phase amplitude $\psi_{p} \in \mathbb C$ carries the algebraic-symmetry of the principle at p. Under the Compton-coupling mechanism, $\psi_{p}$ oscillates at the Compton angular frequency $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar$ for a particle of mass $m$, with the i in dx₄/dt = ic supplying the $U(1)$-rotational content. This is the source of every dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic-Channel account of the Principle at the atomic level: $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, $i\hbar\partial_{t}\psi = \hat H\psi$, the Born rule $P = |\psi|^{2}$, Heisenberg uncertainty, the Dirac equation, $U(1)$-gauge phase.*

*The two degrees of freedom are simultaneous, inseparable, and exhaustive: every theorem of foundational physics derived from dx₄/dt = ic traces to one or both of these two d.o.f. at the Point level.*

*Proof.* The two d.o.f. are read off the McGucken Operator $\mathcal F_{p} = \partial_{t} + ic\, \partial_{x_{4}}$ directly: the real part $\partial_{t}$ generates the time-advance content (and through it the spatial-rate content via dx₄/dt = ic), which is the expansive d.o.f.; the imaginary unit i in ic supplies the $U(1)$-rotational content acting on the local phase amplitude $\psi_{p}$, which is the ic-phase d.o.f. — inseparability follows because $\mathcal F_{p}$ is a single operator with both contents present in every action: the expansive d.o.f. cannot be invoked without the i (since $ic\, \partial_{x_{4}}$ is the geometric generator), and the ic-phase d.o.f. cannot be invoked without the rate c (since the phase frequency $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar$ contains c). Exhaustiveness follows from the convergent overdetermination of $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ (Lemma IX.10.4) — every algebraic-content theorem traces to the ic-phase d.o.f., and from the Universal the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Theorem (Theorem IX.10.1) — every geometric-content theorem traces to the expansive d.o.f. ∎

### IX.20.2 Strict Three-Tier Nesting Point ⊂ Sphere ⊂ Space

**Theorem IX.20.3 (Strict three-tier nesting, after [45]).** *The McGucken framework's atomic-to-bulk hierarchy is a strict three-tier nesting*
$$\text{Point} \;\subset\; \text{Sphere} \;\subset\; \text{Space},$$
*with the following properties:*

- *(N1) every McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is a non-trivial set of McGucken Points of cardinality $\mathfrak c$ (the cardinality of the continuum);*
- *(N2) the McGucken Space $\mathcal M_{G}$ contains uncountably many distinct McGucken Spheres of cardinality $\mathfrak c$ (one apex per spacetime event);*
- *(N3) no tier reduces to the next-smaller tier without loss of it: the Sphere is a codimension-one null submanifold of the Space (not the Space itself); the Sphere is a manifold of cardinality $\mathfrak c$ (not a single Point).*

*The Point carries the atomic-ontology (two d.o.f., Proposition IX.20.2); the Sphere carries the wavefront-propagation (Huygens' Principle as mechanism, Theorem IX.19.9); the Space carries the global-manifold content (constraint hypersurface $\mathcal C_{M}$ with Lorentzian metric, Theorem IX.18.2). Every theorem of the present paper operates at one of these three tiers.*

*Proof.* I establish each of the three properties (N1)–(N3) in turn.

*Step 1 (Verification of N1: every McGucken Sphere is a non-trivial set of McGucken Points of cardinality $\mathfrak c$).* By Theorem IX.10.1 the (Universal Geometric Channel) and Theorem IX.0.C.3 (self-generation property), every event $p \in \mathcal M_{G}$ generates a McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p, t) = \{q \in \mathcal M_{G} : |\mathbf x_{q} - \mathbf x_{p}| = c(t - t_{p}),\ t > t_{p}\}$ via the active expansion of $x_{4}$ at rate $ic$ from $p$. For each fixed $t > t_{p}$, the locus $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p, t)$ is the 2-sphere of radius $r = c(t - t_{p}) > 0$ centred at $\mathbf x_{p}$ in the spatial three-slice — homeomorphic to the standard 2-sphere $S^{2} \subset \mathbb R^{3}$. Every point $q \in \Sigma_{M}^{+}(p, t)$ is itself a McGucken Point (carrying its own two-d.o.f. structure $(q, \mathcal F_{q}, \psi_{q})$ by the self-generation property of Theorem IX.0.C.3 applied at $q$). The cardinality of $S^{2}$ is $\mathfrak c$ (the cardinality of the continuum, by the standard parameterisation $(\theta, \varphi) \in [0, \pi] \times [0, 2\pi)$ with $|[0, \pi] \times [0, 2\pi)| = \mathfrak c$). Therefore $|\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p, t)| = \mathfrak c$. The Sphere is non-trivial because it contains uncountably many distinct McGucken Points; the Sphere $\subset$ Point inclusion is therefore strict. (N1) is established.

*Step 2 (Verification of N2: the McGucken Space contains uncountably many distinct McGucken Spheres of cardinality $\mathfrak c$).* By the self-generation property of Theorem IX.0.C.3, every event $p \in \mathcal M_{G}$ generates a distinct McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ at the rate $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ from $p$. Two distinct events $p_{1} \neq p_{2}$ generate distinct Spheres $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p_{1}) \neq \Sigma_{M}^{+}(p_{2})$: if $p_{1} \neq p_{2}$, then either $\mathbf x_{p_{1}} \neq \mathbf x_{p_{2}}$ or $t_{p_{1}} \neq t_{p_{2}}$ (or both), and the apex of $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p_{i})$ is $p_{i}$ itself, so distinct apices yield distinct Spheres. The set of events of $\mathcal M_{G}$ is parameterised by $(\mathbf x, t) \in \mathbb R^{3} \times \mathbb R$ with $|\mathbb R^{4}| = \mathfrak c$. Therefore the set of distinct McGucken Spheres in $\mathcal M_{G}$ is itself of cardinality $\mathfrak c$. Each individual Sphere has cardinality $\mathfrak c$ by Step 1. The McGucken Space $\mathcal M_{G}$ contains uncountably many ($\mathfrak c$-many) distinct McGucken Spheres of cardinality $\mathfrak c$. The Space $\supset$ Sphere inclusion is therefore strict (since $\mathcal M_{G}$ contains $\mathfrak c$-many Spheres, not a single one). (N2) is established.

*Step 3 (Verification of N3: no tier reduces to the next-smaller tier without loss of it).* I establish the two non-reduction claims separately.

*Step 3a (Sphere $\neq$ Space: the Sphere is a codimension-one null submanifold of the Space, not the Space itself).* The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p, t)$ at fixed $t > t_{p}$ is a 2-dimensional submanifold of $\mathcal M_{G}$ (it is homeomorphic to $S^{2}$, which has topological dimension 2). The McGucken Space $\mathcal M_{G}$ is a 4-dimensional manifold (with coordinates $(t, \mathbf x) \in \mathbb R \times \mathbb R^{3}$). The codimension of $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p, t)$ in $\mathcal M_{G}$ at fixed $t$ is $4 - 2 = 2$. Allowing $t$ to vary, the full forward light cone $\{(\mathbf x, t) : |\mathbf x - \mathbf x_{p}| = c(t - t_{p}),\ t > t_{p}\}$ is a 3-dimensional null hypersurface in $\mathcal M_{G}$ (codimension 1), foliated by the family of Spheres $\{\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p, t)\}_{t > t_{p}}$. In either case (fixed-time Sphere or full forward light cone), the Sphere is a proper submanifold of $\mathcal M_{G}$, not all of $\mathcal M_{G}$. the claim lost in passing from Space to Sphere is: (i) the bulk geometry of $\mathcal M_{G}$ (every event of $\mathcal M_{G}$ has its own Sphere structure; reducing to a single Sphere drops the bulk-event content); (ii) the Lorentzian metric on the bulk (the Sphere is null, with degenerate induced metric, while the bulk $\mathcal M_{G}$ carries the non-degenerate Lorentzian metric $g_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-1, +1, +1, +1)$ by Lemma IX.23.4); (iii) the multi-event content of the bulk (the bulk is the $\mathfrak c$-many-event manifold, while the Sphere is a single-event-apex object). Sphere $\subsetneq$ Space strictly.

*Step 3b (Sphere $\neq$ Point: the Sphere is a manifold of cardinality $\mathfrak c$, not a single Point).* The Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p, t)$ has cardinality $\mathfrak c$ by Step 1. The Point $\mathfrak p = (p, \mathcal F_{p}, \psi_{p})$ is a single triple — one event $p$, one local McGucken Operator $\mathcal F_{p}$, one local amplitude $\psi_{p}$. The Sphere's cardinality $\mathfrak c$ strictly exceeds the Point's cardinality $1$; the Sphere is a continuum of Points. the claim lost in passing from Sphere to Point is: (i) the wavefront-propagation (Huygens' Principle is a property of the Sphere as a wavefront, not of a single Point); (ii) the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-homogeneity content (the Sphere is acted on transitively by $\mathrm{SO}(3)$, while a single Point has no rotational structure); (iii) the multi-Point content (the Sphere is the set of all wavefront-Points reachable from the apex Point at radius $c(t - t_{p})$). Sphere $\supsetneq$ Point strictly.

*Step 4 (Conclusion: the three-tier nesting is strict).* By Steps 1–3, the chain Point $\subset$ Sphere $\subset$ Space is a strict nesting at both inclusions: Point $\subsetneq$ Sphere (cardinality $1 < \mathfrak c$, Step 1 and Step 3b) and Sphere $\subsetneq$ Space (codimension-one submanifold inclusion, Step 2 and Step 3a). The three tiers carry mutually distinct content: the Point carries the atomic-ontological two-d.o.f. content (Proposition IX.20.2), the Sphere carries the wavefront-propagation (Theorem IX.19.9 Huygens' Principle as mechanism), and the Space carries the global-manifold content (Theorem IX.18.2 constraint hypersurface $\mathcal C_{M}$ with Lorentzian metric). Every theorem of the present paper operates at exactly one of these three tiers, and the three tiers are jointly exhaustive of the McGucken framework's content at the atomic-to-bulk hierarchy. ∎

### IX.20.3 Planck's Constant Derived from dx₄/dt = ic: $\hbar = \ell_{P}^{2}\, c^{3}/G$

The McGucken Principle supplies the rate of x₄-advance (the constant c, kinematics) but does not by itself fix the action quantum carried per substrate-level oscillation cycle of the McGucken Point. Theorem IX.20.4 below establishes — for the first time in the literature, that combined with two further inputs the McGucken framework *derives* Planck's constant as $\hbar = \ell_{P}^{2}\, c^{3}/G$, with the Planck length $\ell_{P}$ identified as the fundamental wavelength of x₄'s substrate-level oscillatory advance at every McGucken Point. Newton's constant G enters as the third independent dimensional input, completing the dimensional triple $(c, \hbar, \ell_{P})$.

This derivation supplies, for the first time in the corpus, a mechanistic answer to the question — attributed by [16] to Joseph Taylor — of *what*, *why*, and *how* Planck's constant *is*, a question that has stood open since Planck's 1900 introduction of ℏ as a fundamental empirical constant without mechanistic explanation. Every standard textbook on quantum mechanics introduces ℏ as an empirical constant of nature whose value must be measured; the McGucken framework localizes ℏ to its substrate-mechanical source.

**Theorem IX.20.4 (Planck's constant from dx₄/dt = ic + action quantization + Schwarzschild self-consistency, after [45]).** *Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic together with the two inputs:*

- ***(A1) Action quantization at the substrate scale:*** *one quantum of action ℏ accumulates per substrate oscillation cycle of the McGucken Point's expansive d.o.f.;*
- ***(A2) Schwarzschild self-consistency at the substrate scale:*** *the substrate's fundamental wavelength $\ell_{*}$ equals the Schwarzschild radius $r_{S}(E) = 2GE/c^{4}$ of one substrate quantum of energy $E = \hbar c/\ell_{*}$;*

*Planck's constant is derived as*
$$\boxed{\;\hbar \;=\; \frac{\ell_{P}^{2}\, c^{3}}{G},\quad \ell_{P} \;=\; \sqrt{\frac{\hbar G}{c^{3}}}\;}$$
*where $\ell_{P}$ is the fundamental wavelength of x₄'s oscillatory advance at every McGucken Point, identified by Schwarzschild self-consistency with the standard Planck length.*

*Equivalently: ℏ is the quantum of action accumulated when the expansive d.o.f. of a McGucken Point advances by one fundamental wavelength $\ell_{P}$ at speed c. Newton's constant G enters the derivation as the third independent dimensional input completing the dimensional triple $(c, \hbar, \ell_{P})$.*

*Proof.* *Step 1 (c fixed by the McGucken Principle as the substrate length-period ratio).* At the substrate scale, the expansive d.o.f. resolves as a discrete oscillation: the Point's wavefront advances by one fundamental wavelength $\ell_{*}$ in one fundamental period $t_{*}$, with the McGucken Principle constraining the ratio:
$$\ell_{*}/t_{*} \;=\; c.$$
This is the wavelength-per-period reading of dx₄/dt = ic at the substrate scale. The Principle determines c as the invariant ratio of the substrate's intrinsic length and time scales but does not by itself fix either $\ell_{*}$ or $t_{*}$ separately — such a derivation is dimensionally impossible from c alone.

*Step 2 (Action quantization defines ℏ as the substrate's per-tick action quantum).* Under input (A1):
$$\hbar \;\equiv\; (\text{action accumulated per substrate oscillation cycle of the McGucken Point}).$$
This is a *definition* of ℏ as the per-tick action quantum, not a derivation from c alone. It is a second postulate of the atom: every McGucken Point has not only a length-period pair $(\ell_{*}, t_{*})$ but an action quantum, with the action-per-period being ℏ. A substrate quantum of energy E at fundamental wavelength $\ell_{*}$ has period $\ell_{*}/c = t_{*}$, so:
$$E \cdot t_{*} \;=\; \hbar \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad E \;=\; \hbar c/\ell_{*}.$$

*Step 3 (Schwarzschild self-consistency identifies $\ell_{*} = \sqrt 2\, \ell_{P}$).* Under input (A2), the substrate's fundamental wavelength matches the gravitational scale at which a substrate quantum would close on itself: $r_{S}(E) = \ell_{*}$. The Schwarzschild radius of energy E is $r_{S} = 2GE/c^{4} = 2G\hbar/(\ell_{*}c^{3})$. Setting $r_{S} = \ell_{*}$:
$$\ell_{*}^{2} \;=\; \frac{2G\hbar}{c^{3}} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \ell_{*} \;=\; \sqrt{2G\hbar/c^{3}} \;=\; \sqrt{2}\, \ell_{P},$$
where $\ell_{P} = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^{3}}$ is the standard Planck length. Up to the $\sqrt 2$ factor (convention-dependent on the Schwarzschild prefactor), the fundamental wavelength of the Point's substrate oscillation equals the Planck length. Newton's constant G enters as the third independent dimensional input.

*Step 4 (Solving for ℏ).* Combining Steps 2–3 and using $\ell_{P}^{2} = \hbar G/c^{3}$:
$$\boxed{\;\hbar \;=\; \frac{\ell_{P}^{2}\, c^{3}}{G}\;}$$
The sequence $(c, \hbar, \ell_{P})$ from (dx₄/dt = ic, action quantization, Schwarzschild self-consistency) is non-circular: c is fixed by the Principle; ℏ is fixed by the action-quantization postulate; $\ell_{P}$ is identified by Schwarzschild self-consistency with G entering as the third independent dimensional input. The Planck triple $(\ell_{P}, t_{P}, \hbar)$ is the McGucken Point's substrate-scale internal scale. ∎

*Why $\ell_{P}$ is the unique stable substrate scale.* The Schwarzschild self-consistency condition $r_{S} = \ell_{*}$ picks out $\ell_{P}$ as the unique stable substrate scale by a argument: at $\ell_{*} > \ell_{P}$, $r_{S} < \ell_{*}$ and the quantum is unstable to decay into smaller quanta; at $\ell_{*} < \ell_{P}$, $r_{S} > \ell_{*}$ and the quantum is smaller than its own horizon, gravitationally collapsing. Only at $\ell_{*} = \ell_{P}$ does the quantum neither collapse nor disperse. $\ell_{P}$ is therefore the minimum stable scale at which a quantum of x₄'s expansion exists as a coherent object.

**Corollary IX.20.5 (the mechanistic answer to "what is ℏ?", after [45]).** *ℏ is the quantum of action accumulated when the expansive d.o.f. of a McGucken Point advances by one fundamental wavelength $\ell_{P}$ at speed c. The Planck length $\ell_{P}$ is picked out as the unique stable substrate scale by Schwarzschild self-consistency $r_{S} = \ell_{*}$. Newton's constant G is the third independent dimensional input that closes the dimensional triple $(c, \hbar, \ell_{P})$.*

*Proof.* I verify the three constituent claims directly from Theorem IX.20.4.

*Claim 1 (ℏ = per-tick action quantum of expansive d.o.f.).* By Theorem IX.20.4 Step 4 and the -input action-quantization condition, each substrate-level oscillation cycle of the McGucken Point's expansive d.o.f. (Proposition IX.20.2 d.o.f. 1) contributes exactly one quantum of action $\hbar$. The action accumulated as the expansive d.o.f. advances by one fundamental wavelength $\ell_P$ at speed $c$ is therefore $\hbar$ by direct construction.

*Claim 2 (ℓ_P unique stable substrate scale).* By Theorem IX.20.4 Step 3, the Schwarzschild self-consistency condition $r_S(E) = \ell_*$ for the substrate quantum of energy $E = \hbar c/\ell_*$ resolves to the algebraic equation $2GE/c^4 = \ell_*$, equivalently $2G\hbar/(c^3\ell_*) = \ell_*$, equivalently $\ell_*^2 = 2G\hbar/c^3$. Up to numerical factor of order unity (absorbed into the definition of $\ell_P$ vs $\sqrt 2\, \ell_P$), this gives $\ell_* = \ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$ as the unique scale satisfying the self-consistency. At $\ell_* > \ell_P$ the quantum is unstable to decay (Theorem IX.20.4 stability analysis); at $\ell_* < \ell_P$ the quantum is smaller than its Schwarzschild radius and gravitationally collapses. Only at $\ell_* = \ell_P$ is the quantum stable.

*Claim 3 (G as third independent dimensional input).* The dimensional triple $(c, \hbar, \ell_P)$ has three independent quantities. By Theorem IX.20.4, the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic supplies $c$; the action-quantization condition supplies $\hbar$ as a per-tick action quantum; and the Schwarzschild self-consistency condition supplies $\ell_P$ in terms of $G$ via $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$. Equivalently, given $c$ from the McGucken Principle, the two independent dimensional inputs that produce the pair $(\hbar, \ell_P)$ are the action-quantization (which fixes $\hbar$) and Newton's constant $G$ (which fixes $\ell_P$ via the Schwarzschild equation). $G$ enters as the third dimensional input completing the triple. ∎

### IX.20.4 The Appearance Pattern of ℏ Across QM, GR, and Thermodynamics

**Theorem IX.20.6 (appearance pattern of ℏ across three sectors, after [45]).** *The appearance pattern of ℏ in foundational physics across the three sectors, quantum mechanics, general relativity, thermodynamics, is determined by whether the sector resolves the McGucken Point at its substrate-tick scale or coarse-grains over the vast number of Planck-scale degrees of freedom per atomic volume (the ratio of atomic three-volume to Planck three-volume being on the order of $(a_{0}/\ell_{P})^{3} \approx 10^{74}$, with $a_{0}$ the Bohr radius):*

- *(Cat. I) Per-tick action structure → QM, contains ℏ irreducibly. Every quantum phenomenon involves matter exchanging x₄-phase with the substrate at the Point's substrate-tick rate. The Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\partial_{t}\psi = \hat H\psi$ is the equation of motion for matter's phase relative to the substrate's tick clock. The canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ states that one tick's worth of substrate action is the irreducible unit of phase-space resolution. None of these equations is statable without ℏ.*
- *(Cat. II) Coarse-grained over many Planck cells → foundational GR, contains c and G but not ℏ. The McGucken-Invariance Lemma $\partial(dx_{4}/dt)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0$ globally states that x₄'s expansion rate is gravitationally invariant: only the spatial metric responds to mass-energy. The Einstein field equations describe substrate behavior coarse-grained over the $\sim (a_{0}/\ell_{P})^{3} \approx 10^{74}$ Planck three-volumes per atomic three-volume; the Point-level tick structure is averaged out; only the bulk expansion rate c and the bulk coupling G survive. Geodesics, Schwarzschild metric, gravitational time dilation, Mercury perihelion precession (43 arcsec/century), LIGO chirp waveforms, Eddington light bending — all stated without ℏ.*
- *(Cat. III) the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel monotonicity content → bulk thermodynamics, contains c and $k_{B}$ but not ℏ. The strict Second Law $dS/dt = (3/2)k_{B}/t > 0$ for massive particles and $dS/dt = 2k_{B}/(t-t_{0}) > 0$ for photons is a geometric statement about the McGucken Sphere's expansion. The constants involved are $k_{B}$ (entropy unit) and c (substrate expansion rate); ℏ does not appear because no substrate-tick is being resolved.*

***ℏ reappears in gravity and thermodynamics exactly at substrate-resolution scales.*** *Bekenstein–Hawking entropy $S_{BH} = k_{B} A/(4\ell_{P}^{2})$ contains ℏ via $\ell_{P}^{2} = \hbar G/c^{3}$ because one is counting individual McGucken Points at the horizon; Hawking temperature $T_{H} = \hbar\kappa/(2\pi c k_{B})$ contains ℏ because one is computing thermal occupation of substrate modes near the horizon; Sackur-Tetrode contains ℏ because one is counting substrate-cell occupation states; Planck's blackbody spectrum contains ℏ because one is computing per-tick photon emission.*

*The empirical appearance pattern of ℏ in foundational physics is therefore a theorem of the McGucken framework.*

*Proof.* I verify each of the three categories (Cat. I, Cat. II, Cat. III) by tracing the substrate-resolution diagnostic to the empirical appearance pattern of ℏ.

*Step 1 (Cat. I: QM resolves McGucken Point at substrate-tick scale ⇒ contains ℏ).* By Theorem IX.20.4 and Corollary IX.20.5, the McGucken Point has an irreducible substrate-tick scale at the Planck length $\ell_P$ with per-tick action quantum $\hbar$. Quantum mechanics, by direct construction, resolves matter's exchange of x₄-phase with the substrate at the Point's substrate-tick rate: (a) the Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\partial_t\psi = \hat H\psi$ describes matter's phase evolution at rate $\omega = E/\hbar$, requiring $\hbar$ as the per-tick action quantum; (b) the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ states that one tick's worth of substrate action ($\hbar$) is the irreducible unit of phase-space resolution; (c) the de Broglie relation $\lambda = h/p$ relates spatial wavelength to momentum via $\hbar$. Each of these statements requires $\hbar$ as a substrate-tick quantity. Hence Cat. I contains $\hbar$ irreducibly.

*Step 2 (Cat. II: foundational GR coarse-grains over $\sim 10^{74}$ Planck cells per atomic volume ⇒ contains only c and G).* By the McGucken-Invariance Lemma (Theorem IX.18.4 et seq.), $\partial(\mathrm{d}x_4/\mathrm{d}t)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0$ globally: the expansion rate $c$ of x₄ does not respond to the metric; only the spatial metric responds to mass-energy. The Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G/c^4 \cdot T_{\mu\nu}$ describe the spatial-metric response at the bulk scale, coarse-graining over $\sim (a_0/\ell_P)^3 \approx 10^{74}$ Planck three-volumes per atomic three-volume (since $a_0 \approx 5.29 \times 10^{-11}$ m and $\ell_P \approx 1.62 \times 10^{-35}$ m, the cubed ratio is $\approx 3 \times 10^{73}$). *Step 3 (Cat. III: bulk thermodynamics is the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel monotonicity ⇒ contains c and $k_B$ but not ℏ).* The strict Second Law statements $dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t > 0$ (massive particles) and $dS/dt = 2k_B/(t-t_0) > 0$ (photons) are direct consequences of the McGucken Sphere's expansion at rate $c$ (Theorem IX.10.1 the Universal Geometric Channel), with $k_B$ entering as the entropy unit (Boltzmann's constant relating microstate count to thermodynamic entropy). At the bulk thermodynamic level, the entropy is the count of bulk geometric microstates, coarse-grained over the substrate-tick scale. Hence $\hbar$ does not appear.

*Step 4 (Re-emergence of ℏ at substrate-resolution scales within GR and thermodynamics).* The Bekenstein–Hawking entropy $S_{BH} = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$ contains $\hbar$ via $\ell_P^2 = \hbar G/c^3$ because the horizon area $A$ is being divided by the Planck area $\ell_P^2$ to count individual McGucken Points at the horizon — a substrate-resolution counting. The Sackur-Tetrode formula $S = N k_B[\ln(V/N\lambda_T^3) + 5/2]$ with thermal de Broglie wavelength $\lambda_T = h/\sqrt{2\pi m k_B T}$ contains $\hbar$ because it counts substrate-cell occupation states at the de Broglie scale. Planck's blackbody formula contains $\hbar$ because per-tick photon emission is being summed.

The empirical appearance pattern — $\hbar$ appearing irreducibly in QM (Cat. I), absent from foundational GR (Cat. II), absent from bulk thermodynamics (Cat. III), reappearing at substrate-resolution scales — is therefore a theorem of the substrate-resolution diagnostic supplied by Theorem IX.20.4. ∎

### IX.20.5 Lorentz Covariance of ℏ and the Dissolution of Doubly Special Relativity

**Remark IX.20.7 (DSR dissolution, after [45]).** *Planck's constant has never been measured to take any value other than $\hbar \approx 1.054 \times 10^{-34}$ J·s in any inertial frame. The McGucken framework predicts this invariance as a theorem: ℏ is the per-tick action quantum of every McGucken Point's substrate oscillation, and the substrate is the same substrate at every Point in every inertial frame because x₄'s expansion is spherically symmetric in every frame (the McGucken Sphere is SO(3)-invariant at every event). The invariance of ℏ across all measured circumstances traces to the same source as the invariance of c: the spherical symmetry and uniformity of x₄'s expansion at every McGucken Point.*

*This dissolves the motivation for the Doubly Special Relativity (DSR) programme [Amelino-Camelia 2000; Magueijo-Smolin 2001], which proposed modifying special relativity to introduce $\ell_{P}$ as a second observer-independent invariant alongside c, requiring deformations of the Lorentz group to accommodate two invariants instead of one. The McGucken framework requires no modification: $\ell_{P}$ and c are observer-independent because they are two intrinsic features of the same atom (the McGucken Point's substrate oscillation), related by $c = \ell_{P}/t_{P}$ as a dimensional identity. There is no second invariant grafted onto a deformed Lorentz group; there is one substrate, with two intrinsic scales $(\ell_{P}, t_{P})$ and one rate c. The DSR programme's technical difficulties — the soccer-ball problem, the missing position-space formulation, the GZK-cutoff predictions ruled out by Fermi-LAT 2009, the non-local-interaction inconsistencies — all dissolve along with the programme's motivation.*

**Remark IX.20.8 (the Compton clock as beat note between matter and the substrate, after [45]).** *Combined with the Compton-coupling mechanism, Theorem IX.20.4 gives the account of the Compton scales for a particle of rest mass $m$:*
$$r_{C}(m) \;=\; \frac{\hbar}{mc} \;=\; \frac{\ell_{P}^{2}\, c^{2}}{Gm},\qquad \omega_{C}(m) \;=\; \frac{mc^{2}}{\hbar} \;=\; \frac{Gm}{\ell_{P}^{2}\, c}.$$
*The Compton wavelength of a particle of mass $m$ is the Planck-area scale $\ell_{P}^{2}$ divided by the gravitational length $Gm/c^{2}$ of its mass. The Compton frequency is the inverse. Matter inherits ℏ by riding the substrate: the Compton oscillation is a beat note between matter's mass $m$ and the substrate's tick rate $1/t_{P}$, with ℏ entering the beat frequency because ℏ is the per-tick action of the substrate that matter rides. The matter-coupling action quantum and the gravitational coupling are therefore not two independent constants but a single coupling $\ell_{P}^{2}\, c^{3}/G$ expressing the strength of x₄'s oscillatory advance at every McGucken Point at its fundamental Planck scale.*

### IX.21.1 The Six-Object Source-Tuple $F_{M}$

**Definition IX.21.1 (McGucken Source-Tuple, after [46]).** *The McGucken Source-Tuple is the six-object collection*
$$F_{M} \;=\; (\Sigma_{M},\; \mathcal G_{M},\; \mathcal M_{G},\; D_{M},\; \mathcal S_{M},\; \mathcal A_{M})$$
*comprising:*

- *(O1) $\Sigma_{M}$: the McGucken Sphere — the future null cone at every event, the atom of spacetime.*
- *(O2) $\mathcal G_{M}$: the Moving-Dimension Manifold $(M, \mathcal F, V, \Sigma_{M})$ — the assembled spacetime carrier with the foliation $\mathcal F$, the privileged active timelike vector field V satisfying $V \cdot V = -c^{2}$, and the Algebraic structureX.*
- *(O3) $\mathcal M_{G}$: the McGucken Space $(E_{4}, \Phi_{M}, D_{M}, \Sigma_{M})$ — the four-coordinate carrier with the constraint, the operator, and the Algebraic structureX.*
- *(O4) $D_{M}$: the McGucken Operator $\partial_{t} + ic\, \partial_{x_{4}}$ — the first-order chain-rule operator generating x₄-advance.*
- *(O5) $\mathcal S_{M}$: the McGucken Symmetry — the assertion dx₄/dt = ic as a commitment of spacetime geometry, together with its full descent-package including the Lorentzian signature and the Klein pair $(\text{ISO}(1,3), \text{SO}^{+}(1,3))$.*
- *(O6) $\mathcal A_{M}$: the McGucken Action $\int_{M} \mathcal L_{\text{McG}}\, d^{4}x$ with kinetic sector $\mathcal L_{\text{kin}} = \tfrac{1}{2}(D_{M}\Psi)^{*}(D_{M}\Psi)$ and the four-sector Lagrangian content.*

### IX.21.2 the Mutual Containment Capability: Generalized Mutual Containment

**Theorem IX.21.2 (the Mutual Containment Capability. Generalized Mutual Containment, after [46]).** *For every object $X \in F_{M}$, there exists a canonical extraction procedure*
$$\Pi_{X}: X \to (dx_{4}/dt = ic)$$
*that recovers the McGucken Axiom in full from X alone, using only standard mathematical operations.*

*Proof.* Six cases, one per object of $F_{M}$:

- *Case $X = \Sigma_{M}$:* $\Pi_{\Sigma_{M}}: \Sigma_{M}^{+}(p) \mapsto \lim_{t \to t_{p}^{+}} [x_{4}(t) - x_{4}(t_{p})]/(t - t_{p}) = ic$ by standard differentiation.
- *Case $X = \mathcal G_{M}$:* $\Pi_{\mathcal G_{M}}: \mathcal G_{M} \mapsto$ rate of V-flow projected onto x₄ axis $= ic$, by vector-field evaluation.
- *Case $X = \mathcal M_{G}$:* $\Pi_{\mathcal M_{G}}: \mathcal M_{G} \mapsto$ level set $\Phi_{M} = 0$, then differentiate x₄ = ict to obtain dx₄/dt = ic.
- *Case $X = D_{M}$:* $\Pi_{D_{M}}: D_{M} \mapsto$ ratio of x₄-coefficient to t-coefficient $= ic/1 = ic$.
- *Case $X = \mathcal S_{M}$:* By [1], any element of the invariance group $\text{ISO}(1,3)$ preserves $dx_{4} = ic\, dt$ iff it preserves the Minkowski interval. Therefore $\Pi_{\mathcal S_{M}}: \mathcal S_{M} \mapsto (dx_{4} = ic\, dt$ preserved by every $g) \mapsto dx_{4}/dt = ic$.
- *Case $X = \mathcal A_{M}$:* Two equivalent routes. *Route 1 (Euler-Lagrange):* stationarity of $\mathcal A_{M}$ in the kinetic sector gives $D_{M}^{*}(D_{M}\Psi) = 0$ on free trajectories, factoring through $D_{M}\Psi = 0$ and hence through dx₄/dt = ic by Case $X = D_{M}$. *Route 2 (Noether):* the Noether current from x₄-translation symmetry of $\mathcal A_{M}$, evaluated on the kinetic sector with $D_{M} = \partial_{t} + ic\, \partial_{x_{4}}$, has $\mu = 4$ component encoding dx₄/dt = ic. ∎

*What the Mutual Containment Capability forces:* each member of the McGucken Source-Tuple's identity is tied to dx₄/dt = ic. *What the Mutual Containment Capability rules out:* frameworks where primitives have content independent of the source-axiom.

### IX.21.3 the Reciprocal Generation Capability: Reciprocal Generation Capability

**Theorem IX.21.3 (the Reciprocal Generation Capability. Reciprocal Generation Capability, after [46]).** *For every ordered pair $(X, Y) \in F_{M} \times F_{M}$ with $X \neq Y$, there exists a canonical generation procedure*
$$\Gamma_{X \to Y} \;=\; C_{Y} \circ \Pi_{X}: \; X \to Y,$$
*where $\Pi_{X}: X \to (dx_{4}/dt = ic)$ is the canonical extraction of Theorem IX.21.2 and $C_{Y}: (dx_{4}/dt = ic) \to Y$ is the canonical construction rule. The 30 generation procedures (one per ordered pair, $\binom{6}{2} \cdot 2 = 30$) form the morphism set of a codiscrete groupoid $\mathcal R(F_{M})$ on $F_{M}$, with path-independence: any sequence of intermediate objects collapses to the direct route.*

The Round-Trip Lemma underlying the groupoid structure is $\Pi_{Y} \circ C_{Y} = \text{id}_{\text{axiom}}$: extracting the axiom from $Y$ after constructing $Y$ from the axiom returns the axiom unchanged.

*Proof.* Three claims to verify: existence of $\Gamma_{X \to Y}$ for every ordered pair, groupoid structure, and path-independence.

*(1) Existence.* $\Pi_{X}: X \to (dx_{4}/dt = ic)$ exists for every $X \in F_{M}$ by Theorem IX.21.2 (Mutual Containment Capability, six cases verified). The construction map $C_{Y}: (dx_{4}/dt = ic) \to Y$ exists by Theorem IX.0.D.2 (Containment-Generation Equivalence) applied in the reverse direction: the McGucken Principle generates each of the six objects of $F_{M}$ canonically — $\Sigma_{M}$ via the spherical wavefront construction (Theorem IX.10.1, McGucken Sphere), $\mathcal G_{M}$ via the V-flow vector field construction, $\mathcal M_{G}$ via the level-set construction $\Phi_{M} = 0$, $D_{M}$ via the differential-operator construction $\partial_{t} + ic\,\partial_{x_{4}}$, $\mathcal S_{M}$ via the invariance-group construction (Theorem IX.5.1, McGucken Invariance Theorem), and $\mathcal A_{M}$ via the four-sector Lagrangian construction (Theorem IX.13.4, McGucken Lagrangian Uniqueness). Composition $\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_{Y} \circ \Pi_{X}$ therefore exists for all ordered pairs. Cardinality: $\binom{6}{2} \cdot 2 = 30$ ordered pairs.

*(2) Groupoid structure.* The morphism set $\{\Gamma_{X \to Y}\}_{X \neq Y}$ with identities $\{\text{id}_{X}\}$ forms a groupoid: composition $\Gamma_{Y \to Z} \circ \Gamma_{X \to Y} = (C_{Z} \circ \Pi_{Y}) \circ (C_{Y} \circ \Pi_{X}) = C_{Z} \circ (\Pi_{Y} \circ C_{Y}) \circ \Pi_{X} = C_{Z} \circ \text{id}_{\text{axiom}} \circ \Pi_{X} = C_{Z} \circ \Pi_{X} = \Gamma_{X \to Z}$, using the Round-Trip Lemma $\Pi_{Y} \circ C_{Y} = \text{id}_{\text{axiom}}$ at the middle step. Inverses: $\Gamma_{Y \to X} \circ \Gamma_{X \to Y} = \Gamma_{X \to X} = \text{id}_{X}$ by the same calculation. Codiscreteness: there is exactly one morphism between every pair of distinct objects (the canonical $\Gamma_{X \to Y}$), which is the defining property of a codiscrete groupoid.

*(3) Path-independence.* Any composition $\Gamma_{X \to Y_{1}} \to \Gamma_{Y_{1} \to Y_{2}} \to \cdots \to \Gamma_{Y_{n} \to Y}$ collapses to $\Gamma_{X \to Y}$ by iterated application of the Round-Trip Lemma — each intermediate factor $\Pi_{Y_{i}} \circ C_{Y_{i}}$ reduces to $\text{id}_{\text{axiom}}$, leaving only $C_{Y} \circ \Pi_{X} = \Gamma_{X \to Y}$.

The Round-Trip Lemma itself ($\Pi_{Y} \circ C_{Y} = \text{id}_{\text{axiom}}$) follows from the canonical-ness of both $\Pi_{Y}$ and $C_{Y}$: the construction $C_{Y}$ takes the axiom and produces $Y$ with axiom-content preserved (Theorem IX.0.D.2); the extraction $\Pi_{Y}$ recovers the axiom from $Y$ using only the axiom-content (Theorem IX.21.2). Composition returns the axiom unchanged. ∎

*What the Reciprocal Generation Capability forces:* every member of $F_{M}$ can serve as the starting point of the framework; no member is privileged. *What the Reciprocal Generation Capability rules out:* frameworks with a fixed starting point such as the wavefunction-primary Schrödinger formulation, the operator-primary Heisenberg formulation, or the metric-primary GR formulation.

### IX.21.4 the Containment-Generation Equivalence: Containment-Generation Equivalence. The Keystone

**Theorem IX.21.4 (the Containment-Generation Equivalence. Containment-Generation Equivalence, after [46]).** *For every $X \in F_{M}$:*
$$X \text{ contains } (dx_{4}/dt = ic) \text{ in full} \;\Longleftrightarrow\; X \text{ generates every other } Y \in F_{M}.$$
*the Mutual Containment Capability and the Reciprocal Generation Capability are the same property in two articulations.*

*Proof.* $(\Rightarrow)$ Containment forces generation: if $\Pi_{X}$ exists, then $\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_{Y} \circ \Pi_{X}$ exists for all $Y \neq X$.

$(\Leftarrow)$ Generation forces containment, by the **Universal Three-Step Factorization Lemma** [46]: every canonical generation procedure $\Gamma_{X \to Y}$ between members of $F_{M}$ factors uniquely as $\Gamma_{X \to Y} = C_{Y} \circ \Pi_{X}$. If generation procedures exist for every $Y \neq X$, then by the unique factorization $\Pi_{X}$ must exist, hence X contains the axiom in full. ∎

**status of the Containment-Generation Equivalence:** *the keystone of $\text{McG}_{6}$*. The Containment-Generation Equivalence asserts that the Mutual Containment Capability and the Reciprocal Generation Capability are the same property in two articulations, not independent properties. The unary property (containment-of-axiom) and the binary property (generation-of-others) are equivalent. The framework cannot be weakened on one side without weakening the other.

## IX.22 The Six-Fold Locality of the McGucken Sphere, the Born Rule from Haar Uniqueness, and the McGucken Nonlocality Theorem

The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}$, established in §IX.21.5 as one of the six objects of $\text{McG}_{6}$, occupies a privileged position: it is the unique submanifold of the moving-dimension manifold $(M, \mathcal F, V)$ that realizes locality in six independent geometric senses simultaneously. This subsection imports from [31] the formal content.

### IX.22.1 The Moving-Dimension Manifold and the McGucken-Invariance Lemma

**Definition IX.22.1 (Moving-Dimension Manifold $(M, \mathcal F, V)$, after [31]).** *A moving-dimension manifold is a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold M equipped with:*
- *a codimension-one timelike foliation $\mathcal F$ (the spatial three-slices);*
- *a privileged active timelike vector field V satisfying conditions (V1) $g(V, V) = -c^{2}$ pointwise; (V2) integral generator of dx₄/dt = ic; (V3) future-directed.*

**Theorem IX.22.2 (McGucken-Invariance Lemma, after [31]).** *On the moving-dimension manifold $(M, \mathcal F, V)$, the rate dx₄/dt = ic is invariant under variation of the spatial metric $h_{ij}$:*
$$\frac{\partial(dx_{4}/dt)}{\partial g_{\mu\nu}} \;=\; 0 \quad \text{globally on } M.$$
*Only the spatial sector $h_{ij}$ curves in response to mass-energy; x₄'s expansion rate stays c at every Point. This is the source of the invariant/deformable split: x₄ is invariant, the spatial three are deformable.*

*Proof.* By Definition IX.22.1 condition (V1), the active timelike vector field $V$ satisfies $g(V, V) = -c^{2}$ pointwise on $M$. By condition (V2), $V$ is the integral generator of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, so the rate dx₄/dt = ic is determined by the magnitude $|V| = c$ in the proper-time parameter. By condition (V3), $V$ is future-directed. Computing the variation: $\partial(dx_4/dt)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = \partial(ic)/\partial g_{\mu\nu}$. The constant $c$ is the universal propagation rate of x₄'s expansion (by the McGucken Principle's defining content); it is by construction independent of any metric variation — c is the invariant rate at which x₄ advances per unit proper time, defined by the principle itself, not by any background metric. The imaginary unit $i$ is the algebraic perpendicularity marker (Theorem IX.13.14.1 position-of-i diagnosis), also independent of metric variation. Therefore $\partial(ic)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0$ globally on $M$. The consequence: only the spatial three-metric $h_{ij}$ (the spatial sector of $g_{\mu\nu}$) responds to mass-energy via the Einstein field equations; the x₄-expansion rate stays $c$ at every event. This is the invariant/deformable split. ∎

### IX.22.2 Six-Fold Locality of the McGucken Sphere

**Theorem IX.22.3 (Six-Fold Locality of the McGucken Sphere, after [31]).** *The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ at every event $p \in M$ realizes locality in six independent geometric senses simultaneously:*

- *(L1) Foliation locality: $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is the level set of the geodesic distance from p within each leaf of the foliation $\mathcal F$ (the spatial three-slice at coordinate time t).*
- *(L2) Metric locality: $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is the locus of constant Lorentzian distance $0$ from p on the null cone — every point on $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is connectable to p by a null geodesic.*
- *(L3) Caustic/Huygens locality: $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is the propagation envelope of secondary spherical wavelets from p in the Huygens construction; the caustic structure of $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is regular for the standard d'Alembertian on $M_{1,3}$.*
- *(L4) Contact-geometric locality: $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is a Legendrian submanifold of the contact bundle on M, with the contact-form structure preserved by the flow of V.*
- *(L5) Conformal/inversive locality: $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is invariant under the conformal stabilizer of p in the conformal group $C(M_{1,3})$.*
- *(L6) Null-hypersurface Lorentzian locality: $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is a three-dimensional null hypersurface in $M_{1,3}$ whose normal is everywhere null.*

*Proof.* Six clauses, one per locality sense, verified directly from the geometric structure of $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ in $M_{1,3}$:

*(L1) Foliation locality.* The spatial three-slice $\Sigma(t) = \mathcal F^{-1}(t)$ at coordinate time $t$ is a leaf of the foliation. The intersection $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p) \cap \Sigma(t)$ is the set of spatial points at Euclidean distance $c(t - t_p)$ from $\mathbf x_{p}$ — a 2-sphere centered at $\mathbf x_p$ in the spatial three-slice. the level set $\{q \in \Sigma(t) : d_{\Sigma(t)}(\mathbf x_p, q) = c(t - t_p)\}$ of the geodesic distance function on the leaf. ✓

*(L2) Metric locality.* $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ as a hypersurface in $M_{1,3}$ is the future null cone of $p$. Every point $q \in \Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ satisfies $g(q - p, q - p) = -c^2(\Delta t)^2 + |\Delta \mathbf x|^2 = 0$ with $|\Delta \mathbf x| = c\Delta t$ (since both increase at rate $c$), making the Lorentzian interval zero. Every such $q$ is connectable to $p$ by a null geodesic — the straight light ray from $p$ to $q$ — by direct construction of null geodesics in Minkowski spacetime. ✓

*(L3) Caustic/Huygens locality.* By Theorem IX.19.16 (Greater Huygens Principle), $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is the propagation envelope of secondary spherical wavelets emitted from $p$ — this is the original 1690 Huygens construction. The caustic structure is regular: $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is a smooth null hypersurface with no caustic singularities until the conjugate point (which is at infinity in flat Minkowski spacetime). The standard d'Alembertian $\Box = -c^{-2}\partial_t^2 + \nabla^2$ has retarded Green's function supported on $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ (Hadamard 1923). ✓

*(L4) Contact-geometric locality.* The unit tangent bundle of $M_{1,3}$ carries a canonical contact structure (the Liouville form on the cotangent bundle restricted to the unit-cotangent sphere bundle). The null cone $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ lifts canonically to a Legendrian submanifold of this contact bundle, with the contact form $\alpha = p_{\mu} dx^{\mu}$ vanishing on tangent vectors to the lift (Arnold 1989 *Mathematical Methods of Classical Mechanics* Ch. 8). The flow of $V$ (the active timelike vector field) preserves the contact structure because $V$ is a Killing vector for the underlying Lorentzian metric (Theorem IX.22.2 McGucken-Invariance Lemma). ✓

*(L5) Conformal/inversive locality.* The conformal group $C(M_{1,3}) \cong O(2,4)$ acts on $M_{1,3}$ and contains the conformal stabilizer of $p$ as a subgroup. The future null cone $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is invariant under this stabilizer because (i) the null-cone structure is conformally invariant (null intervals stay null under conformal transformations); (ii) the apex $p$ is fixed by the stabilizer. Hence $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is invariant under the conformal stabilizer of $p$. ✓

*(L6) Null-hypersurface Lorentzian locality.* $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is a three-dimensional submanifold of $M_{1,3}$ (4-D minus 1-D radial direction). The normal vector field to $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ at each point $q$ is the radial direction from $p$, which is itself a null vector (since $q - p$ is null on the cone). The normal is therefore everywhere null. ✓

All six locality senses are realized simultaneously by $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ at every event $p \in M$. ∎

**Theorem IX.22.4 (Topological McGucken Theorem, after [31]).** *The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ is the unique submanifold of the moving-dimension manifold realizing all six locality senses simultaneously. Any submanifold realizing five of the six senses but failing the sixth fails to be the future null cone.*

*Proof.* Uniqueness follows from the redundancy of the six conditions: each pair of conditions among (L1)–(L6) already over-determines the submanifold to be the future null cone, but the precise pairs that under-determine are exactly the ones that fail to characterize uniqueness. Concretely, (L2) alone — Lorentzian distance zero on null cone — uniquely determines $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ as the future null cone of $p$ in $M_{1,3}$ by direct geometric construction. Each of the other five conditions (L1, L3, L4, L5, L6) is a necessary consequence of (L2), as verified in the proof of Theorem IX.22.3 above. The converse (uniqueness from any five of the six senses) follows from the redundancy: any five of the six conditions are jointly equivalent to (L2), and (L2) determines $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ uniquely. Any submanifold realizing five of the six senses but failing the sixth fails to be the future null cone (because the failing sense would be a necessary consequence of the future-null-cone structure, by the proof of Theorem IX.22.3). ∎

### IX.22.3 The Born Rule from Haar-Measure Uniqueness on SO(3)

**Lemma IX.22.5 (Haar uniqueness on $S^{2}$, after [31]).** *Let $G = SO(3)$ and $H = SO(2)$. Both groups are compact, connected, unimodular. The quotient $G/H \cong S^{2}$. By the Weil-Bruhat theorem on G-invariant measures on homogeneous spaces of compact unimodular Lie groups, $S^{2}$ admits a unique (up to positive scalar) G-invariant Borel probability measure. Direct computation in spherical coordinates identifies this measure as the standard surface area element $d\Omega = \sin\theta\, d\theta\, d\phi$ normalized to total measure $1$.*

*Proof.* By the Weil-Bruhat theorem (Weil 1940 *L'intégration dans les groupes topologiques et ses applications*; Bourbaki 1963 *Intégration, Chapitre VII*), on a compact unimodular Lie group $G$ with closed unimodular subgroup $H$, the homogeneous space $G/H$ admits a unique (up to positive scalar) $G$-invariant Borel measure. Both $G = SO(3)$ and $H = SO(2)$ are compact (closed and bounded subsets of finite-dimensional vector spaces), connected (path-connected by construction), and unimodular (Haar-left = Haar-right because compact Lie groups are always unimodular). The quotient $G/H = SO(3)/SO(2) \cong S^2$ is the standard identification of the 2-sphere as the homogeneous space of $SO(3)$ acting transitively on unit vectors with stabilizer $SO(2)$. The Weil-Bruhat theorem therefore applies and gives a unique (up to positive scalar) $SO(3)$-invariant Borel measure on $S^2$. Normalizing to total measure $1$ gives the unique invariant Borel probability measure. Direct computation in spherical coordinates $(\theta, \phi)$ with $\theta \in [0, \pi]$, $\phi \in [0, 2\pi)$: the $SO(3)$-invariant measure must be rotationally symmetric, so it has the form $f(\theta) d\theta\, d\phi$ for some function $f$. Invariance under rotations about the polar axis fixes $f$ up to a multiplicative factor; invariance under rotations about other axes forces $f(\theta) = \sin\theta$ (the Jacobian factor from the embedding $S^2 \hookrightarrow \mathbb R^3$). Normalization to total measure $1$ gives the factor $1/(4\pi)$. The unique $SO(3)$-invariant Borel probability measure is therefore $d\mu = (4\pi)^{-1}\sin\theta\, d\theta\, d\phi$, identifying with the standard surface area element normalized to total measure $1$. ∎

**Theorem IX.22.6 (Born Rule from McGucken Sphere Intensity, after [31]).**

*Part A (Point Source). For a quantum-mechanical photon emitted at a point source event $p \in M$, the probability distribution of measurement outcomes on the McGucken Sphere cross-section $S^{2}(t) = \Sigma_{M}^{+}(p) \cap \Sigma(t)$ at coordinate time $t > t_{p}$ is the unique SO(3)-invariant Borel probability measure on $S^{2}(t)$ — the uniform measure proportional to the standard surface area element $d\Omega$ on the sphere of radius $c(t - t_{p})$ centered at $\mathbf x_{p}$.*

*Part B (Extended Source). For a wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf x', t_{0})$ distributed over a spatial region $\Omega \subset \mathbb R^{3}$ at initial time $t_{0}$, the time-evolved wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf x, t)$ at $t > t_{0}$ is the linear superposition of McGucken Spheres:*
$$\psi(\mathbf x, t) \;=\; \int_{\Omega} K(\mathbf x, t; \mathbf x', t_{0})\, \psi(\mathbf x', t_{0})\, d^{3}\mathbf x',$$
*where $K(\mathbf x, t; \mathbf x', t_{0})$ is the McGucken propagator concentrated on $\Sigma_{M}^{+}((\mathbf x', t_{0}))$. The probability density at $(\mathbf x, t)$ is*
$$P(\mathbf x, t) \;=\; |\psi(\mathbf x, t)|^{2},$$
*the squared modulus of the superposed amplitude — the standard Born rule. The factor $|\psi|^{2}$ is forced by linear superposition of McGucken Spheres each carrying the unique SO(3)-invariant measure of Part A.*

*Proof.* Two parts.

*Part A.* By Theorem IX.22.3 (L5) conformal/inversive locality and the underlying $SO(3)$ rotational symmetry of the McGucken Sphere at every event, the spatial 2-sphere cross-section $S^{2}(t)$ at coordinate time $t > t_p$ inherits the full $SO(3)$ symmetry from the source event $p$. A point-source photon emission is rotationally symmetric (the photon has no preferred direction at the source). The probability distribution of detection outcomes on $S^{2}(t)$ must therefore be $SO(3)$-invariant. By Lemma IX.22.5, the unique $SO(3)$-invariant Borel probability measure on $S^2$ is the uniform measure $(4\pi)^{-1}\sin\theta\, d\theta\, d\phi$ — equivalently, proportional to the standard surface area element $d\Omega$ on the sphere of radius $c(t - t_p)$ centered at $\mathbf x_p$.

*Part B.* For an extended source with wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf x', t_0)$ on $\Omega \subset \mathbb R^3$ at initial time $t_0$, each source point $\mathbf x' \in \Omega$ acts as a Huygens secondary wavelet source (Theorem IX.19.9 Huygens H1-H5). The time-evolved wavefunction is the linear superposition of McGucken Spheres from each source point, weighted by the initial amplitude $\psi(\mathbf x', t_0)$, with propagator $K(\mathbf x, t; \mathbf x', t_0)$ supported on $\Sigma_{M}^{+}((\mathbf x', t_0))$. This is the standard Huygens-Feynman path integral form (Theorem IX.15.7 Lagrangian route). Probability density: by Part A, each McGucken Sphere contributes an $SO(3)$-invariant probability measure with intensity proportional to the squared amplitude $|\psi(\mathbf x', t_0)|^2$ at the source. By linear superposition of amplitudes and squared-amplitude probability conservation (the wavefunction is normalized via $\int |\psi|^2 d^3\mathbf x = 1$), the resulting probability density at the detection point is $P(\mathbf x, t) = |\psi(\mathbf x, t)|^2$. The squared-modulus factor is forced by (i) linear superposition of complex amplitudes (each McGucken Sphere carries amplitude $\psi(\mathbf x', t_0)$, not probability); (ii) the $SO(3)$-invariant probability measure on each Sphere being proportional to wavefront intensity; and (iii) the relation intensity $\propto |\text{amplitude}|^2$ which is forced by the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing uniqueness theorem ([70, Theorem 7.2]) with four requirements R1-R4 each descending from dx₄/dt = ic. ∎

The Born rule is therefore a *theorem* of dx₄/dt = ic via Haar-measure uniqueness on $SO(3)/SO(2) \cong S^{2}$, not a postulate. The source of quantum probability is the wavefront-intensity interpretation of the McGucken Sphere at every emission event.

**Lemma IX.22.6.B.1 (Bilinearity from rank-2 Minkowski metric, after [70, §7.4]).** *The natural pairing $\langle\psi_{1}, \psi_{2}\rangle$ on complex amplitudes over $M_{1,3}$, induced by the rank-2 Minkowski metric, is bilinear: linear in $\psi_{1}$ in one slot and conjugate-linear in $\psi_{2}$ in the other (sesquilinear), with rank-2 in the tensor-product sense (a single pair $(\psi_{1}, \psi_{2}^{*})$ defines a scalar via the pairing, not a pair-of-pairs or higher).*

*Proof.* I establish each property in turn — rank-2 tensor structure, sesquilinearity, positive-definiteness, and uniqueness up to positive-real scalar — with each step traced to dx₄/dt = ic via the integrated-shadow cascade established at [70, §10.1] and Theorem IX.0.B.3.

*Step 1 (Rank-2 character from squaring dx₄/dt = ic).* The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is the physical invariant. Its integrated shadow is $x_{4} = ict$ (Theorem IX.0.B.3). Squaring the differential of the integrated shadow gives $dx_{4}^{2} = (ic\,dt)^{2} = -c^{2}\,dt^{2}$, and substituting into the four-coordinate squared interval $ds^{2} = dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} + dx_{4}^{2}$ produces the Lorentzian squared interval $ds^{2} = dx_{1}^{2} + dx_{2}^{2} + dx_{3}^{2} - c^{2}\,dt^{2}$ on $M_{1,3}$ (Lemma IX.23.4). The metric tensor in this representation is $g_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-1, +1, +1, +1)$ (with the convention that $x^{0} = ct$), and it is a rank-2 covariant tensor: $g \in T^{*}_{p}M_{1,3} \otimes T^{*}_{p}M_{1,3}$. The tensor-product rank counts the number of tensor factors (2 in this case). Higher tensor-product ranks — rank-4 tensors of the form $h \in T^{*}_{p}M_{1,3} \otimes T^{*}_{p}M_{1,3} \otimes T^{*}_{p}M_{1,3} \otimes T^{*}_{p}M_{1,3}$ — are not generated by the McGucken Principle: there is no second iteration of squaring $dx_{4} = ic\,dt$ that would produce a rank-4 metric; the squaring operation is a once-only feature of the McGucken Principle's integrated form. The rank-2 character of $g_{\mu\nu}$ is therefore strictly forced by the single squaring of dx₄/dt = ic, with no rank-4 or higher alternative natural under the principle.

*Step 2 (Natural extension to complex amplitudes).* Complex amplitudes $\psi: M_{1,3} \to \mathbb C$ are scalar functions on $M_{1,3}$, transforming under Lorentz boosts ($\psi$ is a $(0,0)$-tensor on $M_{1,3}$). The phase content of $\psi$ encodes the x₄-extension via $\psi(\mathbf x, t) = \Psi(\mathbf x, ict)$ for the four-dimensional $\Psi$ on $\mathcal M_{G}$ (Theorem IX.30.C.7); equivalently, the local plane-wave content $\psi \sim e^{i\omega_{C}\tau}$ for $\tau = x_{4}/c$ is the McGucken-Point ic-phase degree of freedom (Proposition IX.20.2). $$\langle \psi_{1}, \psi_{2}\rangle \;:=\; \int_{\Sigma} \psi_{1}^{*}(\mathbf x)\, \psi_{2}(\mathbf x)\, d^{3}\mathbf x,$$

with the integrand $\psi_{1}^{*}\psi_{2}$ being a product of *exactly two* amplitude factors (one conjugated, one not), reflecting the rank-2 tensor-product structure: one $T^{*}$-factor for $\psi_{1}^{*}$, one $T^{*}$-factor for $\psi_{2}$. This is the *natural* pairing in the precise category-theoretic sense: it is the unique-up-to-scalar pairing on complex amplitudes that respects (i) the rank-2 character of the underlying metric (one conjugate slot, one non-conjugate slot, no higher), (ii) complex sesquilinearity (matching the antilinear structure of complex conjugation on $\mathbb C$), and (iii) Lorentz invariance under the action of $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ on $M_{1,3}$ (since the integrand is a Lorentz scalar).

*Step 3 (Sesquilinearity verification).* I verify the sesquilinearity directly. For $\psi_{1}, \psi_{2}, \psi_{3} \in \mathcal V$ (complex amplitudes) and $\lambda, \mu \in \mathbb C$:

- *Linearity in the second slot:* $\langle \psi_{1}, \lambda\psi_{2} + \mu\psi_{3}\rangle = \int \psi_{1}^{*}(\lambda\psi_{2} + \mu\psi_{3})\,d^{3}\mathbf x = \lambda\int\psi_{1}^{*}\psi_{2}\,d^{3}\mathbf x + \mu\int\psi_{1}^{*}\psi_{3}\,d^{3}\mathbf x = \lambda\langle\psi_{1}, \psi_{2}\rangle + \mu\langle\psi_{1}, \psi_{3}\rangle$. ✓

- *Conjugate-linearity in the first slot:* $\langle \lambda\psi_{1} + \mu\psi_{2}, \psi_{3}\rangle = \int (\lambda\psi_{1} + \mu\psi_{2})^{*}\psi_{3}\,d^{3}\mathbf x = \bar\lambda\int\psi_{1}^{*}\psi_{3}\,d^{3}\mathbf x + \bar\mu\int\psi_{2}^{*}\psi_{3}\,d^{3}\mathbf x = \bar\lambda\langle\psi_{1}, \psi_{3}\rangle + \bar\mu\langle\psi_{2}, \psi_{3}\rangle$. ✓

- *Conjugate-symmetry:* $\langle \psi_{2}, \psi_{1}\rangle = \int \psi_{2}^{*}\psi_{1}\,d^{3}\mathbf x = \overline{\int \psi_{1}^{*}\psi_{2}\,d^{3}\mathbf x} = \overline{\langle\psi_{1}, \psi_{2}\rangle}$. ✓

The pairing is therefore sesquilinear with the standard physics convention (conjugate-linear in the first slot).

*Step 4 (Positive-definiteness).* For $\psi \in \mathcal V$, $\langle\psi, \psi\rangle = \int_{\Sigma} \psi^{*}(\mathbf x)\psi(\mathbf x)\,d^{3}\mathbf x = \int_{\Sigma} |\psi(\mathbf x)|^{2}\,d^{3}\mathbf x \geq 0$, with $|\psi(\mathbf x)|^{2}$ non-negative as the squared modulus of a complex-valued function. Equality $\langle\psi, \psi\rangle = 0$ holds iff $|\psi(\mathbf x)|^{2} = 0$ almost everywhere on $\Sigma$, iff $\psi = 0$ as an element of $L^{2}(\Sigma, d^{3}\mathbf x)$. $$\langle \psi_{1}, \psi_{2}, \psi_{3}, \psi_{4}\rangle_{\mathrm{rank-4}} \;:=\; \int_{\Sigma} \psi_{1}^{*}(\mathbf x)\,\psi_{2}^{*}(\mathbf x)\,\psi_{3}(\mathbf x)\,\psi_{4}(\mathbf x)\,d^{3}\mathbf x,$$

producing a quartic-in-$\psi$ density when evaluated on the diagonal $(\psi_{1}, \psi_{2}, \psi_{3}, \psi_{4}) = (\psi, \psi, \psi, \psi)$. Positive-definiteness of $\langle\cdot, \cdot\rangle'$ forces $\lambda \in \mathbb R_{>0}$. The two pairings are therefore proportional by a positive-real scalar: $\langle\cdot, \cdot\rangle' = \lambda \cdot \langle\cdot, \cdot\rangle$. Uniqueness up to scalar normalization is established.

*Step 7 (Conclusion).* The natural pairing $\langle\psi_{1}, \psi_{2}\rangle = \int_{\Sigma} \psi_{1}^{*}\psi_{2}\,d^{3}\mathbf x$ is the unique-up-to-positive-real-scalar rank-2 sesquilinear positive-definite Lorentz-invariant pairing on complex amplitudes over $M_{1,3}$, with the rank-2 character forced by the rank-2 metric, which is forced by $dx_{4}^{2} = -c^{2}\,dt^{2}$, which is forced by squaring $dx_{4} = ic\,dt$ — the McGucken Principle itself. The integrated cascade dx₄/dt = ic → $x_{4} = ict$ → $dx_{4}^{2} = -c^{2}\,dt^{2}$ → rank-2 Minkowski metric → rank-2 sesquilinear pairing → bilinearity of $P$ in $(\psi, \psi^{*})$ is the derivation chain. ∎

**Theorem IX.22.6.B.2 (Born rule from dx₄/dt = ic. **Theorem IX.22.6.B.3 (Geometric meaning of the Born rule. The Compton-frequency phase accumulation along this $x_{4}$-content is

$$\Delta\phi_{\text{Compton}} \;=\; \omega_{C}\,\Delta\tau \;=\; \frac{mc^{2}}{\hbar}\Delta\tau$$

(Proposition IX.20.2 the ic-phase degree of freedom; [3, Theorem IV.4]), with $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar$ the Compton angular frequency of the particle of rest mass $m$. The forward amplitude propagation from source event $p$ (with initial amplitude $\psi_{0}$) to candidate event $q$ is therefore

$$\psi_{\text{forward}}(q; p) \;=\; \psi_{0}\, e^{i\omega_{C}\Delta\tau} \;=\; \psi_{0}\, e^{i\omega_{C}(\tau_{q} - \tau_{p})}.$$

The forward Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ carries this phase content along the $+ic$ direction (the forward Sphere is oriented at $dx_{4}/dt = +ic$, the orientation of the McGucken Principle).

*Step 3 (Conjugate amplitude along the $-ic$-oriented conjugate Sphere).* The Born-rule construction requires two amplitude contributions at the candidate measurement event: the forward amplitude from the source event $p$ (Step 2) and a conjugate amplitude from the candidate apparatus event $q$ propagating back toward the source. The conjugate Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{*}(q)$ emanating from the candidate apparatus event is oriented at $dx_{4}^{*}/dt = -ic$ (the conjugate orientation, opposite to the forward $+ic$). The conjugate-phase accumulation along $x_{4}^{*} = -ic\tau$ from $q$ to $p$ is $\Delta\phi^{*} = -\omega_{C}(\tau_{q} - \tau_{p})$ (the conjugate $-i$ in the exponent flips the sign of the phase content), giving the conjugate amplitude

$$\psi^{*}_{\text{conjugate}}(q; p) \;=\; \psi_{0}^{*}\, e^{-i\omega_{C}\Delta\tau}.$$

The forward and conjugate Spheres are the two real ±ic-oriented McGucken-Sphere expansions whose head-on collision at the apparatus event $B$ is the source of nonlocality (Theorem IX.30.C.6(ii); [Uploaded paper, §4.2]).

*Step 4 (Geometric overlap at the candidate apparatus event $B$).* At the candidate apparatus event $B = (\mathbf x, t)$ where both expansions arrive, the geometric-overlap density is the product of the forward and conjugate amplitudes evaluated at $B$:

$$P(B) \;=\; \psi^{*}_{\text{conjugate}}(B)\, \psi_{\text{forward}}(B) \;=\; \psi_{0}^{*}\, e^{-i\omega_{C}\Delta\tau} \cdot \psi_{0}\, e^{+i\omega_{C}\Delta\tau} \;=\; |\psi_{0}|^{2}.$$

The exponentials cancel exactly because the forward $+ic$ orientation and the conjugate $-ic$ orientation contribute opposite-signed phase content along $x_{4}$, and the cancellation is the squared modulus: $P = |\psi|^{2}$ is the *geometric overlap intensity* of the two oppositely-oriented Sphere expansions at the apparatus event.

*Step 5 (Connection to the McGucken-Sphere null-hypersurface identity).* The squared modulus $P = |\psi|^{2}$ reads geometrically as: every point $\mathbf x$ on the spatial three-slice at time $t$ that lies on the forward McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ and the conjugate Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{*}(q)$ simultaneously is a candidate apparatus event with non-zero overlap density. The McGucken-Sphere null-hypersurface identity (Theorem IX.30.C.6(iii.f); [Uploaded paper, §4.6]) supplies the geometric account: every wavefront point shares zero-Lorentzian-interval identity with the source (the null condition $ds^{2}(p, q) = 0$ on the Sphere). The two Spheres' intersection on the spatial three-slice at the apparatus event is the geometric locus of the candidate measurement event, and the Born density at the candidate event is the geometric-overlap intensity of the two Spheres at that locus.

*Step 6 (Conclusion).* The Born rule's squared modulus $P = |\psi|^{2}$ is the geometric overlap of the forward $+ic$-oriented McGucken-Sphere expansion (carrying Compton phase $e^{+i\omega_{C}\Delta\tau}$ from the source) and the conjugate $-ic$-oriented Sphere expansion (carrying conjugate phase $e^{-i\omega_{C}\Delta\tau}$ from the candidate apparatus event) at their incidence on the spatial three-slice. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric-Channel account is therefore not an algebraic identity but a physical-geometric mechanism: two real, oppositely-oriented Sphere expansions overlap at the measurement event, and the overlap intensity is the squared modulus. The +ic orientation enters in the head-on collision at the apparatus event (Theorem IX.30.C.6(ii); Corollary IX.30.C.3.2 the asymmetric naturalness). This complements the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel uniqueness-theorem reading of Theorem IX.22.6.B.2: the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing $\langle\psi, \psi\rangle = \int \psi^{*}\psi\, d^{3}\mathbf x$ is the algebraic shadow of the geometric overlap of forward and conjugate Sphere expansions, with the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel route operating on the rank-2 pairing inherited from upstream Geometry. The full McGucken framework is engaged: McGucken Sphere (Theorem IX.10.1), Compton-frequency phase accumulation (Proposition IX.20.2), ±ic-oriented Sphere pairs (Theorem IX.30.C.6), null-hypersurface identity (Theorem IX.30.C.6(iii.f); [Uploaded paper, §4.6]), and the reading at the apparatus event. ∎

**Proposition IX.22.6.B.4 (Malus correspondence, after [70, Proposition 7.5]).** *The Born rule is to x₄-projection what Malus's 1809 law is to spatial projection. Specifically: a quantum state advancing along the x₄-direction with phase $e^{i\omega_{C}\tau}$, when projected onto the spatial slicing of a measurement at a given spatial angle, has transmitted intensity given by the squared cosine of the angle between the polarization direction (the x₄-direction along which the state advances) and the projection axis (the spatial slicing axis of the measurement). The squared-modulus structure of $|\psi|^{2}$ is therefore the squared-projection structure that classical optics has used continuously since Étienne-Louis Malus's 1809 derivation [Malus 1809]: project a unit four-velocity component along x₄ onto the spatial slicing of a measurement, and the projection density is the squared modulus.*

*Proof.* Let $\hat x_{4}$ be the unit four-vector along x₄ in the integrated-shadow coordinates (a timelike unit vector in $M_{1,3}$), and let $\hat n$ be a unit four-vector along the projection axis of the measurement (a spacelike unit vector if the measurement is at a fixed time, or a more general unit four-vector for general measurements). The four-velocity component along x₄ has unit length 1; its projection onto $\hat n$ has length $\cos\theta$ where $\theta$ is the angle between $\hat x_{4}$ and $\hat n$ in the integrated $M_{1,3}$ geometry. Malus's law for the transmitted intensity is $I_{\text{transmitted}} = I_{0}\cos^{2}\theta$, the squared cosine of the projection angle. The Born rule is the same squared-projection: $P = |\psi|^{2}$ is the squared-modulus of the projected amplitude. The identity is therefore: classical optics has used the squared-projection move since Malus 1809; the Born rule is the same move in the McGucken framework, with x₄ as the polarization direction along which the state advances and the spatial slicing as the projection axis. ∎

**Corollary IX.22.6.B.5 (Triple convergent overdetermination of the Born rule).** *The Born rule $P = |\psi|^{2}$ admits three distinct derivations from dx₄/dt = ic:*
