**Remark IX.29.6 (Gemini as faithful representative of orthodox physics, and the pedagogical value of the dissolution).** *Gemini's articulation of the four contradictions in the dialogue documented at the head of §IX.29 is a faithful representative of the orthodox view as canonically taught — tracking the standard textbook treatments of [von Neumann 1932], [Dirac 1930], [Bohr 1928], [Heisenberg 1958], [Wigner 1963], [Zurek 2003], [Penrose 2004], and [Schlosshauer 2007]. Gemini's closing summary names the contradictions as "The Measurement Problem, which is a great unsolved mystery in modern physics" — an accurate echo of the orthodox view's own self-assessment ([Bell 1990, "Against 'Measurement'," Physics World 3, 33]; [Penrose 2004, §29.1–29.3]). The orthodox view's pattern — when the formalism produces a conflict, add a postulate or invoke an interpretation — is on full display: Gemini lists three interpretive escape hatches (Many-Worlds, Copenhagen, Decoherence) without recognising that none of them escapes the contradiction; they merely relocate it. Each interpretation is internally consistent on its own terms but does not dissolve the underlying conflict at the formalism level.*

*The pedagogical value of §IX.29 is twofold. First, the section supplies a diagnostic for what orthodox physics has been stuck on — the four contradictions named explicitly, with canonical citations, allowing a reader from the orthodox tradition to locate their own pedagogical formation in the literature. Second, the section supplies the McGucken dissolution of each contradiction at full rigour, with the dissolution being not "yet another interpretation" but a mathematical move that traces the apparent conflict to two-channel readings of one geometry. The dual-channel architecture of dx₄/dt = ic is what makes the dissolution possible: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic-symmetry face and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometric-propagation face are two readings of one principle, with the apparent contradictions arising when orthodox physics mistakes the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometry for an extra postulate imposed on the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic dynamics.*

*The value-add over the orthodox interpretive landscape is therefore the **reduction in postulate count**: from the orthodox seven (Schrödinger equation; Born rule; collapse postulate; unitarity postulate; decoherence dynamics; choice of interpretation; subtopic-specific postulates) to a single physical principle dx₄/dt = ic, with the four contradictions dissolved by the dual-channel architecture rather than papered over by interpretive escape hatches. This is the test that distinguishes the McGucken framework from orthodox interpretations of quantum mechanics: orthodox interpretations argue about which postulates to accept (Many-Worlds vs Copenhagen vs decoherence vs GRW); the McGucken framework eliminates the need for the postulates in the first place by tracing them to one principle.*

## IX.30 The Structural Architecture of the McGucken Duality: The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel as Foundational Ontology, The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel as Time-Symmetric Algebraic Shadow, and the Eighteen Structural-Differential Signatures of the Dual-Channel Foundations

### IX.30.0 Opening: The Structural Keystone

The dual-channel architecture established across §§II–VII and formalized at the source-pair level in §§IX.0–IX.10 has been described, throughout the preceding sections, as a *parallel-sibling* structure: the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel derive the same through disjoint machinery, with the 47-theorem catalog of [3] being the dual derivations of time-symmetric content and the mono-channel catalog (the strict Second Law, the arrows of time, the +ic orientation itself, cosmological expansion direction) being the asymmetric content derived only in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel. This sibling framing is descriptively correct but incomplete. The present chapter establishes at the heart of the framework: **The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel are two different *kinds* of mathematical objects, applied simultaneously to the same physics. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel exalts physical geometry — with the McGucken Sphere as the physical, geometric primitive expanding at $+ic$ from every event as a spherically-symmetric wavefront. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is mathematical — algebraic structures existing outside of physical spacetime, with the operator-algebra and symmetry-analytic apparatus of Noether, Heisenberg, Born, Jordan, Stone, von Neumann, Wigner, Wightman, and Haag–Kastler as the algebra. The dual-channel architecture is therefore the geometry/algebra distinction of mathematics applied to foundational physics, with the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$ as the geometric dynamic principle from which both the geometric and algebraic apparatuses descend.**

The identification is: **the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is geometry; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is algebra.** Each side carries multiple differential signatures that distinguish it from the other, with seventeen such differential signatures developed in §IX.30.A below. These differential signatures are seventeen *facets* of the single categorical-mathematical distinction between geometry and algebra, as that distinction applies to foundational physics. Each facet articulates a different empirical consequence of the categorical distinction: ontology versus epistemology, per-event physics versus statistical aggregation, dynamic directional content versus symmetric algebra, active $x_4$-expansion registered by physical clock-readouts versus $t$ as abstract parameter on an operator algebra, light cones as geometric primitives versus the Spectrum Condition as imported algebraic axiom, the McGucken Sphere as definite geometric object versus the wavefunction $\psi$ as the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel statistical encoding, head-on Sphere-collision events at definite spacetime coordinates versus Born-rule probability densities, and so on. The eighteen signatures together constitute the anatomy of the dual-channel architecture; the chapter develops each at the rigor required for the framework's claims.

The keystone of the chapter is the recognition that the dual-channel architecture is *the* fundamental distinction of mathematics — geometry versus algebra — applied to foundational physics. The 2,300-year history of this mathematical distinction (Euclid 300 BCE versus Diophantus 250 CE, sharpening through Descartes 1637, Galois 1830s, Lie 1880s, and the early-twentieth-century axiomatic tradition) is the same intellectual lineage that the McGucken framework identifies as the dual-channel architecture of physics. Physics has been working both halves of mathematics simultaneously for 335 years (since Huygens 1690 supplied the geometry of optical foundations and Newton 1704 supplied the algebraic-corpuscular content), without recognizing that the two channels of foundational physics are the two halves of mathematics applied to the same underlying physical reality — namely the $+ic$-oriented McGucken Sphere expansion at every event of spacetime, with $dx_4/dt = +ic$ as the geometric dynamic principle.

#### IX.30.0.1 Two Distinct Senses of Primacy: Historical-Constructive versus Physical-Foundational

I open the chapter by drawing a distinction that organizes everything that follows. The dual-channel architecture admits two distinct senses in which one might ask whether one channel is "more fundamental" than the other, and the answer to the question depends on which sense is being asked. I record both senses explicitly, because the chapter's central claims operate on the distinction.

Sense 1 — Historical-constructive primacy. *Can each channel's apparatus be developed independently from its own foundations, without invoking the other channel as derivational input?* The answer is **yes for both channels, though the historical labor was asymmetric — the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel was built by the tradition across three decades, the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel by McGucken from the Principle**. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus — the Hilbert space, the operator algebras, the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, Stone's theorem on one-parameter unitary groups, the Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1, 3)$ and Poincaré algebra $\mathfrak{iso}(1, 3)$, the McGucken Lagrangian's four-sector form, the Noether conservation currents, the Wightman axiomatic apparatus — was historically constructed from algebraic and functional-analytic foundations without the McGucken Sphere as input. Noether 1918, Heisenberg 1925, Born–Jordan 1925, Dirac 1925, Stone 1932, von Neumann 1932, Wigner 1939, Wightman 1956, Bargmann 1957, Haag–Kastler 1964 each built portions of the apparatus — Noether from Lie-group invariance of variational problems; Heisenberg, Born, and Jordan from spectroscopic data and the Ritz combination principle; Stone, von Neumann, Wigner, and Wightman from pure mathematical foundations (functional analysis, Hilbert-space theory, representation theory, and axiomatic-QFT formalism). The historical record is clear: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is independently buildable. Theorem IX.30.B.1 below states this formally and exhibits the constructive routes. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is also independently buildable from its own foundations — Theorem IX.30.B.2 exhibits the constructive routes from $dx_4/dt = +ic$ to the McGucken Sphere, the Huygens-iterated wavefront, the Compton-coupling Brownian motion, the Born-rule head-on Sphere-collision derivation, and the Jacobson 1995 thermodynamic derivation of the Einstein field equations, without invoking the operator algebra as input. The two channels are therefore constructively independent as mathematical enterprises — each is buildable from its own foundations without invoking the other — while the historical construction was asymmetric: the tradition built the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel from Heisenberg 1925 to Wightman 1956, and McGucken built the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel from dx₄/dt = ic.

**Sense 2 — Physical-foundational primacy.** *Which channel's content corresponds to the physical reality of the universe — to the $+ic$-oriented active expansion that the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$ asserts as its content?* Here the answer is **The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is foundational and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the algebraic shadow**. The $+ic$ orientation, the arrow of time, the strict Second Law $dS/dt > 0$, the cosmological expansion $H_0 > 0$, the retarded-Green's-function preference, the matter-dominance baryogenesis direction, the monotonic decoherence direction, the black-hole area growth $dA/dt \geq 0$, the McGucken-Wick rotation sign $t \to -i\tau$, and the seventeen further items of the mono-channel catalog of §IX.30.C.2 below are *facts* about the universe. Each of them lives in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel as a direct manifestation of the $+ic$ orientation of the McGucken Sphere expansion at every event. None of them has a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel derivation, by the content-asymmetry theorem of §IX.30.C.3 below: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus is time-symmetric (sign-blind on $+ic$), and time-symmetric operations cannot produce time-asymmetric outputs. The Wightman Spectrum Condition, imposed as an unexplained axiom by Wightman 1956 and carried by every subsequent axiomatic-QFT framework for sixty-eight years, is the historical signature of this: the $+ic$ orientation had to be imported into the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel as an axiom because the apparatus could not derive it. At the physical level the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is the foundations; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the algebraic shadow with the $+ic$ orientation absent because algebra is sign-symmetric and cannot carry geometric directional content.

**Both statements are true at once, and the chapter establishes both rigorously.** the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is historically-constructively independent of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel — Heisenberg in 1925 reached the canonical algebra from spectroscopic data without invoking a McGucken Sphere, and the fact of this independence is recorded as Theorem IX.30.B.1. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is physically-foundationally prior — the $+ic$ orientation of the active expansion at every event is the foundational physics of the universe, and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus is the algebraic shadow of that. Theorems IX.30.B.1 and IX.30.B.2 together establish constructive independence (each channel buildable from its own foundations without invoking the other), with the historical construction being asymmetric — the tradition built the Algebraic Channel across three decades, McGucken built the Geometric Channel from the Principle. Theorem IX.30.C.3 establishes content asymmetry (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel carries content — the $+ic$-oriented geometric primitives — that dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's time-symmetric algebraic apparatus cannot reach). The two facts coexist because they answer different questions: the constructive question asks "can each channel be built from its own foundations?" — yes, both can — and the claim question asks "does one channel's content contain the other's?" — yes, the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's content contains the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's, with the surplus being exactly the geometry that algebra is incapable of carrying.

What Heisenberg built in 1925 was the following. The implication of the distinction is that what Heisenberg constructed in 1925 — and what Born, Jordan, Dirac, Stone, von Neumann, Wigner, and Wightman built after him — is the time-reversal-symmetric algebraic shadow of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$. The shadow is a genuine mathematical object: internally consistent, independently constructible, empirically anchored to atomic spectra and the electron anomalous magnetic moment and every other time-symmetric measurement. Heisenberg's matrix mechanics, the canonical commutator, the Schrödinger equation, the Stone–von Neumann uniqueness theorem, the Wigner classification of unitary representations of the Poincaré group, and the full operator-algebraic apparatus of contemporary quantum field theory are all theorems of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel. Each is independently reachable from spectroscopic and algebraic foundations without a McGucken Sphere. But each is *also* the algebraic shadow of a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel object whose $+ic$ orientation and geometry the algebraic apparatus cannot represent in its vocabulary. Heisenberg reached the algebraic shadow without knowing it was a shadow — without the recognition that the algebra he built was tracking the measurement statistics of a $+ic$-oriented geometry underlying the spectroscopic data. The framework's account: Heisenberg's 1925 construction is the historical demonstration of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's constructive independence; the McGucken framework supplies the identification of what Heisenberg reached as the algebraic shadow of the principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$.

This matters for orthodox foundational physics. The orthodox foundational-physics tradition has, since 1925, treated the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic shadow as the foundations of physics. The Hilbert-space framework is taken as the arena; the operator algebra is taken as the structure; the canonical commutator is taken as the postulate; the universal wavefunction $|\Psi\rangle$ is taken as the object describing the universe. Every contemporary unification programme — Many-Worlds, AdS/CFT, ER=EPR, holography, the Page curve, the holographic-complexity programme, the replica-wormhole / island-formula programme — operates within this dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel interpretive framing, computing in the algebraic apparatus and treating it as the physics itself. The orthodox programmes are mathematically internally consistent and have produced no observable physical predictions for the asymmetric universe in five decades because the $+ic$-oriented content of the universe lives in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometric apparatus, which orthodox physics has been treating as derivative or eliminable. The framework's diagnosis of fifty years of orthodox unification work without observable physics: the work has been computing in the algebraic shadow of the actual physics, missing the geometric source. The closed/open dynamics inversion of §IX.30.D.3 below makes the diagnosis explicit: closed-system unitary dynamics is the algebra (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel) of open-system irreversible dynamics (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel), not its fundamental source. The universal wavefunction $|\Psi\rangle$ is a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel object — the algebraic encoding of the universe's measurement statistics — and the orthodox identification of $|\Psi\rangle$ with the universe is the error of mistaking the algebraic shadow for the geometry.

With the two senses of primacy distinguished and held simultaneously, the chapter now proceeds to the formal articulation of the eighteen differential signatures.

### IX.30.A The Eighteen Ways the Two Channels Differ

The dual-channel architecture is *the* fundamental categorical-mathematical distinction of geometry versus algebra applied to foundational physics. The present section articulates this central fact in eighteen differential signatures, grouped into six categories. Each signature is a distinct facet of the geometry/algebra distinction, with its own theorem-level statement, its own proof or proof-outline, and its own historical and empirical claims. The eighteen are eighteen *facets* of the one categorical distinction, with each facet articulating a different empirical consequence of the categorical-.

The five categories are:

- **§IX.30.A.1** The Categorical Mathematical Distinction (Signatures 1, 11, 13, 16) — geometry versus algebra at the mathematical level.
- **§IX.30.A.2** The Ontological/Epistemological Distinction (Signatures 2, 5, 8, 14, 17) — what each channel *is* in terms of being versus being-about.
- **§IX.30.A.3** The Per-Event/Statistical-Aggregation Distinction (Signatures 5, 8, 14, 15) — how each channel handles individual measurement events versus aggregated statistics.
- **§IX.30.A.4** The Dynamic/Directional Content Distinction (Signatures 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12) — where the $+ic$ orientation lives and where it is absent.
- **§IX.30.A.5** The Constructive-Resource and Historical-Tradition Distinction (Signatures 11, 16) — how each channel descends from the historical record of mathematics and physics.

The categories overlap because the eighteen signatures are facets of one categorical distinction, not independent properties. A given signature may belong to two or three categories at once. The category structure is for expository clarity, not for taxonomy.

#### IX.30.A.1 The Categorical Mathematical Distinction: Geometry versus Algebra

**Theorem IX.30.A.1.1 (Difference 1: Geometry versus algebra).** *The Geometric Channel is geometry — spheres, wavefronts, light cones, and Lorentzian manifolds. The Algebraic Channel is algebra — operator algebras, Lie groups, Hilbert spaces, and axiomatic-QFT structures. The two channels are the two halves of mathematics — the geometric tradition (Euclid 300 BCE, Apollonius 200 BCE, Descartes 1637, Gauss 1827, Riemann 1854, Klein 1872, Cartan 1920s, Whitney 1936, Atiyah–Singer 1963, Connes 1985) and the algebraic tradition (Diophantus 250 CE, al-Khwarizmi 820, Galois 1830s, Cayley 1854, Lie 1880s, Frobenius 1890s, Noether 1910s–1920s, von Neumann 1930s, Gelfand 1940s, Eilenberg–Mac Lane 1945) — applied to the same physical reality.*

*Proof.* the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's apparatus — the McGucken manifold $\mathcal M_G$, the source-pair $(\mathcal M_G, D_M)$ co-generated by $dx_4/dt = +ic$, the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p) = \{(\mathbf x, t) : \|\mathbf x - \mathbf x_p\| = c(t - t_p), t \geq t_p\}$ at every event with its $+ic$ orientation, the Huygens-iterated wavefront construction, the head-on Sphere-collision Born-rule mechanism, the eight forms of entropy with strict-monotonic $+ic$ orientation derived from Compton-coupling Brownian motion on the Sphere, the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$, the McGucken Sphere-recruited-fabric mechanism producing the Einstein field equations via the Jacobson 1995 thermodynamic derivation — is identified at every entry with geometry in the standard mathematical sense. Spheres, wavefronts, light cones, manifolds, metrics, geodesics, curvature tensors, and propagation kernels are paradigmatic objects of the geometric tradition of mathematics.

The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus — the Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, the operator algebra $B(\mathcal H)$, the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, Stone's theorem on one-parameter unitary groups, the Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ as abstract Lie group, the Poincaré algebra $\mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$ as abstract Lie algebra, the gauge groups $U(1) \times SU(2) \times SU(3)$ of the Standard Model as abstract Lie groups, the McGucken Lagrangian as functional, the Noether currents as conserved quantities indexed by symmetry generators, the CPT operator, the Wightman axiomatic apparatus, the Haag–Kastler net of local observable algebras — is identified at every entry with algebra in the standard mathematical sense. Operator algebras, Lie groups and algebras, representation theory, eigenvalue spectra, functionals, indexed conserved quantities, and axiomatic algebraic structures are paradigmatic objects of the algebraic tradition of mathematics.

The two halves of mathematics are roughly 2,300 years old. The distinction goes back to Euclid 300 BCE (geometry) versus Diophantus 250 CE (algebra), sharpening through Descartes 1637 (the partial synthesis of analytic geometry), Galois 1830s (the algebraic theory of equations), Lie 1880s (continuous groups as a bridge object), and the early-twentieth-century axiomatic tradition. The two halves are not reducible to each other. The Gelfand–Naimark theorem (Gelfand–Naimark 1943, "On the Imbedding of Normed Rings into the Ring of Operators in Hilbert Space," *Matematicheskii Sbornik* 12, 197–217) supplies a partial duality between commutative $C^*$-algebras and locally compact Hausdorff topological spaces; the Connes spectral-triple program (Connes 1985, "Noncommutative differential geometry," *Publications mathématiques de l'IHÉS* 62, 257–360; Connes 1994, *Noncommutative Geometry*, Academic Press) supplies a partial duality between certain noncommutative algebras and noncommutative-geometric structures. But the dualities require additional input (spectral triples, KK-theory, cyclic cohomology) that is itself imported rather than derived, and the dualities are partial rather than complete — they bridge specific commutative or pseudo-commutative subcases of the algebraic side with specific topological or geometric subcases of the geometric side without unifying the two halves.

The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content of the McGucken framework descends from the geometric tradition; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel content descends from the algebraic tradition; the two channels of the framework are the two halves of mathematics applied to foundational physics. The 47-theorem dual catalog of [3] is the catalog of theorems where the two halves of mathematics converge on the same physics via disjoint derivations; the seventeen mono-channel items of §IX.30.C.2 are the catalog of geometry that the algebraic side cannot reach because algebraic structure is sign-symmetric on the $+ic$ orientation that the geometric side carries as a primitive. ∎

**Theorem IX.30.A.1.2 (Difference 11: One principle versus many axioms).** *The Geometric Channel is built from one principle — $dx_4/dt = +ic$. The Algebraic Channel requires multiple independent axiomatic commitments: the Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, the Spectrum Condition $\mathrm{Spec}(P^\mu) \subseteq \bar V^+$, Stone's theorem on unitary groups, the Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$, the Poincaré algebra $\mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$, the gauge groups $U(1) \times SU(2) \times SU(3)$, the McGucken Lagrangian as a functional, the Noether currents, the CPT operator, the six Wightman axioms, and the Haag–Kastler axioms — each imposed independently. The Geometric Channel's apparatus is co-generated from the single principle (Theorem IX.18.2); the Algebraic Channel's apparatus cannot be co-generated from any single algebraic principle.*

*Proof.* The full geometric apparatus of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is co-generated from $dx_4/dt = +ic$ via the Co-Generation Theorem (Theorem IX.18.2): integration with origin $x_4(0) = 0$ produces the integrated coordinate $x_4 = ict$ and the constraint surface $\mathcal C_M$; differentiation along the integral flow produces the McGucken operator $D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$; the source-pair $(\mathcal M_G, D_M)$ is the Algebraic structureU; the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ at every event is the propagating wavefront generated by the principle (Definition IX.19.1, after [7]); the Reciprocal Generation Property (Theorem IX.19.4) supplies the iterated wavefront construction; the Compton-coupling Brownian mechanism of [4] supplies the entropy content; the Jacobson 1995 thermodynamic derivation supplies the Einstein field equations. The full dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel apparatus descends from the single principle.

In contrast, the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus requires multiple independent axiomatic commitments. The Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ is an axiomatic structure (complete inner-product vector space) that is not derivable from any single algebraic principle. The canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ is an axiomatic relation between operators that has to be imposed as a postulate. The Spectrum Condition $\mathrm{Spec}(P^\mu) \subseteq \bar V^+$ is an axiomatic constraint imposed by Wightman 1956. Stone's theorem is a functional-analysis theorem, but it operates on an already-assumed Hilbert-space structure. The Lorentz group, the Poincaré algebra, the McGucken Lagrangian, the Noether currents are each independent components of the algebraic apparatus that have to be imported rather than derived from a single algebraic foundation. The Wightman axiomatic framework (Wightman 1956, "Quantum field theory in terms of vacuum expectation values," *Physical Review* 101, 860–866; Streater–Wightman 1964, *PCT, Spin and Statistics, and All That*, W. A. Benjamin) lists six independent axioms for QFT, each of which has to be imposed independently. The Haag–Kastler axiomatic framework (Haag–Kastler 1964, "An algebraic approach to quantum field theory," *Journal of Mathematical Physics* 5, 848–861; Haag 1996, *Local Quantum Physics*, Springer) lists comparable axioms for local-algebra QFT. The asymmetry in axiomatic complexity between the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's one principle and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's multiple axioms is a feature of the geometry/algebra distinction. ∎

**Theorem IX.30.A.1.3 (Difference 13: Different mathematical apparatus).** *The Geometric Channel requires differential geometry, pseudo-Riemannian geometry, fiber bundles, characteristic classes, sheaves, and Lorentzian manifolds. The Algebraic Channel requires linear algebra, functional analysis, operator algebras, Lie algebras, representation theory, group cohomology, homological algebra, and category theory. The two mathematical apparatuses are largely non-overlapping; the partial bridges between them — Gelfand–Naimark duality, Connes spectral triples, the Atiyah–Singer index theorem — each require additional input beyond the algebra to reach the geometry.*

*Proof.* By inspection of the technical apparatus required to develop each channel's content rigorously. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's mathematics — the McGucken manifold as a Lorentzian manifold, the Sphere expansion as a propagating wavefront, the metric tensor with indefinite signature, the curvature content of the Einstein field equations, the eight forms of entropy as kinematic invariants on the Sphere — requires the differential-geometric apparatus developed by Riemann 1854 ("Über die Hypothesen, welche der Geometrie zu Grunde liegen"), Levi-Civita 1916 (the absolute parallelism and curvature tensors), Cartan 1922–1925 (differential geometry of Lie groups, moving frames, connections on principal bundles), Ehresmann 1944 (fiber bundles), and Whitney 1936 (smooth embeddings). The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's mathematics — the operator algebra, the canonical commutator, Stone's theorem, the Wightman axiomatic apparatus, the Haag–Kastler net — requires the algebraic-analytic apparatus developed by Hilbert 1906–1912 (linear integral equations and Hilbert spaces), Stone 1932 (functional analysis of one-parameter unitary groups), von Neumann 1932 (axiomatic Hilbert-space quantum mechanics), Gelfand 1940s (commutative Banach algebras and the Gelfand transform), and the algebraic-quantum-field-theory tradition. The two mathematical traditions developed largely in parallel through the twentieth century with limited cross-fertilization at the level. The McGucken framework's contribution: identify the dual-channel architecture of physics as the dual traditions of mathematics, with $dx_4/dt = +ic$ as the principle from which both traditions descend at the level of foundational physics. ∎

**Theorem IX.30.A.1.4 (Difference 16: Different historical descent).** *The Geometric Channel descends from Huygens 1690 (wavefront propagation), Maxwell 1865 (electromagnetic field propagation), Einstein 1915 (general relativity on a Lorentzian manifold), Jacobson 1995 (thermodynamic derivation of the Einstein field equations), and the McGucken Cosmology of [5]. The Algebraic Channel descends from Noether 1918 (Lie-group invariance of variational problems), Heisenberg 1925 (matrix mechanics), Born–Jordan 1925 (algebraic formulation), Dirac 1925 (algebraic derivation of the canonical commutator), Stone 1932 (one-parameter unitary groups), von Neumann 1932 (Hilbert-space quantum mechanics), Wigner 1939 (unitary irreps of the Poincaré group), Wightman 1956 (axiomatic QFT), and Haag–Kastler 1964 (algebraic QFT). The two traditions have been institutionally separated since the 1930s, with general relativity and quantum mechanics running as disjoint research programmes for almost a century.*

*Proof.* By exhibition of the historical record. The full historical analysis appears at §IX.30.F below, with seven phases tracing the channel split from Huygens 1690 through the present. Phase 0 (1690–1900) establishes the first historical the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel versus the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel battle (Huygens versus Newton on the foundations of light), with the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel winning by Newton's prestige in the 18th century and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel reasserting itself decisively in 1801–1820 (Young, Fresnel, Poisson–Arago) and being cemented at the field-theoretic level by Maxwell 1865. Phase 5 (1927–1956) establishes the axiomatization of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel as foundational in the post-1925 quantum-mechanical tradition (Born 1926, Bohr 1927, von Neumann 1932, Wightman 1956). Phase 6 (1956–present) establishes the consolidation of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel in QFT, Standard Model, and unification programs. The two traditions descend through largely non-overlapping institutional and intellectual lineages, with the McGucken framework's contribution being the identification of both lineages as the two halves of mathematics applied to foundational physics. ∎

**Remark IX.30.A.1.5 (Why the categorical-mathematical distinction is the).** *The geometry/algebra distinction is the single deepest fact of the dual-channel architecture because every other differential signature reduces, in the final analysis, to a facet of this categorical-mathematical distinction. The ontological/epistemological distinction (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is what exists; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is what measurements report) reduces to the geometry/algebra distinction because geometry is in real spacetime and algebra is symbolic content in abstract algebraic structures, with the former being naturally identified with ontology and the latter with epistemology. The per-event/statistical-aggregation distinction reduces to the geometry/algebra distinction because per-event physics is a property of geometric primitives at specific spacetime coordinates and statistical aggregation is a property of algebraic-statistical encodings. The dynamic/directional distinction reduces to the geometry/algebra distinction because directional content requires geometric orientation and algebraic structures are sign-symmetric. The constructive-resource distinction reduces to the geometry/algebra distinction because geometric primitives can be co-generated from a single dynamic principle while algebraic axioms require multiple independent axiomatic commitments. The eighteen signatures are seventeen facets of the one categorical-mathematical distinction; the chapter develops each at the rigor required for the framework's claims but treats them all as facets of the single : the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is geometry; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is algebra.*

#### IX.30.A.2 The Ontological/Epistemological Distinction

**Theorem IX.30.A.2.1 (Difference 2: Ontology versus epistemology).** *The Geometric Channel is what exists at every event of spacetime: real McGucken Spheres expanding at velocity $c$ from every event, with definite radius $c(t - t_p)$, definite area $4\pi c^2 (t-t_p)^2$, definite $+ic$ orientation, and definite Compton-phase content on the wavefront. The Algebraic Channel is what measurements report: the Hilbert-space wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf x, t)$, operator eigenvalue spectra, the Born-rule probability density $|\psi|^2$, the trace formula $\langle \hat O \rangle = \mathrm{Tr}(\rho \hat O)$, and the unitary time-evolution $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$ — a symbolic encoding of the statistical content of detection outcomes. The Geometric Channel is ontology (being-in-spacetime); the Algebraic Channel is epistemology (being-about-measurements).*

*Proof.* The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ at every event $p$ is a geometric primitive in real four-dimensional spacetime: it has definite radius $c(t - t_p)$, definite area $4\pi c^2 (t - t_p)^2$, definite surface curvature $K = 1/[c(t-t_p)]^2$, definite Compton-phase content $\Phi(q; p) = \exp(-i\omega_C \Delta\tau(q; p))$ uniform across the spatial slice, and definite $+ic$ orientation along the timelike direction. As a point-set in the McGucken manifold $\mathcal M_G$, the Sphere occupies definite spatiotemporal coordinates and has definite geometry (radius, area, mean curvature, induced metric) at every event of its existence. The Sphere is an entity in real spacetime, not a symbolic-mathematical encoding. The framework's ontological commitment is that the $+ic$-oriented Sphere expansion at every event is what exists in the universe; this is the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel.

The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus — Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, operator algebra $B(\mathcal H)$, wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf x, t)$, Born-rule probability $P(\mathbf x, t) = |\psi(\mathbf x, t)|^2$, eigenvalue spectra of self-adjoint observables, trace formula $\langle \hat O \rangle = \mathrm{Tr}(\rho \hat O)$, canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, unitary evolution $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$ — encodes the statistical content of measurement outcomes when the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical events are aggregated across repetitions. The wavefunction $\psi$ is a complex-valued function on configuration space whose squared modulus predicts the probability density of where a detection event will register the system; $\psi$ is a calculational object that predicts measurement statistics. The Hilbert space is a mathematical arena for the statistical machinery. The operators are encodings of measurement procedures. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus is epistemology in the strict sense: it is *about* the measurement statistics of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physics, not a description of what is in spacetime. ∎

**Theorem IX.30.A.2.2 (Difference 5: Every measurement event is a Geometric-Channel event).** *Detector clicks, emulsion-grain blackening, Stern–Gerlach silver-atom deposits, photomultiplier cascades, CCD pixel charges, bubble-chamber tracks, and photodiode voltage pulses are all real physical events at definite spacetime coordinates. Each event is a head-on collision between the measured system's $+ic$-oriented Sphere and the detector atom's $+ic$-oriented Sphere; the collision 3-localizes the interaction at $(\mathbf x_q, t_q)$ and produces a definite outcome (the apparatus registers the eigenvalue corresponding to the measurement geometry at $q$). The Algebraic Channel contains no measurement events — only the statistical bookkeeping of the events that happen in the Geometric Channel.*

*Proof.* By the head-on Sphere-collision content of Theorem 7.4 of [MG-Pointwise] and Theorem IX.22.6.B.9 of the present paper. The Born-rule measurement event is the geometric overlap of the forward $+ic$-oriented Sphere from the source event $p$ with the conjugate $+ic$-oriented Sphere from the apparatus detection event $q$, with the inner-product structure being the geometric overlap of the two propagating Spheres at their head-on intersection. The collision is a real physical event: it has definite spacetime coordinates $(\mathbf x_q, t_q)$, definite energy-momentum transfer (the species's mass-shell content delivered to the detector atom), definite electromagnetic or strong or weak interaction content (depending on what the apparatus measures), and definite outcome (the apparatus registers a specific eigenvalue of the observable corresponding to the measurement geometry). The downstream apparatus propagation — the photomultiplier cascade producing an electrical signal, the CCD pixel charging up, the silver atom depositing on the photographic plate, the bubble chamber liquid nucleating along the ionization track — is a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical process operating at the $+ic$-oriented Sphere expansion of the secondary particles produced by the collision, propagating through the apparatus's material at $+ic$ with the apparatus's coupling converting the head-on collision event into a macroscopically visible signal. Every measurement event in physics is a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical event; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel contains no measurement events but only the statistical bookkeeping of events that happen in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel. ∎

**Theorem IX.30.A.2.3 (Difference 8: Direct physics versus symbolic encoding).** *The Geometric Channel contains real physical entities with spatiotemporal location: McGucken Spheres, wavefronts, light cones, geodesics, event horizons, propagating fields, and the Lorentzian metric on $\mathcal M_G$. The Algebraic Channel contains symbolic objects with no spatiotemporal location: operators, state vectors, eigenvalues, probability distributions, group representations, indexed transitions. The two are different kinds of mathematical object. The Sphere at event $p$ occupies definite spacetime coordinates; the Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ does not.*

*Proof.* the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's content is geometric and spatiotemporal. The McGucken Sphere has spatial location (centered at $\mathbf x_p$ at time $t_p$) and temporal evolution (radius $c(t - t_p)$ growing with $t$). Light cones at every event are real geometric objects with definite causal structure. Wavefronts propagate through real space at finite velocity $c$. The McGucken manifold $\mathcal M_G$ is a Lorentzian manifold with definite metric $\eta_{\mu\nu}$ and definite signature. The Einstein field equations operate on the metric as a tensor field on the manifold. All of these are physical-spatiotemporal content.

The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's content is symbolic and abstract. The Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ is an inner-product vector space — an abstract algebraic structureM with no spatiotemporal location. The wavefunction $\psi \in \mathcal H$ is a vector in this abstract space; "where" $\psi$ "is" is a category mistake in the strict ontological sense, because $\psi$ is not the kind of thing that has a where. The operator $\hat H$ is a self-adjoint linear map on $\mathcal H$; again, not a spatiotemporal object. The eigenvalues of $\hat H$ are real numbers, not entities. The probability density $|\psi(\mathbf x, t)|^2$ is a non-negative real number assigned to spacetime points, but the density is a function that takes spacetime points as arguments and returns numbers. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's content is symbolic-mathematical, not physical-spatiotemporal.

The categorical difference between physical-spatiotemporal content (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel) and symbolic-mathematics (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel) is the empirical signature of the geometry/algebra distinction at the level of *what kind of objects* each channel contains. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's objects are entities; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's objects are descriptions. ∎

**Theorem IX.30.A.2.4 (Difference 14: Sphere collision versus Born-rule density).** *In the Geometric Channel, the head-on Sphere collision at apparatus event $q$ is a physical event with definite spacetime coordinates $(\mathbf x_q, t_q)$, definite energy-momentum transfer, and definite outcome (the apparatus registers the eigenvalue corresponding to the measurement geometry at $q$). In the Algebraic Channel, the same collision is encoded as the Born-rule probability density $P(\mathbf x, t) = |\psi(\mathbf x, t)|^2$, a function on configuration space predicting the statistics of where collisions occur under repeated experiment. The collision is an event with definite outcome; the probability density is a function predicting the statistics of events.*

*Proof.* The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Sphere collision at apparatus event $q$ is a physical occurrence: at coordinates $(\mathbf x_q, t_q)$, the system's $+ic$-oriented forward Sphere from source event $p$ meets the detector atom's $+ic$-oriented forward Sphere, with the head-on collision 3-localizing the interaction at $q$ and producing a definite outcome (the apparatus registers the eigenvalue corresponding to the measurement geometry at $q$). The collision has temporal coordinates ($t_q$ definite), spatial coordinates ($\mathbf x_q$ definite), energy transfer (the system's mass-shell energy delivered to the detector atom), and outcome (definite, not statistical). The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel Born-rule probability density $P(\mathbf x, t) = |\psi(\mathbf x, t)|^2$ is a non-negative real-valued function on configuration space whose integral over a region $O$ predicts the probability that a future measurement event will register the system within $O$: $P(\text{event in } O) = \int_O |\psi(\mathbf x, t)|^2\, d^3\mathbf x$. The probability density predicts the statistics of where collisions will occur if many experiments are performed; the collision itself is a distinct object.

The two objects are categorically different: the collision is an event with definite coordinates and definite outcome; the probability density is a function predicting the statistics of events. The Born rule $P = |\psi|^2$ as a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel object is the algebraic-statistical encoding of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel geometric overlap content; the actual events being encoded are the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical occurrences. Theorem IX.30.D.4 below establishes that the Born rule is a theorem about the geometric overlap of forward and conjugate Sphere expansions at the head-on collision event, not a postulate of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel — but the *statistical encoding* of this geometry as a probability density on configuration space is the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel, while the *event* being encoded is the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel. ∎

**Theorem IX.30.A.2.5 (Difference 17: Map versus territory).** *The map–territory distinction of Korzybski 1933 ("A non-aristotelian system and its necessity for rigour in mathematics and physics," paper presented before the American Mathematical Society) supplies the general formulation. The Geometric Channel is the territory: real McGucken Spheres expanding at $+ic$ from every event of spacetime. The Algebraic Channel is the map: what fits on paper as a symbolic description of the territory — Hilbert spaces, operators, eigenvalue spectra, wavefunctions. The map predicts what detectors register at every location with extraordinary precision (atomic spectra to ten decimal places, electron $g-2$ to twelve decimal places, the Lamb shift, the Bell-inequality violations at $2\sqrt 2$). The map is not the territory.*

Every QM textbook from 1932 to the present consists of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel content — equations, operators, vectors, eigenvalue spectra, probability distributions — that can be encoded in symbolic-mathematical form. **Remark IX.30.A.2.6 (Empirical adequacy and ontological status are different categories).** *The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's empirical successes do not promote the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel to ontological status. #### IX.30.A.3 The Per-Event/Statistical-Aggregation Distinction

**Theorem IX.30.A.3.1 (Difference 15: Per-event physics versus statistical aggregation).** *The Geometric Channel is per-event: each individual Sphere collision at apparatus event $q$ occurs at definite spacetime coordinates $(\mathbf x_q, t_q)$ with definite outcome (the apparatus registers the eigenvalue corresponding to the measurement geometry at $q$). The Sphere is at $q$ if the head-on collision occurs at $q$; it does not have a probability of being at $q$. The Algebraic Channel is statistical aggregation: the wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf x, t)$ encodes the probability density $|\psi|^2$ that a measurement event will register the system at $\mathbf x$ at time $t$; the trace formula $\mathrm{Pr}(\lambda_n) = \mathrm{Tr}(\rho \hat P_n)$ predicts the probability of obtaining eigenvalue $\lambda_n$; the correlation functions, partition function, and Born rule all encode statistics of aggregated measurement outcomes across repetitions.*

*Proof.* the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus is intrinsically statistical-aggregational. The wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf x, t)$ encodes the probability density that a measurement event will register the system at $\mathbf x$ at time $t$; the prediction $P(\mathbf x, t) = |\psi(\mathbf x, t)|^2$ is meaningful only when the experiment is performed many times and the statistical distribution of registration events is tabulated. The eigenvalue spectrum of a self-adjoint observable predicts the possible outcomes of measurement; the probability of obtaining a specific eigenvalue is given by the trace formula $\mathrm{Pr}(\lambda_n) = \mathrm{Tr}(\rho \hat P_n)$ where $\hat P_n$ is the projector onto the eigenspace of $\lambda_n$. The Born rule, the trace formula, the partition function, the correlation function are all statistical-aggregational objects: they predict statistical properties of aggregated measurement outcomes, not the outcome of any individual event. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the statistical encoding of measurement aggregates.

The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's content is per-event physical. Each individual Sphere collision at apparatus event $q$ occurs at definite spacetime coordinates $(\mathbf x_q, t_q)$ with definite outcome (the apparatus registers the eigenvalue corresponding to the measurement geometry at $q$, not a statistical distribution over eigenvalues). The Sphere does not have a "probability" of being at $q$ — the Sphere is at $q$ if the head-on collision occurs at $q$. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content of a specific measurement event is the specific spacetime coordinates, the specific energy-momentum transfer, the specific interaction content, and the specific outcome of that one event. The statistical regularity of the outcomes when aggregated across many events is a derived property — it follows from the geometric distribution of where head-on Sphere collisions occur given the source's $+ic$-oriented forward Sphere and the detector's $+ic$-oriented forward Sphere geometries — but the events themselves are per-event the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel occurrences. ∎

**Remark IX.30.A.3.2 (The +ic orientation in per-event versus aggregated form).** *The $+ic$ orientation is a per-event property of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel. At every event of spacetime, the Sphere expands at $+ic$ in a definite direction; the direction is a per-event feature of the Sphere's geometry. When the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel events are aggregated across repetitions, the per-event directional content is preserved: every event has the $+ic$ direction; the aggregate carries the $+ic$ orientation as a property shared by every event in the aggregate. When the aggregate is encoded into the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic apparatus, however, the per-event directional content is not registered by the aggregation — statistical aggregation does not track per-event directionality because the aggregation operates on the outcomes (eigenvalues, positions, momenta) without tracking the directional structure of the underlying events. The $+ic$ orientation is therefore present in every individual the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel event but absent from the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel statistical encoding of the aggregated events. This is the mechanism by which the algebraic apparatus loses the geometric directional content: not because the apparatus performs a "projection" that explicitly forgets the orientation, but because statistical aggregation by its nature does not register per-event directional properties. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus is the optimal algebraic encoding of aggregated measurement statistics; the directional content is absent from the encoding because the aggregation does not carry it.*

#### IX.30.A.4 The Dynamic/Directional Content Distinction

**Theorem IX.30.A.4.1 (Difference 3: Physical fourth-coordinate expansion registered by clock-readouts versus $t$ as abstract algebra parameter).** *In the Geometric Channel, $x_4$ is the physical fourth coordinate of the McGucken manifold $\mathcal M_G$ actively expanding at velocity $ic$ as stated by the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$. The differential $dt$ in the Principle is a physical clock-tick: $t$ is what real clocks read, and every physical clock is an $x_4$-rider whose ticks are manifestations of $x_4$'s expansion — the photon clock (a photon's momenergy surfs $x_4$'s expansion at velocity $c$; the tick is a light-flight-time on the null cone), the atomic clock (atomic transition frequencies are Compton-clock beats between matter's rest energy $mc^2$ and the substrate's per-tick action $\hbar$, per Remark IX.20.8), the mechanical clock (oscillator periods are set by energy-exchange processes that all ride $x_4$'s expansion), and every biological clock. Time is not an external parameter with respect to which $x_4$ advances; time is the operational readout of $x_4$'s expansion via clocks that are themselves $x_4$-riders. The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ at every event $p$ is the $+ic$-oriented wavefront generated by this active $x_4$-expansion, propagating through real spacetime with radius $c(t - t_p)$, area $4\pi c^2 (t - t_p)^2$, and definite $+ic$ orientation, where $(t - t_p)$ is the clock-reading between event $p$ and the Sphere's current surface. In the Algebraic Channel, $t$ is a real-valued parameter indexing a one-parameter group of automorphisms of the operator algebra, with Stone's theorem (Stone 1932, "On One-Parameter Unitary Groups in Hilbert Space," *Annals of Mathematics* 33, 643–648) supplying the generator $\hat H$ via $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$; the algebra contains no fourth coordinate $x_4$, no expansion, no physical clock mechanism, no $x_4$-rider. $t$ enters as an abstract group label, disconnected from the physical fact that clocks are readout devices for $x_4$'s expansion. The Hilbert space does not move through anything and the operators do not propagate through anything; $t$ is a symbolic label flowing through the algebraic group.*

*Proof.* Stone's theorem establishes the bijective correspondence between strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups and self-adjoint operators. The unitary group $U(t)$ is a one-parameter family of bounded linear operators on $\mathcal H$ satisfying $U(0) = \mathbb 1$, $U(t_1) U(t_2) = U(t_1 + t_2)$, and strong continuity in $t$. The generator $\hat H$ is the limit $\hat H = -i\hbar \lim_{t \to 0} [U(t) - \mathbb 1]/t$ taken in the strong operator topology on the dense domain $D(\hat H) \subseteq \mathcal H$. The Schrödinger equation $i\hbar \partial_t |\psi(t)\rangle = \hat H |\psi(t)\rangle$ is the differential form of $|\psi(t)\rangle = U(t) |\psi(0)\rangle$; the equation states how the state vector $|\psi\rangle$ rotates in Hilbert space as the parameter $t$ flows. No motion in any physical space, no propagation of any physical entity, no geometry — only algebraic conjugation by a unitary operator parametrized by a real number. This is the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's dynamics: $t$ as parameter, $U(t)$ as algebraic automorphism group, $\hat H$ as algebraic generator, Schrödinger or Heisenberg picture as two equivalent algebraic presentations.

The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$, integrated with origin $x_4(0) = 0$, gives the coordinate identification $x_4 = ict$ (Step 1 of Theorem XI.5, Definition IX.18.2), with $x_4$ as the physical fourth coordinate of the McGucken manifold $\mathcal M_G$, $i$ as the perpendicularity-and-orientation marker of the principle (the Frobenius involutivity content of §XI), and $t$ as the clock-readout of $x_4$'s expansion. Clocks are physical devices whose ticks register $x_4$'s advance: the photon clock's tick is a light-flight-time on the null cone (the photon's momenergy surfs $x_4$'s expansion at velocity $c$, per §I); the atomic clock's tick is a Compton-clock beat between matter's rest energy $mc^2$ and the substrate's per-tick action $\hbar$ (Remark IX.20.8); the mechanical clock's tick is set by oscillator-period exchanges that all ride $x_4$'s expansion. The equation $dx_4/dt = ic$ is therefore self-consistent physical: $x_4$'s active expansion at velocity $c$ is what clocks register as their tick, and clocks register this expansion as the parameter $t$; the ratio $dx_4/dt$ evaluated at clock-readings equals $ic$ by the physical constitution of what clocks are. The active $x_4$-expansion at velocity $c$ in the $+ic$-oriented direction at every event of $\mathcal M_G$ produces the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ as the propagating wavefront generated at event $p$ (Definition IX.19.1, after [7]). The Sphere is a real geometric primitive: a 2-sphere with definite radius $c(t - t_p)$ where $(t - t_p)$ is a clock-reading, definite area $4\pi c^2 (t - t_p)^2$, definite surface curvature $K = 1/[c(t-t_p)]^2$, definite Compton phase content uniform across the spatial slice, and definite $+ic$ orientation at every clock-reading $t > t_p$. This is the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's dynamics: $x_4$ as the physical fourth coordinate of $\mathcal M_G$ carrying the $+ic$ orientation, $t$ as the clock-readout of $x_4$'s expansion by physical timekeepers that are themselves $x_4$-riders, the Sphere as real propagating geometric object generated by the active $x_4$-expansion. ∎

**Theorem IX.30.A.4.2 (Difference 4: Continuous propagation versus discrete spectra).** *The Geometric Channel's dynamics is continuous: the McGucken Sphere's radius $c(t-t_p)$, area $4\pi c^2(t-t_p)^2$, and Compton-phase content vary continuously with $t$; Huygens propagation, geodesic motion, and Einstein's field equations all admit continuous solutions on $\mathcal M_G$. The Algebraic Channel's content is discrete at the spectral level: atomic energy levels are discrete, angular-momentum quantum numbers are integer-valued, spin eigenvalues for half-integer spin are $\{+\hbar/2, -\hbar/2\}$, and measurement outcomes register as specific eigenvalues of the observable. The spectral theorem (von Neumann 1929, "Allgemeine Eigenwerttheorie Hermitescher Funktionaloperatoren," *Mathematische Annalen* 102, 49–131) exhibits the point-spectrum content of self-adjoint operators.*

*Proof.* By inspection of the dynamics of each channel. The McGucken Sphere's geometry varies continuously with the time coordinate: the radius $c(t-t_p)$ is a continuous function of $t$; the area $4\pi c^2 (t-t_p)^2$ is a continuous function of $t$; the Compton phase content $\Phi(q; p) = \exp(-i\omega_C \Delta\tau(q; p))$ varies continuously across the spatial slice and across time. Maxwell's wave equation $\Box \mathbf E = 0$ admits continuous solutions; Huygens' iterated wavefront construction operates on continuous wavefronts; Einstein's geodesic equation has continuous solutions. The geometric apparatus of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is intrinsically continuous in its dynamics.

In contrast, the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's content is discrete at the spectral level. The spectral theorem for self-adjoint operators (von Neumann 1929, "Allgemeine Eigenwerttheorie Hermitescher Funktionaloperatoren," *Mathematische Annalen* 102, 49–131) establishes that self-adjoint operators on Hilbert space admit spectral decompositions, with the point spectrum (eigenvalue spectrum) typically being discrete for bounded operators and for operators with compact resolvent. Atomic energy levels are discrete; angular-momentum quantum numbers are discrete; spin eigenvalues for half-integer spin are $\{+\hbar/2, -\hbar/2\}$; measurement outcomes are typically discrete (registered as specific eigenvalues of the measured observable). The Heisenberg matrix-mechanical formulation of QM is paradigmatically discrete: matrices indexed by state pairs, with the transitions between states being indexed by integer quantum numbers, and the spectroscopic data driving the formulation being intrinsically discrete (Rydberg's formula, Ritz combination principle, Balmer series). The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus is intrinsically discrete at the spectral level. ∎

**Remark IX.30.A.4.3 (Continuous-discrete duality and the position-of-i diagnosis of §IX.13.14).** *The continuous-discrete duality between the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the dynamic-content version of the discreteness/continuity diagnosis of §IX.13.14 (Diagnosis P.1.4.C of the Preface): the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel operates with substrate-tick discreteness (discrete spectra, indexed transitions, quantized outcomes); the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel operates with bulk-propagation continuity (continuous wavefronts, continuous fields, continuous geometric propagation). The duality is a feature of the geometry/algebra distinction: geometric primitives admit continuous variation as a feature (the Sphere expands continuously, the wavefront propagates continuously, the metric tensor varies continuously across the manifold); algebraic primitives admit discrete eigenvalue structures as a feature (the spectral theorem produces discrete or continuous spectra depending on the operator, with bounded operators typically having discrete spectra and unbounded operators typically having continuous spectra). The two features — continuous geometric propagation and discrete algebraic spectra — coexist in foundational physics because the two halves of mathematics carry both features ; the dual-channel architecture preserves both features by recognizing the geometric and algebra as the two halves of the architecture rather than collapsing them into one.*

**Theorem IX.30.A.4.4 (Difference 6: The +ic orientation lives in the Geometric Channel).** *The directional content of physics lives in the Geometric Channel as the geometry of the $+ic$-oriented Sphere expansion at every event: the $+ic$ orientation itself, the arrows of time, the strict Second Law $dS/dt > 0$, the retarded-Green's-function preference, the cosmological expansion direction $H_0 > 0$, the matter-dominance baryogenesis direction, monotonic decoherence, black-hole area growth $dA/dt \geq 0$, the Hawking-radiation outgoing flux, the CMB redshift direction, Penrose's Weyl-curvature arrow, the Wick-rotation sign $t \to -i\tau$, the causal-cone orientation, structure formation, and the past-low-entropy boundary condition. *Proof.* The Wigner antiunitary time-reversal operator $T$ (Wigner 1932, "Über die Operation der Zeitumkehr in der Quantenmechanik," *Nachrichten der Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen, Mathematisch-Physikalische Klasse* 1932, 546–559) acts on the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus by sending $i \to -i$ (antilinear), $\hat q \to \hat q$, $\hat p \to -\hat p$ (canonical commutator preserved: $[\hat q, -\hat p] = -i\hbar$, which is the same identity rewritten with both sides multiplied by $-1$), $\hat H \to \hat H$ (for time-reversal-invariant Hamiltonians), and $t \to -t$. The Lorentzian metric, the Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$, the Poincaré algebra, the canonical commutator, the unitary one-parameter groups, the McGucken Lagrangian, the Noether currents are all preserved (modulo conventions on parameter direction that are not part of the algebra) under the time-reversal action. This is that dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic apparatus is time-symmetric.

The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's apparatus is acted on non-by $T$: the future-directed Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ is sent to the past-directed Sphere $\Sigma_M^-(p)$; the $+ic$ orientation is sent to $-ic$; the retarded Green's function is sent to the advanced Green's function; the strict Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ is sent to $dS/dt < 0$; the Hubble expansion $H_0 > 0$ is sent to $H_0 < 0$; every $+ic$-oriented geometric primitive is sent to its time-reversed counterpart. The geometric directional content of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is time-asymmetric.

The consequence: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's time-symmetric apparatus cannot produce time-asymmetric outputs. Any function of time-symmetric data is itself time-symmetric; a time-symmetric function cannot distinguish $+ic$ from $-ic$ because $T$ exchanges them. The $+ic$ orientation is absent from the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus not because it has been "projected away" by a specific operation but because algebra is sign-symmetric and cannot carry geometric directional content. The directional content lives in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel because geometric primitives have orientations as features; algebra does not have orientations as features because the algebraic structures of operator algebras, Lie groups, eigenvalue spectra, and probability distributions are sign-symmetric. ∎

**Theorem IX.30.A.4.5 (Difference 7: Open and irreversible versus closed and unitary dynamics).** *The Geometric Channel's dynamics is open and irreversible: the $+ic$-oriented Sphere expansion at every event carries strict entropy increase via Compton coarse-graining (Theorem 14 of [4]), the cosmological expansion is $+ic$-oriented, decoherence is monotonic forward in time, and black-hole area grows monotonically. *Proof.* The Lindblad equation $\dot\rho = -i[\hat H, \rho]/\hbar + \mathcal L[\rho]$ has a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel piece (the Hamiltonian commutator, time-symmetric closed-unitary content) and a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel piece (the Lindbladian $\mathcal L[\rho]$, producing strict monotonic entropy increase via Spohn's theorem (Spohn 1978, "Entropy production for quantum dynamical semigroups," *Journal of Mathematical Physics* 19, 1227–1230)). **Theorem IX.30.A.4.6 (Difference 9: Light cone as geometric primitive versus Wightman Spectrum Condition as algebraic axiom).** *In the Geometric Channel, the future light cone $V^+(p)$ at every event $p$ is a real geometric object with definite causal content: $V^+(p) = \{q \in \mathcal M_G : q - p \in \bar V^+\}$, where $\bar V^+$ is the closed forward Lorentzian light cone. Wightman 1956 ("Quantum field theory in terms of vacuum expectation values," *Physical Review* 101, 860–866) imposed the Spectrum Condition as a primitive axiom; the axiomatic-QFT tradition (Streater–Wightman 1964, Haag–Kastler 1964, Osterwalder–Schrader 1973–75, Glimm–Jaffe constructive QFT) has carried it as a primitive axiom for sixty-eight years (1956–2024). This is a real geometric object with at every event of the manifold. The Wightman Spectrum Condition imposes the same orientation algebraically: $\mathrm{Spec}(P^\mu) \subseteq \bar V^+$ states that the joint spectrum of the four-momentum operators $P^\mu = (\hat H, \mathbf{\hat P})$ lies in the closed forward light cone, with the Hamiltonian spectrum being non-negative ($\hat H \geq 0$) for physical states. The Spectrum Condition selects $\bar V^+$ over $\bar V^-$ as the locus of allowed energy-momentum; this selection breaks the time-symmetric $\bar V^+ \cup \bar V^-$ structure that dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's time-symmetric algebra would naturally produce. Wightman 1956 imposed the Spectrum Condition as primitive in his axiomatic-QFT framework; Streater–Wightman 1964 (PCT, Spin and Statistics, and All That, W. A. Benjamin) treats it as one of the axioms; the entire subsequent axiomatic-QFT tradition (Haag–Kastler 1964, Osterwalder–Schrader 1973–75, Glimm–Jaffe constructive QFT) has carried the Spectrum Condition as a primitive axiom for sixty-eight years (1956–2024) without deriving it from the rest of the apparatus. The Spectrum Condition is the algebraic shadow of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometric causal-cone orientation, imported as an axiom because the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's time-symmetric algebraic apparatus cannot derive it (Theorem IX.30.D.1 below develops this in full detail with the Wightman Spectrum Condition as the sixty-eight-year historical residue of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's $+ic$ orientation surviving as an unexplained the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel axiom). ∎

**Theorem IX.30.A.4.7 (Difference 10: Position of the imaginary unit — exterior versus interior).** *In the Geometric Channel, the imaginary unit $i$ sits exterior to the real differential $c\,dt$ in the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$, acting as a geometric perpendicularity-marker showing that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is perpendicular to the spatial three-slice at every event of $\mathcal M_G$ (Frobenius involutivity content, §XI). The two positions of $i$ carry different roles — exterior perpendicularity marker versus interior algebraic element enforcing Hermitian and unitary relations.*

In the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometry, $i$ functions as a geometric perpendicularity-marker: $dx_4 = ic\, dt = i \cdot c\, dt$, with the imaginary unit on the *outside* of the real differential $c\, dt$ encoding that $x_4$ is a fourth-dimensional perpendicular extension from the spatial three-slice. Exteriorising $i$ via the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ gives $dx_4 = c\, d\tau$ with $\tau$ a real Euclidean coordinate; the imaginary unit is then absent from the Euclidean coordinate description, with the geometric perpendicularity-content carried by the relation $\tau = x_4/c$ rather than by the $i$ itself. The $i$ in the principle is doing geometric work: marking the perpendicularity of $x_4$ relative to the spatial slice, with the $+ic$ orientation distinguishing the forward-perpendicular direction from the time-reversed direction.

In the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebra, $i$ functions as an interior algebraic element. The canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ has the imaginary unit on the right-hand side as the element that makes the commutator skew-symmetric (since $[\hat q, \hat p] = -[\hat p, \hat q]$ implies the commutator is non-Hermitian unless paired with $i$). The Schrödinger equation $i\hbar \partial_t \psi = \hat H \psi$ has the $i$ inside the algebraic equation as the element relating the Hermitian generator $\hat H$ to the unitary time-evolution. The unitary group $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$ has the $i$ inside the exponential as the element converting the Hermitian operator $\hat H$ into a unitary operator $U(t)$ via the spectral theorem. The $i$ in the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is doing algebraic work: enforcing the Hermitian / anti-Hermitian / unitary relations that the algebraic apparatus requires.

The exterior-i versus interior-i distinction is the position-of-i diagnosis: the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel has $i$ on the outside of the geometry; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel has $i$ on the inside of the algebra. The two positions of $i$ are not equivalent — they reflect different roles of the imaginary unit in geometry versus algebra. ∎

**Theorem IX.30.A.4.8 (Difference 12: What survives Wigner's time-reversal operator $T$).** *The Algebraic Channel's content is exactly the fixed-point set of Wigner's antiunitary time-reversal operator $T$ (modulo parameter-direction conventions): the Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$, the Poincaré algebra $\mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$, the gauge groups, the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, the Schrödinger equation, Stone's one-parameter unitary group, the operator algebra $B(\mathcal H)$, the Noether currents, and the CPT operator. *Proof.* By Remarks IX.30.A.4.4 above and §IX.30.C.2 below. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's content is the fixed-point set of the time-reversal action on the framework: $\mathcal A = \mathcal B^T$ because the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus consists of objects preserved by $T$ (modulo conventions). The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's content includes the fixed-point set of $T$ (all the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel content) plus the time-asymmetric directional content (the $+ic$-oriented Sphere expansion, the arrows of time, the cosmological expansion direction, the matter-dominance, the eight forms of entropy with strict-monotonic $+ic$ orientation, and the further twelve mono-channel items enumerated at §IX.30.C.2). The content asymmetry between the two channels is the difference between the time-reversal fixed point set (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel) and the full geometry with $+ic$ orientation included (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel). ∎

The constructive-resource and historical-tradition distinctions (Signatures 11 and 16) have already been treated in §IX.30.A.1 as facets of the categorical-mathematical distinction. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel descends from an algebraic tradition — Noether 1918, Heisenberg 1925, Born–Jordan 1925, Dirac 1925, Stone 1932, von Neumann 1932, Wigner 1939, Wightman 1956, Bargmann 1957, Haag–Kastler 1964 — built from multiple independent axiomatic commitments. The full historical-evolution analysis of the dual-channel architecture appears at §IX.30.F below, tracing the channel split through seven phases from Huygens 1690 to the present.*

**Remark IX.30.A.5.2 (The eighteen signatures as facets of one categorical distinction).** *The eighteen differential signatures developed in §§IX.30.A.1–IX.30.A.6 are eighteen facets of the single categorical-mathematical distinction between geometry and algebra applied to foundational physics. The signatures are consequences of the one underlying distinction. Each signature articulates a different empirical facet of the geometry/algebra distinction at the level of foundational physics: ontology versus epistemology, per-event versus aggregated, dynamic versus parametric, continuous versus discrete, directional versus symmetric, light-cone versus Spectrum-Condition, perpendicularity-marker versus algebraic-, behavior under Wick rotation versus behavior under $T$, and so on. #### IX.30.A.6 The Behavior-under--Operations Distinction: Complementary T/Wick Symmetry Duality

The eighteenth differential signature concerns the behavior of each channel under the two fundamental operations of the framework: Wigner's antiunitary time-reversal operator $T$ (Definition IX.30.1) and the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ (§IX.13). The two channels exhibit a precise complementary-symmetry duality: each is invariant under exactly one of the two operations and transformed by the other. Difference 18 (Complementary $T$/Wick behavior). *The Geometric Channel's primitive object — the McGucken Sphere on $\mathcal M_G$ — is preserved by the McGucken–Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ (the Sphere is the same point-set under either signature) yet breaks time-symmetry ($T$ sends $+ic \to -ic$, flipping the Sphere's outward orientation). The Algebraic Channel's primitive apparatus — the operator algebra, the Hilbert space, Stone's unitary group, the canonical commutator, the Lorentz group, the Wightman axioms — is time-symmetric under $T$ (Theorem IX.30.C.3) but is not preserved by the Wick rotation: the unitary group $U(t)$ becomes a contractive semigroup $e^{-\hat H\tau/\hbar}$, the Wightman apparatus becomes the Osterwalder–Schrader apparatus, $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)$ becomes $\mathrm{ISO}(4)$, and the complex Hilbert space with sesquilinear pairing becomes a real Hilbert space with bilinear pairing. Each channel is preserved by exactly one of the two operations and transformed by the other.*

: **geometry has, at the framework's primitives, a symmetry that algebra lacks.** The Sphere is one object in $\mathcal M_G$ admitting two signature structures (Lorentzian, Euclidean) on the same point-set; the Algebraic Channel's apparatus is two distinct objects (Wightman, Osterwalder–Schrader) related by a functor (the OS reconstruction theorem [Osterwalder–Schrader 1973, 1975]) but not the same object.
