### IX.30.B Constructive Independence of Both Channels

The eighteen differential signatures of §IX.30.A establish the dual-channel architecture at the level of the categorical-mathematical distinction between geometry and algebra. The present section establishes that *each channel can be developed independently from its own foundations without invoking the other as derivational input*. The historical-constructive primacy of neither channel over the other (Sense 1 of §IX.30.0.1) is this section: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is independently buildable from algebraic-functional-analytic foundations (Theorem IX.30.B.1, exhibiting the historical-constructive routes from Noether 1918 through Wightman 1956); the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is independently buildable from geometric foundations starting from $dx_4/dt = +ic$ (Theorem IX.30.B.2, exhibiting the geometric-constructive routes from the principle to the full dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel apparatus).

The constructive-independence theorems establish that each channel is buildable from its own foundations without invoking the other; the historical construction, however, was asymmetric — the tradition built the Algebraic Channel from Heisenberg 1925 to Wightman 1956, and McGucken built the Geometric Channel from the Principle. The content asymmetry between the two channels — that dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel carries directional geometry (the $+ic$ orientation, the seventeen mono-channel items of §IX.30.C.2) that dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's time-symmetric algebraic apparatus cannot reach — is the subject of §IX.30.C below. The constructive-independence content of the present section is historical; the content-asymmetry content of §IX.30.C is mathematical.

#### IX.30.B.1 the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's Constructive Independence

**Theorem IX.30.B.1 (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's constructive independence).** *The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus — the Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, the algebra $B(\mathcal H)$, the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, Stone's theorem on unitary one-parameter groups, the Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ with metric $\eta_{\mu\nu}$, the Poincaré algebra $\mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$, the McGucken Lagrangian $\mathcal L_{\text{McG}}$ with its four sector-uniqueness theorems, the Noether conservation currents, the CPT operator, the Wightman axiomatic apparatus, the Haag–Kastler net of local observable algebras — can be developed entirely within algebraic foundations (Hilbert space theory, operator algebra, variational calculus, Lie group and Lie algebra theory) without ever invoking the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$, the $+ic$ orientation, or the Sphere-expansion as derivational input.*

*Proof.* The proof is by exhibition of the historical-constructive development of each dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel object from algebraic foundations alone.

The Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ was developed by Hilbert 1906–12 [Hilbert 1912, *Grundzüge einer allgemeinen Theorie der linearen Integralgleichungen*, B. G. Teubner] and von Neumann 1932 [von Neumann 1932, *Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik*, Springer] as the natural arena for the spectral theory of linear operators, with no reference to a McGucken Sphere.

The operator algebra $B(\mathcal H)$ was developed by von Neumann 1932 and Murray–von Neumann 1936–43 [Murray–von Neumann 1936–43, "On Rings of Operators I–IV," *Annals of Mathematics* 37 (1936) 116–229; *Transactions of the AMS* 41 (1937) 208–248; *Annals of Mathematics* 41 (1940) 94–161; *Annals of Mathematics* 44 (1943) 716–808] as the algebra of bounded linear maps on $\mathcal H$, with no Sphere as input.

The canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ was derived by Heisenberg 1925 [Heisenberg 1925, "Über quantentheoretische Umdeutung kinematischer und mechanischer Beziehungen," *Zeitschrift für Physik* 33, 879–893], Born–Jordan 1925 [Born–Jordan 1925, "Zur Quantenmechanik," *Zeitschrift für Physik* 34, 858–888], and Dirac 1925 [Dirac 1925, "The fundamental equations of quantum mechanics," *Proceedings of the Royal Society A* 109, 642–653] from the empirical claims of atomic spectra plus the algebraic requirement that the equations of motion be consistent with the correspondence-principle limit; no Sphere appears in any of these derivations.

Stone's theorem on unitary one-parameter groups was proved by Stone 1932 [Stone 1932, "On One-Parameter Unitary Groups in Hilbert Space," *Annals of Mathematics* 33, 643–648] as a purely functional-analytic theorem on the relation between bounded self-adjoint operators and strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups, with no Sphere as input.

The Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ and Poincaré algebra $\mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$ were developed by Poincaré 1905 [Poincaré 1906, "Sur la dynamique de l'électron," *Rendiconti del Circolo Matematico di Palermo* 21, 129–176, presented to the Académie des Sciences July 1905], Minkowski 1908 [Minkowski 1909, "Raum und Zeit," *Physikalische Zeitschrift* 10, 75–88], Wigner 1939 [Wigner 1939, "On Unitary Representations of the Inhomogeneous Lorentz Group," *Annals of Mathematics* 40, 149–204], and Bargmann 1954 [Bargmann 1954, "On unitary ray representations of continuous groups," *Annals of Mathematics* 59, 1–46] from the empirical Lorentz invariance of Maxwell's equations and the algebraic structure of the corresponding isometry group; no Sphere appears.

The McGucken Lagrangian's four-sector form — kinetic + Dirac + Yang–Mills + Einstein–Hilbert — was developed by Yang–Mills 1954 [Yang–Mills 1954, "Conservation of Isotopic Spin and Isotopic Gauge Invariance," *Physical Review* 96, 191–195], Dirac 1928 [Dirac 1928, "The quantum theory of the electron," *Proceedings of the Royal Society A* 117, 610–624], Hilbert 1915 [Hilbert 1915, "Die Grundlagen der Physik," *Königliche Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen, Mathematisch-Physikalische Klasse, Nachrichten* 395–407] from variational principles plus gauge-invariance requirements; no Sphere appears (though the McGucken framework's §XVII supplies the dual-channel re-derivation that does invoke the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel).

The Noether conservation currents were derived by Noether 1918 [Noether 1918, "Invariante Variationsprobleme," *Königliche Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen, Mathematisch-Physikalische Klasse, Nachrichten* 235–257] from variational symmetries; no Sphere.

The CPT operator was established by Pauli 1955 [Pauli 1955, "Exclusion Principle, Lorentz Group and Reflexion of Space-Time and Charge," in W. Pauli (ed.), *Niels Bohr and the Development of Physics*, Pergamon Press, pp. 30–51] and Lüders 1957 [Lüders 1957, "Proof of the TCP Theorem," *Annals of Physics* 2, 1–15] from Lorentz invariance plus locality plus Hermitian Hamiltonian; no Sphere.

The Wightman axiomatic apparatus was developed by Wightman 1956 [Wightman 1956, "Quantum field theory in terms of vacuum expectation values," *Physical Review* 101, 860–866], Streater–Wightman 1964 [Streater–Wightman 1964, *PCT, Spin and Statistics, and All That*, W. A. Benjamin] from axioms on vacuum-expectation distributions; no Sphere as input.

The Haag–Kastler net of local observable algebras was developed by Haag–Kastler 1964 [Haag–Kastler 1964, "An algebraic approach to quantum field theory," *Journal of Mathematical Physics* 5, 848–861], Haag 1996 [Haag 1996, *Local Quantum Physics*, Springer] from algebraic-QFT axioms; no Sphere as input.

Every the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel object in the framework was historically constructed without the Sphere as input. The constructions proceed within algebraic foundations and reach the canonical algebra. The McGucken framework's later derivations of these same objects through the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel (via the source-pair $(\mathcal M_G, D_M)$ generated by $dx_4/dt = +ic$) are *additional* derivations that supply the same through different machinery, but the original constructive independence of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus is a documented. The 47-theorem dual catalog of [3] is the catalog of objects for which both constructions exist. ∎

**Remark IX.30.B.1.1 (Constructive independence is not derivational primacy).** *Theorem IX.30.B.1 establishes that dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus can be built without the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel as input. This is a statement about constructibility, not about derivational primacy. The question of which channel is "more fundamental" — the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel as the historical-constructive starting point of operator quantum mechanics, or the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel as the McGucken-principle starting point of the framework — is a question about explanatory order, not about whether each channel's apparatus is constructively self-sufficient. Both channels are constructively self-sufficient; the framework's position is that dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is the geometric ontology (Sense 2 of §IX.30.0.1) and supplies the physical principle from which the geometry of physics descends, while the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's constructive self-sufficiency is that orthodox physics has been able to build its operator-algebraic apparatus without recognizing the geometry underneath.*

#### IX.30.B.2 the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's Constructive Independence

**Theorem IX.30.B.2 (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's constructive independence).** *The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's apparatus — the McGucken manifold $\mathcal M_G$, the source-pair $(\mathcal M_G, D_M)$ co-generated by $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Theorem IX.18.2), the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ at every event with its $+ic$ orientation, the Huygens-iterated wavefront construction (Theorem IX.19.9), the Born-rule head-on Sphere-collision derivation (Theorem 7.4 of [70]), the eight forms of entropy with strict-monotonic $+ic$ orientation (§III.A.6, after [4]), the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ as physical coordinate identification (§IX.13), the McGucken Sphere-recruited-fabric mechanism producing the Einstein field equations via Jacobson's 1995 thermodynamic derivation (§IX.25.B) — can be developed entirely from $dx_4/dt = +ic$, without invoking the operator algebra $B(\mathcal H)$, the canonical commutator, Stone's theorem, the Lorentz algebra brackets, the Wightman axiomatic apparatus, or the Haag–Kastler net of local observable algebras as derivational input.*

*Proof.* The proof proceeds by tracing the constructive development of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's apparatus from the McGucken Principle alone.

From $dx_4/dt = +ic$ at every event, integration with origin $x_4(0) = 0$ produces the integrated coordinate $x_4 = ict$ (Step 1 of Theorem XI.5).

The McGucken manifold $\mathcal M_G = (E_4, \Phi_M, D_M, \Sigma_M)$ is co-generated from the principle by the Co-Generation Theorem (Theorem IX.18.2): integration produces the constraint surface $\mathcal C_M = \{(t, x_4) : x_4 = ict\}$; differentiation along the integral flow produces the McGucken operator $D_M = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}$.

The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p) = \{(\mathbf x, t) \in \mathbb R^3 \times \mathbb R : \|\mathbf x - \mathbf x_p\| = c(t - t_p), t \geq t_p\}$ at every event $p$ is the future-null-cone propagation surface of the principle (Definition IX.19.1, after [7]).

The Huygens-iterated wavefront construction is the Reciprocal Generation Property of Theorem IX.19.4: every point $p \in \mathcal M_G$ generates the pointwise McGucken Operator $D_M^{(p)}$; the family $\{D_M^{(p)}\}_{p \in \mathcal M_G}$ generates the McGucken Space; the family of McGucken Spheres $\{\Sigma_M^+(p)\}_{p \in \mathcal M_G}$ generates the iterated wavefront propagation by the envelope construction of Huygens 1690 [Huygens 1690, *Traité de la Lumière*, Pierre van der Aa, Leiden] (the wavefront at parameter $t + \delta t$ is the envelope of secondary wavelets emanating from every point of the wavefront at parameter $t$).

The Born-rule head-on Sphere-collision construction is Theorem 7.4 of [70]: the absorber's backward (conjugate) Sphere from the apparatus event $q$ propagates back through time at $-ic$ to meet the emitter's forward Sphere from the source event $p$ at the intersection locus, with the inner-product structure being the geometric overlap of the two propagating Spheres.

The eight forms of entropy with strict-monotonic $+ic$ orientation are derived in [4] as kinematic consequences of the McGucken Sphere's $SO(3)$-invariant Brownian motion with Compton-coupling $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$; the strict monotonicity $dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t > 0$ for massive particles is forced by the $+ic$ orientation of the active expansion.

The McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ is the coordinate identification bridging Lorentzian ($x_4 = ict$, signature $(-, +, +, +)$) and Euclidean ($\tau = t$, signature $(+, +, +, +)$) descriptions of the same physical Sphere expansion (§IX.13, after [49]).

The Einstein field equations descend via Jacobson 1995's thermodynamic derivation [Jacobson 1995, "Thermodynamics of Spacetime: The Einstein Equation of State," *Physical Review Letters* 75, 1260–1263] from the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T\,dS$ on local Rindler horizons, with the McGucken Sphere supplying the horizon tangent structure (§IX.25.B).

None of these constructions invokes Hilbert space, operator algebra, canonical commutators, Stone's theorem, Lorentz algebra brackets, Wightman axiomatic apparatus, or Haag–Kastler nets as derivational input. The geometry of the McGucken Sphere is sufficient. The framework's algebraic-QFT apparatus is reached via the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel, which is constructively independent of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel (Theorem IX.30.B.1); equivalently, the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is constructively independent of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel. The two channels can each be developed from their own foundations, with neither requiring the other as input. ∎

**Remark IX.30.B.2.1 (Both channels are constructively independent).** *Theorems IX.30.B.1 and IX.30.B.2 together establish that the Geometric and Algebraic Channels are constructively independent: each is buildable from its own foundations without invoking the other. The historical construction was asymmetric — the tradition built the Algebraic Channel from Heisenberg 1925 through Wightman 1956, and McGucken built the Geometric Channel from dx₄/dt = ic. The 47-theorem dual catalog of [3] is the catalog of objects for which the two independent constructions reach the same theorem; the dual-channel disjointness predicate of Definition IX.26.2 is the formal statement that the two constructions share no intermediate machinery (the Bayesian likelihood ratio $\gtrsim 10^{141}$ of Theorem IX.26.11 is computed on this disjointness).*

The constructive-independence theorems of §IX.30.B establish that each channel can be built from its own foundations without invoking the other. #### IX.30.C.1 The Catalog of Symmetries: The 47-Theorem Dual Catalog Where Both Channels Agree

The 47-theorem dual catalog of [3] is the catalog of theorems where the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel (algebra) and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel (geometry) converge on the same physical statement via disjoint derivations. **Remark IX.30.C.1.2 (Wimsatt overdetermination as the evidential mode for symmetric content).** *The 47-theorem dual catalog supplies what Wimsatt 1981 [Wimsatt 1981, "Robustness, Reliability, and Overdetermination," in M. B. Brewer and B. E. Collins (eds.), *Scientific Inquiry and the Social Sciences*, Jossey-Bass, pp. 124–163] calls convergent overdetermination: when multiple independent routes converge on the same conclusion, the conclusion is robust against any single-route failure, and the convergence is itself evidential. The Bayesian-likelihood-ratio content of Theorem IX.26.11 ($\gtrsim 10^{141}$) is computed on this overdetermination. The McGucken framework's 47 dual derivations supply Wimsatt-style robustness for the symmetric content — each theorem is reached by two independent routes that share no intermediate machinery, and the joint convergence is the empirical-evidential signature that both routes are tracking a real (the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$).*

*The asymmetric content of §IX.30.C.2 below does not enjoy Wimsatt overdetermination — the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel cannot produce the strict Second Law, the arrow of time, the $+ic$ orientation, etc., because the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic apparatus is time-symmetric and cannot carry the directional content. The asymmetric content has a different evidential mode: principle-level forcing. The $+ic$ in the principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$ is the direct source of every asymmetric theorem; there is no need for a second route because right there in the sign of the principle. Wimsatt overdetermination applies to symmetric content; principle-level forcing applies to asymmetric content. Both are forms of empirical-support, but they have different characters.*

**Remark IX.30.C.1.3 (Historical founding case of the dual-derivation pattern: Heisenberg-Schrödinger 1925-1926 as the first instance).** *The dual-derivation pattern the 47-theorem catalog systematizes has a specific historical founding case: the Heisenberg-Schrödinger 1925-1926 dual derivation of the Bohr hydrogen energy spectrum. Heisenberg 1925 [Heisenberg, W. 1925, "Über quantentheoretische Umdeutung kinematischer und mechanischer Beziehungen," Zeitschrift für Physik 33, 879-893], with subsequent formalization by Born and Jordan [Born-Jordan 1925, "Zur Quantenmechanik," Zeitschrift für Physik 34, 858-888] and by the "Drei-Männer-Arbeit" [Born-Heisenberg-Jordan 1926, "Zur Quantenmechanik II," Zeitschrift für Physik 35, 557-615], derived the hydrogen spectrum by requiring position and momentum matrices $Q, P$ satisfying $[P, Q] = -i\hbar$ and diagonalizing the Hamiltonian matrix $H$. Schrödinger 1926a-d [Schrödinger, E. 1926a-d, "Quantisierung als Eigenwertproblem," Annalen der Physik 79, 361; 79, 489; 80, 437; 81, 109] derived the same spectrum by finding eigenvalues of the differential wave equation $-(\hbar^2/2m)\nabla^2 \psi + V(x)\psi = E\psi$ built from the Hamilton-Jacobi analogy of classical mechanics.*

*The two derivations converged on the same theorem — Bohr's hydrogen spectrum, correctly reproducing the empirically-measured Balmer, Lyman, Paschen series — from disjoint mathematical apparatuses. Matrix algebra with Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization on the Heisenberg side (with matrix theory itself unknown to Heisenberg at the time of derivation per Connes 2000 verbatim, "Heisenberg didn't know about matrices, he just worked it out, but he was told later by Born, Jordan and Dirac that the algebra he had worked out was known to mathematicians as the algebra of matrices"). Hamilton-Jacobi mechanics with Sturm-Liouville PDE eigenvalue theory on the Schrödinger side (with mathematician Hermann Weyl supplying mathematical collaboration).*

*The two derivations started from different empirical foundations. Heisenberg targeted spectrograph output — the frequencies and intensities of atomic emission spectral lines from photographic plates, with the Ritz combination principle [Ritz, W. 1908, "On a new law of series spectra," Astrophysical Journal 28, 237-243] as the primary observational commitment. Schrödinger targeted a theoretical construct rather than a new empirical measurement — the de Broglie matter-wave hypothesis of 1924 [de Broglie, L. 1924, "Recherches sur la théorie des Quanta," Doctoral thesis, University of Paris], with the Bohr hydrogen spectrum as convergence benchmark. Muller 1997 [Muller, F.A. 1997, "The equivalence myth of quantum mechanics — Parts I and II," Studies in History and Philosophy of Modern Physics 28, 35-61 and 219-247] and Madrid-Casado 2008 [ScienceDirect S1355219808000063, "Why were Matrix Mechanics and Wave Mechanics considered equivalent?"] both record verbatim: "The Matrix Mechanics was an algebraic approach employing the technique of manipulating matrices. The Wave Mechanics, in contrast, employed differential equations and had a basic partial differential wave equation at its heart. In addition, the formalisms were initially applied to two distinct sets of experimental results."*

*Schrödinger 1926e ["Über das Verhältnis der Heisenberg-Born-Jordanschen Quantenmechanik zu der meinen," Annalen der Physik 79, 734-756] supplied the first formal equivalence-proof between the two formulations via identification of matrix elements with integrals of wave functions over configuration space, opening with the verbatim statement of the derivational disjointness: "Considering the extraordinary differences between the starting-points and the concepts of Heisenberg's quantum mechanics and of the theory which has been designated 'undulatory' or 'physical' mechanics, and has lately been described here, it is very strange that these new two theories agree with one another with regard to the known facts, where they differ from the old quantum theory... starting-points, presentations, methods and in fact the whole mathematical apparatus, seem fundamentally different." Schrödinger 1926e's proof is the first historical instance of a Wimsatt-style convergent-overdetermination proof for a QM theorem — two derivations sharing no intermediate machinery converging on the same physical statement.*

*The 47-theorem catalog of Proposition IX.30.C.1.1 above extends the pattern that Heisenberg-Schrödinger 1925-1926 instantiated at one theorem (the hydrogen spectrum) to 46 additional theorems across QM and GR, and identifies the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic as the source principle from which both derivational channels descend. Full historical documentation with verbatim primary and scholarly quotes appears in Remark P.3.3.1 of the Preface (§P.3.3).*

*Scope-marking of what the framework does not claim as novel. The convergent-overdetermination pattern itself is not a framework innovation. The 1925-1926 case is prior art for the pattern: the Bohr hydrogen spectrum was reached twice, from different empirical starting-data (Ritz-combination spectral-line intensities for Heisenberg; de Broglie matter-wave hypothesis transmitted via Einstein 1925 for Schrödinger), through different mathematical apparatuses (matrix algebra with Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization; Hamilton-Jacobi mechanics with Sturm-Liouville PDE theory), by investigators with different training (Heisenberg 23, Munich-Göttingen-Copenhagen spectroscopic apprentice; Schrödinger 38, Vienna continuum-physics veteran of fifteen years), within twelve months, with nobody intending the double derivation. Wimsatt-style convergent overdetermination as an evidential mode is therefore documented at one QM theorem in 1925-1926 and does not require the McGucken framework to introduce it. What the framework claims is narrower and checkable at the technical level. First, the convergence is systematic rather than accidental — every one of the 47 catalogued theorems admits both a dx₄/dt=ic-Algebraic-Channel derivation and a dx₄/dt=ic-Geometric-Channel derivation, and the systematicity is verified theorem-by-theorem in [3] and Lemma IX.10.4. Second, the convergence recurs at 47 theorems across QM and GR sectors rather than one accidental case at the hydrogen spectrum. Third, both derivational channels descend from a single identified source principle dx₄/dt = ic rather than from unrelated starting-points that happened to converge. Fourth, the derivational disjointness of the two channels at each theorem is verifiable via Definition IX.26.2's Dual-Channel Disjointness Predicate rather than being claimed only informally. The framework's contribution beyond the 1925-1926 prior art is (a) the systematicity of the pattern across 47 theorems, (b) the identification of dx₄/dt = ic as the common upstream source, and (c) the disjointness predicate as the technical criterion that makes the pattern checkable at each theorem. These four are what a referee could dispute at the technical level; the phenomenon of two-derivations-converging-on-one-theorem at the founding of QM is not the framework's to claim.*

*Scholarly caveat on the equivalence claim. Muller 1997 argued that the 1920s consensus on Heisenberg-Schrödinger equivalence rested on an ontologically-specific proof (matching hydrogen energy levels, not general Hilbert-space isomorphism), with the rigorous general isomorphism established only in von Neumann 1932 [von Neumann, J. 1932, Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik, Springer]. The Stone-von Neumann uniqueness theorem [Stone 1930, von Neumann 1931] later provided the finite-degree-of-freedom uniqueness result. In infinite degrees of freedom (QFT), three independent lines of work establish that the two pictures diverge in ways the finite-dimensional equivalence proofs do not cover. First, Haag's theorem [Haag 1955] establishes that the interaction picture does not exist as a proper Hilbert-space representation and inequivalent representations of the canonical commutation relations exist in QFT. Second, the categorical inequivalence result of Johnson-Freyd 2021 [Johnson-Freyd, T. 2021, "Heisenberg-Picture Quantum Field Theory," in Alekseev, A., Frenkel, E., Rosso, M., Webster, B., and Yakimov, M. (eds), *Representation Theory, Mathematical Physics, and Integrable Systems: In Honor of Nicolai Reshetikhin*, Progress in Mathematics Vol. 340, pp. 371-409, Birkhäuser/Springer; arXiv:1508.05908] establishes at the categorical level that the Schrödinger picture is captured by Atiyah-Segal-type functors (symmetric monoidal functors from an $(\infty, d)$-category of spacetimes to an $(\infty, d)$-category of vector spaces), while the Heisenberg picture requires factorization-algebra or skein-theory structure with target categories of pointed vector spaces or associative algebras. Third, Dirac himself in 1965 [Dirac, P.A.M. 1965, "Quantum Electrodynamics without Dead Wood," Physical Review 139(3B), pp. B684-B690] — the physicist who had unified matrix mechanics and wave mechanics via transformation theory in 1927 and via the 1930 *Principles of Quantum Mechanics* textbook — raised the inequivalence of the two pictures in QED. Verbatim from the Dirac 1965 abstract: "In quantum electrodynamics one can obtain a Hamiltonian which gives reasonable field equations in the Heisenberg picture, but which does not allow of solutions of the wave equation to represent physical states in the Schrödinger picture. The inference is that the Heisenberg picture is a good picture, the Schrödinger picture is a bad picture, and the two pictures are not equivalent. The usual proof of the equivalence of the two pictures fails because the state vector of the Schrödinger picture does not remain in Hilbert space." Bédard 2025 [Bédard, C.A. 2025, "Realism and the Inequivalence of the Two Quantum Pictures," arXiv:2510.02138, forthcoming in Ney, A. (ed.), *Local Quantum Mechanics: Everett, Many Worlds, and Reality*, Oxford University Press] extends the inequivalence to the realism level: verbatim from the abstract, "Whereas the Schrödinger picture posits a time-evolving wave function, the Heisenberg picture posits so-called descriptors, time-evolving generators of the algebra of observables. These two structures are non-isomorphic: descriptors surject onto but do not reduce to the Schrödinger state. Hence, under realism, the pictures are inequivalent." The McGucken framework's dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic-Channel and dx₄/dt=ic Geometric-Channel distinction extends and refines the Heisenberg-Schrödinger split by identifying dx₄/dt = ic as the source principle and by extending the split beyond QM to GR, thermodynamics, and cosmology, with the derivational disjointness criterion of Definition IX.26.2 above supplying the mathematical criterion that the historical Heisenberg-Schrödinger case instantiates.*

#### IX.30.C.2 The Catalog of Asymmetries: Seventeen Mono-Channel Items with the Loschmidt No-Go Theorem

The Catalog of Asymmetries enumerates the claim carried by the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel alone — the directional geometry that dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's time-symmetric algebraic apparatus cannot reach. Each item in the catalog is time-asymmetric under Wigner's antiunitary $T$ (sent to a sign-reversed object that does not exist as a physical phenomenon in our universe). Each is therefore the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel-inaccessible and lives in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometry alone.

**Proposition IX.30.C.2.1 (ACatalog of Symmetries).** *The following 17 items constitute the catalog of time-asymmetric the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content of the McGucken framework. Each is forced by the $+ic$ orientation of the active expansion $dx_4/dt = +ic$ and has no dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel derivation:*

*(G1) The $+ic$ orientation itself.* The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ at every event expands at $+ic$, not $-ic$. Under $T$, $+ic \to -ic$. The orientation choice is the asymmetric content; every other item below descends from it.

*(G2) The strict Second Law for massive particles.* $dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t > 0$ for $t > 0$, derived in §III.A.6 from Compton-coupling Brownian motion on the McGucken Sphere ([4, Theorems 4–14]). Under $T$, the strict-monotonic inequality flips to $dS/dt < 0$, which is not observed.

*(G3) The strict Second Law for photon ensembles.* $dS/dt = 2k_B/(t - t_0) > 0$ for photon ensembles on the McGucken Sphere ([4]). Same status as (G2).

*(G4) The thermodynamic arrow of time.* The combined fact that all entropy-bearing processes in the universe have $dS/dt > 0$, manifesting at every scale from molecular collisions to cosmological structure formation. The aligned arrow is the consequence of (G1) at every event.

*(G5) The radiative arrow of time.* The retarded Green's function $G_R(t - t', \mathbf x - \mathbf x') = \theta(t - t')[\ldots]$ is preferred over the advanced $G_A$ in empirical electromagnetic propagation. Maxwell's equations admit both; the physical universe uses retarded. Under $T$, $G_R \to G_A$. Wheeler–Feynman 1945's absorber theory attempted to derive the retarded preference via future-boundary conditions; the McGucken framework derives it as the $+ic$ Sphere expansion's commitment.

*(G6) The cosmological arrow of time.* $H_0 > 0$. The universe expands rather than contracts. Under $T$, expansion becomes contraction. The Hubble flow, the CMB redshift, the cosmic recession of galaxies — all the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content carried by the $+ic$.

*(G7) The quantum-mechanical arrow at measurement.* The Born rule's measurement event happens forward in time: $P = |\psi|^2$ is the probability of *future* detection given preparation, not past memory. Measurement is irreversible. Under $T$, the measurement-event direction flips, which is not observed.

*(G8) Decoherence monotonicity.* Off-diagonal density-matrix elements in the pointer basis decay monotonically to zero; coherent superpositions become classical mixtures, not the other way around. Under $T$, the decay direction reverses, producing spontaneous coherence regeneration from classical mixtures, which is not observed.

*(G9) The Wick rotation sign $t \to -i\tau$.* The convergent Euclidean path integral requires the specific sign $t \to -i\tau$, producing $\exp(-S_E/\hbar)$; the opposite sign $t \to +i\tau$ would produce $\exp(+S_E/\hbar)$ which diverges. The sign is fixed by the $+ic$ Sphere expansion direction. Under $T$, the Wick-rotation sign flips, and the Euclidean path-integral construction fails.

*(G10) Causal cone orientation.* The future light cone $V^+(p)$ at every event $p$ is the locus of physically accessible signals; the past light cone $V^-(p)$ is the locus of signals already received. Causality says effects follow causes. Under $T$, $V^+ \leftrightarrow V^-$, reversing the causal arrow.

*(G11) Sphere recursion direction.* The Huygens-iterated wavefront propagation runs forward in time: every Sphere point generates a secondary Sphere at $+ic$, ad infinitum. Under $T$, the recursion runs backward, contradicting Huygens 1690's empirical-physical construction.

*(G12) Cosmological structure formation.* Structure forms over cosmic time — gravitational collapse produces galaxies, stars, planets. The recruited-fabric mechanism operates in the $+ic$ direction. Under $T$, structure decays into uniformity, contradicting the empirical record.

*(G13) Black hole area growth $dA/dt \geq 0$.* Hawking's area theorem [Hawking 1971, "Gravitational radiation from colliding black holes," *Physical Review Letters* 26, 1344–1346] states the total horizon area of black holes is non-decreasing in time. Under $T$, the area decreases, violating the area theorem.

*(G14) Hawking radiation outgoing-flux direction.* Hawking radiation propagates outward from the black-hole horizon, carrying energy away to infinity. Under $T$, the radiation propagates inward (incoming from infinity to a white hole), a configuration not observed in nature for astrophysical black holes.

*(G15) CMB redshift direction.* The cosmic microwave background photons are redshifted by the cosmological expansion. Under $T$, redshift becomes blueshift, contradicting the observed CMB spectrum.

*(G16) Matter-antimatter asymmetry / baryogenesis direction.* The universe is matter-dominated rather than antimatter-dominated. Under $T$, matter ↔ antimatter (via the $+ic/-ic$ Sphere pair, Sub-theorem F6 of Theorem IX.23.20), reversing the asymmetry direction. The Sakharov 1967 conditions for baryogenesis [Sakharov 1967, "Violation of CP Invariance, C asymmetry, and baryon asymmetry of the universe," *JETP Letters* 5, 24–27] (baryon number violation, C-violation, CP-violation, departure from thermal equilibrium) are themselves the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel asymmetric content; two of three (C-violation, CP-violation) are explicitly listed in the mono-channel catalog.

*(G17) Penrose Weyl curvature arrow.* Penrose's Weyl curvature hypothesis [Penrose 1989, *The Emperor's New Mind*, Oxford University Press; Penrose 2010, *Cycles of Time*, Bodley Head]: the Weyl curvature of the universe was very low at the Big Bang (smooth, uniform) and grows monotonically as black holes form and the universe becomes clumpy. Under $T$, the Weyl curvature evolution reverses, contradicting the observed cosmological structure formation.

*Each of (G1)–(G17) is time-asymmetric, the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel-inaccessible, and has no dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel image. The mono-channel catalog is the catalog of directional geometry carried by the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel alone.*

*Proof.* Each item (G1)-(G17) is verified time-asymmetric by direct application of Wigner's antiunitary $T$ as defined in §IX.30.A: $T$ sends $i \to -i$, $t \to -t$, momentum $\mathbf p \to -\mathbf p$, angular momentum $\mathbf L \to -\mathbf L$, and reverses temporal orientation. (G1) Under $T$, $+ic \to -ic$, a sign-reversed orientation. (G2) Under $T$, $dS/dt > 0$ becomes $dS/dt < 0$ (the time derivative flips sign). (G3) Same mechanism as (G2). (G4)-(G6) The thermodynamic, radiative, and cosmological arrows all flip direction under $T$. (G7) Measurement irreversibility's forward direction reverses. (G8) Decoherence monotonicity's direction reverses. (G9) The Wick rotation sign $t \to -i\tau$ becomes $t \to +i\tau$, producing $\exp(+S_E/\hbar)$ which diverges. (G10) The causal cone $V^+ \leftrightarrow V^-$. (G11) Sphere recursion reverses. (G12) Structure formation becomes structure dissipation. (G13) $dA/dt \geq 0$ becomes $dA/dt \leq 0$. (G14) Hawking radiation flux direction reverses. (G15) CMB redshift becomes blueshift. (G16) Matter ↔ antimatter via Sub-theorem F6 of Theorem IX.23.20. (G17) Penrose Weyl curvature evolution reverses. All seventeen items are therefore time-asymmetric. Their Algebraic Channel inaccessibility follows from Theorem IX.30.A.4.4: the Algebraic Channel's apparatus is time-symmetric, and a time-symmetric algebraic structure cannot produce time-asymmetric output from time-symmetric input (the involution preserves the time-symmetric class). The mono-channel catalog is therefore the catalog of directional geometry carried by the Geometric Channel alone. ∎

**Theorem IX.30.C.2.2 (Loschmidt no-go theorem).** *Under the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$ with the McGucken-Sphere Compton-coupling Brownian mechanism of [4] (diffusion coefficient $D_x^{\text{(McG)}} = \varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega/(2\gamma_L^2)$, Theorem 14 of [4]), no entropy-decreasing macroscopic trajectory exists.*

*Proof.* Such a trajectory would require the McGucken Sphere to contract rather than expand at every event involved in the trajectory — equivalently, the active expansion rate would have to be $-ic$ rather than $+ic$. By the principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$ as the physical commitment of the framework, the orientation is fixed at $+ic$ at every event. The Compton-coupling Brownian mechanism of [4, Theorems 4–14] derives the strict-monotonic $dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t > 0$ from the $+ic$-oriented Sphere expansion plus the spatial-projection isotropy of $x_4$-driven displacement (Proposition 4.5.2 of [4]) plus the Wiener-process measure on iterated Sphere steps (Proposition 4.5.3 of [4]) plus the central limit theorem on the heat-kernel Gaussian (Proposition 4.5.4 of [4]). #### IX.30.C.4 The Complementary T/Wick Symmetry Duality: The Categorical-Mathematical Theorem of the Dual-Channel Architecture

The content-asymmetry theorem (Theorem IX.30.C.3) establishes that the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel carries directional geometry that the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's time-symmetric algebraic apparatus cannot reach. The position-of-i diagnosis (Signature 10, Theorem IX.30.A.4.7) establishes that $i$ sits exterior to the Geometric Channel's principle (as perpendicularity marker) and interior to the Algebraic Channel's apparatus (as algebraic-element). Both facts admit a *single* unifying explanation: the two channels exhibit a precise complementary symmetry duality under the two fundamental operations of the framework, with each channel invariant under exactly one operation and transformed by the other. The present section establishes this duality as the theorem of the dual-channel architecture, from which both the position-of-i diagnosis and the content-asymmetry theorem descend as derivative consequences.

**Theorem IX.30.C.4 (Complementary $T$/Wick symmetry duality of the dual-channel architecture).** *The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel exhibit a precise complementary-symmetry duality under the two fundamental operations of the framework: Wigner's antiunitary time-reversal operator $T$ (Definition IX.30.1) and the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ (§IX.13).*

*(i) Geometric-Channel symmetry: the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's primitive object (the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ as a real geometric object on $\mathcal M_G$) is preserved by the McGucken-Wick rotation but is not time-symmetric. The $+ic$ orientation of the Sphere expansion is the foundational directional content that $T$ sends to $-ic$; under Wick rotation, the same Sphere as a point-set on $\mathcal M_G$ admits two signature readings (Lorentzian with Huygens wavefront propagation; Euclidean with Wiener-process diffusion) without the geometric primitive being transformed.*

*(ii) Algebraic-Channel symmetry: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's primitive apparatus (the operator algebra, Hilbert space, Stone's one-parameter unitary group, canonical commutator, Lorentz group, Wightman axioms) is time-symmetric (Theorem IX.30.C.3) but is not preserved by the McGucken-Wick rotation. Under $T$, the algebraic apparatus is preserved modulo conventions on parameter direction (Theorem IX.30.A.4.4). Under Wick rotation, the apparatus is form-transformed: the unitary one-parameter group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat Ht/\hbar}$ becomes the contractive semigroup $e^{-\hat H\tau/\hbar}$ (no longer a group, Stone's theorem replaced by Hille–Yosida); the Wightman axiomatic apparatus becomes the Osterwalder–Schrader axiomatic apparatus (different axiomatic structure related by OS reconstruction under reflection positivity [Osterwalder–Schrader 1973, 1975]); the Poincaré group $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)$ becomes the Euclidean group $\mathrm{ISO}(4)$ (different real forms of the same complexification $\mathrm{ISO}(4,\mathbb C)$); the complex Hilbert space with sesquilinear pairing becomes a real Hilbert space with bilinear pairing.*

*(iii) Complementarity: each channel is invariant under exactly one of the two operations and transformed by the other. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the channel of time-symmetry; the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is the channel of Wick-rotation-invariance. The complementarity is exact and ; no channel is invariant under both, and no channel is invariant under neither.*

*Proof.* The complementary symmetry duality follows from the position-of-i analysis (Signature 10, Theorem IX.30.A.4.7) combined with the primitives of each channel.

*Step 1 (The Geometric Channel under $T$).* The Sphere expansion is generated by the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$ with the $+ic$ orientation as the primitive distinguishing forward Sphere expansion (causal-cone-future, $\Sigma_M^+(p)$) from past-directed contraction ($\Sigma_M^-(p)$). The time-reversal action of Definition IX.30.1 sends $i \to -i$ and $t \to -t$, hence sends $dx_4/dt = +ic$ to $dx_4/dt = -ic$, hence sends $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ to $\Sigma_M^-(p)$. The Sphere is not time-symmetric; its orientation is reversed. Equivalently: the $+ic$ orientation is the seventeen-mono-channel-item-generating asymmetric content of §IX.30.C.2; the time-reversal action exchanges $+ic$ with $-ic$; the seventeen mono-channel items are exactly the time-asymmetric content of the framework.

*Step 2 (The Geometric Channel under Wick rotation).* The McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ is a coordinate identification on the real four-manifold $\mathcal M_G$ (§IX.13), not a transformation of the geometric primitive but a re-labeling of the time coordinate. The Sphere as a subset of $\mathcal M_G$ — defined by the locus $|\mathbf x - \mathbf x_p|^2 = c^2(t - t_p)^2$ in Lorentzian signature, equivalently $|\mathbf x - \mathbf x_p|^2 + (\tau - \tau_p)^2 = r^2$ on the Euclidean section under the rotation $t = -i\tau$ — is the same point-set on $\mathcal M_G$, with different signature labels producing different interpretations of the Sphere's content. In Lorentzian signature the Sphere generates Huygens wavefront propagation at velocity $c$ with Compton phase accumulation $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$; in Euclidean signature the Sphere generates Wiener-process diffusion with diffusion coefficient $D = \hbar/(2m)$. The two readings are related by the Feynman–Kac formula [Kac 1949] applied to the analytic continuation $t \to -i\tau$. The geometric primitive is preserved by the rotation; only the signature on top of it changes.

*Step 3 (The Algebraic Channel under $T$).* By Theorem IX.30.C.3, every primitive of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is time-symmetric. The Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ admits an antiunitary time-reversal action preserving the inner product. The operator algebra is preserved by conjugation under $T$. The unitary one-parameter group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat Ht/\hbar}$ has the inverse $U(-t) = U(t)^{-1}$ in the same group; conjugation by $T$ sends $U(t)$ to $U(-t)$ which is in the same group. The canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ is preserved by $T$ modulo conventions on parameter direction: $T\hat qT^{-1} = \hat q$, $T\hat pT^{-1} = -\hat p$, $TiT^{-1} = -i$, giving $T[\hat q, \hat p]T^{-1} = [\hat q, -\hat p] = -[\hat q, \hat p] = -i\hbar$ which equals $TiT^{-1}\cdot\hbar$, so the commutator is preserved under the antilinear action. The Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ admits $T$ as one of its discrete automorphisms. The Wightman axiomatic apparatus is time-symmetric via the CPT theorem (combined with $C$ and $P$).

*Step 4 (The Algebraic Channel under Wick rotation).* The unitary group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat Ht/\hbar}$ under the substitution $t = -i\tau$ becomes $U(-i\tau) = e^{-\hat H\tau/\hbar}$. This is a contractive semigroup, not a unitary group: it is norm-decreasing for $\tau > 0$ when $\hat H \geq 0$ (which holds by the Wightman Spectrum Condition); it lacks inverses (no $\tau < 0$ branch in the physical domain of states with finite energy); Stone's theorem does not apply because the family is not a continuous one-parameter unitary group. The Wightman axiomatic apparatus — Lorentz-covariant operator-valued distributions, Spectrum Condition $\mathrm{Spec}(P^\mu) \subseteq \bar V^+$, cluster decomposition, polynomial Heisenberg algebra — transforms under Wick rotation to the Osterwalder–Schrader axiomatic apparatus — Euclidean-covariant Schwinger distributions, reflection positivity, cluster decomposition, polynomial algebra on the Euclidean section. The two apparatuses are equivalent in content under reflection positivity (OS reconstruction theorem [Osterwalder–Schrader 1973, 1975]) but are not the same apparatus: they have different axiomatic structures, different group actions ($\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)$ versus $\mathrm{ISO}(4)$), different Hilbert spaces (complex with sesquilinear pairing versus real with bilinear pairing), different time-evolution objects (unitary group versus contractive semigroup), and different positivity conditions (Spectrum Condition versus reflection positivity). The form is transformed; reconstructable via the OS theorem under the reflection-positivity hypothesis.

*Step 5 (Complementarity).* The source of the complementary duality is the geometric-versus-algebraic primitive analysis. The Geometric Channel's primitive — the Sphere as a point-set on $\mathcal M_G$ — is intrinsic to the manifold and does not depend on which signature is read on top of it; it is preserved by Wick rotation (which changes only the signature) but is transformed by $T$ (which changes the orientation of the Sphere expansion). The Algebraic Channel's primitive — the operator algebra, Hilbert space, group action — is built on top of a chosen signature; it must be re-built when the signature changes, so it is transformed by Wick rotation. The Algebraic Channel's apparatus contains no directional content as primitive (every algebraic structure is sign-symmetric on $+ic$ because algebraic operations preserve time-symmetry of operator-algebraic structures); it is therefore preserved by $T$. The complementarity is exact at the level of primitives. ∎

**Corollary IX.30.C.4.1 (The position-of-i diagnosis as a derivative consequence of the symmetry duality).** *The position-of-i diagnosis of §P.1.4.A (Signature 10, Theorem IX.30.A.4.7) — that $i$ sits exterior in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ (as perpendicularity marker showing $x_4 \perp$ spatial slice) and interior in the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus (as algebraic-element enforcing Hermitian / anti-Hermitian / unitary relations) — is a derivative consequence of the complementary $T$/Wick symmetry duality.*

*Proof.* Wick rotation acts on $i$ via the relation $t = -i\tau$. Where $i$ sits exterior to the channel's primitive (as in the Geometric Channel's $dx_4/dt = ic$), the rotation acts outside the primitive: the $i$ is absorbed into the signature label, leaving the Sphere as a real geometric primitive in either signature. Where $i$ sits interior to the channel's apparatus (as in the Algebraic Channel's operator algebra), the rotation acts inside the apparatus: the $i$ in $U(t) = e^{-i\hat Ht/\hbar}$ is exchanged with the real parameter $\tau$, transforming the unitary group to the contractive semigroup. The position of $i$ relative to the channel's primitive *determines* whether Wick rotation acts outside (preserving the primitive) or inside (transforming the apparatus). The complementary symmetry duality of Theorem IX.30.C.4 is therefore equivalent to the position-of-i diagnosis; each implies the other via the algebraic-versus-geometric primitive analysis. ∎

**Corollary IX.30.C.4.2 (The content-asymmetry theorem as a derivative consequence of the symmetry duality).** *The content-asymmetry theorem (Theorem IX.30.C.3) — that the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel carries directional geometry the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus cannot reach — is a derivative consequence of the complementary $T$/Wick symmetry duality.*

The content-asymmetry theorem follows: the seventeen mono-channel items of §IX.30.C.2 are exactly the $+ic$-oriented directional content carried by the Geometric Channel and inaccessible to the Algebraic Channel. ∎

**Corollary IX.30.C.4.3 (Greater symmetry of geometry than algebra at the foundational-primitive level).** *The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's primitive (the McGucken Sphere) admits Wick rotation as an internal symmetry — the rotation acts on the Sphere by changing the signature without changing the primitive object. *Proof.* By Theorem IX.30.C.4 (Steps 3-5), the Wick rotation $t \to -i\tau$ preserves the Sphere as a point-set on $\mathcal M_G$ while changing the signature from Lorentzian to Euclidean (Step 3). The Sphere's symmetry group with respect to signature inversion is therefore $\{\text{identity, Wick rotation}\}$ (a two-element group acting on the primitive object); the Algebraic Channel apparatus's symmetry group with respect to signature inversion is $\{\text{identity}\}$ alone (the Wick rotation transforms the apparatus into a different apparatus, not preserving the primitive). Geometry therefore carries one additional symmetry — signature inversion as primitive-preserving — that algebra does not carry. The asymmetry is at the level of primitive-object preservation, not at the claim level (OS reconstruction supplies content-equivalence under reflection positivity). ∎

#### IX.30.C.5 Necessity and Sufficiency of dx₄/dt = ic for Quantum Mechanics, General Relativity, and Thermodynamics

The dual-channel architecture established in §§IX.30.A–IX.30.C.4 supplies the framework within which the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic operates. I now establish that dx₄/dt = ic is **necessary and sufficient** for the three subfields of physics — quantum mechanics, general relativity, and classical thermodynamics — at the level of their full theorem content. The proof is in three parts: sufficiency by exhibition (the 47-theorem catalog of [3] + the 23 classical thermodynamic theorems of [4] together supplying seventy independent derivations from dx₄/dt = ic), component-necessity (each of the three components of dx₄/dt = ic — the imaginary unit $i$, the rate $c$, the active expansion $d/dt$ — is independently necessary, with explicit specification of which subset of physics collapses under removal of each component), and joint necessity-and-sufficiency of the combined nonlocal active expansion at $c$.

**Theorem IX.30.C.5 (Necessity and sufficiency of dx₄/dt = ic for quantum mechanics, general relativity, and thermodynamics).** *The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is necessary and sufficient for the full theorem content of quantum mechanics, general relativity, and classical thermodynamics. Specifically:*

*(i) Sufficiency. dx₄/dt = ic generates the 47-theorem catalog of [3] (24 general-relativistic theorems and 23 quantum-mechanical theorems, 94 derivations total across both channels) and the 23 classical thermodynamic theorems of [4] (the strict Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ via the Compton-coupling Brownian mechanism, the zeroth, first, and third laws as derived corollaries, and the Boltzmann–Gibbs distributions as forced consequences). The 70 derivations carry the cumulative empirical Bayesian likelihood ratio $\gtrsim 10^{141}$ at conservative benchmarks (Theorem IX.26.11).*

#### IX.30.C.6 The Nonlocality-from-i Theorem: The Imaginary Unit in dx₄/dt = ic Is the Source of Quantum Nonlocality

The previous subsection established that the imaginary unit $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$ is independently necessary for the framework. The present subsection establishes the *reason*: the $i$ is the source of the Lorentzian null structure that makes the McGucken Sphere a *single nonlocal surface* — a foliation leaf, level set, Huygens caustic, Legendrian submanifold, conformal pencil member, and null-hypersurface cross-section — rather than a collection of independent points at positive Euclidean distance. The nonlocality of quantum mechanics traces, through this source, to the imaginary unit in the McGucken Principle.

**Theorem IX.30.C.6 (The Nonlocality-from-$i$ Theorem).** *The imaginary unit $i$ in the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the source of quantum nonlocality. Specifically:*

*(i) Counterfactual without the $i$. Under $dx_4/dt = c$ (real, without the $i$), squaring gives $dx_4^2 = +c^2\,dt^2$, producing the Euclidean line element $ds^2_E = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + c^2\,dt^2$ on the four-manifold. The locus $ds^2_E = 0$ reduces to the single point at the origin; no null cone exists; no light cone; no causal structure; the McGucken Sphere reduces to a real Euclidean 3-sphere of radius $r = ct$ with positive Euclidean distance from every wavefront point to the source, and positive Euclidean pairwise distance between distinct wavefront points. The wavefront's surface points are independent points in Euclidean space, not a single connected nonlocal entity.*

*(ii) Actual structure with the $i$. Under $dx_4/dt = ic$ (with the imaginary unit), squaring gives $dx_4^2 = -c^2\,dt^2$, producing the Lorentzian line element $ds^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 - c^2\,dt^2$ with indefinite $(-, +, +, +)$ signature. The locus $ds^2 = 0$ is the full null cone — a codimension-one null hypersurface in $\mathcal M_G$, with the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ as its spacelike-slice cross-section at every retarded time. Every wavefront point on $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ satisfies $|\mathbf x - \mathbf x_p|^2 - c^2(t - t_p)^2 = 0$ — zero Lorentzian interval between the wavefront point and the source event $p$. The McGucken Sphere is a single nonlocal surface — one wavefront spanning the full 2-sphere at every retarded time, with all surface points sharing the source event $p$, the same $x_4$-coordinate at emission, and the same Compton phase content.*

*(iii) Six independent senses of geometric nonlocality (after [Uploaded paper, §4]).* The McGucken Sphere as nonlocal surface admits six independent mathematical characterizations, each yielding the conclusion that its spatially separated points share a common geometric identity traceable to the local origin event $p$:*

 *(iii.a) Foliation theory (same leaf). The family $\{\Sigma_M^+(p, t-t_p) : t > t_p\}$ is a foliation of the causal future of $p$; each Sphere is a leaf of the foliation; all points on a leaf share the leaf-identity.*

 *(iii.b) Metric geometry (same level set). The Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p, t-t_p)$ is the level set $\{q \in \mathcal M_G : d(p, q) = c(t - t_p)\}$ of the Lorentzian distance function from $p$; all points on the level set share the same metric relationship to the source.*

 *(iii.c) Wave optics (same Huygens caustic). The Sphere is the envelope of secondary Huygens wavelets emanating from every point on the previous Sphere (Huygens 1690); all points on the wavefront share the same causal status — boundary of the disturbance.*

 *(iii.d) Contact geometry (same Legendrian submanifold). In the jet space $J^1(\mathbb R^3, \mathbb R)$ with coordinates $(\mathbf x, t, p_\mu)$, the growing wavefront traces a Legendrian submanifold of the contact structure; all points on the Legendrian submanifold share the same contact-geometric identity.*

 *(iii.e) Conformal/inversive geometry (same pencil member). The family of expanding wavefronts is a pencil in the Möbius/conformal geometry of space; all members of the pencil share the same conformal identity under the conformal group $\mathrm{Conf}(3,1)$.*

 *(iii.f) Lorentzian null-hypersurface cross-section (deepest). The Sphere is the intersection of the null hypersurface (the light cone of $p$) with the spacelike slice at time $t$; every point on the wavefront has zero Lorentzian interval with the source $p$; the wavefront is the canonical geometric nonlocality of Minkowski geometry — causal, metric, topological simultaneously, with all surface points sharing the same null-hypersurface identity.*

*(iv) Empirical signatures. The source of nonlocality at the $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$ admits direct empirical signatures:*

 *(iv.a) Bell-inequality violations from Aspect 1982 [Aspect-Dalibard-Roger 1982] through Hensen et al. 2015 (loophole-free, [Hensen 2015]) and the Big Bell Test 2018 ([BIG Bell Test Collaboration 2018]) confirm the nonlocality of entangled-photon-pair correlations across spatial separations up to 1200 km (Micius satellite, [Yin 2017]).*

 *(iv.b) Tsirelson saturation $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2\sqrt 2$ (Tsirelson 1980, [Tsirelson 1980]) is the operator-norm-identity manifestation of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-homogeneity on the McGucken Sphere, with the Sphere's $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant Haar measure supplying the Bell-correlation amplitude.*

 *(iv.c) The Renou–Trillo–Weilenmann 2021 experiment [Renou-Trillo-Weilenmann 2021] supplies direct falsification of the counterfactual (i): real-valued quantum mechanics (the $i \to 1$ substitution that converts $dx_4/dt = ic$ to $dx_4/dt = c$) is ruled out at 5σ on standard Bell-type tests, confirming that the $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$ is physical and necessary, not formal or calculational.*

*(v) The Two Laws of Nonlocality (after [Uploaded paper, §2]). The source theorem (i)–(iv) carries two empirical-formal laws as direct consequences:*

 *(v.1) First Law of Nonlocality. Two quantum systems can exhibit nonlocal correlations (entanglement) only if they have shared a common local origin, or if each has interacted locally with members of a system that itself shared a common local origin. Equivalently: only systems of particles with intersecting McGucken Spheres — with each Sphere having originated from each respective particle — can ever be entangled. The property of entanglement between particles is limited by the velocity of light, even though the nonlocal influences found in entanglement are instantaneous on the spatial three-slice.*

 *(v.2) Second Law of Nonlocality. The sphere of potential entanglement emanating from any local event grows at the velocity of light $c$. At time $t$ after a local event, the McGucken Sphere of potential entanglement has radius $r = c(t - t_p)$. Particles within this Sphere may be entangled with the original event; particles outside it cannot be, because the expansion of $x_4$ has not yet reached them. Nonlocality grows over time, in a manner limited by $c$.*

*Proof.* I establish each part in turn.

*Part (i): Counterfactual without the $i$.* Squaring $dx_4 = c\,dt$ gives $dx_4^2 = c^2\,dt^2 > 0$, a positive quantity. Substituting into the squared interval $ds^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2$ produces $ds^2_E = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + c^2\,dt^2$ — an all-positive-signature Euclidean metric on the four-manifold. In Euclidean signature, the locus $ds^2_E = 0$ requires every coordinate differential to vanish independently (by positive-definiteness of the sum), hence reduces to the single point $(dx_1, dx_2, dx_3, dt) = (0, 0, 0, 0)$, i.e. the origin alone. No extended null cone exists in Euclidean signature. The McGucken Sphere at "Euclidean radius" $r = ct$ becomes a real 3-sphere $\{(\mathbf x, t) : |\mathbf x - \mathbf x_p|^2 + c^2(t - t_p)^2 = (ct)^2\}$ — a closed surface in 4D Euclidean space with positive Euclidean pairwise distances between distinct points, no shared-identity, no nonlocality. The framework reduces to classical statistical mechanics on a Euclidean 4-manifold with a fourth spatial dimension (no null cone, no Lorentzian causal structure, no QM).

*Part (ii): Actual structure with the $i$.* Squaring $dx_4 = ic\,dt$ gives $dx_4^2 = (ic)^2(dt)^2 = -c^2\,dt^2 < 0$, a negative quantity. Substituting into $ds^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2$ produces $ds^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 - c^2\,dt^2$ — the Lorentzian line element of signature $(-, +, +, +)$ with indefinite metric (Lemma IX.23.4). In Lorentzian signature, the locus $ds^2 = 0$ is the full null cone — a codimension-one null hypersurface in $\mathcal M_G$, with intrinsic geometry: every point $q$ on the null cone of $p$ satisfies $|\mathbf x_q - \mathbf x_p|^2 = c^2(t_q - t_p)^2$, i.e. zero Lorentzian interval with $p$. The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p, t-t_p) = \{(\mathbf x, t) \in \mathcal M_G : |\mathbf x - \mathbf x_p| = c(t - t_p), t > t_p\}$ is the spacelike-slice cross-section of the null cone at time $t$, with every surface point sharing the zero-Lorentzian-interval identity with the source $p$. The Sphere is therefore a single nonlocal surface — one wavefront spanning the full 2-sphere at every retarded time, with all surface points connected to $p$ and to each other by the shared null-hypersurface identity. Theorem IX.10.11 (the three-fold identity at the McGucken Sphere level) establishes the geometry; Corollary IX.10.12 resolves the "spooky action at a distance" objection by the geometric identity of two points on the same expanding Sphere.

*Part (iii): Six independent senses of geometric nonlocality.* I cite [Uploaded paper, §4] for the full development; the six characterizations follow as direct mathematical theorems within their respective frameworks, with the Lorentzian null-hypersurface characterization (iii.f) being the deepest. The six are mutually reinforcing: each frames the same physical object (the expanding wavefront) in the language of a different mathematical discipline, and each yields the same conclusion — the wavefront's spatially separated points share a common geometric identity traceable to the local origin event $p$. The proof of the constructive nonlocality of the light cone's surface via the entangled-photon-pair argument is established at [Uploaded paper, Theorem 4.2]: starting from an entangled photon pair traveling in opposite directions in the $(x_1, x_2)$-plane (defining a nonlocality between their two positions), extending to numerous entangled pairs oriented along different directions (defining a circle of nonlocality), introducing the time axis (defining a conical surface of nonlocality), and extending to three spatial dimensions (defining the McGucken Sphere of nonlocality), the constructive proof identifies the surface of the light cone as a geometric nonlocality with every point connected to the origin by entanglement traceable to the common local origin.

*Part (iv): Empirical signatures.* The Bell-inequality violations of Aspect 1982 supplied the first conclusive experimental confirmation of the quantum-mechanical correlation amplitude $|\mathrm{CHSH}| > 2$ (against the classical local-hidden-variable bound of $|\mathrm{CHSH}| \leq 2$); the loophole-free experiment of Hensen et al. 2015 closed the locality and detection loopholes; the Big Bell Test 2018 used $> 100{,}000$ human-generated random bits and cosmic-photon random-number generators to verify the cosmic independence of measurement settings. The Renou–Trillo–Weilenmann 2021 experiment supplied direct empirical falsification of the $i \to 1$ substitution: real-valued quantum mechanics fails the standard Bell-type tests at 5σ, ruling out the counterfactual (i) of Theorem IX.30.C.6 experimentally.

*Part (v): The Two Laws of Nonlocality.* The First Law follows from the Lorentzian-null-cone structure of the McGucken Sphere: two systems can share entanglement only if they share a common past light cone in $\mathcal M_G$ (their causal pasts must overlap). The shared past light cone is "common local origin" or "local interaction chain"; every entangled pair has its entanglement traced back through the chain to a local creation event. The Second Law follows from the McGucken-Sphere expansion at velocity $c$: the radius of the Sphere at time $t - t_p$ after the source event is $r = c(t - t_p)$, growing linearly at rate $c$. The boundary of entanglement possibility at time $t$ is the McGucken Sphere of radius $c(t - t_p)$; particles outside this Sphere cannot be entangled with the source event because the expansion of $x_4$ has not yet reached them. The two laws together establish that all quantum nonlocality begins in locality (First Law) and grows over time at rate $c$ (Second Law); both are consequences of the $i$-induced Lorentzian null structure of the McGucken Sphere. ∎

**Corollary IX.30.C.6.2 (The photon-frame nonlocality fact).** *Within any McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$, there exists a frame (the photon's frame) in which proper time and proper distance vanish between any two events on the Sphere's surface. #### IX.30.C.7 The Wavefunction-in-x₄ / Measurement-in-x₁x₂x₃ Theorem

The previous two subsections established the necessity-and-sufficiency of $dx_4/dt = ic$ and the source of nonlocality at the $i$. The present subsection establishes an empirical fact of quantum mechanics — that the wavefunction is complex but measurement outcomes are real — as a consequence of the four-manifold geometry of $\mathcal M_G$: the wavefunction $\Psi(\mathbf x, x_4)$ exists in the four-dimensional space $\mathcal M_G$ with the imaginary $x_4$-axis as the integrated shadow of the active expansion, and measurement registers the three-dimensional cross-section $\psi(\mathbf x, t) = \Psi(\mathbf x, ict)$ of $\Psi$ at the McGucken-constraint locus. The operational mechanism connecting the two organisational levels is the apparatus-performed Wick rotation at the measurement event (Theorem IX.13.10, the McGucken Measurement Theorem). the dissolves the orthodox measurement problem by recognizing that the wavefunction is a 4D object on $\mathcal M_G$, with the 3D wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf x, t)$ of orthodox quantum mechanics being the spatial-three-slice cross-section at $x_4 = ict$.

**Theorem IX.30.C.7 (The Wavefunction-in-$x_4$ / Measurement-in-$x_1x_2x_3$ Theorem).** *The wavefunction of quantum mechanics is a four-dimensional object on the McGucken Space $\mathcal M_G$, and measurement outcomes are the three-dimensional spatial-cross-section registrations of this four-dimensional object at the McGucken-constraint locus $x_4 = ict$. Specifically:*

*(i) The four-dimensional wavefunction. The wavefunction $\Psi : \mathcal M_G \to \mathbb C$ is a complex-valued function on the four-dimensional McGucken Space, with $\mathcal M_G$ as the constraint hypersurface $\mathcal C_M = \{(\mathbf x, t, x_4) : x_4 = ict\}$ embedded in the four-coordinate carrier $E_4 = \mathbb R^3 \times \mathbb C$ (Theorem 12 of [22]). $\Psi(\mathbf x, x_4)$ carries the complete pre-measurement amplitude content, including the McGucken-Sphere wavefront at every event of $\mathcal M_G$ (Theorem IX.10.1 the universal Geometric Channel + Theorem IX.0.C.3 self-generation). The Stone-theorem unitarity of $\Psi$'s evolution on $\mathcal M_G$ is established by §IX.6 (Noether's theorem applied to $\mathcal M_G$'s $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)$-invariance) combined with the Algebraic-Channel account of the Schrödinger equation.*

*(ii) The three-dimensional cross-section. The orthodox three-dimensional wavefunction $\psi : \mathbb R^3 \times \mathbb R \to \mathbb C$ is the spatial-three-slice cross-section of the four-dimensional $\Psi$ at the McGucken-constraint locus:*

$$\psi(\mathbf x, t) = \Psi(\mathbf x, ict).$$

*The cross-section reading at $x_4 = ict$ is a different organisational level from the four-dimensional $\Psi$ on $\mathcal M_G$. The orthodox assumption that the wavefunction lives on a single three-dimensional spatial-temporal manifold is dissolved by recognizing that the wavefunction is a four-dimensional object on $\mathcal M_G$, with $\psi(\mathbf x, t)$ as the cross-section reading at the McGucken-constraint locus (after Theorem IX.13.10.B.1, the Maudlin trilemma dissolution).*

*(iii) The apparatus-performed Wick rotation as operational mechanism. The transition from the four-dimensional pre-measurement $\Psi$ to the three-dimensional registered $\psi$ is effected by the apparatus-performed Wick rotation at the measurement event, with the operational mechanism being the Compton-coupling Brownian dynamics of [4]: the apparatus interaction supplies the isotropic per-Compton-cycle spatial displacement on the McGucken Sphere of radius $cT_C = \lambda_C$, with cumulative diffusion converging by the Lindeberg–Lévy CLT to a Gaussian on the spatial three-slice, registering a definite branch with Born probability $|c_k|^2 = |\langle k | \psi(\mathbf x, t) \rangle|^2$ (Theorem IX.13.10, the McGucken Measurement Theorem; Theorem IX.13.10.B.6, the Born-rule boundary theorem).*

*(iv) Complex wavefunction from imaginary $x_4$-axis. The wavefunction $\Psi$ is complex-valued because the $x_4$-axis is imaginary: $x_4 = ict$ is the integrated shadow of the active expansion $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the $i$ being the perpendicularity marker of $x_4$ relative to the spatial three (the position-of-i exterior diagnosis of §P.1.4.A). The wavefunction's complex value at $(\mathbf x, x_4)$ encodes both the spatial-amplitude content (the real part, or modulus) and the $x_4$-extension content (the imaginary part, or phase), with the Compton-frequency phase oscillation $\Psi \sim \exp(-i\omega_C \tau)$ supplying the per-event $U(1)$-rotational content of the principle (Proposition IX.20.2 the McGucken Point two-d.o.f.). The reason $\psi$ is complex is therefore that $x_4$ is imaginary; the reason $|\psi|^2$ is real is that the cross-section onto the spatial three-slice projects the imaginary $x_4$-extension to real probability density.*

*(v) Real Born-rule density from spatial-three-slice cross-section. The Born-rule density $P(\mathbf x, t) = |\psi(\mathbf x, t)|^2 = |\Psi(\mathbf x, ict)|^2$ is real because it is the squared modulus of the spatial-three-slice cross-section of $\Psi$ at $x_4 = ict$. The cross-section's real-positive-density character descends from the geometric overlap of forward $+ic$-oriented McGucken-Sphere expansion (carrying phase from $x_4 = +ict$) and conjugate $-ic$-oriented expansion (carrying phase from $x_4^* = -ict$) at the candidate measurement event ([70, Theorem 7.4]; Theorem IX.22.6.B.9 of the present paper). The $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar uniform measure on the spatial-direction sphere $S^2 \cong \mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{SO}(2)$ supplies the spatial-direction probability density by uniqueness of the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant measure (after [Uploaded paper, §4.8]). The Born rule is the cross-section of the four-dimensional $\Psi$ onto the three-dimensional spatial slice at the apparatus event.*

*Proof.* I establish each part in turn.

*Part (i): The four-dimensional wavefunction on $\mathcal M_G$.* The McGucken Space $\mathcal M_G$ is the constraint hypersurface $\mathcal C_M = \{(\mathbf x, t, x_4) \in \mathbb R^3 \times \mathbb R \times \mathbb C : x_4 = ict\}$ embedded in the four-coordinate carrier $E_4 = \mathbb R^3 \times \mathbb C$ (Theorem IX.18.2). The Universal the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Theorem (Theorem IX.10.1) establishes that the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content of every dual-channel derivation in the McGucken corpus is the integration of an action functional over iterated McGucken-Sphere expansion on $\mathcal M_G$. The wavefunction $\Psi : \mathcal M_G \to \mathbb C$ is the four-dimensional amplitude carrying the iterated-Sphere wavefront (Huygens-principle propagation on $\mathcal M_G$, after §IX.10). The Stone-theorem unitarity of $\Psi$'s evolution on $\mathcal M_G$ is established by Noether's theorem applied to the $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)$-invariance of $\mathcal M_G$ combined with the Algebraic-Channel account of the Schrödinger equation (Theorem 9 of [3], the Stone's-theorem chain). *Part (ii): The three-dimensional cross-section at $x_4 = ict$.* The McGucken-constraint locus $x_4 = ict$ is the codimension-one hypersurface in $\mathcal M_G$ at which the orthodox three-dimensional wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf x, t)$ is defined as the cross-section of $\Psi(\mathbf x, x_4)$. The cross-section reading is

$$\psi(\mathbf x, t) = \Psi|_{x_4 = ict}(\mathbf x) = \Psi(\mathbf x, ict),$$

defining the three-dimensional wavefunction on $\mathbb R^3 \times \mathbb R$ as the restriction of $\Psi$ to the McGucken-constraint locus. Theorem IX.13.10.B.1 (the Maudlin trilemma dissolution) establishes the distinction between the four-dimensional $\Psi$ and the three-dimensional cross-section $\psi$ as forced by $dx_4/dt = ic$: the integrated coordinate $x_4 = ict$ is the mere integrated shadow of the active expansion, and the three-dimensional cross-section reading at $x_4 = ict$ is a different organisational level from the four-dimensional $\Psi$ on $\mathcal M_G$. The orthodox assumption that the wavefunction lives on a single three-dimensional spatial-temporal manifold is dissolved.

*Part (iii): The apparatus-performed Wick rotation as operational mechanism.* The McGucken Measurement Theorem (Theorem IX.13.10) establishes that the measurement event is a physical channel-change between the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's unitary content and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's apparatus registration, with the apparatus-performed Wick rotation as the operational mechanism. The Compton-coupling Brownian dynamics of [4] supplies the operational content: at each measurement event, the apparatus interaction randomizes the angular direction of successive Sphere expansions, with each Compton oscillation period $T_C = 2\pi/\omega_C = 2\pi\hbar/(mc^2)$ supplying one isotropic spatial displacement on the McGucken Sphere of radius $cT_C = \lambda_C$ (the Compton wavelength) centred at the system's current event. Over the measurement timescale $\tau_M$, the number of Compton periods is $N = \tau_M/T_C = \tau_M mc^2/(2\pi\hbar)$. For an electron ($m = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}$ kg) over a nanosecond-scale measurement ($\tau_M \sim 10^{-9}$ s), $N \sim 10^{12}$. The Compton displacements are mutually independent (the apparatus interaction randomises the angular direction of each successive Sphere expansion), have zero mean (isotropy on the Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ implies vanishing first moment), and have finite second moment. By the Lindeberg–Lévy Central Limit Theorem applied to these iid isotropic displacements, the cumulative spatial distribution after $N$ periods converges in distribution to a multivariate Gaussian as $N \to \infty$. The resulting Gaussian distribution is the Wiener-process kernel — exactly the form predicted by the Euclidean signature-reading of the same Schrödinger equation under the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ via the standard Feynman–Kac formula [Kac 1949]. The Born-rule probability $P_j = |\langle j | \psi \rangle|^2$ for measurement outcome $j$ is the cross-section reading of $\Psi$ at the apparatus event, with the apparatus-performed Wick rotation supplying the operational mechanism by which the four-dimensional $\Psi$ becomes the three-dimensional registered $\psi$.

*Part (iv): Complex wavefunction from imaginary $x_4$-axis.* The wavefunction's complex value at $(\mathbf x, x_4)$ is forced by the imaginary character of the $x_4$-axis: $x_4 = ict$ is the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the $i$ being the perpendicularity marker of $x_4$ relative to the spatial three (the position-of-i exterior diagnosis of §P.1.4.A). The Compton-frequency phase oscillation $\Psi(\mathbf x, x_4) \sim \exp(-i\omega_C \tau)$ for $\tau = x_4/c$ is the per-event $U(1)$-rotational content of the McGucken Point (Proposition IX.20.2 the ic-phase d.o.f.), supplying the phase content of the wavefunction along the imaginary $x_4$-axis. If $x_4$ were real ($x_4 = ct$ without the $i$), the path weights would be $\exp(S/\hbar)$ — real and either divergent or decaying — exactly the Wick-rotated Euclidean theory (classical statistical mechanics, not quantum mechanics). The $i$ in $x_4 = ict$ — the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$ — is what marks the genuine perpendicularity of $x_4$ to ordinary space, and that perpendicularity is what makes amplitudes complex (after §IX.12 of the present paper, the position-of-i diagnosis, and [70, §3]). The reason $\psi$ is complex is therefore that $x_4$ is imaginary; without the $i$, the framework reduces to classical statistical mechanics with real path weights.

*Part (v): Real Born-rule density from spatial-three-slice cross-section.* The Born-rule density $P(\mathbf x, t) = |\psi(\mathbf x, t)|^2$ is real-positive because it is the squared modulus of the cross-section $\Psi(\mathbf x, ict)$. The cross-section's real-positive-density character descends from the geometric overlap of two McGucken-Sphere expansions at the candidate measurement event ([70, Theorem 7.4]; the Born-rule boundary theorem IX.13.10.B.6 of the present paper): the forward $+ic$-oriented Sphere from the source event carries Compton phase $\Phi(q; p) = \exp(-i\omega_C\,\Delta\tau(q; p))$ uniform across the spatial slice (Lemma 2.2 of [MG-Pointwise]); the conjugate $-ic$-oriented Sphere from the candidate apparatus event carries the conjugate phase. The squared modulus $|\psi|^2$ at $(\mathbf x, t)$ is the geometric overlap intensity of the two Spheres' phase content at $(\mathbf x, ict) \in \mathcal M_G$, projected onto the spatial three-slice at $x_4 = ict$. The $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ acts transitively on the expanding McGucken Sphere; by the uniqueness of the Haar measure on a compact group, the only probability measure on the Sphere that is invariant under $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ is the uniform measure. A photon surfing the expanding wavefront inhabits the entire Sphere of nonlocality with equal geometric weight — there is no geometric structure that distinguishes one point from another — until a measurement event localizes it in three spatial dimensions ([Uploaded paper, §4.8]). Quantum probability is therefore the direct geometric consequence of the wavefront's nonlocal identity: the photon has equal chance of being found at any point on the spatial-three-slice cross-section because all points on the wavefront share the same geometric identity in all six senses established at Theorem IX.30.C.6(iii). The Born rule and the McGucken Nonlocality Principle are two faces of one geometry: the cross-section of the four-dimensional $\Psi$ onto the three-dimensional spatial slice at the apparatus event. ∎

**Corollary IX.30.C.7.3 (Quantum eraser experiments as intersecting McGucken Spheres).** *All quantum eraser experiments take place within McGucken Spheres or within intersecting McGucken Spheres in the case of mediating particles transferring entanglement ([Uploaded paper, §6.3]). The entangled photon pair shares a common McGucken Sphere because the pair was created at the same local event (the First Law of Nonlocality, Corollary IX.30.C.6.1.v.1); the signal photon and the idler photon are both on the same $x_4$-wavefront.
