*Proof.* The identity $V^{+}(p) \cap \Sigma_{t} = \Sigma_{M}^{+}(p, t - t_{p})$ at every event $p$ and every time $t > t_{p}$ follows from item (i) (the spatial slice of the future null cone at time $t$ is the two-sphere of radius $c(t - t_{p})$ centred at $\mathbf x_{p}$, standard Minkowski 1908 construction) combined with item (ii) (the McGucken Sphere at expansion time $t - t_{p}$ is the two-sphere of radius $c(t - t_{p})$ centred at $\mathbf x_{p}$, definition of the Sphere in the McGucken framework §III of the present paper). Therefore $V^{+}(p) \cap \Sigma_{t} = \Sigma_{M}^{+}(p, t - t_{p})$ at every $(p, t)$. The zero-spacetime-distance content follows from the null-vector property $\mathbf r \cdot \mathbf r = -c^{2}(t - t_{p})^{2} + |\mathbf x_{q} - \mathbf x_{p}|^{2} = 0$ for every $q$ on the light cone (Minkowski 1908, standard textbook computation), combined with the identification of the light cone with the McGucken Sphere established above. Consequence 1 (Photon-never-ages) follows from the null-geodesic property of photon worldlines (zero proper time along null worldlines, standard SR/GR result) combined with the identification of the null cone with the McGucken Sphere. Consequence 2 (Entanglement transport along the Sphere-surface) follows from the observation that every pair of points on the Sphere is joined through the source event $p$ by two zero-length null radii, combined with the empirical fact that entangled particles created at $p$ propagate along the future null cone $V^{+}(p) = \Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$. The physical mechanism identification (correlation transport along the shared Sphere-surface rather than superluminal signaling through the Sphere-interior) is the McGucken framework's Cell (1) → Cell (4) inter-cell reading of the same physical primitive: what Cell (1) — the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel on the differential-rate form of the Principle, Quantum Mechanics — reads as nonlocal correlation between spatially separated measurement events, Cell (4) — the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel on the integrated-coordinate form of the Principle, General Relativity — reads as zero spacetime distance along the null cone from the common source, and the Sphere-Surface Identity of the present corollary identifies both as the same physical structure: the McGucken Sphere expanding from the source event $p$ at rate $c$, with the pair of detectors at points on its surface. ∎*

#### IX.30.C.13.D Universal Trace-Back: Every Physical Phenomenon as an Algebraic Channel / the Geometric Channel Assignment or the Specifiable combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel Combination on the McGucken Sphere Expanding at Rate $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ from Every Event of $\mathcal M_{G}$

**Theorem IX.30.C.13.D.1 (Universal trace-back to $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ through the four channel categories).**

*Every physical phenomenon in the McGucken framework falls into one of four categories, each traceable to the McGucken Principle $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ through a specifiable channel assignment:*

**Corollary IX.30.C.13.D.1 (Electromagnetism sector-by-sector: the wave sector as the classical Algebraic Channel limit, the static sector as the Wick-rotated Geometric Channel, and the radiation-reaction sector as specifiable combination of both channels).**

*Classical electromagnetism (Maxwell 1865) reads at first as neither Algebraic Channel nor the Geometric Channel: real-valued fields $\mathbf E$, $\mathbf B$ satisfying Maxwell's equations $\nabla \cdot \mathbf E = \rho/\varepsilon_{0}$, $\nabla \times \mathbf B - \varepsilon_{0}\mu_{0}\partial_{t}\mathbf E = \mu_{0}\mathbf J$, $\nabla \cdot \mathbf B = 0$, $\nabla \times \mathbf E + \partial_{t}\mathbf B = 0$, with no explicit $i$ and no explicit entropy. The sector-by-sector reading of Theorem IX.30.C.13.D.1 assigns each of Maxwell's three sectors to one of the four channel categories:*

*The wave sector — electromagnetic radiation, propagation of light, plane waves $\exp(i(\mathbf k \cdot \mathbf x - \omega t))$ with $\omega = c|\mathbf k|$ — is the classical many-photon coherent-state limit of the Algebraic Channel. The Maxwell wave equation $\square A^{\mu} = \mu_{0}J^{\mu}$ (in Lorenz gauge $\partial_{\mu}A^{\mu} = 0$) is the classical limit of the quantum photon propagator, which is an Algebraic Channel object. Classical electromagnetic waves are the Algebraic Channel stripped of its explicit $i$: the $i$ is present in the plane-wave phase $\exp(i(\mathbf k \cdot \mathbf x - \omega t))$ that generates the real-valued fields via real and imaginary parts, and the coherent-state expectation value of the quantum photon field reproduces the classical Maxwell field. Maxwell's wave sector traces to the Algebraic Channel via the classical-limit reduction of the quantum photon.*

*The static sector — Coulomb's law $F = k_{e}q_{1}q_{2}/r^{2}$, magnetostatics — is the Geometric Channel on the integrated-coordinate form via the Wick-rotated propagator. Static Coulomb interaction descends from the imaginary-time (Euclidean) two-point function of the photon field: $\langle A_{0}(x)A_{0}(x')\rangle_{\rm Euclidean} \sim 1/|\mathbf x - \mathbf x'|$ at coincident Euclidean time gives the Coulomb potential. In statistical-field-theory formulations, static electromagnetic interactions are Euclidean-Green-function readings — the Geometric Channel on the integrated-coordinate form of the Principle, with the $i$ absorbed into the Wick-rotated coordinate $\tau_{W} = x_{4}/c$.*

*The radiation-reaction and thermal-radiation sector — black-body spectrum, Larmor formula $P = q^{2}a^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_{0}c^{3})$, Abraham-Lorentz equation — is a specifiable combination of both channels: coherent radiation modes (The Algebraic Channel) reading against an entropic ensemble of source charges or a heat bath (The Geometric Channel). Planck's 1900 blackbody derivation is the historical case: single-oscillator the Algebraic Channel quantized modes summed over the ensemble Geometric Channel thermal distribution give the Planck spectrum $u(\nu, T) = (8\pi h\nu^{3}/c^{3})/(e^{h\nu/k_{B}T} - 1)$, with the numerator carrying the Algebraic Channel ($h\nu$ per quantum) and the denominator carrying the Geometric Channel (the thermal Boltzmann weight). Every electromagnetic phenomenon involving both coherent quantum modes and thermal or dissipative interactions with charges lives in this sector.*

**Corollary IX.30.C.13.D.2 (The optical theorem as canonical the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel instance: $\mathrm{Im}\,f(0) = (k/4\pi)\sigma_{\rm tot}$ relating an Algebraic Channel quantity to a Geometric Channel quantity by unitarity).**

*The optical theorem of scattering theory [Peskin-Schroeder 1995, §7.3] relates the imaginary part of the forward-scattering amplitude to the total cross section:*

$$\mathrm{Im}\,f(0) = \frac{k}{4\pi}\sigma_{\rm tot}$$

*where $f(\theta)$ is the scattering amplitude, $f(0)$ is its forward value, $k = |\mathbf k|$ is the incident wavenumber, and $\sigma_{\rm tot}$ is the total scattering cross section (elastic plus inelastic). The left-hand side $\mathrm{Im}\,f(0)$ is an Algebraic Channel quantity: the imaginary part of an S-matrix amplitude, computed from Feynman diagrams with $i$ interior in every propagator ($1/(p^{2} - m^{2} + i\varepsilon)$) and every vertex factor. The right-hand side $(k/4\pi)\sigma_{\rm tot}$ is a Geometric Channel quantity: the total cross section, a statistical rate over an ensemble of scattering events, real-valued and non-negative. Unitarity of the S-matrix ($S^{\dagger}S = 1$) forces the two sides to be equal via the identity $\mathrm{Im}\,T = \tfrac{1}{2}T^{\dagger}T$ for $S = 1 + iT$. The optical theorem is therefore the canonical statement that Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel are two readings of the same underlying physics related by unitarity, with each specific scattering process instantiating a specifiable combination of both channels.*

*The identification of every well-defined the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel in physics — measurement, decoherence, open systems, Bell violations, scattering amplitudes, radiation-reaction electromagnetism, Standard-Model cross sections, particle-physics decay rates — as an instance of the category (D) trace-back is the McGucken framework's reading; each combination is a phenomenon where the two channels interact in a specifiable way rather than either channel being read alone.*

#### IX.30.C.13.E The Planck 1900 Blackbody Derivation as the Historical Proof-of-Concept for the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel Combination Category of the McGucken Framework: Thermodynamics Alone Could Not Solve the Problem, and Planck's "Act of Desperation" Was the Empirically-Forced Import of the Algebraic Channel Content ($h$ as Per-Cycle Action Quantum of the Wavefront Advance of $x_{4}$ at Rate $c$) into a Geometric Channel Calculation

*McGucken Principle anchor.* The McGucken Principle $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ states the physical reality that the fourth dimension is expanding at velocity $c$ at every event of spacetime. From this single physical rate two derivational routes descend: (The Algebraic Channel) the differential-rate reading with $i$ interior, tracking the oscillatory phase-carrying face of the McGucken Sphere wavefront, with the per-cycle action quantum $h$ set by the wavefront's phase advance at rate $c$ (§I.1.S.1: $h$ as the action quantum accumulated per cycle of the wavefront's phase advance, identified as the twin property of $c$ under the constitutive identity $c = \ell_{P}/t_{P}$ with $\ell_{P} = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^{3}}$, $t_{P} = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^{5}}$); (The Geometric Channel) the Wick-rotated reading with $i$ absorbed into the real coordinate $\tau_{W} = x_{4}/c$, tracking the expansive dissipative face of the McGucken Sphere at rate $c$, with Boltzmann weights $e^{-\beta\hat H}$ as ensemble-face manifestations (Corollary IX.30.C.13.B.2: KMS-Matsubara $\tau_{W} = \beta\hbar$ at Compton scale). Both channels are foundationally traced back to $dx_{4}/dt = ic$: the Algebraic Channel reads the differential rate directly through the interior-$i$ algebra of Stone's theorem and the canonical commutator; the Geometric Channel reads the differential rate through its Wick-rotated section on the same manifold $\mathcal M_{G}$. The blackbody radiation problem — spectral distribution of electromagnetic radiation in a cavity at temperature $T$ — requires both faces of the McGucken Sphere simultaneously (oscillatory mode structure at frequency $\nu$ from the Algebraic Channel, ensemble thermal distribution over modes from the Geometric Channel), and is therefore a Category (D) specifiable combination of both channels on the McGucken Sphere per Theorem IX.30.C.13.D.1. The historical episode of Planck 1897–1900 — three years of failed pure-thermodynamic derivation, followed by the December 14, 1900 "act of desperation" in which Planck was empirically forced to import the Algebraic Channel content ($\varepsilon = h\nu$ per oscillator mode) into a Geometric Channel calculation (Boltzmann's $S = k \log W$) — is the historical proof-of-concept for the Category (D) combination.

**Theorem IX.30.C.13.E.1 (The Planck 1900 blackbody derivation as historical instantiation of the combined-channel category: the pure Geometric Channel could not solve blackbody radiation, and Planck's derivation of the correct spectrum required the empirically-forced import of the Algebraic Channel content into a Geometric Channel calculation).**

*The historical sequence of Planck's blackbody work between 1897 and December 14, 1900 exhibits, in five documentable stages, the empirical inadequacy of the pure Geometric Channel for blackbody radiation and the necessity of the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel for the correct spectral distribution. Each stage is documented at primary sources; the McGucken framework's identification of each stage with a specific channel content is the framework's reading of the documented history.*

*Stage 1 (1893–1899): The maximum pure-Channel-B derivable form (Wien 1893) and Planck's pure-Channel-B position.* *Wien 1893 [Wien 1893] established, by a thermodynamic argument using adiabatic compression of blackbody radiation combined with the Stefan-Boltzmann law $u_{\rm tot}(T) \propto T^{4}$ and the Doppler effect, that pure thermodynamics plus classical electromagnetism constrains the blackbody spectral distribution to the form*

$$u(\nu, T) = \nu^{3} f(\nu/T)$$

*where $f$ is an undetermined function of the single dimensionless combination $\nu/T$ — the Wien displacement law. Wien 1893's result demarcates the maximum extent of what the pure Geometric Channel (thermodynamics + classical electromagnetism, with the McGucken Sphere read on the Wick-rotated face alone with $i$ absorbed into the real coordinate $\tau_{W} = x_{4}/c$) can determine about the blackbody spectrum: the functional dependence on $\nu/T$ is fixed by the pure Geometric Channel, but the specific functional form of $f$ is not determined by the pure Geometric Channel. Wien 1896 [Wien 1896] supplied a specific form $f(\nu/T) = \alpha \exp(-\beta\nu/T)$ — Wien's radiation law $\rho_{W}(\nu, T) = \alpha\nu^{3}\exp(-\beta\nu/T)$ — by adding a Maxwell-Boltzmann-like assumption about the frequency distribution of emitting molecules, an assumption that went beyond pure thermodynamics and classical electromagnetism. Planck's stated goal from 1897 onward was to derive Wien 1896's specific functional form from the two laws of thermodynamics alone, without the Maxwell-Boltzmann distributional assumption. Planck succeeded Kirchhoff at the University of Berlin in 1889 as chair of theoretical physics, was author of a canonical textbook on thermodynamics, and was the world's premier expert on classical thermodynamics [Kragh 2000]. Kirchhoff had posed in 1860 the challenge of deriving a universal law for the spectral distribution of blackbody radiation as a function of frequency and temperature (Kirchhoff's challenge, [Kirchhoff 1860]). Planck did not believe in atoms; he did not believe entropy should be given a statistical interpretation; he explicitly opposed Boltzmann's kinetic-theory $S = k \log W$ formulation on philosophical grounds because probability could not, in Planck's view, yield an absolute physical law [Kragh 2000]. Planck's five 1897–1899 papers on blackbody radiation attempted to derive the entropy of ideal dipole oscillators from what he called a "principle of elementary disorder" (Prinzip der elementaren Unordnung), a purely thermodynamic construction with no atomistic or statistical content [Kragh 2000; Duncan-Janssen 2020]. The derivation produced Wien's law and was widely regarded as complete: the resulting spectral distribution was called the Wien-Planck law. This entire construction is the pure Geometric Channel: entropy, dipole oscillator ensembles, thermodynamic reversibility, no per-cycle action quantum, no oscillator quantization, no $h$. In McGucken framework terms, Wien 1893's displacement law is the maximum spectral information the pure Geometric Channel can supply (the functional form $u = \nu^{3} f(\nu/T)$ with $f$ undetermined), and Planck's 1897–1899 attempt to determine $f$ from the pure Geometric Channel was — as the subsequent stages of this theorem establish — provably beyond what the pure Geometric Channel can accomplish. Stage 1 is Planck attempting to solve the blackbody problem by reading the Wick-rotated face of the McGucken Sphere alone, with $i$ absorbed into the real coordinate and the oscillatory phase-carrying face of the Algebraic Channel treated as continuous classical-oscillator content without quantization.*

*Stage 2 (September–October 1900): Experimental refutation of the pure Geometric Channel.* *Between 1899 and 1900 the experimentalists at the Physikalisch-Technische Reichsanstalt in Berlin — Otto Lummer and Ernst Pringsheim, and independently Heinrich Rubens and Ferdinand Kurlbaum — extended blackbody radiation measurements into the far infrared beyond 20 $\mu$m and later beyond 50 $\mu$m [Rubens-Kurlbaum 1900; Lummer-Pringsheim 1900]. At the longer wavelengths (lower frequencies) the measured spectral radiance was proportional to $T$ and to $\nu^{2}$, contradicting Wien's exponential suppression $\exp(-\beta\nu/T)$ which predicted a $T$-independent limit at low frequency. On October 7, 1900, Rubens visited Planck at Planck's home and reported the new infrared measurements directly; the Wien-Planck law failed at long wavelengths beyond the experimental error bars. The Pure Geometric Channel, as instrumented in Planck's 1897–1899 five-paper derivation, was empirically refuted at the specific frequency range where the ensemble-face Boltzmann content transitions from exponential Wien behavior to the linear-in-$T$ Rayleigh regime.*

*Stage 3 (October 19, 1900): Empirical interpolation without physical derivation.* *On October 19, 1900, Planck presented to the Deutsche Physikalische Gesellschaft an empirical interpolation formula that fitted Wien's law at high frequency and the new experimental data at low frequency: $u(\nu, T) = c_{1}\nu^{3}/(\exp(c_{2}\nu/T) - 1)$ [Planck 1900a]. The formula was an interpolation between two limits with no physical derivation. Rubens compared the formula against his and Kurlbaum's data the same night and found it fitted at every wavelength within experimental error [Kragh 2000]. Planck was distressed by the empirical-only status of the formula: a theoretician was, on the standard of the period, obligated to derive a spectral law from fundamental principles rather than fit it to data. In McGucken framework terms, Stage 3 is the empirical constraint that both the Algebraic Channel high-frequency limit (Wien: single-mode dominance, $h\nu \gg k_{B}T$) and the Geometric Channel low-frequency limit (Rayleigh: equipartition, $h\nu \ll k_{B}T$) must be reproduced by any correct derivation of the spectrum.*

*Stage 4 (November 1900): Renewed attempts at the pure Geometric Channel, all failing.* *Between October 19 and December 14, 1900, Planck attempted to derive the empirical interpolation formula from pure thermodynamics — the same Geometric Channel methodology of the 1897–1899 papers, now applied to the new spectrum rather than to Wien's. Planck's own account [Kragh 2000, quoting Planck's 1931 letter to R.W. Wood]: "For six years I had struggled with the blackbody theory. I knew the problem was fundamental and I knew the answer. I had to find a theoretical explanation at any cost, except the inviolability of the two laws of thermodynamics." The traditional continuum-thermodynamic approach — the pure Geometric Channel — provably failed to yield the empirical interpolation formula. The failure was not a computational difficulty but a formal impossibility: no continuum-thermodynamic construction on continuous oscillator modes could produce the $\exp(h\nu/k_{B}T) - 1$ denominator, because the "$-1$" arises from the discrete counting of energy elements $\varepsilon = h\nu$ in Boltzmann's combinatorial formula $W = (N - 1 + P)!/[(N - 1)!P!]$, and continuous thermodynamics has no such combinatorial content. The Pure Geometric Channel provably cannot yield the correct blackbody spectrum.*

*Stage 5 (December 14, 1900): The "act of desperation" — the empirically-forced import of the Algebraic Channel content into a Geometric Channel calculation.* *On December 14, 1900, Planck presented to the Deutsche Physikalische Gesellschaft his derivation of the empirical interpolation formula using two moves he had philosophically opposed: (a) Boltzmann's statistical entropy formula $S = k \log W$ (The Geometric Channel ensemble-face); (b) the division of the total oscillator energy $E_{N}$ into $P$ indistinguishable energy elements $\varepsilon = h\nu$ per oscillator mode of frequency $\nu$ (The Algebraic Channel per-cycle action quantum) [Planck 1900b; Planck 1901]. Planck's own account of the reluctance [Kragh 2000; Planck to R.W. Wood 1931]: "an act of desperation... I had to obtain a positive result, under any circumstances and at whatever cost." The derivation combines two channels: Boltzmann's $S = k \log W$ is the Geometric Channel (ensemble statistical mechanics, Wick-rotated face of the McGucken Sphere with $i$ absorbed into $\tau_{W} = x_{4}/c$); the energy element $\varepsilon = h\nu$ is the Algebraic Channel (per-cycle action quantum of the wavefront's oscillatory phase-carrying face at frequency $\nu$, with $h$ as the twin property of $c$ per §I.1.S.1). Planck introduced $h$ as a mathematical device for counting Boltzmann complexions; he did not identify $h$ as a physical quantum, and he did not identify oscillator energies as quantized per se [Duncan-Janssen 2020; Kragh 2000]. The formal move was the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel even though Planck did not read it as such. Einstein 1906 was the first to identify $\varepsilon = nh\nu$ as a physical constraint on oscillator energies rather than as a formal counting device [Einstein 1906; Duncan-Janssen 2020]. **Theorem IX.30.C.13.E.2 (The structure of the Planck spectrum as explicit decomposition into the Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel on $dx_{4}/dt = ic$).**

*The Planck spectrum $u(\nu, T) = (8\pi\nu^{2}/c^{3}) \cdot h\nu / (e^{h\nu/k_{B}T} - 1)$ admits a decomposition into the Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel in which each factor is foundationally traceable to the McGucken Principle $dx_{4}/dt = ic$:*

*Factor 1: $8\pi\nu^{2}/c^{3}$ — the electromagnetic mode density in a cavity at frequency $\nu$. In the classical (Rayleigh 1900) counting, the number of standing electromagnetic wave modes per unit volume per unit frequency interval in a cubic cavity is $8\pi\nu^{2}/c^{3}$, where the factor $c^{-3}$ carries the three-dimensional volume of $\mathbf k$-space per mode and $\nu^{2}$ is the spherical-shell measure at frequency $\nu$. This factor is an Algebraic Channel structural quantity: the count of oscillatory-phase-carrying modes of the wavefront advance of $x_{4}$ at velocity $c$, per the McGucken Sphere expanding at rate $c$ from every event of the cavity (Theorem IX.30.C.11 entry 5, path-integral phase weight; §I.1's identification of $c$ as the rate at which $x_{4}$'s wavefront advances). The mode density $8\pi\nu^{2}/c^{3}$ is traceable to $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ via the identification of $c$ as the wavefront advance rate and the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ isotropy of the spatial three-slice on which the mode structure is built.*

*Factor 2: $h\nu$ — the per-cycle action quantum of one oscillatory mode at frequency $\nu$. This is an Algebraic Channel quantity: the per-cycle action of the wavefront's phase advance at rate $c$, with $h$ identified at §I.1.S.1 as the twin property of $c$ (the two constants are two articulations of the one advance; $c$ articulates the velocity dimension, $h$ articulates the per-cycle action dimension of the same wavefront). The identification of $h$ as an Algebraic Channel quantity is direct: $h$ appears interior to the algebraic apparatus of the Algebraic Channel (canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$; Stone's unitary group $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$; Feynman phase weight $\exp(iS/\hbar)$; all with $i$ interior per Theorem IX.30.A.4.7). The relation $\varepsilon = h\nu$ is the assignment of one action quantum $h$ per cycle of the oscillator mode at frequency $\nu$, with $h$ traceable to $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ via the Planck-scale identification $h = 2\pi\hbar = 2\pi\ell_{P}^{2}c^{3}/G$ (§IX.20 of the present paper).*

*Factor 3: $1/(e^{h\nu/k_{B}T} - 1)$ — the Bose-Einstein distribution, the mean occupation number of the oscillator mode at temperature $T$. This is a Geometric Channel quantity: the Boltzmann weight $e^{-\beta\hat H}$ evaluated on a harmonic-oscillator Hamiltonian $\hat H = \hbar\omega(\hat n + 1/2)$ with $\omega = 2\pi\nu$, giving the geometric-series sum $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} n e^{-n\beta h\nu} = 1/(e^{\beta h\nu} - 1)$ per standard statistical-mechanics derivation. The Bose-Einstein distribution is the ensemble-face reading of the McGucken Sphere at temperature $T$ per Corollary IX.30.C.13.B.2's KMS-Matsubara mechanism $\tau_{W} = \beta\hbar$, applied at oscillator scale rather than at particle-rest-mass scale. The distribution is traceable to $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ via the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau_{W} = x_{4}/c$ on the real four-manifold $\mathcal M_{G}$ (Theorem IX.13.13), which converts the interior-$i$ algebraic evolution $\exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$ of the Algebraic Channel into the exterior-$i$ semigroup evolution $\exp(-\tau_{W}\hat H/\hbar) = \exp(-\beta\hat H)$ of the Geometric Channel at $\tau_{W} = \beta\hbar$.*

*Every factor of the Planck spectrum is therefore traceable to $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ through a specifiable channel assignment: Factor 1 through the wavefront advance rate $c$; Factor 2 through the per-cycle action quantum $h$ as twin property of $c$; Factor 3 through the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau_{W} = x_{4}/c$ applied at oscillator scale. The multiplicative combination is the explicit Category (D) the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel of Theorem IX.30.C.13.D.1, with the Algebraic Channel oscillatory-mode content (Factors 1 and 2) multiplied against the Geometric Channel ensemble-thermal content (Factor 3). The historical necessity of both channels for blackbody radiation is the specific empirical constraint that made the 1900 derivation require both.*

**Corollary IX.30.C.13.E.1 (The Rayleigh-Jeans failure as an Algebraic Channel / the Geometric Channel category mismatch: continuous oscillator modes with the Geometric Channel equipartition).**

*Rayleigh 1900 [Rayleigh 1900] applied Maxwell-Boltzmann equipartition ($k_{B}T$ per mode) to electromagnetic modes in a cavity and obtained the spectral distribution $\rho(\nu, T) = (8\pi\nu^{2}/c^{3}) \cdot k_{B}T$, later corrected by Jeans 1905 for the numerical factor. Integrated over all frequencies, this spectrum gives infinite total energy — the "ultraviolet catastrophe" [Ehrenfest 1911, who coined the term]. The failure is an Algebraic Channel / the Geometric Channel category mismatch. Rayleigh used the correct Algebraic Channel mode-counting factor $8\pi\nu^{2}/c^{3}$ (Factor 1 above), but treated the mode energies as continuous classical-oscillator variables and applied the Geometric Channel equipartition $\langle E \rangle = k_{B}T$ per mode without accounting for the per-cycle action quantum $h$ that Algebraic Channel requires. The mismatch is between the Algebraic Channel mode structure (which has a per-cycle action quantum $h$ setting the discrete energy quanta $\varepsilon = h\nu$) and the Geometric Channel equipartition rule (which assumes continuous energy variables with $\langle E \rangle = k_{B}T$). At high frequency $h\nu \gg k_{B}T$, the Algebraic Channel quantization matters: the mode is thermally frozen out because a single quantum $h\nu$ exceeds the thermal energy scale, giving the exponential Boltzmann suppression $\exp(-h\nu/k_{B}T)$ in the Wien limit. Equipartition, being a continuous-oscillator the Geometric Channel rule, misses this Algebraic Channel quantization and predicts $k_{B}T$ per mode at every frequency, giving unbounded total energy. The Planck spectrum's correct form $h\nu/(e^{h\nu/k_{B}T} - 1)$ interpolates: at low frequency $h\nu \ll k_{B}T$ it reduces to $k_{B}T$ (The Geometric Channel equipartition recovered because $h\nu$ is negligible against thermal fluctuations), at high frequency $h\nu \gg k_{B}T$ it reduces to $h\nu \exp(-h\nu/k_{B}T)$ (The Algebraic Channel quantization dominates because $h\nu$ exceeds thermal energy). The ultraviolet catastrophe is not a paradox of classical physics: it is the diagnostic evidence that pure Geometric Channel (with the correct Algebraic Channel mode-counting factor but without the Algebraic Channel per-cycle action quantum in the mode energies) cannot solve blackbody radiation. The Planck spectrum resolves the catastrophe by combining both channels correctly, as Theorem IX.30.C.13.E.2 above states.*

**Corollary IX.30.C.13.E.2 (The specific-heat problem — Einstein 1907, Debye 1912 — as the second historical instantiation of the combined-channel category).**

*The Dulong-Petit law (1819) of specific heats — that the molar heat capacity of a solid is $3R$ independent of substance and temperature — was known to fail at low temperatures, where measured specific heats fall well below $3R$. The Dulong-Petit derivation is the pure Geometric Channel: equipartition applied to $3N$ atomic oscillators gives $3Nk_{B}T$ total thermal energy and $3R$ per mole. Einstein 1907 [Einstein 1907] solved the low-temperature specific-heat problem by importing the Algebraic Channel content into the Geometric Channel calculation, exactly as Planck 1900 had done for blackbody radiation: Einstein treated the atomic oscillators as quantized with energies $E_{n} = nh\nu_{E}$ (The Algebraic Channel, per-cycle action quantum $h$ at Einstein frequency $\nu_{E}$) and applied Boltzmann statistics (The Geometric Channel) to obtain the specific-heat formula $C_{V} = 3R (h\nu_{E}/k_{B}T)^{2} e^{h\nu_{E}/k_{B}T}/(e^{h\nu_{E}/k_{B}T} - 1)^{2}$. This formula reduces to $3R$ at high temperature ($k_{B}T \gg h\nu_{E}$, the Geometric Channel equipartition recovered) and to $3R(h\nu_{E}/k_{B}T)^{2} \exp(-h\nu_{E}/k_{B}T)$ at low temperature ($k_{B}T \ll h\nu_{E}$, the Algebraic Channel quantization dominates). Debye 1912 [Debye 1912] refined Einstein's model by treating the oscillator frequencies as a distribution rather than a single frequency, obtaining the $T^{3}$ law at low temperature. Both Einstein 1907 and Debye 1912 instantiate Category (D) of Theorem IX.30.C.13.D.1: the Algebraic Channel quantized-oscillator content combined multiplicatively with the Geometric Channel Boltzmann statistics. The specific-heat problem is the second historical episode after blackbody radiation in which the pure Geometric Channel was empirically refuted and the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel was empirically forced.*

**Corollary IX.30.C.13.E.3 (The Sackur-Tetrode absolute-entropy equation — Sackur 1911, Sackur 1912, Tetrode 1912 — as the third historical instantiation of the combined-channel category, and the first instance in which Planck's constant entered the statistical mechanics of massive matter, more than a decade before quantum mechanics).**

*Classical thermodynamics can pin down the entropy of an ideal gas only up to an arbitrary additive constant. The Boltzmann-Planck statistical entropy formula $S = k_{B}\log W$ requires counting the number $W$ of microstates compatible with a given macrostate; but microstates in classical phase space form a continuum in position and momentum coordinates $(q, p)$, and counting the continuum requires a discretization into elementary cells of some volume $\delta q\,\delta p$. Classical physics has no natural scale for the phase-space cell — a purely-classical counting produces $W$ modulo an arbitrary volume normalization, and the resulting entropy is determined only up to the corresponding additive constant $s_{0}$. In the pure Geometric Channel classical formulation:*

$$S(E, V, N) = k_{B} N \left[\ln\left(\frac{V}{N}\right) + \frac{3}{2}\ln\left(\frac{E}{N}\right) + s_{0}\right]$$

*with $s_{0}$ undetermined by pure thermodynamics or pure classical statistical mechanics. Absolute entropy — as opposed to entropy differences — is empirically accessible for a monoatomic ideal gas through Nernst's third law programme [Nernst 1906] and the chemistry of gas reactions, and by 1911 the empirical value of $s_{0}$ for monoatomic vapors (mercury, argon, helium) was known from thermodynamic measurements to a precision that permitted numerical comparison. The Pure Geometric Channel could not produce the empirical value of $s_{0}$ because it had no way to set the phase-space cell volume.*

*Otto Sackur (1880–1914) at Breslau and Hugo Tetrode (1895–1931) at Amsterdam independently resolved the empirical problem in 1911–1912 by importing the Algebraic Channel content into the Geometric Channel ensemble counting. Sackur's October 6, 1911 paper "Die Anwendung der kinetischen Theorie der Gase auf chemische Probleme" [Sackur 1911] developed the formula for the entropy $S$ of a monoatomic ideal gas as a function of the size of the elementary phase-space cell; Sackur's spring 1912 paper "Die Bedeutung des elementaren Wirkungsquantums für die Gastheorie und die Berechnung der chemischen Konstante" [Sackur 1912] postulated that the elementary cell volume in phase space is $h^{n}$ where $h$ is Planck's constant and $n$ is the number of degrees of freedom; Tetrode's March 18, 1912 paper "Die chemische Konstante der Gase und das elementare Wirkungsquantum" [Tetrode 1912] independently derived the same result with the elementary cell taken as $(zh)^{n}$ for a dimensionless factor $z$ that Tetrode fixed by comparison to experimental data on mercury vapor. Both derivations gave the absolute entropy of a monoatomic ideal gas in the form now known as the Sackur-Tetrode equation:*

$$S(T, V, N) = k_{B} N \left[\ln\left(\frac{V}{N}\left(\frac{m k_{B} T}{2\pi\hbar^{2}}\right)^{3/2}\right) + \frac{5}{2}\right]$$

*where $m$ is the atomic mass and $\hbar = h/2\pi$. The equation gives absolute entropy — no arbitrary additive constant — as a function of the thermodynamic state $(T, V, N)$ and the atomic mass $m$, with Planck's constant $h$ appearing explicitly through $\hbar^{2}$ inside the logarithm. The empirical test: Sackur and Tetrode both applied the equation to the monoatomic vapor of mercury, using the empirically-known absolute entropy of mercury vapor to extract $h$ from thermodynamic measurements, and compared the value of $h$ so obtained to Planck's 1900 value from blackbody radiation [Planck 1900b, Planck 1901]. The numerical agreement was satisfactory and confirmed both the Sackur-Tetrode formula and the identification of the phase-space cell volume with $h^{n}$ [Grimus 2013].*

*In McGucken framework terms, the Sackur-Tetrode equation is the third historical instantiation of Category (D) of Theorem IX.30.C.13.D.1 after Planck 1900 blackbody and Einstein 1907 specific heat: the Algebraic Channel per-cycle action quantum $h$ (from §I.1.S.1: $h$ is the per-cycle action quantum of the wavefront advance of $x_{4}$ at velocity $c$, dimensionally $h = \delta q \, \delta p$ = position × momentum) supplies the phase-space cell volume $\delta q\,\delta p = h$ per degree of freedom, and the Geometric Channel Boltzmann statistics ($S = k_{B}\log W$ on the Wick-rotated ensemble face of $dx_{4}/dt = ic$) supplies the counting apparatus. The multiplicative combination is direct: the number of microstates $W$ is the classical phase-space volume divided by $h^{n}$, and the resulting entropy carries $h$ inside the logarithm as $\ln(1/\hbar^{3})$ per particle. Every appearance of $h$ in the Sackur-Tetrode equation is the Algebraic Channel per-cycle-action-quantum content of $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ imported into a Geometric Channel Boltzmann calculation, and every appearance of $k_{B}\log$ is the Geometric Channel Wick-rotated ensemble content of $dx_{4}/dt = ic$, per Corollary IX.30.C.13.B.2's KMS-Matsubara mechanism.*

*The historical significance for the McGucken framework's Category (D) claim: prior to Sackur 1911, Planck's constant $h$ had been associated only with the oscillatory phase-carrying face of the Sphere expansion (radiation modes at Planck 1900, single-photon absorption at Einstein 1905, quantized atomic transitions at Bohr 1913, quantized atomic oscillators at Einstein 1907). Sackur 1911 and Tetrode 1912 established that Planck's constant $h$ appears in the classical thermodynamics of ordinary matter — a jar of monoatomic mercury vapor in thermal equilibrium — through the phase-space cell volume that classical Boltzmann counting requires and the pure Geometric Channel cannot supply. This is the first historical case where $h$ entered classical thermodynamics rather than the oscillatory-mode physics of light or atomic transitions; the empirical arrival of $h$ in the statistical mechanics of massive matter more than a decade before the 1925–1926 formalization of quantum mechanics is the historical signature that the combined-channel category was already forced by the empirical thermodynamics of ordinary gases at the pre-quantum level. Grimus 2013 summarizes: "Until then, $h$ was primarily associated with harmonic oscillators and photons. With the work of Sackur and Tetrode it became clear that Planck's constant was not only relevant for counting the number of states in the case of photons but also in the case of massive particles. In this way, $h$ became ubiquitous in statistical physics, more than ten years before the advent of quantum mechanics."*

*The low-temperature failure of the Sackur-Tetrode equation as diagnostic of the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel insufficiency and the necessity of the full Algebraic Channel quantum statistics at low $T$. The Sackur-Tetrode entropy $S(T, V, N) \to -\infty$ as $T \to 0$ (through the $\ln(T^{3/2})$ dependence inside the logarithm going to $-\infty$), which violates Nernst's third law of thermodynamics [Nernst 1906] requiring $S \to 0$ as $T \to 0$ for any physical system in equilibrium. The Sackur-Tetrode failure at low $T$ is diagnostic evidence that the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel with Maxwell-Boltzmann classical statistics is insufficient at low temperatures where quantum statistics become relevant: at $T$ small enough that the thermal de Broglie wavelength $\lambda_{\rm dB} = h/\sqrt{2\pi m k_{B} T}$ becomes comparable to the interparticle spacing $(V/N)^{1/3}$, the particles' Algebraic Channel wavefronts overlap and the classical Maxwell-Boltzmann counting must be replaced by quantum Bose-Einstein statistics (for bosons) or Fermi-Dirac statistics (for fermions). Both replacements are the full Algebraic Channel on the differential-rate form of the Principle: Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac statistics are the ensemble faces of unitary quantum evolution of many-body wavefunctions, computed via the KMS-Matsubara mechanism $\tau_{W} = \beta\hbar$ applied to bosonic or fermionic quantum fields. The Sackur-Tetrode $S \to -\infty$ divergence at low $T$ is the diagnostic signature that the classical-Maxwell-Boltzmann the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel — which sufficed for room-temperature monoatomic ideal gases in 1912 — must be replaced by the full Algebraic Channel quantum statistics as $T \to 0$. This is precisely analogous to the Rayleigh-Jeans ultraviolet catastrophe of Corollary IX.30.C.13.E.1 as diagnostic evidence of the Algebraic Channel vs the Geometric Channel category mismatch: the classical Maxwell-Boltzmann Sackur-Tetrode formula is a partial combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel that supplies only the phase-space cell normalization $h^{n}$ but not the full quantum-statistical the Algebraic Channel content of overlapping wavefronts, and its low-$T$ failure diagnoses the necessity of the fuller Algebraic Channel content that only the 1925–1926 quantum mechanics supplied.*

**Remark IX.30.C.13.E.1 (The McGucken framework's physical reading of $h$: $h$ as the per-cycle action quantum of the wavefront advance of $x_{4}$ at velocity $c$).**

*Planck introduced $h$ in 1900 as an empirical constant fitted to the blackbody data with no physical interpretation [Planck 1900b]. Einstein 1905's photoelectric effect established $h$ as physically real rather than as a formal counting device [Einstein 1905], but neither Planck nor Einstein identified what $h$ physically is. Bohr 1913's atomic model used $h$ in the angular-momentum quantization $L = n\hbar$ without physical interpretation [Bohr 1913]. The 1925–1926 formalization of quantum mechanics by Heisenberg, Born, Jordan, Schrödinger, and Dirac made $h$ (as $\hbar = h/2\pi$) interior to the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ and Stone's unitary group $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$, but the algebraic apparatus does not answer what $h$ physically is — it uses $h$ as an unexplained empirical input. Throughout the subsequent century $h$ appears across physics (Planck spectrum, photoelectric, Bohr atom, canonical commutator, Schrödinger equation, Compton wavelength $\lambda_{C} = h/(mc)$, de Broglie wavelength $\lambda_{\rm dB} = h/p$, path-integral weight $\exp(iS/\hbar)$, KMS periodicity $\tau_{W} = \beta\hbar$, Hawking temperature $T_{H} = \hbar\kappa/(2\pi c k_{B})$) as an empirical constant with no physical mechanism supplying its role in the standard formalism.*

*The McGucken framework's physical reading of $h$ at §I.1.S.1: $h$ is the per-cycle action quantum of the wavefront advance of $x_{4}$ at velocity $c$. The velocity $c$ is the rate at which $x_{4}$'s wavefront advances at every event of $\mathcal M_{G}$; the reduced Planck constant $\hbar$ is the action quantum that accumulates per cycle of the wavefront's phase advance. The two constants are two articulations of the one advance — $c$ articulates the spatial-velocity property of $x_{4}$'s wavefront expansion, $\hbar$ articulates the per-cycle action property of the same wavefront. The dimensional identity $c = \ell_{P}/t_{P}$ with $\ell_{P} = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^{3}}$ and $t_{P} = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^{5}}$ is the numerical signature of this twin-property fact. On the framework's reading, every appearance of $h$ in physics — from Planck 1900's blackbody derivation onward — is the Algebraic Channel content of the McGucken Sphere's oscillatory phase-carrying face, foundationally traced back to $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ through the identification of $c$ as the wavefront advance rate. The Planck 1900 blackbody derivation is, on this reading, the first historical instance of $h$ appearing in physics because it is the first historical instance of the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel being empirically forced, and $h$ is the Algebraic Channel per-cycle action quantum that had to be imported into the Geometric Channel ensemble calculation. The framework's reading is a physical identification of $h$ with the McGucken Sphere's per-cycle action quantum; the strength of the identification within the McGucken corpus is set by Theorem 7 of [494] and §22.5.3 of [4] (Compton-cycle action floor reading of $\hbar$) and by the Disjunctive Forcing Theorem of [13, §X.7.5] applied to the twin-constants pair $(c, h)$. Alternative readings of $h$ that are consistent with the same empirical data are not excluded by the present remark; the framework's reading is presented here as the McGucken-framework physical identification, and the uniqueness arguments that would elevate it to a stronger claim are stated at the cited corpus theorems.*

**Remark IX.30.C.13.E.2 (The reluctant-revolutionary attitude of Planck as the strongest possible historical evidence that the two-channel structure is empirically forced by physics rather than framework-artifact).**

*Planck's own attitude toward his December 14, 1900 derivation is documented at length in his correspondence and retrospective writings [Kragh 2000; Duncan-Janssen 2020]. Planck did not believe he had introduced physical quantization; he treated the energy element $\varepsilon = h\nu$ as a mathematical device for counting Boltzmann complexions rather than as a physical constraint on oscillator energies. Planck did not believe in atoms; he did not believe entropy should be statistical; he had spent three years opposing Boltzmann's kinetic-theory approach and turned to Boltzmann's $S = k \log W$ only because pure thermodynamics had provably failed. Planck's own characterization was "an act of desperation." Kragh 2000: "The 'discovery' of quantum theory should not be seen as a moment of insight in December 1900, but as an extended process by which Planck became a revolutionary against his will." Planck spent the subsequent decade attempting to derive his 1900 result without quantization and without statistical entropy, and never fully accepted the quantum interpretation of his own work.*

*The strength of Planck's opposition supplies the strongest possible historical evidence for the McGucken framework's Category (D) claim. Planck was the world's leading thermodynamicist, philosophically committed to the pure Geometric Channel (thermodynamics, deterministic entropy, continuous variables, no atomism, no statistical mechanics). He spent three years attempting the pure Geometric Channel derivation. The Pure Geometric Channel failed empirically. He then attempted, in November 1900, to derive the correct spectrum from a different pure-Channel-B approach. That also failed. He was then forced, against every philosophical commitment he held, to combine the Algebraic Channel content ($\varepsilon = h\nu$) with the Geometric Channel content ($S = k \log W$) to obtain the correct spectrum. The reluctant-revolutionary character of the episode establishes that the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel for blackbody radiation is not a framework artifact — Planck was philosophically motivated to avoid it and would have derived the spectrum without it if the pure Geometric Channel had been sufficient. The Pure Geometric Channel was empirically insufficient, and the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel was empirically forced. This is precisely the strength of the Category (D) claim of Theorem IX.30.C.13.D.1: blackbody radiation is a combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel as a matter of the underlying physics, not as a matter of the McGucken framework's identification.*

#### IX.30.C.13.F The Historical Development of Physics from Galilean Relativity (1632) Through Modern Cosmology and Horizon Thermodynamics (1922–2020) as Successive Empirical Instrumentations of the Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel of $dx_{4}/dt = ic$: Each Historical Episode Grounded in Its Founding Experiments and Identified with the Algebraic Channel Content, the Geometric Channel Content, or a Specifiable Combination of Both Channels on the McGucken Sphere Expansion at Rate $c$ from Every Event of $\mathcal M_{G}$

*McGucken Principle anchor.* The McGucken Principle $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ states the physical reality that the fourth dimension is expanding at velocity $c$ at every event of spacetime. The expansion produces the McGucken Sphere from every event, expanding radially at rate $c$ in real space with per-cycle action quantum $h$ accumulated per cycle of the wavefront's phase advance. From the Principle two channels descend as two direct readings of the same expanding wavefront: **The Geometric Channel recognizes the nonlocal, dissipative expansion of $x_{4}$ at velocity $c$ — the spatially spreading wavefront in real space, the McGucken Sphere as a physically real expanding surface, the source of entropy increase and thermodynamic dissipation**; **The Algebraic Channel recognizes the quantum nature of the spherically-symmetric wavefront's advance — the per-cycle action quantum $h$ that the wavefront carries, the phase $i$ that tracks the oscillatory advance, the algebraic-Hilbert-space encoding of the wavefront's quantum content**. Both channels are direct readings of the Principle, and neither is derived from the other: Geometric Channel and the Algebraic Channel recognize two different features of the same expanding spherical wavefront simultaneously present in $dx_{4}/dt = ic$. The Geometric Channel is physically foundational at §IX.30.C.8 (the wavefront is a physically real object expanding in real space); the Algebraic Channel is the algebraic-Hilbert-space representation of the same wavefront's quantum-phase content (with $i$ inherited from the Principle's $ic$ and $h$ from the per-cycle action of the wavefront's phase advance per §I.1.S.1). The substrate symmetries of $\mathcal M_{G}$ — the Poincaré group in the relativistic regime, the Galilean group in the $v \ll c$ approximation, and the internal gauge symmetries $U(1) \times SU(2) \times SU(3)$ — are Poincaré-covariance properties that both channels carry directly, because both channels are Poincaré-covariant readings of the Principle on $\mathcal M_{G}$: the Geometric Channel under thermal-state constructions on globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifolds per Bisognano-Wichmann; the Algebraic Channel under unitary representations per the Wightman axiomatization (Theorem IX.30.A.4.6). The historical development of physics from 1632 to 2020 is the empirical exploration of these two channels of the McGucken Sphere expansion at rate $c$ through experiments that accessed the nonlocal dissipative expansion (The Geometric Channel — rigid-body inertia, thermodynamics, gravitation, cosmology, horizon thermodynamics) or the quantum wavefront-advance content (The Algebraic Channel — Faraday-Maxwell wave sector, Noether reversible-symmetry apparatus, quantum mechanics) or specifiable combinations of both simultaneously (blackbody radiation, specific heat, Sackur-Tetrode entropy). Each major theoretical development is grounded in a specific experimental basis, and each is identifiable with the Algebraic Channel content, the Geometric Channel content, or a specifiable combination of both channels of the Principle.

**Theorem IX.30.C.13.F.1 (Historical mapping of major physics developments 1632–1926 to substrate symmetries and channels of $dx_{4}/dt = ic$, grounded in founding experiments).**

*The thirteen major theoretical developments of physics from Galileo 1632 through the LIGO gravitational-wave observations of 2015–2017 each identify with the Algebraic Channel content, the Geometric Channel content, or a specifiable combination of both channels of the McGucken Principle $dx_{4}/dt = ic$, grounded in a specific experimental basis. The substrate symmetries (Galilean, Poincaré, gauge) that appear across these developments are joint properties of both channels rather than a separate category, because both channels descend from $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ on the same manifold $\mathcal M_{G}$ and inherit its isometry and gauge symmetries. Each identification is stated below with the founding experiments named at primary sources.*

*(1) Galileo — inertia and free fall (Galileo 1632, 1638) — the Geometric Channel in the classical low-velocity regime: inertia is mass coupling to the nonlocal dissipative expansion of $x_{4}$ at rate $c$; Galilean frame invariance is the $v \ll c$ approximation of the Poincaré symmetry that Geometric Channel carries on $\mathcal M_{G}$ (item 8).* *Galileo's *Dialogo sopra i due massimi sistemi del mondo* [Galileo 1632] and *Discorsi e Dimostrazioni Matematiche intorno a Due Nuove Scienze* [Galileo 1638] established two related empirical facts: the equivalence of uniform motion and rest at the level of rigid-body dynamics (Galilean frame invariance), and the universal-inertial-mass content of freely-falling bodies. The founding empirical arguments were the ship-mast experiments (stones dropped from the top of a moving ship's mast land at the base of the mast, not behind it, so terrestrial uniform motion is undetectable by internal rigid-body mechanics), the fly-and-fish-in-cabin thought experiment (*Two Chief Systems*, Day II), the inclined-plane rolling-ball timing experiments (rigid-body acceleration under gravity, quantifying the equivalence-of-uniform-motion-and-rest at the dynamical level), and the pendulum-isochronism observations (pendulum period independent of amplitude for small oscillations, again a rigid-body inertial phenomenon). All of these are observations of rigid-body inertial mechanics of macroscopic massive objects at velocities $v \ll c$, in the classical regime where the McGucken Sphere expansion at rate $c$ is empirically invisible and the per-cycle action quantum $h$ is empirically invisible. In McGucken framework terms, inertia — the mass $m$ that resists acceleration in $F = ma$, the same $m$ that appears in gravitational attraction, the same $m$ that appears in the Compton frequency $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar$ — is the Geometric Channel content: mass is the coupling of a massive particle to the nonlocal dissipative expansion of $x_{4}$ at rate $c$, with $\omega_{C}$ setting the rate at which the Sphere's substrate ticks for a particle of mass $m$. *(12) Modern cosmology and the cosmological constant (Einstein 1917 → Friedmann 1922 → Lemaître 1927 → Hubble 1929 → Gamow-Alpher-Herman 1948 → Penzias-Wilson 1965 → COBE 1992 → WMAP 2003 → Planck 2018) — the Geometric Channel on the integrated-coordinate form applied at the cosmological horizon, with the cosmological constant $\Lambda$ identified through the Gibbons-Hawking mechanism at the de Sitter horizon and the McGucken cosmology paper [5] supplying the specific-value derivation and twelve zero-free-parameter observational tests.* *Einstein 1917 [Einstein 1917] introduced the cosmological constant $\Lambda$ in a static-universe modification of the 1915 field equations, motivated by the empirical astronomical belief in a static cosmos, later called by Einstein his "greatest blunder" after the empirical arrival of Hubble's redshift-distance data. **Remark IX.30.C.13.F.1 (Founding experiments enumerated with primary-source citations).**

*Each of the ten historical developments of Theorem IX.30.C.13.F.1 is grounded in specific founding experiments enumerated with primary-source citations:*

*Galilean relativity: ship-mast experiments ([Galileo 1632, Day II, Second Day arguments]); inclined-plane experiments ([Galileo 1638, *Discorsi e dimostrazioni matematiche intorno a due nuove scienze*, Third Day]).*

*Huygens' principle: refraction and Snell's law observations; birefringence in Iceland spar ([Huygens 1690, Chapter V]); Huygens' pendulum-clock experiments establishing periodic-motion foundations.*

*Newton's laws of motion: Galileo's inclined-plane data ([Galileo 1638]); Kepler's three laws of planetary motion from Tycho Brahe's precision astronomical data ([Kepler 1609, *Astronomia Nova*; Kepler 1619, *Harmonices Mundi*]); Huygens' pendulum studies; Newton's own experiments on falling bodies and cometary orbits ([Newton 1687, Books I–III]).*

*Newton's law of gravitation: Kepler's third law $T^{2} \propto a^{3}$; the Moon test comparing the Moon's centripetal acceleration to the acceleration of a falling apple at Earth's surface ([Newton 1687, Book III, Proposition IV]); cometary orbital calculations.*

*Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction: Faraday's 1831 experiments with moving magnets and current-carrying coils (August 29 – November 24, 1831; recorded in [Faraday 1832]); the Faraday disc (December 1831); the observed generation of currents by time-varying magnetic fields.*

*Maxwell's equations: Coulomb's inverse-square law for static electric charges ([Coulomb 1785]); the Biot-Savart law and Ampère's circuital law for magnetostatics ([Ampère 1826]); Faraday's law of induction ([Faraday 1832]); the absence of magnetic monopoles from experimental data; Hertz's 1887–1888 experiments detecting radio waves confirming Maxwell's electromagnetic wave prediction ([Hertz 1888]).*

*Thermodynamics: steam-engine efficiency measurements (Watt, Trevithick, and subsequent generations of engineers, motivating Carnot's 1824 heat-engine analysis); calorimetric measurements of heat capacities (Joule 1843–1850, Regnault 1840s); Maxwell's velocity-distribution measurements from viscosity data; Boltzmann's H-theorem grounded in molecular kinetic theory; Gibbs's axiomatic reformulation.*

*Special relativity: Michelson-Morley 1887 experiment establishing the null result for aether-drift measurements at sensitivity $10^{-9}$ in $\Delta c/c$ ([Michelson-Morley 1887]); Fizeau's 1851 experiment measuring the speed of light in flowing water ([Fizeau 1851]); Kaufmann's 1901–1906 measurements of the mass increase of high-speed electrons.*

*General relativity: the anomalous perihelion precession of Mercury (43″/century unaccounted for by Newtonian gravity plus known perturbations, matched by Einstein's calculation on November 18, 1915 [Einstein 1915-Mercury]); the Eötvös experiments 1889–1908 establishing the equivalence of inertial and gravitational mass to precision $\sim 10^{-9}$ ([Eötvös et al. 1922]); Eddington's 1919 solar-eclipse expedition confirming the predicted gravitational light-bending ([Dyson-Eddington-Davidson 1920]).*

*Noether's theorem: the formal founding context is Hilbert 1915's variational derivation of general relativity from the action $S_{\rm EH} = \int \sqrt{-g}\,R\,d^{4}x$ ([Hilbert 1915]), which left open the question of how energy-momentum conservation is expressed in a diffeomorphism-invariant theory. Hilbert requested Noether at Göttingen to resolve this question. Noether's First Theorem (global symmetries → conserved currents) was empirically anchored by the well-established conservation laws of nineteenth-century classical mechanics and electromagnetism (conservation of energy, momentum, angular momentum in Lagrangian systems; conservation of electric charge in Maxwell theory), which Noether's theorem systematized as consequences of Poincaré and $U(1)$ gauge symmetries respectively. Noether's Second Theorem (local/gauge symmetries → identities among field equations) was empirically anchored by the observed automatic satisfaction of the Bianchi identities $\nabla_{\mu}G^{\mu\nu} = 0$ in general relativity, which the Second Theorem identified as the consequence of diffeomorphism invariance. Cited at Theorem IX.30.C.13.F.1(10) as the formal machinery of the Algebraic Channel reversible-symmetries tradition.*

*Quantum mechanics: Rubens-Kurlbaum 1900 blackbody measurements refuting Wien's law at long wavelengths ([Rubens-Kurlbaum 1900]); Millikan 1916 photoelectric-effect measurements confirming Einstein's linear frequency-energy relation ([Millikan 1916]); the Franck-Hertz 1914 experiment confirming discrete atomic energy levels ([Franck-Hertz 1914]); the Stern-Gerlach 1922 experiment establishing spin quantization ([Stern-Gerlach 1922]); Compton 1923's photon-electron scattering confirming particle-like light ([Compton 1923]); Davisson-Germer 1927 electron-diffraction confirming wave-like matter ([Davisson-Germer 1927]).*

*Modern cosmology and the cosmological constant: Einstein 1917's introduction of $\Lambda$ in a static-universe modification of the 1915 field equations ([Einstein 1917]); Friedmann's 1922 derivation of the dynamic-universe solutions ([Friedmann 1922]); Lemaître's 1927 independent derivation and prediction of the linear velocity-distance relation ([Lemaître 1927]); Hubble's 1929 empirical measurement of extragalactic-nebula recession velocities confirming the expansion ([Hubble 1929]); the Gamow-Alpher-Herman 1948 prediction of a relic Big Bang thermal radiation with present-day temperature of a few Kelvin ([Alpher-Bethe-Gamow 1948; Alpher-Herman 1948]); the Penzias-Wilson 1965 discovery of the cosmic microwave background at 2.7 K at Bell Labs ([Penzias-Wilson 1965]); the COBE 1992 satellite measurements establishing the CMB as a Planck spectrum at $T = 2.725 \pm 0.001$ K and detecting the temperature anisotropies at the $10^{-5}$ level ([Smoot et al. 1992; Mather et al. 1994]); the WMAP 2003 measurement of the cosmological parameters ([Spergel et al. 2003]); the Planck 2018 satellite refinement of the concordance $\Lambda$CDM model with $\Omega_{\Lambda} \approx 0.685$, $\Omega_{m} \approx 0.315$, and $H_{0} \approx 67.4$ km/s/Mpc ([Planck 2018]). Cross-referenced to the McGucken cosmology paper [5] for the specific-value dark-sector derivations and the twelve zero-free-parameter cosmological tests.*

*Black-hole entropy and horizon thermodynamics: Bekenstein 1973's derivation of black-hole entropy $S_{\rm BH} = k_{B}A/(4\ell_{P}^{2})$ from the second-law requirement ([Bekenstein 1973]); Hawking 1974–1975's derivation of the Hawking temperature $T_{H} = \hbar\kappa/(2\pi c k_{B})$ from quantum field theory in curved spacetime ([Hawking 1974; Hawking 1975]); Unruh's 1976 extension to accelerated observers with $T_{U} = \hbar a/(2\pi c k_{B})$ ([Unruh 1976]); the Gibbons-Hawking 1977 extension to the de Sitter cosmological horizon ([Gibbons-Hawking 1977]); Jacobson's 1995 derivation of the Einstein field equations from the Clausius relation $\delta Q = TdS$ applied to local Rindler horizons ([Jacobson 1995]); Padmanabhan's 2010 systematic thermodynamic derivation across gravitational actions ([Padmanabhan 2010]); Verlinde's 2011 entropic-force derivation of Newtonian gravitation ([Verlinde 2011]); LIGO's 2015 GW150914 first direct detection of gravitational waves ([Abbott et al. 2016]); the 2017 GW170817 binary neutron-star merger detected in gravitational waves and electromagnetic radiation ([GW170817]).
