#### IX.30.D.4 The Born Rule as the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Geometric Overlap, Not the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel Postulate

**Theorem IX.30.D.4 (Born rule as the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel geometric overlap).** *Under the ontological-epistemological asymmetry of §IX.30.A.2, the Born rule $P = |\psi|^2$ is recognized as a theorem about the geometric overlap of forward and conjugate $+ic$-oriented McGucken Sphere expansions at the head-on collision event, not as a postulate of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel. The probability of a measurement event registering the system in a region $O$ of configuration space at time $t$ is the geometric overlap of the source's forward Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ at retarded time $t - t_p$ with the conjugate (backward-propagating) Sphere $\Sigma_M^-(q)$ from candidate apparatus detection events $q$ with $\mathbf x_q \in O$, normalized by the Haar measure on $\mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{SO}(2) \cong S^2$ that the spatial-direction probability density imposes (§IX.22.6, Theorem 7.4 of [MG-Pointwise], Theorem IX.22.6 Haar-uniqueness on the spatial-direction sphere). The Born rule is therefore a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel geometric statement about Sphere overlap; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel formula $P = |\psi|^2$ is the algebraic-statistical encoding of this geometry.*

*Proof.* The detailed proof appears at Theorem 7.4 of [MG-Pointwise] and Theorem IX.22.6.B.9 of the present paper. the claim: $\psi(\mathbf x, t)$ as a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel object is the complex-valued amplitude on configuration space whose squared modulus predicts measurement statistics; under the framework's account, $\psi$ is the algebraic encoding of the $+ic$-oriented Sphere expansion's geometry at retarded time $t$. The forward Sphere from the source event carries Compton phase $\Phi(q; p) = \exp(-i\omega_C \Delta\tau(q; p))$ uniform across the spatial slice (Lemma 2.2 of [MG-Pointwise]); the conjugate Sphere from the candidate apparatus event carries the conjugate phase. The inner product $\langle q | \psi \rangle$ at configuration-space point $q$ is the geometric overlap of the two phase-content distributions at the candidate detection event $q$. The squared modulus $|\langle q | \psi \rangle|^2$ is the geometric overlap intensity, with the Haar measure on $\mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{SO}(2)$ supplying the spatial-direction probability density (by uniqueness of the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant measure on the spatial-direction sphere $S^2$). The Born rule is therefore the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel algebraic encoding of this dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel geometric overlap content; it is a theorem of the dual-channel architecture. ∎

### IX.30.E The Measurement Dissolution: All Measurement Events are the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Physical Events; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the Statistical Encoding; the Orthodox Measurement Problem is Dissolved at the Source

The dual-channel architecture of §§IX.30.A–IX.30.C establishes the ontological/epistemological distinction (Signatures 2, 5, 8, 14, 17 of §IX.30.A.2) as a foundational facet of the dual-channel architecture. The present section develops the consequence of the ontological/epistemological distinction for the orthodox measurement problem of quantum mechanics: **The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel carries the ontology — what exists in the universe — and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel carries the epistemology — what measurements report when the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical events are registered. All measurement events are the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical events.** The distinction is real, not metaphorical, and it dissolves the orthodox measurement problem at the source rather than resolving it within the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's confines.

**Theorem IX.30.E.1 (Ontological-epistemological asymmetry of the dual-channel architecture, restated as a theorem).** *Under the dual-channel architecture of §§IX.30.A–IX.30.C:*

*(i) the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is ontological in the sense of being the spatiotemporal-physics of the universe. The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ expanding at $+ic$ from every event of spacetime is a real geometric object in real four-dimensional spacetime, with definite radius $c(t - t_p)$, definite area $A(t) = 4\pi c^2(t - t_p)^2$, definite Compton angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ for the massive species emitted, definite $+ic$ orientation distinguishing forward Sphere expansion from time-reversed contraction, and definite spatiotemporal coordinates at every instant of its existence. The Sphere expansion is what is happening in the universe at every event.*

*(ii) the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is epistemic in the sense of encoding the statistics of what measurements report on the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical events. The Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, the operator algebra $B(\mathcal H)$, the wavefunction $\psi$ as element of $\mathcal H$ or as complex-valued function on configuration space, the Born rule $P = |\psi|^2$, the eigenvalue spectra of self-adjoint observables, the trace formula $\langle \hat O \rangle = \mathrm{Tr}(\rho \hat O)$, the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, the unitary one-parameter group $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$ — all of these are calculational objects that predict the statistics of measurement outcomes when the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical events are aggregated across repetitions. They are encodings of what entities in spacetime report when measured.*

*(iii) Every measurement event is a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical event. A detector click, a photographic emulsion grain blackening, a Stern-Gerlach apparatus depositing a silver atom on a detection screen, a photomultiplier cascade, a CCD pixel charge, a bubble chamber track, a photodiode voltage pulse — every one of these is a real physical occurrence at a definite spacetime event $q = (\mathbf x_q, t_q)$ in real four-dimensional spacetime, with the system's $+ic$-oriented Sphere meeting the detector atom's $+ic$-oriented Sphere in a head-on collision at $q$ that 3-localizes the interaction and produces a definite outcome (Theorem 7.4 of [MG-Pointwise]; §IX.22.6.B.9 of the present paper). The collision is a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical event; the resulting localization is a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical event; the propagation of the detection signal outward at $+ic$ from the collision event into the detection apparatus is a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical process.*

*(iv) the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel contains no measurement events. The unitary evolution $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$ of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus is silent on which spacetime moments are measurement moments. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel requires an external specification of "a measurement has been performed at event $q$" to deploy the Born rule and update the statistical encoding. That external specification is the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical event of a head-on Sphere collision at $q$. Without the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical events, the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus runs unitarily forever and never produces a definite outcome.*

*Proof.* Statement (i) follows from the foundations $\Phi = (\mathcal M_G, dx_4/dt = ic, +ic)$ (Definition IX.28.3) of the framework: the principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$ asserts at every event of $\mathcal M_G$ the existence of a $+ic$-oriented active expansion, with the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ as the propagating wavefront generated at event $p$ by the principle (Definition IX.19.1, after [7]). The Sphere is a specific point-set in $\mathcal M_G$: $\Sigma_M^+(p) = \{(\mathbf x, t) \in \mathbb R^3 \times \mathbb R : \|\mathbf x - \mathbf x_p\| = c(t - t_p), t \geq t_p\}$. As a point-set in the manifold, the Sphere has definite spatiotemporal coordinates, definite geometry (radius, area, mean curvature, induced metric), and definite directional content (the $+ic$-orientation distinguishing forward expansion from time-reversed contraction). It is an entity in real four-dimensional spacetime, not a mathematical-statistical encoding.

Statement (ii) follows from Theorem IX.30.B.1 and the dual-channel architecture of §IX.30.C: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus is the time-symmetric subalgebra $\mathcal A = \mathcal B^T$ of the full geometry $\mathcal B$, with the $+ic$ orientation absent because algebra is sign-symmetric and cannot carry geometric directional content. The objects of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel — Hilbert spaces, operator algebras, wavefunctions, unitary one-parameter groups, the Born rule — are mathematical-algebraic structures whose function is to predict the statistical distribution of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel measurement events when those events are aggregated across repetitions. The Born rule $P(q \in O) = \int_O |\psi(\mathbf x, t)|^2\, d^3\mathbf x$ predicts the probability that a measurement event will register the system in a region $O$ of configuration space, not the location of the actual measurement event itself. The wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf x, t)$ encodes the statistical distribution of where the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Sphere-collision events would occur at retarded time $t$ if a detection apparatus were placed at $\mathbf x$; the actual event happens or doesn't happen in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel at a specific point. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus is the bookkeeping; the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's events are the entries being bookkept.

Statement (iii) follows from the head-on Sphere-collision content of Theorem 7.4 of [MG-Pointwise] and Theorem IX.22.6.B.9 of the present paper: the Born rule's measurement event is the geometric overlap of the forward $+ic$-oriented Sphere from the source event $p$ with the conjugate $+ic$-oriented Sphere from the apparatus detection event $q$, with the inner-product structure being the geometric overlap of the two propagating Spheres at their head-on intersection. The collision is a real physical event: it has definite spacetime coordinates ($\mathbf x_q, t_q$), definite energy-momentum transfer (the species's mass-shell content delivered to the detector atom), definite electromagnetic or strong or weak interaction content (depending on what the apparatus measures), and definite outcome (the apparatus registers a specific eigenvalue of the observable corresponding to the measurement geometry). The downstream apparatus propagation — the photomultiplier cascade producing an electrical signal, the CCD pixel charging up, the silver atom depositing on the photographic plate, the bubble chamber liquid nucleating along the ionization track — is a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical process: it operates at the $+ic$-oriented Sphere expansion of the secondary particles produced by the collision, propagating through the apparatus's material at $+ic$ with the apparatus's coupling to the registered species converting the head-on collision event into a macroscopically visible signal.

Statement (iv) follows from the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus alone. The unitary group $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$ is a one-parameter subgroup of the unitary group of $\mathcal H$ generated by the self-adjoint Hamiltonian $\hat H$ via Stone's theorem (§II.1). It evolves the wavefunction $|\psi(t)\rangle = U(t)|\psi(0)\rangle$ smoothly with respect to the parameter $t$ for all $t \in \mathbb R$, with no distinguished moments at which "a measurement is performed" or "an outcome is produced." The orthodox measurement problem (§IX.29) is the recognition that within the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel alone, the unitary evolution does not select preferred moments at which definite outcomes occur, and the orthodox formalism requires a separate postulate — the "collapse postulate" or "projection postulate" — to update $|\psi\rangle$ when a measurement event is registered. The framework's account: the collapse postulate is the algebraic-statistical artifact of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's encoding being updated when a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical event has occurred. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel supplies the events; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel updates the encoding. Without the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical events, the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's unitary evolution runs forever without producing any definite outcomes, exactly as the orthodox measurement problem identifies. With the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical events at specific spacetime coordinates, the encoding updates accordingly, and the "collapse" is recognized as the bookkeeping change induced by the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel event rather than as a physical mechanism in need of a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel explanation. ∎

**Remark IX.30.E.2 (The orthodox measurement problem is dissolved at the source).** *The measurement problem of orthodox quantum mechanics — articulated by Bohr 1928, von Neumann 1932, Wigner 1963, Bell 1990 ("Against 'Measurement'"), Penrose 2004, Schlosshauer 2007 — is the question: how does the unitary evolution of $|\psi\rangle$ in the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's apparatus produce definite measurement outcomes? Within the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel alone, the question has no answer. Many-Worlds (Everett 1957, DeWitt 1970) responds by denying that collapse occurs, treating every dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel unitary branch as equally real and relocating the "definite outcome" question to observer-relative branching. GRW (Ghirardi–Rimini–Weber 1986) responds by adding a stochastic collapse term to the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel dynamics, postulating an unmotivated modification of the unitary evolution. Bohmian mechanics (Bohm 1952, Dürr–Goldstein–Zanghì 1992) responds by adding particle positions as the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel hidden variables guided by $|\psi\rangle$, producing the right statistics at the cost of nonlocality that does not sit naturally in a relativistic framework. QBism (Caves–Fuchs–Schack 2002, Fuchs 2010) responds by denying the ontological reading of $|\psi\rangle$ entirely and treating the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel as the agent's personal probability assignments, refusing to say anything about the universe itself. Decoherence-based resolutions (Zurek 1981–2003, Joos–Zeh 1985, Schlosshauer 2007) respond by appealing to environmental interaction to suppress off-diagonal density-matrix elements in the pointer basis, with the resulting mixed state interpreted as the absence of definite outcomes despite the unitary evolution being preserved.*

*Every one of these orthodox resolutions operates within the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel — within the time-symmetric epistemic apparatus that is sign-blind on the $+ic$ orientation. By the content-asymmetry theorem (Theorem IX.30.C.3), the ontology needed to produce definite measurement events at specific spacetime coordinates lives in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel, outside the reach of the Algebraic Channel. The orthodox project of locating the source of definite measurement outcomes inside the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is impossible because the source is not there. Every orthodox resolution fails for the same reason: it is looking in the wrong place for almost a century.*

*The framework's dissolution: there is no collapse to mechanism because there is no foundational $|\psi\rangle$ that collapses. There is the $+ic$-oriented McGucken Sphere expansion in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel at every event of spacetime; there is the head-on Sphere-collision event at the detector that 3-localizes the interaction at a specific spacetime coordinate; there is the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's statistical encoding that updates when the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel event is registered. The "collapse" is the bookkeeping change induced by the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel event, not a physical mechanism in need of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel explanation. The "preferred basis" of decoherence is selected by which Sphere-collision geometry occurs at the detection event in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel, not by environmental-coupling content of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's reduced density matrix. The "definite outcomes" of the measurement problem are the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical events at specific spacetime coordinates, not emergent products of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's unitary evolution. The measurement problem dissolves because the question is malformed: it asks how the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's epistemic apparatus produces ontology, and the answer is that the ontology was never in the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel to begin with. The ontology is in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the symmetric statistical encoding. Once the categorical confusion is removed, the problem evaporates.*

**Remark IX.30.E.3 (Empirical adequacy and ontological status are different categories).** *The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's empirical successes — the prediction of atomic spectra to ten or more decimal places, the electron $g - 2$ to twelve decimal places, the Lamb shift, the Stern-Gerlach beam deflection, the double-slit interference pattern, the Bell-inequality violations at $2\sqrt 2$, the entire empirical record of quantum mechanics — do not promote the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel to ontological status. Empirical adequacy and ontological status are different categories. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel predicts what measurements report with extraordinary precision; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is therefore an excellent epistemic encoding of the statistical content of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical events. But the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is the statistical encoding of what is in the universe. The McGucken Sphere expanding at $+ic$ at every event is what is in the universe; the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's predictions are accurate because the encoding accurately tracks the statistics of the Sphere-collision events that constitute measurements. The empirical success of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is a confirmation of the framework's account, not a refutation of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's ontological priority: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's accuracy as a statistical encoding is exactly what the geometry/algebra-distinction architecture predicts, since algebra is the optimal time-symmetric symbolic encoding of the geometry's statistical signatures at measurement events.*

**Remark IX.30.E.4 (The Wigner's-Friend, Quantum Suicide, and Decoherence-Preferred-Basis problems dissolve under the same architecture).** *Three further measurement-problem variants commonly discussed in the foundations literature dissolve under the ontological-epistemological asymmetry. Wigner's Friend (Wigner 1961): the question of how an "outside observer" sees an "inside observer" who is in superposition assumes that the inside observer's superposition is a physical state; under the framework's account, the inside observer is a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical entity whose state is the $+ic$-oriented Sphere content at their spacetime location, not a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel wavefunction superposition. There is no "outside observer sees inside observer in superposition" problem because the inside observer occupies a definite the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel state, while the outside observer's the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel description of them is the statistical encoding pending the next the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel interaction event between them. Quantum Suicide and the Many-Worlds-derived paradoxes of personal identity across branches: these dissolve under the same architecture because there are no branches in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel — there is one universe with one $+ic$-oriented Sphere expansion at every event, and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's multi-branched description is the statistical encoding's representation of multiple possible measurement outcomes pending the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel events that select among them. The decoherence-preferred-basis problem (Zurek 1981, Joos–Zeh 1985, Schlosshauer 2007): the question of why the universe has a preferred basis (position-eigenstates rather than momentum-eigenstates as the macroscopic-classical basis) dissolves because the preferred basis is selected in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel by the head-on Sphere-collision geometry that 3-localizes detection events, not by environmental-coupling content of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's reduced density matrix. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Sphere-collision mechanism naturally produces position-localization at the detection event because the Sphere is a spatial wavefront expanding through three-dimensional space, not a momentum-space distribution.*

### IX.30.F Historical Evolution of Physics Through the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel: Why Statistical-Measurement Data Drove the Algebraic Foundations

The reading of §IX.30.E — the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel as ontological substrate, the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel as statistical-epistemic encoding, all measurement events as the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical occurrences — supplies a diagnosis of the historical evolution of foundational physics from the late nineteenth century to the present. The diagnosis is that physics evolved primarily through the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel because the empirical data available to physics was the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel data — statistical-measurement reports of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical events. The algebraic foundations that emerged in 1925–1932 and dominated foundational physics thereafter were the natural mathematical encoding of the statistical-measurement data, not the natural mathematical description of the underlying the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel physical reality. The framework's historical claim: physics has been doing the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel foundations for a century because the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is what measurements give us; the +ic-oriented the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content has been retroactively recoverable only when geometric-reasoning was applied to the same phenomena (Einstein 1915 on gravitation, Boltzmann 1872 on H-theorem-derived entropy increase, Huygens 1690 on wavefront propagation), and the geometric-tradition has been institutionally separated from the algebraic-tradition for nearly a century.

The present subsection traces this historical evolution explicitly, identifying for each major development in the foundations of quantum mechanics and thermodynamics whether the development proceeded through the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel reasoning (statistical-algebraic analysis of measurement data), the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel reasoning (geometric-propagation analysis of physics), or some mixture of the two with subsequent reinterpretation.

**Theorem IX.30.F.1 (Historical evolution of foundational physics is the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel-biased).** *The major developments in foundational physics from approximately 1859 to the present have proceeded primarily through the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel reasoning — algebraic-statistical analysis of measurement data — with the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel reasoning appearing in specific cases (Huygens 1690, Maxwell 1865, Boltzmann 1872, Einstein 1905 photoelectric/Brownian-motion, Einstein 1915 general relativity, de Broglie 1924 matter waves, Schrödinger 1926 wave-mechanical derivation) but with the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content typically reinterpreted as the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel within months or years of its appearance. The cause: the empirical data driving foundational physics was statistical-measurement data (spectroscopic frequencies, scattering cross-sections, blackbody radiation intensities, photoelectric stopping voltages, electron diffraction patterns, particle decay rates, beta-asymmetry distributions, CHSH correlation values), which is intrinsically the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel data — the report of measurement events aggregated across repetitions — and the mathematical apparatus that most directly encodes this data is the algebraic-statistical apparatus of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel (operator algebras, Hilbert spaces, eigenvalue spectra, probability distributions, density matrices, partition functions). The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel reasoning — geometric-propagation analysis of physics — requires the prior commitment that there is a definite physics in spacetime to be analyzed, a commitment that orthodox physics has resisted on epistemological grounds since Bohr 1927 (complementarity) and Born 1926 (probability interpretation of $\psi$).*

*Outline of the historical evidence.* The historical record divides into roughly seven phases, each characterized by a particular relationship between empirical input, mathematical apparatus, and commitments to the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel or the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel content. The pre-quantum optical foundations (1690–1900) constitute Phase 0; the kinetic-theory developments (1859–1924) constitute Phase 1; the old quantum theory (1900–1925), the matrix-mechanical crystallization (1925–1927), the wave-mechanical reinterpretation (1925–1927), the von Neumann axiomatization (1927–1956), and the post-1956 consolidation through QFT and unification programs constitute Phases 2 through 6 respectively.

*Phase 0 (1690–1900): The first historical the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel vs the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel battle — Huygens versus Newton on the foundations of light, with the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel winning by Newton's prestige and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel reasserting itself decisively in 1801–1820.* The first historically documented appearance of the channel split in foundational physics is the Huygens-Newton dispute about the nature of light, beginning with Huygens 1690's *Traité de la Lumière* and Newton 1704's *Opticks*, continuing through the 18th century with Newton's corpuscular theory dominating by Newton's prestige rather than empirical superiority, and reaching decisive resolution in favor of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel with Young 1801's double-slit experiment, Fresnel 1818's diffraction analysis, and the Poisson-Arago bright spot confirmation. The dispute is paradigmatic for the framework's historical claim because it shows the channel split appearing in physics for the first time, with explicit the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel (Huygens) and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel (Newton) competing frameworks for the same physical phenomenon, and the eventual decisive the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel victory in classical optics being followed by the reintroduction of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel at the quantum level in 1905.

*(P0.1) Huygens 1690 [Huygens 1690, *Traité de la Lumière*, Pierre van der Aa, Leiden] as paradigmatic the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel foundational physics.* Huygens published the *Traité* with the claim that light is a wavefront propagating through a luminiferous medium at velocity $c$, with every point of the wavefront acting as a secondary source of spherical wavelets, and with the envelope of the secondary wavelets reconstructing the next instant's wavefront. This is **pure the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel reasoning**: light is a real physical entity (a wavefront) propagating through real spacetime (the medium) at finite velocity ($c$), with definite geometry at every instant of its propagation (the wavefront's spatial shape, the secondary wavelets' spherical structure, the envelope reconstruction's geometry). The +ic-oriented forward-propagation direction is built into the construction: Huygens used envelopes of *forward-emitted* secondary wavelets, not backward-emitted; the retarded-Green's-function preference (item G5 of the Catalog of Asymmetries in §IX.30.C.2) is implicit in Huygens' choice of envelope direction; the Sphere recursion direction (item G11 of the Catalog of Asymmetries) is Huygens' iterated wavelet construction made explicit. *Huygens 1690 has the McGucken Sphere construction in everything but name* — spherical wavelets emanating from every event of the wavefront at velocity $c$, iterated forward in time, with the envelope reconstruction giving the next instant's wavefront, and the +ic-oriented forward direction implicit in the choice of envelope. The framework's account: Huygens supplied the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel at the founding of physical optics, 335 years before the McGucken framework articulates the dual-channel architecture explicitly.

*(P0.2) Newton 1704 [Newton 1704, *Opticks*, Sam. Smith and Benj. Walford, London] as paradigmatic pre-quantum the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel foundational physics.* Newton published the *Opticks* with the claim that light is a stream of discrete corpuscles, each carrying definite momentum, travelling in straight lines except where deflected by forces at material interfaces. This is **pre-quantum the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel reasoning**: light is a collection of indexed entities (the corpuscles), with refraction, reflection, and dispersion explained by per-corpuscle force laws and statistical aggregation across many corpuscles. The mathematical apparatus is algebraic-mechanical: corpuscular momentum, force-law deflection at interfaces, statistical distribution of corpuscle trajectories across many incidents. Newton's analysis treats light as a discrete-particle ensemble whose statistical behavior is the foundational physics; the wavefront-as-geometric-object reading of Huygens is rejected as unnecessary. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel character of the analysis is in the *particle-statistical* framing: light is a countable collection of entities whose individual behaviors aggregate to the observed phenomena, with the macroscopic optical effects (Snell's law of refraction, the inverse-square law of intensity, the geometry of image formation through lenses) recovered by force-law analysis of individual corpuscle trajectories plus statistical aggregation. This is the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel at the pre-quantum level: the algebraic-statistical reading of a physical phenomenon, without the underlying the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel geometric-propagation recognized as foundational. Newton was reading the *bad* the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel approximation — corpuscles as classical particles with deterministic trajectories — which is wrong because the corpuscles aren't classical particles. The framework's account (recoverable retrospectively from §IX.30.9): the corpuscles are the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel statistical content of head-on McGucken-Sphere collisions at detection events; Newton was approximating the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel statistical content with a classical-particle ontology, which is the wrong dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic-Channel account because the correct dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic-Channel account required the post-1925 quantum-electrodynamic apparatus.

*(P0.3) The 18th-century dominance of Newton's corpuscular theory by prestige, not empirical superiority.* Through approximately 1700–1800, Newton's corpuscular theory dominated the foundations of optics, primarily by Newton's enormous prestige following the *Principia* (1687) rather than by empirical superiority over Huygens' wave theory. Four factors contributed to the 18th-century the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel dominance: (i) the mathematical apparatus for analyzing wave behavior did not yet exist — Euler began developing differential-equation methods for wave propagation in the 1750s; Lagrange built on it in the 1780s; Fourier's analytical theory of heat (1822), which gave physicists the technique of decomposing functions into sinusoidal components, would not appear for another 60 years; without Fourier analysis, Huygens' wave reasoning was geometrically clear but analytically limited — one could draw envelopes but one could not compute diffraction patterns quantitatively; (ii) diffraction was poorly understood — Grimaldi had observed diffraction effects in 1665 but could not analyze them quantitatively, and Newton's corpuscular theory needed auxiliary hypotheses ("fits of easy reflection and easy transmission" in *Opticks* Query 17) to explain Newton's rings and other interference phenomena, a sign that the corpuscular theory was already in trouble at the periphery but the trouble was not yet decisive; (iii) Newton's prestige following the *Principia* made it sociologically expensive to propose alternatives to Newtonian optics — anyone challenging the corpuscular theory was implicitly challenging the *Principia*-era research program; (iv) the corpuscular theory had no significant predictive failures within the experimental precision available in the 18th century — refraction, reflection, dispersion through prisms, image formation through lenses, the inverse-square law of intensity were all handled adequately by Newton's force-law analysis of corpuscular trajectories. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel won the optical-foundations battle of 1700–1800 for sociological reasons (Newton's prestige) and mathematical reasons (the wave-analysis apparatus did not yet exist), not for empirical reasons. The framework's historical claim: the 18th-century the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel dominance of optics is the first historical instance of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel winning a foundational battle against the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel without the empirical record forcing the result; it is a precedent for the 20th-century the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel dominance of QM foundations after 1925, which similarly proceeded by mathematical-apparatus availability and institutional commitment rather than by empirical refutation of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel.

*(P0.4) The 1801–1820 the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel reassertion: Young, Fresnel, Poisson-Arago.* Thomas Young in 1801 [Young 1804, "Experiments and Calculations Relative to Physical Optics," *Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London* 94, 1–16; with the original double-slit demonstration in lectures of 1801–1803] performed the double-slit experiment, demonstrating unambiguous wave interference: light passing through two slits produces a pattern of bright and dark fringes that can only be explained by wavefront interference, with constructive interference at maxima and destructive interference at minima. *Augustin-Jean Fresnel in 1818 [Fresnel 1819, "Mémoire sur la diffraction de la lumière," *Mémoires de l'Académie des Sciences de l'Institut de France* 5, 339–475, awarded the Académie's Grand Prix in 1819] won the French Académie des Sciences prize for his wave-theoretic analysis of diffraction, derived from the Huygens-Fresnel principle (Huygens' secondary-wavelet envelope construction refined with phase-and-amplitude content from each wavelet). François Arago performed the experiment in 1818 and observed the bright spot exactly where Fresnel's wave theory predicted, at the position predicted by Huygens-Fresnel envelope construction with phase content. ### IX.30.G Wheeler's Smoky Dragon as the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel/the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel Distinction Made Visible

John Archibald Wheeler in 1983 (in Wheeler and Zurek, *Quantum Theory and Measurement*, Princeton University Press, Princeton, 1983, in Wheeler's essay "Law without law" reprinted in that volume, pp. 182–213) introduced the metaphor of the "great smoky dragon" to articulate what the orthodox interpretation of quantum mechanics had been struggling with for half a century. Wheeler wrote: "The mouth of the dragon is sharp, where it bites the counter. The tail of the dragon is sharp, where the photon starts. ### IX.30.H The Minkowski Reading of $x_4 = ict$ Was Algebraic, Not Geometric: Einstein 1915 Geometrized Relativity; Minkowski 1908 Algebraicized It; the McGucken Framework Completes Einstein's Geometric Program

The geometry/algebra distinction of §IX.30.A.1 illuminates a historical case that is otherwise easy to misread: the Minkowski 1908 reformulation of special relativity through the coordinate $x_4 = ict$. The standard textbook framing of Minkowski 1908 — present in every relativity textbook from Einstein-Infeld 1938 through Misner-Thorne-Wheeler 1973 through Carroll 2003 — is that Minkowski geometrized special relativity, taking Einstein's 1905 kinematic theory and recasting it as a four-dimensional geometry of spacetime. The present subsection establishes that this standard framing is wrong: **Minkowski 1908 algebraicized special relativity, not geometrized it. The genuine geometrization of relativity came with Einstein 1915 (general relativity with real Lorentzian metric). The McGucken framework's recovery of dx₄/dt = +ic as the geometric principle completes Einstein's geometric program by extending the geometric account from gravitation to all of foundational physics.**

**Theorem IX.30.H.1 (Minkowski 1908 was algebraic; Einstein 1915 was geometric).** *Under the geometry/algebra distinction of Theorem IX.30.A.1.1, the Minkowski 1908 reformulation of special relativity through the coordinate $x_4 = ict$ is algebraic rather than geometric. The Einstein 1915 general-relativistic reformulation through the real Lorentzian metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ on a real manifold is geometric. The historical confusion — standardly framed as "Minkowski geometrized relativity" — derives from the use of geometric language (light cones, Minkowski diagrams, worldlines, simultaneity surfaces) in the Minkowski 1908 reformulation, where the underlying foundations is algebraic structure dressed in geometric pedagogy.*

*Proof.* Real geometry in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel sense — what Huygens 1690 did for optics, what Riemann 1854 did for manifolds, what Einstein 1915 did for gravitation — operates on a manifold with a metric tensor whose signature carries physics. The Lorentzian metric $\eta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-c^2, +1, +1, +1)$ has indefinite signature with explicit physical meaning: the negative time-component reflects that time and space are different kinds of dimensions, causally distinguished, with light cones separating them. The signature is built into the geometry. Light cones at every event are real geometric objects with definite causal structure (the partial order $p \preceq q$ if and only if $q$ is in the future light cone of $p$). The +ic orientation along the timelike direction is geometry. The metric tensor with indefinite signature is the geometric primitive.

What Minkowski 1908 did is not this. Minkowski 1908 [Minkowski 1909, "Raum und Zeit," *Physikalische Zeitschrift* 10, 75–88, address delivered at the Naturforscher-Versammlung in Cologne in September 1908] took the indefinite signature of the Lorentzian metric and *algebraicized* it by absorbing the sign-difference into a complex coordinate. The coordinate $x_4 = ict$ makes the metric look Euclidean (positive-definite sum of squares) algebraically: $ds^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 - c^2 dt^2$, with the indefinite signature pushed into the imaginary unit on the $x_4$ coordinate. The light cones don't appear naturally in this formulation; they have to be reconstructed by tracking where $x_4$ has imaginary values that, when squared, produce the negative timelike contribution to $ds^2$. The causal structure isn't visible in the coordinate system; it has to be reconstructed algebraically by tracking the sign of $ds^2$ for different displacements.

the position-of-i diagnosis of §IX.13.14 (Diagnosis P.1.4.A of the Preface): when the imaginary unit is on the *outside* of the coordinate ($x_4 = ict$, with $i$ exterior to the real coordinate $t$), the apparatus has algebra masquerading as geometry. The Lorentzian signature is genuine geometry (a feature of the real metric tensor on the real manifold); absorbing it into $x_4 = ict$ is the *algebraic encoding* of the geometry, not the geometry itself. The Minkowski 1908 reformulation is therefore the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel in the framework's sense: an algebraic encoding of geometry with the geometry compressed into a complex coordinate.

The contrast with Einstein 1915 [Einstein 1915, "Die Feldgleichungen der Gravitation," *Sitzungsberichte der Königlich Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Berlin*, 844–847; and Einstein 1916, "Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie," *Annalen der Physik* 49, 769–822] is illuminating. General relativity uses the real Lorentzian metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ explicitly. The metric is a tensor field on a real manifold; light cones at every event are real geometric objects (the null vectors of $g_{\mu\nu}$ at each event); the Bianchi identity, the Riemann curvature tensor, the geodesic equation, and the Einstein field equations all operate on the real geometry with the indefinite signature treated as a geometric feature, not absorbed into an algebraic coordinate. Einstein deliberately did *not* use $x_4 = ict$ in GR. He used the real metric with explicit indefinite signature because the geometry was important to his reading. Einstein regretted the $x_4 = ict$ notation he had briefly used in his 1905 work; by 1915 he was committed to the real Lorentzian metric and the geometric account.

Hermann Weyl [Weyl 1918, *Raum, Zeit, Materie*, Springer; English edition Weyl 1922, *Space, Time, Matter*, Methuen], Élie Cartan [Cartan 1922, "Sur les variétés à connexion affine et la théorie de la relativité généralisée," *Annales scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure* 40, 325–412; and Cartan 1923–1925 series of papers on differential geometry of Lie groups], and the broader differential-geometry tradition (Riemann 1854, Ricci 1888, Levi-Civita 1916, Schouten 1924, Whitney 1936) developed the apparatus of pseudo-Riemannian geometry with indefinite metrics because the geometry of the indefinite signature is important. The Minkowski $x_4 = ict$ formulation obscures this by absorbing it into algebra, and the pseudo-Riemannian-geometry tradition deliberately rejected the Minkowski formulation in favor of the real-metric formulation. Weyl 1918 explicitly criticizes the Minkowski formulation as obscuring the geometry; Cartan 1922 develops the differential-geometric apparatus that became the framework for GR without any use of the imaginary coordinate.

The reading: **Minkowski 1908 made special relativity more algebraic, not more geometric, despite the standard textbook framing.** The Minkowski diagrams that look geometric — light cones drawn on a sheet of paper with worldlines and simultaneity surfaces — are pedagogical illustrations of the algebraic structure of Lorentz transformations, not geometry. They depict the algebraic structure in a visualizable way, but the underlying foundations of Minkowski's formulation is algebraic: the Lorentz transformations as an abstract group, the four-dimensional rotational structure with $i$ absorbing the signature, the invariant interval as an algebraic identity rather than a geometric quantity. The visualizations are useful — physicists love Minkowski diagrams because they make the algebraic structure of Lorentz transformations easy to think about. But the visualizations are not the foundations. They are pedagogical projections of the algebraic structure onto a Euclidean drawing surface. The foundations is the algebraic structure of the Lorentz group acting on four-dimensional coordinates with $x_4 = ict$. ∎

**Remark IX.30.H.2 (The standard textbook framing is wrong, and the McGucken framework's account corrects it).** *The standard textbook framing "Minkowski geometrized relativity" appears in every relativity textbook from the early twentieth century to the present. **Theorem IX.30.H.3 (The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = +ic completes Einstein's 1915 geometric program).** *The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = +ic and the Minkowski coordinate $x_4 = ict$ stand in the same relation as Einstein's 1915 real Lorentzian metric stands to Minkowski's 1908 imaginary-coordinate algebraic encoding. *Proof.* The Minkowski 1908 reading of $x_4 = ict$ takes the imaginary unit $i$ as a sign-encoding device for the Lorentzian signature: $i$ is exterior to the real coordinate $t$, and its appearance in the algebraic identity $x_4 = ict$ encodes the negative timelike component of the metric without supplying any geometry beyond the algebraic encoding itself. Under the position-of-i diagnosis (§IX.13.14, Diagnosis P.1.4.A), this is the *algebraic* role of $i$: $i$ is doing the work of distinguishing the timelike direction from the spatial directions at the algebraic-coordinate identity, with no geometry of $i$ as a feature of the manifold itself.

The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = +ic gives $i$ a different role. Under the framework's account, $i$ is the perpendicularity marker showing that $x_4$ is perpendicular to the spatial slice at every event of $\mathcal M_G$ (the Frobenius involutivity content of §XI), with the +ic orientation being the geometry of the active expansion direction. Minkowski 1908 reached the algebraic shadow without the geometric principle behind it; the McGucken framework recovers the geometric principle and identifies $x_4 = ict$ as its integrated coordinate label.

**Remark IX.30.H.4 (Einstein's resistance to Minkowski's algebraicization and his ultimate adoption of pseudo-Riemannian geometry).** *Einstein's historical relationship to Minkowski 1908 is itself revealing. ### IX.30.I Dynamics in Each Channel: Algebraic Time as Parameter (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel) versus Geometric Time as Coordinate (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel)

The geometry/algebra distinction of §IX.30.A.1 and the Minkowski-Einstein historical analysis of §IX.30.H illuminate a further question that is foundational for understanding the dual-channel architecture: *where does dynamics appear in each channel?* The present subsection answers the question explicitly. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's dynamics is algebraic: time is a parameter indexing a one-parameter unitary group of automorphisms of the operator algebra, with Stone's theorem supplying the generator (the Hamiltonian). The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's dynamics is geometric: $x_4$ is the physical fourth coordinate of the spacetime manifold $\mathcal M_G$ actively expanding at velocity $ic$ via the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$, with $t$ as the clock-readout of that expansion by physical timekeepers (photon clocks, atomic clocks, mechanical clocks) that are themselves $x_4$-riders. The McGucken Sphere is a real geometric object propagating outward at velocity $c$ along the $+ic$-oriented direction as $x_4$ expands. The two dynamics agree on the time-evolution statistics that detectors register because the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is set up to encode the statistics of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometry, but the dynamics are *different kinds of objects*: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's dynamics is a path through unitary-operator space; the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's dynamics is an active $x_4$-expansion in real spacetime registered by physical clock-readouts. The distinction is the dynamic analog of the geometry/algebra distinction itself, with $t$ as abstract algebra parameter versus $x_4$ as actively expanding physical coordinate whose expansion clocks measure being the dynamic version of the two halves of mathematics applied to foundational physics.

**Theorem IX.30.I.1 (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel dynamics: time as parameter indexing a one-parameter automorphism group of the algebra).** *In the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic framework, dynamics enters as a one-parameter group of automorphisms of the operator algebra. Stone's theorem (Stone 1932, "On One-Parameter Unitary Groups in Hilbert Space," Annals of Mathematics 33, 643–648) establishes that every strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group $U(t)$ acting on a Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ is generated by a unique (up to a constant) self-adjoint operator $\hat H$ via $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/\hbar)$. The Hamiltonian $\hat H$ is the generator of time-translation; the parameter $t$ flows as a real-valued label that indexes the family of unitary automorphisms; the unitary group law $U(t_1) \cdot U(t_2) = U(t_1 + t_2)$ is the algebraic statement of time-translation composition. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's dynamics is therefore purely algebraic: time is a parameter, not a coordinate; the Hilbert space does not move through time; the operators do not propagate through anything; nothing geometric happens.*

*Proof.* Stone's theorem is a theorem of functional analysis: the bijective correspondence between strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups and self-adjoint operators is established without geometric input. The unitary group $U(t)$ is a one-parameter family of bounded linear operators on $\mathcal H$ satisfying $U(0) = \mathbb 1$, $U(t_1) U(t_2) = U(t_1 + t_2)$, and strong continuity in $t$. The generator $\hat H$ is the limit $\hat H = -i\hbar \lim_{t \to 0} [U(t) - \mathbb 1]/t$ taken in the strong operator topology on the dense domain $D(\hat H) \subseteq \mathcal H$. The Schrödinger equation $i\hbar \partial_t |\psi(t)\rangle = \hat H |\psi(t)\rangle$ is the differential form of $|\psi(t)\rangle = U(t) |\psi(0)\rangle$; the equation states how the state vector $|\psi\rangle$ rotates in Hilbert space as the parameter $t$ flows. No motion in any physical space, no propagation of any physical entity, no geometry — only algebraic conjugation by a unitary operator parametrized by a real number.

The Heisenberg picture makes the algebraic character of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel dynamics even more transparent. In the Heisenberg picture, the state vector $|\psi\rangle$ is fixed and observables evolve via $\hat O(t) = U(t)^\dagger \hat O U(t)$. Time-evolution is now visibly an automorphism of the operator algebra — at each value of $t$, you have a new operator $\hat O(t)$ obtained from $\hat O$ by algebraic conjugation. The dynamics is the one-parameter family of automorphisms $\sigma_t : \hat O \mapsto U(t)^\dagger \hat O U(t)$ of the operator algebra $B(\mathcal H)$, with the parameter $t$ indexing the family. The Stone-von Neumann uniqueness theorem (Stone 1931, von Neumann 1931) establishes that the Heisenberg and Schrödinger pictures are unitarily equivalent — they describe the same one-parameter algebraic automorphism group, with the conjugation applied to operators (Heisenberg) or to state vectors (Schrödinger). Both pictures are paradigmatic the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel dynamics: algebraic time-evolution, with $t$ as a parameter and no geometry. ∎

**Theorem IX.30.I.2 (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel dynamics: $x_4$ as the actively expanding physical fourth coordinate of $\mathcal M_G$, with $t$ as clock-readout of that expansion and the McGucken Sphere expanding at +ic at every event).** *In the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometric framework, dynamics enters as the active +ic-oriented $x_4$-expansion at every event of spacetime, with the McGucken Sphere as the wavefront generated by that expansion and $t$ as the operational readout of that expansion by physical clocks. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = +ic IS the dynamic principle of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel: it states that the fourth coordinate $x_4$ expands at velocity $ic$, with the differential $dt$ being a physical clock-tick and $t$ being what physical timekeepers read — timekeepers that are themselves $x_4$-riders whose ticks are manifestations of $x_4$'s expansion (photon clocks whose photon momenergy surfs the expansion at velocity $c$; atomic clocks whose transition frequencies are Compton-clock beats between $mc^2$ and $\hbar$; mechanical and biological clocks whose oscillator periods are set by processes riding the expansion). The +ic orientation distinguishes forward expansion from time-reversed retreat. The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p, t - t_p) = \{(\mathbf x, t) \in \mathbb R^3 \times \mathbb R : \|\mathbf x - \mathbf x_p\| = c(t - t_p), t \geq t_p\}$ at clock-reading difference $t - t_p$ from source event $p$ is the real geometry that propagates through real four-dimensional spacetime as $x_4$ expands, with the propagation registered at any spatial detector by that detector's own clock. The retarded Green's function $G_R(t - t', \mathbf x - \mathbf x') = \theta(t - t')[\delta(\|\mathbf x - \mathbf x'\| - c(t - t'))]/(4\pi \|\mathbf x - \mathbf x'\|)$ supplies the explicit geometric propagation kernel along the +ic-oriented null cone. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's dynamics is therefore purely geometric: $x_4$ is the actively expanding physical fourth coordinate of the spacetime manifold, clocks are physical $x_4$-riders that read the expansion as $t$, and the Sphere is a real geometric object propagating outward at velocity $c$, with (radius, area, Compton phase, +ic orientation) at every clock-reading of its propagation.*

*Proof.* The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = +ic, integrated with origin $x_4(0) = 0$, gives the coordinate identification $x_4 = ict$ (Step 1 of Theorem XI.5, Definition IX.18.2). The integrated coordinate label, with $i$ appearing as the residue of the geometric perpendicularity-and-orientation content of the principle, defines the timelike direction of the McGucken manifold $\mathcal M_G$. The active expansion at velocity $c$ in the +ic-oriented direction at every event of $\mathcal M_G$ produces the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_M^+(p)$ as the propagating wavefront generated at event $p$ (Definition IX.19.1, after [7]). The Sphere is a real geometric primitive: a 2-sphere with definite radius $c(t - t_p)$, definite area $4\pi c^2 (t - t_p)^2$, definite surface curvature $K = 1/[c(t-t_p)]^2$, definite Compton phase content $\Phi(q; p) = \exp(-i\omega_C \Delta\tau(q; p))$ uniform across the spatial slice, and definite +ic orientation at every value of $t > t_p$.

The Huygens-iterated wavefront construction (Theorem IX.19.4, Reciprocal Generation Property) is the geometric dynamics of the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel made explicit: every point of the wavefront at parameter $t$ generates a secondary McGucken Sphere with origin at that point, and the wavefront at parameter $t + \delta t$ is the envelope of all secondary Spheres. This is the explicit geometric propagation rule: real Spheres at real spacetime events, expanding outward at velocity $c$, with the next instant's wavefront constructed by geometric envelope of the secondary Spheres. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's dynamics is therefore geometric time-evolution: real wavefronts moving through real space with at every event, with $t$ as a coordinate of the spacetime manifold and the dynamics being the active +ic-oriented expansion at every event. ∎

**Theorem IX.30.I.3 (The dual-channel dynamics distinction: algebraic $t$ as abstract parameter versus geometric $x_4$-expansion registered by physical clock-readouts).** *The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's dynamics is algebraic: $t$ is a parameter indexing a one-parameter group of algebra automorphisms, with no coordinate role, no physical space, and no clock mechanism behind it. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's dynamics is geometric: $x_4$ is the physical fourth coordinate of the spacetime manifold $\mathcal M_G$ actively expanding at velocity $ic$ via dx₄/dt = +ic, with $t$ as the clock-readout of that expansion by physical timekeepers that are themselves $x_4$-riders, and the McGucken Sphere as the wavefront propagating as $x_4$ expands. **Remark IX.30.I.4 (The Schrödinger equation as the algebraic shadow of the Sphere's geometric propagation).** *The Schrödinger equation $i\hbar \partial_t |\psi(t)\rangle = \hat H |\psi(t)\rangle$ has been treated by orthodox QM as the dynamic equation of quantum mechanics, with $|\psi(t)\rangle$ as the state and $\hat H$ as the dynamic generator. **Remark IX.30.I.5 (The Hamilton and Lagrange formulations as algebraic dynamics dressed in geometric language).** *Classical mechanics in its Hamilton and Lagrange formulations is the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel despite the appearance of geometric language. The Hamiltonian formulation uses phase space as a symplectic manifold, the Hamiltonian as a function on phase space, time-evolution as the flow generated by the Hamiltonian vector field, and the Hamilton equations $\dot q = \partial H/\partial p$, $\dot p = -\partial H/\partial q$ as the dynamics. Phase space looks geometric: it has coordinates $(q, p)$, a symplectic form $\omega = \sum_i dq_i \wedge dp_i$, Hamiltonian flows, and Poisson brackets. But phase space is an algebraic structure dressed in geometric language. The foundations of the Hamiltonian formulation is the Poisson algebra of observables on phase space (a $C^*$-algebra in the classical limit), with the symplectic form being the algebraic structure that determines the Poisson bracket and the Hamiltonian flow being the algebraic time-evolution of observables under the Hamiltonian's Poisson bracket with them. Phase space is the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel pretending to be the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel: algebraic structure with geometric pedagogy.*

Configuration space is a manifold; the Lagrangian is a function on the tangent bundle; the equations of motion are the Euler-Lagrange equations derived by variational analysis. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel character of the Lagrangian formulation is in the *variational* framing: time-evolution as the path through configuration space that extremizes a functional, with the dynamics determined by an algebraic-variational condition rather than by geometric propagation of a physical entity through spacetime. Einstein deliberately chose the geometric formulation of GR over algebraic alternatives because the geometry was important to his reading. The McGucken framework's recovery of dx₄/dt = +ic as the geometric dynamic principle of QM extends Einstein's geometric program from gravitation to all of foundational physics; the McGucken Sphere is the geometric primitive whose propagation through spacetime is the dynamics, with the Hamiltonian formulation of classical mechanics and the Schrödinger formulation of QM being recovered as the algebraic shadows of the geometric dynamics.*

**Theorem IX.30.I.7 (The historical pattern of dynamics from Huygens 1690 to the present, under the geometry/algebra distinction).** *Under the geometry/algebra distinction of §IX.30.A.1 and the dynamics analysis of §§IX.30.I.1–IX.30.I.3, the historical record of foundational physics from Huygens 1690 to the present exhibits a pattern in which the dynamics has alternated between geometric and algebraic foundations, with the McGucken framework's recovery of dx₄/dt = +ic as the geometric dynamic principle completing a program that has been institutionally fragmented across the geometric (GR, classical wave optics, statistical-mechanical Stosszahlansatz) and algebraic (Hamilton's classical mechanics, QM, QED, QFT, Standard Model, AdS/CFT) traditions of foundational physics for the past 333 years.*

**Remark IX.30.I.8 (The Heisenberg-Schrödinger picture equivalence as a feature of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel algebra).** *The orthodox Heisenberg-Schrödinger picture equivalence (Stone-von Neumann uniqueness theorem 1931) is now illuminating under the geometry/algebra and dynamics distinctions.
