## XI.5 The Poincaré–Minkowski Thought Experiment: The Question That Took a Century to Complete

The history of §§XI.3–XI.4 admits a sharp consolidation in the form of a thought experiment that brings the entire missed opportunity of twentieth-century foundational physics into focus. The experiment, due in this form to [22], proceeds as a dialogue with Henri Poincaré in 1905 or Hermann Minkowski in 1908, immediately following their introductions of the Lorentzian-spacetime metric with x₄ = ict.

*"In the spacetime metric you have just introduced, with x₄ = ict (the integrated shadow of dx₄/dt = ic), suppose we Lorentz-boost a ruler — rotate it through some angle in the $(t, x)$ plane via a hyperbolic rotation. Does this not produce length contraction in the three spatial dimensions, and a change of the ruler's velocity in 3-space?"*

The answer of Poincaré or Minkowski is immediate and confident: *"Yes, of course. That is exactly what Lorentz transformations are. A hyperbolic rotation through rapidity $\eta$ in the $(t, x)$ plane produces length contraction by factor $\cosh\eta = \gamma$ and a velocity change in 3-space. This is the entire textbook content of special relativity."*

*"Then does that not mean that the fourth dimension x₄ is a real direction along which things can be re-oriented? That x₄ is a geometric axis with respect to which a ruler can be rotated, not merely a label, having its extent and velocity re-distributed between x₄ and the spatial dimensions? And if x₄ is a real direction along which the ruler is re-oriented, must not the ruler have an *extent* along x₄, and a *velocity* along x₄? And if the ruler has a velocity along x₄, what *is* that velocity?"*

This is where Poincaré and Minkowski go silent. For one hundred and twenty years.

**Remark XI.10 (the anatomy of the century of silence).** The silence is a artefact of three conceptual blocks that congealed simultaneously around the 1905–1908 emergence of relativity. The Poincaré–Minkowski machinery treats x₄ exactly as a direction: the hyperbolic rotation re-distributes the ruler's four-velocity between the x₄ component and the spatial components. A ruler at spatial rest has its full four-velocity budget allocated to x₄-advance (configuration 1 of the four-fold ontology). A ruler in motion has some of that budget diverted from x₄ into the spatial axes (intermediate configurations, with the photon at configuration 2 having zero x₄-advance and full spatial velocity). The hyperbolic rotation *is* a re-distribution of motion between x₄ and the spatial axes, which means x₄ is a direction along which things move, which means x₄ has a rate of change, which means dx₄/dt is a well-defined quantity, which means the question *"what is dx₄/dt?"* is the obvious next question — the one Poincaré and Minkowski had themselves set up but did not ask.

**Theorem XI.11 (the answer to the question).** *The answer to the question Poincaré and Minkowski posed in 1905–1908 and did not complete is:*
$$\frac{dx_{4}}{dt} \;=\; ic.$$
*The rate of x₄-advance is c, marked by i because x₄ is perpendicular to the spatial axes. The McGucken Principle is therefore not a foreign import into the relativistic tradition; it is the completion of the question Poincaré and Minkowski posed but did not finish — the third step after their first step (the Lorentzian metric) and their second step (the four-dimensional geometric account), made askable only after a century of conceptual development cleared the blocks that had stopped them.*

*Proof.* The answer is established by three. (1) The rate of x₄-advance is $c$: this is forced by the four-velocity budget $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ (Lemma IX.23.4) combined with the spatial-rest configuration of the four-fold ontology (configuration 1: massive particle at spatial rest has full $c$-budget allocated to $x_4$-advance). The rate is therefore $c$, not some other value. (2) The rate is marked by $i$ because $x_4$ is perpendicular to the spatial three-slice: by the Frobenius theorem (Theorem XI.3), the perpendicular axis has algebraic generator $i \in \mathbb C$. The signed rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ encodes both the perpendicularity (the $i$) and the magnitude (the $c$). (3) The principle is the completion of the Poincaré-Minkowski question: their machinery established the Lorentzian metric (1905) and the four-dimensional geometric account (1908) but stopped short of asking what the rate of $x_4$-advance is. By Remark XI.10, the next obvious question was blocked by the three conceptual blocks of Remark XI.12 (block-universe reading, formalist reading of $i$, disciplinary expectation of static spacetime). The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is the third step that the Poincaré-Minkowski tradition had implicitly set up but did not complete. ∎

**Remark XI.12 (the three conceptual blocks).** The three conceptual blocks that prevented Poincaré, Minkowski, and the subsequent twentieth-century tradition from asking the question are catalogued in [70]:

*Block 1: The block-universe reading.* Spacetime is a static four-dimensional manifold; coordinates do not have rates of change. This account congealed around the new relativity, partly under Poincaré's own conventionalist influence and Minkowski's geometric account, and dominated the textbook tradition from 1916 through the present. Within the block-universe reading, dx₄/dt is a category error — coordinates are static labels, not dynamical quantities. The block-universe reading therefore makes the obvious next question unaskable.

*Block 2: The formalist reading of i.* The imaginary unit is a useful algebraic device without geometry. This account is the standard mathematical interpretation since Cauchy's 1820s rigorisation of complex analysis. Under the formalist reading, the i in x₄ = ict has no geometry — it is merely the algebraic mark that converts $dt^{2}$ to $-c^{2}dt^{2}$ on substitution, without committing to any claim about the physical character of x₄. The formalist reading therefore decouples the i from any statement about x₄, making the perpendicularity-marker reading unavailable.

*Block 3: The disciplinary expectation that "spacetime" is a finished manifold.* The disciplinary commitment that spacetime is a finished four-dimensional manifold, rather than an active geometric process, discouraged asking what the manifold's own dynamics might be. Within this commitment, the question *"what is the dynamics of spacetime itself?"* is treated as inaccessible or as belonging to quantum gravity; the dynamics of the four-coordinate manifold is not a topic of classical physics. The disciplinary commitment therefore makes the active-expansion account of x₄ invisible to the classical tradition.

All three blocks had to fail simultaneously for the obvious next question to become askable. They failed simultaneously at Princeton in 1989–1990 in the lineage of John Archibald Wheeler, with the principle dx₄/dt = ic as the answer ([70]; [14]; [67]). The active-expansion account of x₄, which Poincaré and Minkowski's machinery had implicitly set up in 1905–1908, became foundationally available only after the three blocks were cleared by a century of conceptual development.

**Remark XI.13 (the account of the century).** The hundred-year silence is therefore not a failure of attention or imagination but a consequence of the three conceptual blocks that obstructed the obvious next question. The i in x₄ = ict has been a flag since 1905 — announcing, in every foundational equation in which it has appeared (the Lorentz signature, the Schrödinger evolution, the canonical commutator, the path-integral weight, the $+i\varepsilon$ prescription, the Dirac equation, the $U(1)$ gauge phase, the CFT torus modular parameter, the Bloch-sphere relative phase, the spinor double covering, the Wick substitution, the Minkowski–Euclidean action bridge), that there exists a fourth dimension perpendicular to ordinary 3-space, expanding at rate c, carrying action ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation. The orthodox tradition has seen the flag and called it formal. The McGucken Principle is the first statement to hear what the flag has been saying for one hundred and twenty years: *every theorem traces to the active expansion; the coordinate label x₄ = ict is its mere integrated shadow; and every i in physics is the algebraic announcement of the active expansion at one perpendicular axis.*

## XI.6 The McGucken-Cogenerative Stone–von Neumann Uniqueness: Promotion from Inherited 1931 Result to Corollary of the Four-Step Cogeneration Cascade

The Stone–von Neumann uniqueness theorem (Stone 1932 [Stone 1932]; von Neumann 1931 [von Neumann 1932]) states that the Weyl-form irreducible unitary representation of the canonical commutation relation $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ on a complex separable Hilbert space is unique up to unitary equivalence, and that the unique representation is the Schrödinger representation $\hat q\psi(q) = q\psi(q)$, $\hat p\psi(q) = -i\hbar\partial_{q}\psi(q)$ on $L^{2}(\mathbb R, dq)$. The theorem has historically been read as an external classification theorem applied to the postulated structure of quantum mechanics: given the canonical commutator and the Hilbert space as axioms, the Schrödinger representation is unique. The status of Stone–von Neumann uniqueness in the Abstract's the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel list has been correspondingly described as Tier 2 — the McGucken framework supplies the McGucken-internal physical instance (the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ overdetermined by the dual-route Theorem IX.23.14, the Hilbert space cogenerated by Theorem XI.5, the Schrödinger representation constructed directly via Propositions H.1–H.4 of §II.1), but the uniqueness statement itself has been treated as inherited from the von Neumann 1931 classification.

The present subsection promotes Stone–von Neumann uniqueness from Tier 2 (inherited uniqueness statement) to Tier 1 (corollary of the four-step McGucken cogeneration cascade). The key observation: the McGucken framework does not invoke Stone–von Neumann uniqueness to *assert* that the Schrödinger representation is unique — it *constructs* the Schrödinger representation directly via the four-step cogeneration cascade (Theorem XI.5) and *derives* the canonical commutator on this constructed representation via the dual-route argument (Theorem IX.23.14). Uniqueness then follows as a corollary of the constructive uniqueness of the cogeneration cascade itself, not as an external classification theorem. I now develop this.

**Theorem XI.6.1 (McGucken-Cogenerative Stone–von Neumann Uniqueness, after [70] together with the four-step cogeneration cascade of Theorem XI.5).** *Let $\mathcal H$ denote the McGucken-cogenerated Hilbert space established at Theorem XI.5 — the complete complex inner-product space $\mathcal H \cong L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}, d^{3}\mathbf x)$ obtained as the Cauchy completion of the pre-Hilbert space of square-integrable complex amplitudes on the spatial three-slice of $\mathcal M_{G}$, with the four-step cogeneration cascade*
$$dx_{4}/dt = ic \;\to\; \mathcal M_{G} \;\to\; M_{1,3} \;\to\; (\mathcal V, \text{rank-2 sesquilinear pairing on } \mathbb C \text{ amplitudes}) \;\to\; \mathcal H$$

Let $\hat q_{j}, \hat p_{k}$ for $j, k \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ denote the position and momentum operators on $\mathcal H$ constructed directly via the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel route of Propositions H.1–H.5 of §II.1, satisfying the canonical commutation relations $[\hat q_{j}, \hat p_{k}] = i\hbar\,\delta_{jk}$ established at Step 4 of the Hamiltonian route. The uniqueness is established by direct construction of the unitary intertwiner, not by invocation of the inherited 1931 classification theorem.*

*Proof.* The proof has four steps, each grounded in McGucken framework already established.

**Step 1 (Existence — direct construction of $\pi_{\text{McG}}$).** By Theorem XI.5 Step 4, the McGucken-cogenerated Hilbert space is $\mathcal H \cong L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}, d^{3}\mathbf x)$, with inner product $\langle \varphi, \psi\rangle = \int_{\mathbb R^{3}} \varphi^{*}(\mathbf x)\psi(\mathbf x)\, d^{3}\mathbf x$. # XII. The Linear–Rotational Duality of the Principle Itself
*(McGucken Duality framing for the Principle-itself level.)* The linear–rotational duality of dx₄/dt = ic developed in this section operates at the **Principle level** of the McGucken Duality — celebrating dx₄/dt = ic's **The McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel** face (the linear-change content dx₄/dt as the algebraic-derivative articulation) and dx₄/dt = ic's **The McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel** face (the rotation content ic as multiplication by i = rotation by $\pi/2$ in ℂ, the geometric-perpendicularity articulation). The equation dx₄/dt = ic admits a reading that has not, to the present author's knowledge, been articulated in the prior literature: it is a statement of duality between linear change and rotation, written in a single line.

## XII.1 The Two Sides of the Principle

The left-hand side dx₄/dt is a *linear rate of change*: the derivative of the fourth-dimension coordinate with respect to time. The right-hand side ic is a *rotation*: multiplication by i is, in ℂ, rotation by $\pi/2$, and c is the magnitude. The equation equates a linear rate with a rotation. The linear-rotational duality is the equation's literal content.

## XII.2 Spin Is Forced

**Proposition XII.1 (spin is forced by the principle).** *Every quantum object advancing in x₄ carries a rotational degree of freedom whose half-integer or integer character is determined by the algebra of i in the relevant spinor or tensor representation.*

*Proof.* The advance dx₄/dt = ic generates, via the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's representation-theoretic side, the unitary one-parameter group $\{U(t) = e^{-iHt/\hbar}\}$ acting on the Hilbert space of states. The state space carries representations of the spin group $\text{Spin}(1, 3) \cong SL(2, \mathbb C)$. The two fundamental representations are spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ (Weyl spinors, transforming by i as i² = −1 — a π rotation in spinor space corresponds to a $2\pi$ rotation in spacetime, so a full $2\pi$ rotation in spacetime acts as $-1$ on the spinor, and a $4\pi$ rotation acts as $+1$); spin-$1$ (four-vectors, transforming by $i^{4} = 1$); spin-$0$ (scalars, no transformation). The half-integer/integer split is forced by the algebra of $i^{n}$ for $n = 1, 2, 3, 4$ in the relevant representation. ∎

**Corollary XII.2.** *The photon's two-state polarization is forced by the null-worldline character of the photon's x₄-rest condition (item (2) of the four-fold ontology): on the null hypersurface, only two transverse polarization directions exist.*

The two remaining polarization directions are transverse to the propagation direction $\mathbf k$, lying in the spatial plane perpendicular to $\mathbf k$. The two-state polarization is therefore forced by the photon's null worldline; the photon has helicity $\pm 1$ corresponding to the two transverse polarization eigenstates of circular polarization. ∎

**Corollary XII.3.** *The Higgs field's spin-$0$ character is forced by the geometric account of "alignment with the direction of x₄-advance" as opposed to "rotation in x₄".*

*Proof.* The Higgs field $\phi$ is a Lorentz scalar: $\phi$ transforms under Lorentz transformations $\Lambda \in \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$, i.e., $\phi(x) \to \phi(\Lambda^{-1} x)$. Spin-1 corresponds to full-cycle rotation (the photon's polarization vector under spatial rotations). The Higgs field's spin-0 character is therefore "alignment with the direction of x₄-advance" (no rotation perpendicular to propagation) as opposed to "rotation in x₄" (Dirac fermions, gauge bosons). The linear-rotational duality is *visible* in the equation dx₄/dt = ic the moment one reads i as a rotation generator rather than as an opaque algebraic symbol. # XIII. The Genealogy of the Static-Coordinate Reading: Why Nobody Saw It
*(McGucken Duality framing for the genealogy.)* The genealogy of the static-coordinate reading developed in this section traces the historical mechanism by which the **The McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel** face of dx₄/dt = ic was suppressed across the 20th century in favor of the **The McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel** algebraic-coordinate reading — from Minkowski 1908 through Pauli 1921, Sommerfeld, Weyl, the Copenhagen tradition, MTW 1973 (the textbook banishment of x₄ = ict), and the algebraic-axiomatic QFT tradition of Wightman, Haag–Kastler, and Connes. The McGucken Duality is the completion that recognises both channels as foundationally equiprimitive faces of dx₄/dt = ic.

I now address the historical question: given that the McGucken Principle's mathematics has been visible in x₄ = ict since Minkowski 1908, why did the physics community not state dx₄/dt = ic as a principle during the century 1908–2008? The answer is a combination of four conceptual blocks plus one historical contingency. I address the historical contingency in this section and the four conceptual blocks in §XIV.

## XIII.1 Minkowski 1908: The Coordinate Convention

Minkowski's 1908 Cologne address introduced four-dimensional spacetime with the convention x₄ = ict. The convention served a *technical* purpose: with the imaginary fourth coordinate, the Lorentz transformations became Euclidean rotations, and the Lorentz invariant $-c^{2}t^{2} + x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}$ became the positive-definite norm $x_{1}^{2} + x_{2}^{2} + x_{3}^{2} + x_{4}^{2}$. This was a *coordinate reading*: x₄ was a *static* fourth coordinate, useful for calculational simplification.

The active-expansion account dx₄/dt = ic — that the fourth dimension is *spherically expanding* at the velocity of light *from every spacetime event* — was not what Minkowski stated. Minkowski's x₄ = ict is the integrated coordinate shadow of dx₄/dt = ic; Minkowski did not state the dynamics. The reason was twofold: (i) Minkowski died in 1909, before the implications of his framework could be developed; (ii) Minkowski's purpose was the *geometric simplification* of special relativity, not the *dynamical reading* of x₄ as an actively expanding spherical wavefront.

## XIII.2 Pauli 1921 and the Textbook Tradition

Pauli's *Theory of Relativity* [Pauli 1921] adopted the Minkowski convention with x₄ = ict and propagated it through the textbook tradition for half a century. Pauli's encyclopedia article was the standard reference; subsequent textbooks (Sommerfeld, Weyl, von Laue, Tolman) inherited the coordinate reading. Pauli stated the convention as a *useful formal device*. The active-expansion account was not stated.

By the 1960s, the signature-$(+, -, -, -)$ convention with real time displaced the $ict$ convention in the textbook tradition; the coordinate x₄ = ict disappeared as a object and survived only as a Wick-rotation device in path-integral computation. With the coordinate having faded, the dynamical reading dx₄/dt = ic had no surface from which to be articulated.

## XIII.2.A Misner–Thorne–Wheeler 1973: The Explicit Textbook Execution of x₄ = ict in *Gravitation*

The decisive textbook moment at which x₄ = ict was *explicitly executed* from the standard physics curriculum is Box 2.1 of Misner, Thorne, and Wheeler's 1973 monograph *Gravitation*, the canonical graduate textbook of general relativity for the half-century from 1973 to the present. The Box is titled, with rhetorical finality, ***"Farewell to 'ict'."*** Its argument is important enough to reproduce in summary:

> *"One sometime participant in special relativity will have to be put to the sword: '$x^{4} = ict$.' This imaginary coordinate was invented to make the geometry of spacetime look formally as little different as possible from the geometry of Euclidean space; to make a Lorentz transformation look on paper like a rotation; and to spare one the distinction that one otherwise is forced to make between quantities with upper indices (such as the components $p^{\mu}$ of the energy-momentum vector) and quantities with lower indices (such as the components of the energy-momentum 1-form). However, it is no kindness to be spared this latter distinction. Without it, one cannot know whether a vector is meant or the very different geometric object that is a 1-form. If in a region where spacetime is flat, one can hide this from view by writing $(\Delta s)^{2} = (\Delta x^{1})^{2} + (\Delta x^{2})^{2} + (\Delta x^{3})^{2} + (\Delta x^{4})^{2}$, with $x^{4} = ict$, no one has discovered a way to make an imaginary coordinate work in the general curved spacetime manifold. If 'x₄ = ict' cannot be used there, it will not be used here. In this chapter and hereafter, as throughout the literature of general relativity, a real time coordinate is used, $x^{0} = t = ct_{\text{conv}}$ (superscript 0 rather than 4 to avoid any possibility of confusion with the imaginary time coordinate)."*
> — Misner, Thorne, and Wheeler, *Gravitation* [Misner-Thorne-Wheeler1973], Box 2.1, p. 51.

The verbatim quote above contains x₄ = ict written down by Minkowski, Sommerfeld, Pauli, and the entire generation of textbooks that taught it through the 1960s. The McGucken framework reads MTW's banishment as the moment the integrated shadow x₄ = ict was severed from its dynamics dx₄/dt = ic, with the cost being the 117-year delay before the active-expansion account was articulated. This Box is the **smoking-gun document** of the textbook-tradition concealment of the McGucken framework. It is important for the genealogy of §XIII for the following reasons.

**First**, MTW *explicitly identify* the feature that the McGucken framework would later show is the physical principle of the universe — the imaginary unit i in x₄ = ict, and then *explicitly execute it* from the standard physics curriculum. **Second**, MTW's *grounds* for the elimination are decisive for the historical contingency of §XIII.5. ## XIII.3 The Penrose Convention and the Wightman Axiomatization

The signature-$(+, -, -, -)$ convention with real time, propagated by Penrose [Penrose 2010] and adopted by the Wightman axiomatic field theory [Wightman 1956, Streater-Wightman 1964], became standard after the 1960s. In this convention, time is a real coordinate; i appears only in the imaginary-unit normalization of the canonical commutation relation and in the Wick rotation. The i in $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ became a formal algebraic feature; the i in the Wick rotation became a formal computational device. *Neither was read as the integrated shadow of an active spherical expansion.*

## XIII.4 The Kaluza-Klein Detour

Kaluza 1921 [Kaluza 1921] and Klein 1926 [Klein 1926] proposed a fifth dimension to unify electromagnetism with gravity, with the fifth dimension *compact* (Klein) and *spatial*. The Kaluza-Klein tradition explored extra dimensions of *spatial* character, not extra-temporal-active-expansion character. The McGucken Principle is orthogonal: the "fourth dimension" of dx₄/dt = ic is the *imaginary, actively expanding, temporally oriented* dimension already present in Minkowski's x₄, read *dynamically*. Kaluza-Klein's detour into compact spatial dimensions further obscured the dynamical reading of the original Minkowski fourth dimension [50].

## XIII.5 The Historical Contingency

The historical contingency, then, is the combination of: (i) Minkowski's death in 1909 cutting short the development of his framework; (ii) Pauli's coordinate-formal adoption propagating through textbooks; (iii) the Penrose-Wightman signature convention displacing $ict$ and consigning i to formal-device status; (iv) the Kaluza-Klein detour into compact spatial dimensions absorbing the foundational-extra-dimension intuition. Each of these is a sociological obstruction. The mathematics for the active-expansion account was available the moment Minkowski wrote x₄ = ict — once $x_4 = ict$ is written down, differentiation gives $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the dynamics of which $x_4 = ict$ is the integrated shadow, and the active-expansion account follows. The community did not articulate it because the community did not look for it, and the community did not look for it because the four conceptual blocks of §XIV obstructed the relevant question. We turn to those blocks now, but first to the documented priority record of the McGucken Principle itself, which establishes that the active-expansion account was articulated in print starting in 1998–99 and elaborated continuously thereafter, in a corpus that predates the precision tests that now verify the Principle.

### XIII.A.6 The Significance of the FQXi Priority Record

The five FQXi essays establish, at the highest authoritative standard available to a theory in the published record, that the McGucken Principle's content was articulated in print continuously from 2008 through 2013. The essays were submitted to a major foundations-of-physics venue (FQXi, founded by Anthony Aguirre and Max Tegmark in 2006, supported by the John Templeton Foundation), were reviewed by the FQXi community, and remain publicly accessible at the URLs cited above. The author's profile at https://forums.fqxi.org/u/dmcgucken contains the complete record.

This priority record is decisive for the predictive-not-postdictive content of §IX.0.10. A postdictive theorist constructing a hypothesis to fit known data could in principle construct one derivation chain from a formal scheme to each known theorem, but the timestamped FQXi essays of 2008, 2009, 2011, 2012, and 2013 *predate* the modern precision-test catalogue that now verifies the Principle at Bayesian likelihood ratio $\gtrsim 10^{141}$:

- GW170817 (gravitational-wave / electromagnetic counterpart, August 17, 2017): predates the 2008 priority essay by **nine years**.
- Hensen et al. loophole-free Bell test (Nature 526, 2015): predates the 2008 priority essay by **seven years**.
- LIGO first direct detection of gravitational waves (GW150914, September 14, 2015): predates the 2008 priority essay by **seven years**.
- The Big Bell Test (Nature 557, 2018): predates the 2008 priority essay by **ten years**.
- Electron $g - 2$ measurement at 12-decimal precision (Fan et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 130, 2023): predates the 2008 priority essay by **fifteen years**.
- The FLRW twelve zero-free-parameter cosmological tests (final assembly through 2023–2025): predate the 2008 priority essay by **fifteen to seventeen years**.

The author's 1998–99 UNC Chapel Hill dissertation appendix [8] predates the 2008 essay by an additional nine years, extending the priority record to a quarter-century before the most recent precision tests that confirm the Principle. The dual-channel derivations of [3] are therefore predictions forced by a principle that was published before the data existed. This is the history that, combined with the formal Dual-Channel Disjointness Predicate of Definition IX.26.2 and the Bayesian likelihood-ratio computation of Theorem IX.26.11, establishes the Principle's epistemic status as a *physical principle in the strict sense of Definition IX.26.6*. A single dynamics about physical reality with zero adjustable parameters, direct empirical claims, and a documented priority record predating its own verification.

The McGucken Principle therefore stands, in the canonical priority sense, with Newton's *Principia* (1687) verified at universal-gravitation scale and Maxwell's *Treatise* (1873) verified at electromagnetic-unification scale: a physical principle stated in print and subsequently verified by independent empirical work over multiple decades. The five FQXi essays of 2008–2013, the 1998–99 dissertation appendix [8], the two books (2016–17), and the corpus of 40+ technical papers at elliotmcguckenphysics.com (October 2024–present) [10] are the documented record of the Principle's published priority.

## XIII.B the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel vs. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel Blindspots Across the History of Physics: How Single-Channel Vision Obstructed Unification for Three and a Half Centuries

> *"All science is either physics or stamp collecting."*
> — Ernest Rutherford [Birks1962]

> *"The most incomprehensible thing about the universe is that it is comprehensible."*
> — Albert Einstein [Einstein-Ideas1995]

> *"The world is full of magical things, patiently waiting for our wits to grow sharper."*
> — Bertrand Russell [Russell1924]

The history of physics from Huygens 1690 to the present is, in retrospect, a 335-year history of *single-channel* discoveries: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel discoveries that articulated the algebraic-symmetry of physics without the geometric-propagation, the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel discoveries that articulated the geometric-propagation without the algebraic-symmetry, and a small number of figures who saw fragments of both but lacked the unifying source-pair architecture that would have shown the two channels to be two faces of a single object. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, by supplying the source-pair $(\mathcal M_{G}, D_{M})$ co-generated by a relation, makes visible *retrospectively* what the single-channel discoveries missed: that every dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel discovery had a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel counterpart waiting to be seen, and vice versa, and that the failure to see this is what blocked the unification of quantum mechanics and general relativity for over a century.

This section catalogues the principal the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel vs. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel blindspots across the history of physics, identifies the specific content each side missed, and shows how the McGucken framework's bidirectional Klein-correspondence account of the source-pair (§IX.0.A) makes the missed content visible. The catalogue is not exhaustive — the history of physics contains many smaller episodes of the same pattern, but the principal episodes establish the: **single-channel vision is what blocked unification, and dual-channel vision is what makes unification visible.**

### XIII.B.1 The Master Blindspot Catalogue: the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel Asymmetries from Huygens 1690 to Wolfram 2020

The following catalogues, in chronological order, the 37 principal episodes in which a figure of physics articulated one channel of what would later be revealed as a dual-channel content of dx₄/dt = ic, missing the other channel and therefore missing the claim that would have unified the discovery with adjacent results. Each entry identifies the figure, the year, the discovery, the channel articulated, the channel missed, and the claim that the missing channel would have supplied.

Entry 1. Huygens (1690).

- *Discovery:* Huygens' Principle: every point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets.
- *Channel articulated:* **The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel** (geometric-propagation: spherical wavefronts $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p)$ at every point, iteration generates new wavefronts).
- *Channel missed:* **The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel** (algebraic: the wavefront construction is a Stone-theorem one-parameter flow; the secondary-wavelet sources form an operator family $\{D_{M}^{(p)}\}$).
- *What the missing channel would have supplied:* Identification of Huygens' Principle as the geometric face of a source-pair whose algebraic face is the Stone-theorem generator; the Reciprocal Generation Property already present in Huygens 1690 in vernacular form. Huygens had the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel in 1690 — 335 years before its formalisation, but lacked the algebraic vocabulary to name what he had.

**Entry 2. Newton (1687).**

- *Discovery:* *Principia*: universal gravitation, three laws of motion, calculus.
- *Channel articulated:* **The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel** (algebraic-symmetry: $F = ma$ as a Lie-algebraic generator equation; absolute space and absolute time as separable arena).
- *Channel missed:* **The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel** (geometric-propagation: gravitational influence as wavefront from each mass at finite speed; spacetime as carrier of propagation).
- *What the missing channel would have supplied:* The propagation speed of gravity (Newton assumed instantaneous; the McGucken Sphere gives propagation at c); the geometry of inertia (later supplied by GR the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel). Newton himself was uneasy with action-at-a-distance — *"That gravity should be innate, inherent and essential to matter, so that one body may act upon another at a distance through a vacuum, without the mediation of any thing else. Is to me so great an absurdity that I believe no man who has in philosophical matters a competent faculty of thinking can ever fall into it."* (Newton to Bentley 1693), but lacked the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel geometric vocabulary to articulate what the mediation must be.

Entry 3. Leibniz (1714).

- *Discovery:* Relational theory of space and time (*Monadologie*; correspondence with Clarke).
- *Channel articulated:* Fragmentary anticipation of **The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel** (relational geometry: space and time as relations among bodies rather than absolute container) without the algebraic completion.
- *Channel missed:* Both channels'. Leibniz lacked the integration of dx₄/dt = ic, the rate c, and the imaginary unit i.
- *What the missing channel would have supplied:* The active-expansion: time as the integration parameter of x₄'s expansion at velocity c from every event. Leibniz's relational theory anticipates this in vernacular form (time arises from relations among bodies' positions) but lacks the rate c and the perpendicularity marker i. **Entry 37. Wolfram physics (2020).**

- *Channel articulated:* **The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel** (algebraic: rewrite-rule formalism on hypergraphs).

### XIII.B.2 Boltzmann and Carathéodory: The 154-Year Persistence of Loschmidt's Objection as a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel-Only Artefact

The most consequential single the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel blindspot in the history of physics is the Boltzmann–Carathéodory–Lieb–Yngvason articulation of thermodynamics as a purely algebraic-axiomatic system, missing the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel geometry that supplies strict monotonicity from x₄'s active expansion.

Boltzmann's 1872 H-theorem [Boltzmann1872] showed that the quantity $H = \int f \ln f\, d^{3}v$ is monotonically non-increasing under the Boltzmann transport equation, with $S = -k_{B}H$ identified as entropy. The derivation invokes the *Stosszahlansatz* (molecular chaos assumption), which Loschmidt 1876 [Loschmidt1876] showed is asymmetric in time direction: applying time-reversal to the microstates produces an anti-Stosszahlansatz that yields $dH/dt > 0$, contradicting the H-theorem. Loschmidt's objection has been called the *reversibility paradox*, and its resolution has occupied statistical physics for **154 years and counting**.

The McGucken framework dissolves the paradox at once. Loschmidt's objection applies to the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel only — the algebraic-statistical content of ensemble averaging over microstates. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel geometry of dx₄/dt = ic supplies what the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel cannot: strict monotonicity $dS/dt = (3/2)k_{B}/t > 0$ for massive particles via the McGucken Sphere's $SO(3)$-invariant Brownian-motion content, with the +ic orientation of x₄'s expansion fixing the time direction at the geometric level rather than at the ensemble-averaging level (Theorem 9 of [4]; §IX.16 of the present paper). The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel is time-symmetric and Loschmidt's objection applies; the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is strictly time-asymmetric by the +ic orientation and Loschmidt's objection does not apply. **The 154-year persistence of the paradox is a direct artifact of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel-only vision of mathematical-thermodynamics**. Carathéodory 1909's axiomatisation, the Lieb–Yngvason 1999 framework, and the entire post-Boltzmann statistical-mechanics tradition treat thermodynamics as a single-channel algebraic-axiomatic system, missing the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel geometry that resolves the paradox.

The Past Hypothesis (Penrose's $10^{-10^{123}}$ fine-tuning of the initial cosmological state to a low-entropy macrostate) is similarly an artefact of the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel-only vision. The Penrose figure measures an improbability under the prior of an unconstrained initial macrostate. The McGucken-Sphere geometry (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel) supplies the natural prior: at x₄'s origin, the Sphere has radius $R = 0$, hence area $4\pi R^{2} = 0$, hence entropy $S(t) = k_{B}\ln(4\pi(c(t-t_{0}))^{2}) \to -\infty$ as $t \to t_{0}^{+}$. The origin of x₄'s expansion is the geometrically necessary lowest-entropy moment — no fine-tuning required, and Penrose's $10^{-10^{123}}$ measures an improbability under the wrong prior.

### XIII.B.3 The Schrödinger Equation as Thermodynamic: The Susskind Blindspot, the Black Hole War as a Half-Equation Engagement, and the Single-Photon Refutation

The thirty-year Black Hole War (Hawking 1976; Susskind 2008, *The Black Hole War*) was a foundational dispute over whether information is destroyed in black-hole evaporation (Hawking's position) or preserved by unitary evolution (Susskind's position). Susskind won the orthodox sociological verdict — black-hole complementarity (Susskind, Thorlacius, Uglum 1993), holography ('t Hooft 1993; Susskind 1995), the Strominger–Vafa microstate counting (1996), Maldacena's AdS/CFT (1997), ER=EPR (Maldacena–Susskind 2013), the Page curve, replica wormholes, and the island formula were all built around defending the unitarian commitment. **Yet the diagnosis of the present synthesis paper — corroborated independently by Theorems 22–24e of [4] — reveals that the entire fifty-year dispute was a half-equation engagement: both sides accepted the orthodox one-channel account of the Schrödinger equation, Hawking attacking the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel and Susskind defending the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel, while the actual physics Hawking was detecting lived in the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel, never on either side's map.** The thirty-year war was fought over a phantom.

The blindspot is simple to state. The Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\,\partial_{t}\psi = \hat H\psi$ is doubly forced by dx₄/dt = ic through two distinct routes: (i) **The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel** — via the converse direction of Stone's theorem on one-parameter unitary groups applied to the time-translation invariance of dx₄/dt = ic (Proposition II.2 of the present paper), yielding the equation as the generator of unitary time evolution on a separable complex Hilbert space, with the imaginary unit i supplying the algebra of the unitarity; and (ii) **The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel** — via the non-relativistic limit of the Klein-Gordon wave equation, which is itself the differential statement of Huygens-wavefront propagation on the McGucken Sphere expanding at +ic, augmented by the Compton-coupling rest-mass phase factor $\exp(-imc^{2}\tau/\hbar)$ (Propositions II.6–II.10 of the present paper; [4]). **The same claimor of i in $i\hbar\,\partial_{t}\psi$** that produces $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat Ht/\hbar)$ unitary via Stone's theorem **also produces, via Huygens-iterated McGucken-Sphere projection, the strict Second Law $dS/dt = (3/2)k_{B}/t > 0$ of Theorem III.A.7 of the present paper**, identically of [4]. Both contents are intrinsic to the single equation; neither is an emergent statistical addition imported from an adjacent discipline.

This dual-channel content of the Schrödinger equation is a well-known fact of physics that the contemporary unification programme has *organisationally suppressed*. The derivation of the Schrödinger equation from Huygens' Principle was established by Feynman 1948 in *Reviews of Modern Physics*, deepened in Feynman–Hibbs 1965 (*Quantum Mechanics and Path Integrals*, McGraw-Hill, Chapter 4), made rigorous in Kac 1949 / Trotter 1959 / Nelson 1985, and developed as stochastic-mechanics by Nelson 1966–1985 and as stochastic quantization by Parisi–Wu 1981. The Wick rotation $\tau = it$ converting Schrödinger to a diffusion equation (Wick 1954; treated as a coordinate identification rather than a formal device in the present paper, §IX.13) was a by 1960. The Feynman–Kac correspondence between quantum-mechanical and statistical-mechanical path integrals was, by the 1970s, standard graduate-level material in mathematical physics. *That the Schrödinger equation contains diffusive geometric-propagation has been of physics for seventy-eight years*. What the McGucken framework adds is the *physical principle* dx₄/dt = ic that forces both channels as parallel readings of one geometric primitive, with the strict-monotonic +ic orientation of the active expansion making the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel Second Law strict, and with the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content recognised as *equally physical* with the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel content rather than dismissed as a "formal computational trick".

Susskind, as a physicist, cannot legitimately dismiss the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel content as a formalism. the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is the geometric-propagation of the Schrödinger equation — the iterated Huygens–McGucken-Sphere wavefront expansion at +ic that *physically generates* the equation in its Feynman–Hibbs derivation. The Schrödinger equation is doubly forced by dx₄/dt = ic, with the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel supplying the explicit physical mechanism through Compton-coupled Brownian motion ([4]). To defend "information cannot be destroyed" by appealing only to the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel unitarity is to read half the Schrödinger equation while ignoring the half that contains the strict Second Law. As a matter of physics, this half-equation reading is untenable: the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel is just as physical as the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel, supported by Huygens 1690, Feynman 1948, Feynman–Hibbs 1965, Kac 1949, Trotter 1959, Nelson 1966–1985, and Parisi–Wu 1981, and supplying the explicit Compton-coupled Brownian mechanism that drives the Brownian Hamlet to dissolution (Theorem III.A.6 of the present paper) and the Brownian Iliad–Odyssey beakers to mutually indistinguishable equilibria ([4]).

The Banks–Peskin–Susskind theorem operates exclusively on the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel and is silent on the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel. The 1984 Banks–Peskin–Susskind theorem, on which Susskind's "unitarity is non-negotiable" position centrally rests, establishes that non-unitary modifications of $U(t)$ at the S-matrix level — replacement of unitary U by a non-unitary $\$$-operator mapping pure states to mixed states — cannot be confined to high-energy or near-horizon regions under reasonable assumptions of locality, energy conservation, and Lorentz invariance; the modifications propagate and produce gross violations of observed phenomena (energy non-conservation at low energy, locality violation, catastrophic vacuum heating). This theorem rules out the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel non-unitarity. It is silent on monotonic +ic-driven geometric-propagation effects (the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel) that leave $U(t)$ unitary while inducing operational information loss via spherical x₄-dilution, horizon crossing, or causal-region exit. **Hawking's 1976 intuition of gravitational information loss was the correct identification of a dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel phenomenon in a black-hole spacetime, miscoded as a dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel claim. Susskind defended the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel against a phantom; the actual physics Hawking was detecting, operational information loss via the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel, was never on either side's map.** Full diagnosis: [4].

The single-photon refutation follows from the undetected-photon accessibility going to zero. refutation of Susskind's commitment operates at the single-quantum level, without invoking any thermodynamic ensemble. Following [4], consider a single photon emitted at time $t_{0}$ from a localised laboratory source. By the spherical-symmetry of Theorem 3 of [4] (Huygens-wavefront propagation on the McGucken Sphere), the photon's wavefunction occupies a spherical shell of radius $R(t) = c(t - t_{0})$ at observer time t, with the surface area $4\pi R^{2}(t)$ growing quadratically in t. The probability density at any fixed solid-angle element decreases as $|\psi|^{2} \sim 1/R^{2}(t)$. For any bounded observer of cross-section $\sigma_{\text{obs}}$ at distance $r_{\text{obs}}(t)$ from the source, the probability of detection in interval $[t, t+dt]$ is bounded above by

$$P_{\text{accessible}}(t)\,dt \leq \frac{\sigma_{\text{obs}}\,c\,dt}{4\pi r_{\text{obs}}^{2}(t)}.$$

For an isotropically emitted photon with no detector intercepting the wavefront, $P_{\text{accessible}}(t) \to 0$ as $t \to \infty$, *while the global integral $\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|\psi|^{2} = 1$ is preserved exactly throughout*. The global integral remains unity by the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel unitarity; the operational probability of detection at any realisable observer falls to zero by the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel spherical x₄-dilution. The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel integral is preserved as a Platonic mathematical artefact on a region no observer can probe; the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel operational quantity is destroyed monotonically as the wavefront expands. Both are theorems of dx₄/dt = ic, both are carried by the same claimor of i, neither requires any thermodynamic ensemble.

The undetected-photon refutation is complete on its own. Susskind's "information cannot be destroyed" commitment now faces an operational-versus-metaphysical dichotomy with no orthodox third position. **The Brownian Hamlet many-particle case refutes the counter.** The Brownian Hamlet experiment (Theorem III.A.6 of the present paper; [4]) places 1,000 glass beakers each containing Shakespeare's *Hamlet* encoded in $\sim 8.75 \times 10^{7}$ dust particles into a thermostatted enclosure. After the dissolution timescale $\tau_{d} \approx 8$ s per letter (computed from the Compton-coupled Brownian diffusion of [4]), the encoded text is gone. **The Brownian Iliad–Odyssey two-text case refutes the counter.** The Brownian Iliad–Odyssey experiment ([4]) sharpens the Brownian Hamlet by preparing 1,000 beakers each containing Homer's *Iliad* and 1,000 beakers each containing Homer's *Odyssey*, with the two texts encoded using *identical resources*: same color palette, same number of particles of each color, same total mass, same total energy, same temperature, same volume, same vanishing global conserved charges. No experimental procedure performed on a single dissolved beaker — measurement, computation, holographic data extraction, fine-grained microstate readout, AdS/CFT bulk-boundary reconstruction, ER=EPR entanglement-tracing — can distinguish an Iliad beaker from an Odyssey beaker with success probability exceeding $1/2 + \epsilon$ for any $\epsilon > 0$ as $N \to \infty$ and $t \to \infty$. The text-distinguishing information is destroyed as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via Compton-coupled Brownian motion that preserves every conserved quantity while randomising the spatial ordering; the strict Second Law makes the destruction monotonic and irreversible.

The Brownian Aristotle–Plato philosophical-content case refutes the counter. The Brownian Aristotle–Plato experiment ([4]) extends the refutation from textual content to philosophy. **Remark XIII.B.3.4 (historical parallel: the 19th-century Loschmidt–Zermelo–Poincaré Platonic-mathematical reaction to empirical thermodynamics, after [40]).** The methodological retreat documented in Theorem XIII.B.3.1 has a precise historical parallel in the 19th- and early-20th-century reaction of the Platonic-mathematical tradition against the empirical-operational character of thermodynamics. *Loschmidt 1876* [Loschmidt 1876] invoked the time-reversibility of microscopic dynamics against Boltzmann's H-theorem; *Zermelo 1896* [Zermelo 1896, *Ueber einen Satz der Dynamik und die mechanische Wärmetheorie*, *Annalen der Physik* 293, 485] invoked *Poincaré's 1893 recurrence theorem* [Poincaré 1893, *Sur les équations de la dynamique et le problème des trois corps*, *Acta Mathematica* 13, 1–270], that for a Hamiltonian system with bounded phase space, almost every phase-space trajectory returns arbitrarily close to its initial state after sufficient time — against the strict monotonicity of the Second Law. The same retreat pattern appears in the AdS/CFT and ER=EPR domain-shifts. The methodological retreat is a recurring move at the level of *spacetime selection*, not a singular event in Susskind's framework. The Hawking–Susskind information paradox in its original 1976 form was a question about *our* black holes — astrophysical black holes formed by stellar collapse in our four-dimensional asymptotically-flat spacetime. Maldacena's 1997 AdS/CFT correspondence, incorporated by Susskind into the holographic-information programme, shifted the discussion to a different spacetime entirely: anti-de Sitter space, with its conformal boundary, its negative cosmological constant, and its absence in observed cosmology. The argument, that information is preserved in the AdS/CFT setting because the boundary CFT is manifestly unitary and supplies a dual description of the bulk — is a genuine result *about AdS spacetimes*. The application of this result to defend information preservation in our universe, which is asymptotically de Sitter rather than anti-de Sitter, is a second domain-shift retreat: the original question about *our* black holes is answered by a result about *not our* black holes. ER=EPR ([Maldacena–Susskind 2013]) repeats the move at the level of wormhole geometry: the identification of entanglement with Einstein–Rosen bridges supplies a picture in *eternal* AdS black-hole spacetimes (the thermofield double) and is then offered as a resolution of the information paradox for astrophysical black holes that are neither eternal nor AdS. Each retreat is a legitimate result in its arena; each declaration of victory in the operational physics arena is a category error of the type diagnosed by Theorem XIII.B.3.1. # XIV. Four Conceptual Blocks That Obstructed the Active-Expansion Reading
*(McGucken Duality framing for the four blocks.)* The four conceptual blocks identified in this section are the four commitments by which the 20th-century tradition foreclosed the **McGucken Duality** at the level — each block treating one face of dx₄/dt = ic (typically **The McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel**) as foundational and the other (**The McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel**) as adjacent computational technology. The McGucken framework's correction is the recognition that both channels are parallel articulations of the same principle dx₄/dt = ic, with the duality between them being a feature of physics rather than a methodological convenience.

The conceptual blocks are deeper than the historical contingencies. They are the *interpretive* commitments of twentieth-century physics that prevented the active-expansion account from being articulated even after the mathematics was in place. I identify four.

## XIV.1 Block 1: Wick Rotation as Formal Trick

The Wick rotation $t \to it_{E}$ has been read since the 1950s as a *formal computational device* for converting the Minkowski path integral into a Euclidean integral with absolute convergence properties [Wick 1954]. The interpretive commitment was: *the imaginary unit in Wick rotation has no physics; it is a mathematical convenience.* Under this commitment, the appearance of i in $\det(\eta_{\mu\nu}) = -1$, in the Wick-rotated Lagrangian $iS_{M} = -S_{E}$, in the Schwinger proper-time integral, and so on, was *not* read as evidence for an underlying geometric structure in which i is the active-expansion generator. The McGucken framework reverses this: the Wick-rotation i is the *same* i as in dx₄/dt = ic, with the same geometry. The block was the formal-trick reading; removing the block reveals the geometry [49].

## XIV.2 Block 2: Metric Signature as Convention

The choice between signature $(+, -, -, -)$ and $(-, +, +, +)$ has been treated as a *pure convention*: a sign choice with no physics, fixed by author preference. The interpretive commitment was: *signature is convention; the physics is the same in either signature.* Under this commitment, the underlying ℂ-structure of $C\ell(1, 3)$, which depends on the relative sign of $i^{2}$ and the signature, was not read as carrying physics. The McGucken framework reads the signature as *not* convention: the relative signs encode the active-expansion's geometric structure, and the i of dx₄/dt = ic is the algebraic-geometric generator that fixes the signature physically. The block was the signature-is-convention reading; removing the block reveals the geometry of the signature.

## XIV.3 Block 3: Path Integral as Formal Construction

Feynman's 1948 path integral was read for half a century as a *formal sum over histories* whose interpretation was indeterminate ("nature does not know which path the particle takes"). The interpretive commitment was: *the path integral is a calculational device; its geometry, if any, is not foundational.* The Trotter and Feynman-Kac formulas established its mathematical equivalence to the operator formulation without supplying a geometric foundation. Under this commitment, the path integral was the *formal counterpart* of the operator formulation, with neither side foundational. The McGucken framework reads the path integral as the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometric face of dx₄/dt = ic — the Huygens propagation of the null hypersurface, with the operator formulation as the McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic face. The block was the path-integral-as-formal-device reading; removing the block reveals the path integral as the geometric channel of the algebraic structureE [17].

## XIV.4 Block 4: Bell as Philosophy

Bell's 1964 theorem and the subsequent experimental violations have been read in the philosophy-of-physics literature as establishing *interpretive constraints* on quantum mechanics: local realism is incompatible with experiment; either locality or realism must be abandoned. The interpretive frameworks (Copenhagen, Bohmian, many-worlds, relational, QBism) each pick a position in this interpretive space. The interpretive commitment was: *the consequences of Bell's theorem are philosophical, to be settled by interpretation, not by deriving the correlations from a geometric primitive.* Under this commitment, nonlocality was a *phenomenon to be interpreted*, not a *geometric structure to be derived*. The McGucken framework reads nonlocality as the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel-mediated sharing of a single McGucken-Sphere event-of-origin between spacelike-separated measurement events (Theorem VI.A). The block was the Bell-as-philosophy reading; removing the block reveals nonlocality as a geometric structure derivable from dx₄/dt = ic [23].

## XIV.5 The Four Blocks as a System

The four blocks form a system. Block 1 prevents the Wick i from being read geometrically; Block 2 prevents the signature from being read geometrically; Block 3 prevents the path integral from being read geometrically; Block 4 prevents Bell correlations from being read geometrically. Together they *systematically* prevent any portion of mathematical physics that involves i, the signature, the path integral, or Bell from being read as a geometric structure derivable from a primitive. The McGucken framework removes all four blocks by supplying the primitive (dx₄/dt = ic) from which each formal structure is derived as a geometric consequence.

The four blocks together are *why nobody saw it*. The mathematics was available since Minkowski 1908. The interpretive commitments of twentieth-century physics obstructed the question. The McGucken framework removes the obstructions by stating the active-expansion principle as foundational.

## XV.1 The Empirical Prediction

The diffusion coefficient for a particle of relativistic factor γ coupled to the active expansion at strength ε and Compton frequency Ω in the local rest frame is
$$D_{x}^{\text{(McG)}} \;=\; \frac{\varepsilon^{2} c^{2} \Omega}{2\gamma_{L}^{2}}\,,$$

## XV.2 Empirical Falsifiability Criteria

Falsification Criterion F1 (functional form). *If, in a precision experiment, the measured spatial diffusion of a particle is observed to depend on $\gamma_{L}$ or Ω with functional dependence inconsistent with $D_{x}^{\text{(McG)}} \propto c^{2} \Omega / \gamma_{L}^{2}$, the McGucken framework's coupling prediction is falsified.*

## XVII.1 The Four-Sector Form of $\mathcal L_{\text{McG}}$

**Definition XVII.1 (the McGucken Lagrangian, after [26]).** *The McGucken Lagrangian is the four-sector functional*
$$\mathcal L_{\text{McG}} \;=\; \mathcal L_{\text{kin}} \;+\; \mathcal L_{\text{Dirac}} \;+\; \mathcal L_{\text{YM}} \;+\; \mathcal L_{\text{EH}}$$
*comprising:*

- *(S2) The Dirac matter sector $\mathcal L_{\text{Dirac}} = \bar\psi(i\gamma^{\mu}\partial_{\mu} - m)\psi$ — the relativistic spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ matter Lagrangian whose Euler-Lagrange equation is the Dirac equation $(i\gamma^{\mu}\partial_{\mu} - m)\psi = 0$.*
- *(S3) The Yang–Mills gauge sector $\mathcal L_{\text{YM}} = -\tfrac{1}{4}F^{a}_{\mu\nu} F^{a\,\mu\nu}$ — the gauge-invariant kinetic term for the connection $A^{a}_{\mu}$ on a principal G-bundle for compact Lie group G, with field strength $F^{a}_{\mu\nu} = \partial_{\mu}A^{a}_{\nu} - \partial_{\nu}A^{a}_{\mu} + g f^{abc} A^{b}_{\mu}A^{c}_{\nu}$.*

## XVII.2 The Four Sector-Uniqueness Theorems

**Theorem XVII.2 (kinetic-sector uniqueness, after [26]).** *The free-particle kinetic Lagrangian $\mathcal L_{\text{kin}} = -mc\sqrt{-g_{\mu\nu}\dot x^{\mu}\dot x^{\nu}}$ is the unique Lorentz-covariant, reparameterisation-invariant, first-order Lagrangian on a Lorentzian four-manifold producing geodesic motion as the Euler-Lagrange equation. The uniqueness is forced by Lorentz covariance + reparameterisation invariance + first-order derivative dependence + Newtonian-limit normalization.*

*Proof.* Four constraints fix the form: (i) Lorentz covariance: $\mathcal L_{\text{kin}}$ must be a Lorentz scalar built from $\dot x^\mu$ and $g_{\mu\nu}$; (ii) reparameterisation invariance under $\tau \to f(\tau)$: $\mathcal L$ must transform as $d\tau$, equivalently $\mathcal L$ must be a homogeneous function of degree 1 in $\dot x^\mu$; (iii) first-order derivative dependence: $\mathcal L$ depends on $\dot x^\mu$ but not $\ddot x^\mu$; (iv) Euler-Lagrange equation must produce geodesic motion. Constraints (i)+(ii)+(iii) restrict $\mathcal L$ to $\mathcal L = -k\sqrt{-g_{\mu\nu}\dot x^\mu \dot x^\nu}$ for some constant $k$ (the unique Lorentz-scalar, degree-1 homogeneous, first-order Lagrangian on a Lorentzian manifold). The Newtonian-limit normalization (matching the non-relativistic kinetic energy $T = (1/2)m v^2$) fixes $k = mc$. The Euler-Lagrange equation produces the geodesic equation by direct computation. The form $\mathcal L_{\text{kin}} = -mc\sqrt{-g_{\mu\nu}\dot x^\mu \dot x^\nu}$ is therefore the unique kinetic Lagrangian satisfying all four constraints. ∎

**Theorem XVII.3 (Dirac-sector uniqueness, after [26]).** *The Dirac matter Lagrangian $\mathcal L_{\text{Dirac}} = \bar\psi(i\gamma^{\mu}\partial_{\mu} - m)\psi$ is the unique Lorentz-covariant, first-order, Hermitian Lagrangian for a spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ Weyl-spinor field on a Lorentzian four-manifold producing the Dirac equation as the Euler-Lagrange equation. The uniqueness is forced by Lorentz covariance + first-order derivative dependence + Hermiticity + Clifford-algebra structure of $C\ell(1, 3)$ via the Frobenius theorem (Theorem XI.2 of §XI).*

*Proof.* Four constraints fix the form: (i) Lorentz covariance: $\mathcal L_{\text{Dirac}}$ must be a Lorentz scalar built from spinor field $\psi$, its Dirac conjugate $\bar\psi = \psi^\dagger \gamma^0$, the gamma matrices $\gamma^\mu$, and $\partial_\mu$; (ii) first-order derivative dependence: $\mathcal L$ depends on $\partial_\mu\psi$ but not $\partial_\mu\partial_\nu\psi$; (iii) Hermiticity: $\mathcal L = \mathcal L^*$; (iv) Clifford-algebra structure $\{\gamma^\mu, \gamma^\nu\} = 2\eta^{\mu\nu}$ from the Frobenius-forced $C\ell(1,3)$ representation (Theorem XI.2). The most general Lorentz-scalar, first-order, Hermitian bilinear in $\psi$ and $\bar\psi$ with one derivative is $\mathcal L = a\bar\psi i\gamma^\mu \partial_\mu \psi + b\bar\psi\psi$ with $a, b$ real. Hermiticity requires $a = a^*$ (real). The Newtonian-limit / mass-shell normalization fixes $a = 1$ and $b = -m$. The form $\mathcal L_{\text{Dirac}} = \bar\psi(i\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu - m)\psi$ is therefore the unique Dirac Lagrangian. The Euler-Lagrange equation $\partial\mathcal L/\partial\bar\psi - \partial_\mu(\partial\mathcal L/\partial(\partial_\mu\bar\psi)) = 0$ produces the Dirac equation $(i\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu - m)\psi = 0$. ∎

**Theorem XVII.4 (Yang–Mills-sector uniqueness, after [26]).** *The Yang–Mills gauge Lagrangian $\mathcal L_{\text{YM}} = -\tfrac{1}{4}F^{a}_{\mu\nu} F^{a\,\mu\nu}$ is the unique gauge-invariant, Lorentz-scalar, renormalizable Lagrangian (mass dimension $\leq 4$) on a principal G-bundle for any compact Lie group G, producing the Yang–Mills equation as the Euler-Lagrange equation. The uniqueness is forced by gauge invariance + Lorentz invariance + locality + renormalizability (mass dimension $\leq 4$) + parity invariance.*

*Proof.* Five constraints fix the form: (i) gauge invariance: $\mathcal L$ must be built from gauge-covariant objects, namely $F^a_{\mu\nu} = \partial_\mu A^a_\nu - \partial_\nu A^a_\mu + g f^{abc} A^b_\mu A^c_\nu$ (field strength) and gauge-covariant derivatives $D_\mu = \partial_\mu - ig T^a A^a_\mu$; (ii) Lorentz scalar: $\mathcal L$ must be built from Lorentz-scalar contractions; (iii) locality: $\mathcal L$ depends on $A^a_\mu$ at a single spacetime point; (iv) renormalizability (mass dimension $\leq 4$): $[A^a_\mu] = 1$, $[F^a_{\mu\nu}] = 2$, so quadratic in $F$ is mass dimension 4; (v) parity invariance: $\mathcal L$ must be parity-even, excluding the $\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}$ topological-charge term $F^a_{\mu\nu}\tilde F^{a\,\mu\nu}$ (which is parity-odd; it appears as a separate theta-vacuum term, not the YM kinetic term). The unique form satisfying all five constraints is $\mathcal L_{\text{YM}} = -(1/4) F^a_{\mu\nu} F^{a\,\mu\nu}$, with the $-1/4$ coefficient fixed by the Maxwell-limit normalization (recovering $\mathcal L_{\text{Maxwell}} = -(1/4)F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}$ for $G = U(1)$). The Euler-Lagrange equation produces the Yang-Mills equation $D_\mu F^{a\,\mu\nu} = J^{a\,\nu}$. ∎

**Theorem XVII.5 (Einstein–Hilbert-sector uniqueness, after [26] and Lovelock 1971 [Lovelock 1971]).** *The Einstein–Hilbert gravitational Lagrangian $\mathcal L_{\text{EH}} = (c^{4}/16\pi G)\, R$ is the unique diffeomorphism-invariant scalar Lagrangian in four spacetime dimensions whose Euler-Lagrange equation is a second-order differential equation in the metric and contains the metric and its first two derivatives only. The uniqueness is forced by Lovelock's theorem: in four dimensions, the only divergence-free symmetric tensor constructible from $g_{\mu\nu}$ and its first two derivatives is $G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu}$ (with the cosmological constant Λ as the only additional invariant). The Newtonian-limit normalization fixes the coupling at $c^{4}/(16\pi G)$.*

*Proof.* By Lovelock's theorem (Lovelock 1971), the only divergence-free symmetric (0,2)-tensor constructible from $g_{\mu\nu}$ and its first two derivatives in four-dimensional Lorentzian manifolds is $A_{\mu\nu} = \alpha G_{\mu\nu} + \beta g_{\mu\nu}$ for constants $\alpha, \beta$. The Einstein tensor $G_{\mu\nu} = R_{\mu\nu} - (1/2)R g_{\mu\nu}$ is the Euler-Lagrange tensor of the scalar Lagrangian $\mathcal L = k R$ (Hilbert action) where $k$ is a coupling constant. Diffeomorphism invariance forces $\mathcal L$ to be a Lorentz scalar built from curvature invariants ($R$, $R_{\mu\nu}R^{\mu\nu}$, $R_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}R^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}$,..); second-order EL-equation forces $\mathcal L$ to be linear in second derivatives of the metric, which restricts $\mathcal L$ to be proportional to $R$ (plus possibly a constant $\Lambda$). The unique form is therefore $\mathcal L_{\text{EH}} = (c^4/16\pi G)(R - 2\Lambda)$. The Newtonian-limit normalization (matching Poisson's equation $\nabla^2\Phi = 4\pi G\rho$) fixes the coupling at $c^4/(16\pi G)$. The cosmological constant $\Lambda$ is determined by FLRW observational input $\Omega_\Lambda \approx 0.69$ (Theorem IX.27.6). ∎

**Corollary XVII.6 (the four sectors are independent uniqueness theorems).** *Each of the four sectors $\mathcal L_{\text{kin}}$, $\mathcal L_{\text{Dirac}}$, $\mathcal L_{\text{YM}}$, $\mathcal L_{\text{EH}}$ is independently forced by an independent uniqueness theorem. The four-sector Lagrangian $\mathcal L_{\text{McG}}$ is therefore the unique consistent Lagrangian compatible with the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic on a moving-dimension manifold $(M, F, V)$ supporting matter (spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ fermions), gauge fields (compact Lie group G), and gravity (Lorentzian metric $g_{\mu\nu}$).*

*Proof.* By Theorems XVII.2-5, each of the four sectors is independently fixed by its own uniqueness theorem: $\mathcal L_{\text{kin}}$ by Lorentz covariance + reparameterisation invariance + first-order dependence + Newtonian limit (Theorem XVII.2); $\mathcal L_{\text{Dirac}}$ by Lorentz covariance + first-order dependence + Hermiticity + Frobenius-forced $C\ell(1,3)$ Clifford algebra (Theorem XVII.3); $\mathcal L_{\text{YM}}$ by gauge invariance + Lorentz scalar + locality + renormalizability + parity invariance (Theorem XVII.4); $\mathcal L_{\text{EH}}$ by Lovelock 4D uniqueness + Newtonian-limit normalization (Theorem XVII.5). The four uniqueness theorems are independent: each operates on its own field content (worldlines for kin, spinor fields for Dirac, gauge connections for YM, metric for EH) with no overlap. The sum $\mathcal L_{\text{McG}} = \mathcal L_{\text{kin}} + \mathcal L_{\text{Dirac}} + \mathcal L_{\text{YM}} + \mathcal L_{\text{EH}}$ is therefore the unique consistent Lagrangian compatible with dx₄/dt = ic on a moving-dimension manifold supporting matter, gauge fields, and gravity. ∎

John Archibald Wheeler — my undergraduate research advisor at Princeton (Fall 1989, general-relativity independent-work project) and one of the figures of twentieth-century theoretical physics — articulated his most concentrated statement of the program of physics in the 1983 essay "Law Without Law" [Wheeler 1983, in J. ## XVIII.1 Wheeler's Central Thesis: "No Elementary Phenomenon Is a Phenomenon Until It Is a Registered (Observed) Phenomenon"

Wheeler's most-repeated formulation in "Law Without Law," appearing in multiple sections of the essay, is the doctrine he attributed to Bohr in modern form: *"No elementary phenomenon is a phenomenon until it is a registered (observed) phenomenon."* Wheeler elaborates: a phenomenon is not yet a phenomenon until it has been brought to a close by an *irreversible act of amplification* such as the blackening of a grain of silver bromide emulsion or the triggering of a photodetector. The doctrine is Wheeler's most direct articulation of quantum measurement: the act of registration is constitutive of the phenomenon, not merely revelatory of a pre-existing fact.

**Theorem XVIII.1 (Wheeler's "registered phenomenon" identified with the apparatus-performed McGucken-Wick rotation).** *Wheeler's "irreversible act of amplification" that brings the elementary phenomenon to a close, the locus of the act of registration, is, under the McGucken framework's account, the apparatus-performed McGucken-Wick rotation at the measurement event, established at Theorem IX.13.10 (the McGucken Measurement Theorem). Wheeler's "indelible record" of the measurement is the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel-only +ic-orientation that the apparatus inherits from the macroscopic Compton-Brownian process.*

*(iii) **The rotation is what brings the pre-phenomenon to "close."** Before the rotation, the 4D wavefunction $\Psi(\mathbf x, x_4)$ on the McGucken Space $\mathcal M_G$ carries the complete pre-phenomenon content (Theorem IX.13.10.B.1's claim 1.A); after the rotation, the 3D cross-section reading $\psi(\mathbf x, t) = \Psi(\mathbf x, ict)$ at the McGucken-constraint locus has registered one definite branch with Born probability $|c_k|^2$ (Theorem IX.13.10.B.1's claim 1.C). ## XVIII.2 Wheeler's Line of Demarcation: "We Possess Today No Mathematical or Legalistic Formula for What the Line Is or Where It Is to Be Drawn"

Wheeler raises in "Law Without Law" the question of the line of demarcation between observer-participator and system under view. He records a verbatim dialogue with his interlocutor:

*"Do we possess today any mathematical or legalistic formula for what the line is or where it is to be drawn?"*

*"No."*

*"Then what is important about this demarcation?"*

*"Existence, yes; position, no."*

Wheeler's claim is : the line's *existence* as a feature is the without-which-nothing of every elementary quantum phenomenon, but the line's *position*. Its mathematical or legalistic specification — is unavailable to the orthodox tradition. Wheeler quotes Leibniz: *"Omnibus ex nihil ducendis sufficit unum"*. For producing everything out of nothing, one principle is enough. Wheeler proposes that "the necessity to draw a line between the observer-participator and the system under view" is the candidate for that single principle — or, as he writes, "the clue to the central principle in constructing out of nothing everything."

Wheeler's "existence, yes; position, no" answer is, under the McGucken framework, upgraded to "existence, yes; position, also yes": the position of the line is the modulus operation, with the four Born-rule requirements (R1)–(R4) distributed across the boundary in the manner established at Corollary IX.13.10.B.4. R3 (phase invariance) the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel; R4 (bilinearity) the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel; R1 (reality) and R2 (non-negativity) boundary-imposed by the apparatus.*

*Proof.* The Modulus-Boundary Corollary (Corollary IX.13.10.B.4) establishes the modulus operation $|\,\cdot\,|^2$ as the exact boundary between the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's derivational reach and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's apparatus registration, with the four Born-rule requirements distributed across the boundary with each requirement on a definite side. ## XVIII.3 Wheeler's Challenge: Derive Quantum Mechanics from the Requirement That the Universe Have a Way to Come Into Being

In a verbatim exchange with his interlocutor in "Law Without Law," Wheeler raises the converse direction of the relation between the quantum and the requirement that the universe come into being:

*"Let me ask if your reasoning couldn't be turned around. You talk of the observer-participancy of quantum theory as the mechanism for the Universe to come into being. If that is a proper way of speaking, would the converse not also hold: The strange necessity of the quantum as we see it everywhere in the scheme of physics comes from the requirement that—via observer-participancy—the Universe should have a way to come into being?"*

*"Your point is exciting indeed. If true—and it is attractive—it should provide someday a means to derive quantum mechanics from the requirement that the Universe must have a way to come into being."*

Wheeler's delayed-choice experiment, articulated in "Law Without Law" through both the laboratory beam-splitter (fig. 4 of the essay) and the cosmological-scale version using the gravitational lens at quasar 0957+561A,B (figs. 5 and 6 of the essay), is Wheeler's most direct empirical-thought-experimental demonstration of observer-participancy. ## XVIII.6 Wheeler's "Law Without Law": The Statistical-dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and Deterministic-dx₄/dt=ic the Algebraic Channel Structure

Wheeler's most challenging claim in "Law Without Law" is his proposal that the laws of physics themselves are statistical at the foundation, that physical regularities emerge from the multitudinous individual quantum acts of observer-participancy in the way that thermodynamic regularities emerge from molecular chaos. *"Individual events. Events beyond law. Events so numerous and so uncoordinated that, flaunting their freedom from formula, they yet fabricate firm form."*
