*Wheeler's verbatim formulation — "Individual events. Events beyond law. Events so numerous and so uncoordinated that, flaunting their freedom from formula, they yet fabricate firm form" — is, under the McGucken framework, that the apparatus's individual cross-section readings (the registered phenomena) are statistically distributed via the Born rule, with the macroscopic empirical claims of the universe being the statistical aggregate of these individual readings. The "firm form" Wheeler refers to is the law-like content of macroscopic observation, which is the convergent overdetermination supplied by the dual-channel architecture: the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's deterministic content and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's statistically-distributed cross-section readings together produce the empirical claims of the universe at every scale from the individual quantum event through the cosmological scale.*

*Proof.* The dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel deterministic content (4D unitary evolution, Stone's theorem, canonical commutator, Heisenberg uncertainty, Schrödinger equation) is established across the 23-theorem QM content of [3], with Theorems 5.1, 7.2, 8.2, 9.1 of [70] supplying the specific operator-algebraic structure. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel statistical content (Born-rule cross-section reading, apparatus-performed Wick rotation, Compton-Brownian process) is established at Theorem IX.13.10 of the present paper, [4], and [70, Theorem 7.4]. The algebraic structureS is established at Theorems IX.13.10.B.1 through IX.13.10.B.3. The identification of Wheeler's "law without law" with the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel-statistical / the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel-deterministic derivational disjointness is by direct correspondence: Wheeler's "events beyond law" $\leftrightarrow$ the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's apparatus cross-section readings as the locus of the statistical content; Wheeler's "firm form" $\leftrightarrow$ the macroscopic convergent overdetermination supplied by the dual-channel architecture. ∎

## XVIII.7 The Student-Master Tradition and the Duty of Engagement

**Remark XVIII.7 (the student-master tradition and the duty of engagement with the master's work).** *The Western scientific tradition, in addition to its commitment to simple principles documented at Theorem IX.13.10.B.12 and Table IX.13.10.D.A, carries a distinct ethical commitment that is part of its living inheritance: the student's duty to engage seriously with the master's work, to respect what was articulated, to understand what was asked, and to attempt to stand on the master's shoulders so as to see further. The tradition has carried this commitment from Aristotle's engagement with Plato, through Aquinas's engagement with Aristotle, through Galileo's engagement with Aristotle and Archimedes, through Newton's "If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of Giants" (letter to Hooke, 5 February 1675/76), through Einstein's engagement with Maxwell, Lorentz, and Poincaré, to the foundations-of-physics work of the present generation engaging with Bohr, Einstein, von Neumann, Dirac, Heisenberg, Schrödinger, and Wheeler.*

*The present section is offered as my dutiful engagement with the work of my undergraduate research advisor, John Archibald Wheeler. Wheeler's "Law Without Law" of 1983 articulated the program of physics in its most demanding form: derive quantum mechanics from the requirement that the universe have a way to come into being; identify the line of demarcation between observer-participator and system; account for the elementary phenomenon as the act of observer-participancy; account for the laws of physics themselves as statistical at the foundation; account for the self-excited-circuit structure of the participatory universe. Wheeler proposed the program but did not supply the principle that would meet it. He left the search to the next generation — to his students and theirs.*

*The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, articulated in my UNC Chapel Hill dissertation appendix of 1998–1999 (eight years after the Princeton independent-work projects under Wheeler in Fall 1989), developed through Moving Dimensions Theory posts on Usenet in 2001, formalised through FQXi essay contest papers in 2008–2013, expanded through books in 2016–2017, and brought to its current rigorous formulation through the dual-channel architecture of [70, 76, 3, 4, 5] and the present paper, is offered as my attempt to meet Wheeler's challenge at the principle. The principle is the active-expansion requirement that the universe comes into being at every event through the active expansion of $x_4$ at velocity $c$; the principle supplies the line of demarcation as the modulus boundary; the principle supplies the irreversible act of amplification as the apparatus-performed Wick rotation; the principle supplies the self-excited circuit as the active-expansion structure of $\mathcal M_G$; the principle supplies the "law without law" structure as the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel-statistical / the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel-deterministic dual-channel disjointness.*

*I cannot know whether the McGucken framework is the right framework. The tradition has corrected itself repeatedly across two and a half millennia: Euclid's parallel postulate, Newton's absolute time, Maxwell's luminiferous ether, all reformulated by subsequent generations as the understanding advanced. What I can offer is faithful engagement with the master's work in the form of a candidate principle that meets the specific challenges Wheeler articulated, expressed with the rigor the tradition has carried since Euclid, and acknowledged as a contribution to the cumulative structure of physics rather than as a final answer. Wheeler asked his students to make all possible mistakes as fast as possible and to recognize them; the framework is my attempt at that task, with the explicit retractions of overclaimed content (Remark IX.13.10.B.10) and the tier-delimitation of Theorem IX.13.15.3.B serving as the record that the framework is offered in the spirit of inquiry the master valued.*

*To Wheeler, with the gratitude of a student who has tried to stand on his shoulders so as to see further: the work continues. The framework is offered in the spirit of "Law Without Law", that the universe has a way to come into being, that the act of observer-participancy is central, that the line of demarcation is the without-which-nothing of the elementary phenomenon, and that physics is the attempt to derive the laws of the world from a principle as simple and as deep as the world admits. Whether $dx_4/dt = ic$ is that principle is a question for the foundations-of-physics community to determine over the coming decades. What can be said now is that the framework engages with each of the specific challenges Wheeler posed in "Law Without Law," with the rigor the tradition requires and with the acknowledgment of what remains open that the master's example demands.*

# XIX. The Meta-Theorem on Paradox Resolution: Why dx₄/dt = ic's Dual-Channel Architecture Naturally Resolves the Paradoxes and Contradictions of Foundational Physics, and the Heroic-Scientific-Philosophical Tradition of Finding the Simple Truth

The dual-channel architecture of $dx_4/dt = ic$ exhibits a property that explains the framework's pattern of paradox-resolution across the preceding sections: **every paradox in foundational physics is, by its own internal logical structure, a demand for a algebraic structureU** — two elements that are simultaneously related (otherwise they would not be in conversation with each other) and disjoint (otherwise they would not be in tension with each other), and the dual-channel architecture of one principle with two disjoint readings is what such a algebraic structureU looks like in its simplest mathematically-defensible form. The framework does not dissolve paradoxes one by one through different cleverness; it dissolves them by the same four-step pattern, because the architecture is what the form of a paradox demands.

This is the **Meta-Theorem on Paradox Resolution**. It is the philosophy of the framework: the methodological reason that one short equation can dissolve impasses across the foundations of quantum mechanics, the foundations of general relativity, the foundations of thermodynamics, and the foundations of cosmology. The meta-theorem connects $dx_4/dt = ic$ to the tradition of Western science — what Wheeler called *the Noble in physics*: the search for the simple idea behind it all, articulated in a single short equation, from which the seeming-contradictions of the standard frameworks dissolve when the algebraic structureU is recognized.

I formalise this through six numbered statements (Theorem XIX.1 — the form of a paradox; Theorem XIX.2 — why single-channel frameworks cannot resolve paradoxes; Theorem XIX.3 — the four-step pattern of dual-channel paradox resolution; Theorem XIX.4 — the worked list of dissolved paradoxes; Theorem XIX.5 — the Heroic-Scientific-Philosophical tradition of finding the Simple Truth; Remark XIX.6 — the methodological commitment the framework inherits from the tradition), one detailed left-justified 10pt table (Table XIX.A — the eight worked dissolved paradoxes with channel-assignment), and a closing companion-paper cross-reference to [Companion 2026, *The Orthodox Postulate-Accumulation Pattern in Foundational Physics*] which works the ten-postulate accumulation pattern in detail.

## XIX.1 the Form of a Paradox

**Theorem XIX.1 (The form of a paradox in foundational physics is the simultaneous relatedness-and-disjointness of two elements).** *Take any paradox in foundational physics — wave-particle duality, the measurement problem, EPR-Bell non-locality, the black-hole information paradox, the unitarity-versus-randomness contradiction, Maudlin's three measurement problems, the determinism-versus-Born-statistics tension, the cosmological-versus-thermodynamic arrow of time, the locality-versus-entanglement tension, the time-symmetry-versus-arrow-of-time tension. The form is invariant across all of them:*

*— **Element X** is asserted by the orthodox framework on one set of grounds: experimental evidence supporting Claim X, mathematical derivation forcing Claim X, necessity requiring Claim X, a cherished axiom that entails Claim X.*

*— **Element Y** is asserted by the orthodox framework on a different set of grounds: a separate body of experimental evidence supporting Claim Y, a different mathematical derivation forcing Claim Y, a different necessity requiring Claim Y, a different cherished axiom that entails Claim Y.*

*— **The relatedness**: X and Y are about the same physical phenomenon, or the same physical system, or the same physical process. They are meet at a point, they share a referent, they participate in the same physical situation.*

*— **The disjointness**: X and Y assert things that cannot both be true under a single-channel account of the orthodox framework. X requires Y to be false, and Y requires X to be false, when read on the orthodox framework's single available channel.*

*This form characterizes every paradox in foundational physics. The simultaneous relatedness-and-disjointness is what a paradox IS. The orthodox response, almost without exception, is to deny one of the two horns by adding a postulate that obscures it; the consequence is the postulate-accumulation pattern documented in detail at [Companion 2026]. The McGucken framework's response is different: to recognize that the two horns are dual readings of a single source. The dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel readings of $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the source supplying the relatedness (one principle) and the algebraic structureE supplying the disjointness (the two channels share no intermediate machinery between the principle and the conclusion, established at Definition IX.26.2's Dual-Channel Disjointness Predicate).*

*Proof.* By inspection of representative paradoxes:

*Unitarity-versus-randomness.* X = quantum mechanics is strictly unitary (Schrödinger evolution, information conservation). Y = randomness is genuine in measurement, thermal noise, chaos, and vacuum fluctuations. Relatedness: both claims are about the same quantum-mechanical substrate. Disjointness: a strictly unitary substrate cannot support genuine randomness under a single-channel account because unitary dynamics is deterministic and time-reversible.

*Determinism-versus-Born-statistics in measurement.* X = the Schrödinger equation determines $|\psi(t)\rangle$ uniquely given $|\psi(0)\rangle$. Y = the measurement outcome is probabilistic with the Born rule giving the distribution. Relatedness: both claims are about the same wavefunction at the same time. Disjointness: a uniquely-determined wavefunction cannot have multiple equally-probable outcomes under a single-channel account.

*Locality-versus-entanglement.* X = quantum field theory is local (operators at spacelike-separated points commute). Y = entangled particles exhibit Bell-violating correlations that cannot be explained by local hidden variables. Relatedness: both claims are about spacelike-separated systems. Disjointness: strict locality cannot support Bell-violating correlations under a single-channel account.

*Information-conservation-versus-Hawking-radiation.* X = unitarity preserves information through every physical process. Y = Hawking radiation is thermal and appears to destroy the information of matter that fell into the black hole. Relatedness: both claims are about the same black-hole evaporation process. Disjointness: strict unitarity cannot accommodate thermal information loss under a single-channel account.

*Time-symmetry-versus-arrow-of-time.* X = the fundamental dynamics (Hamiltonian, Schrödinger evolution, Einstein equations) is time-symmetric. Y = the empirical arrow of time is undeniable (we remember the past not the future, entropy increases, etc.). Relatedness: both claims are about the same physical universe at the same time. Disjointness: a time-symmetric fundamental dynamics cannot support an empirical arrow of time under a single-channel account.

The form (X, Y, relatedness, disjointness) holds across all five paradoxes; by enumeration across the foundational-physics literature, the form holds across every paradox in the foundations. ∎

## XIX.2 Why Single-Channel Frameworks Cannot Resolve Paradoxes

**Theorem XIX.2 (Single-channel frameworks cannot resolve paradoxes; the resolution requires a source supplying both horns as dual readings).** *A single-channel framework — orthodox quantum mechanics treating the Schrödinger equation alone, general relativity treating the metric alone, classical statistical mechanics treating the Hamiltonian alone — has, by its own commitments, only one channel through which the foundations of the theory flows. When confronted with a paradox of the form (X, Y, relatedness, disjointness) characterized by Theorem XIX.1, the single-channel framework has only three options:*

*(i) **Deny X by postulating a new piece of machinery that obscures the X horn.** This is the Bohmian response to the measurement problem (denying claim 1.A by postulating hidden particle positions), the GRW response (denying claim 1.B by postulating spontaneous-localization terms), and one direction of orthodox accommodation across many paradoxes. The cost: the postulated machinery is itself often unmotivated, unobservable, or in tension with other parts of the standard framework.*

*(ii) **Deny Y by postulating a new piece of machinery that obscures the Y horn.** This is the Many-Worlds response to the measurement problem (denying claim 1.C by postulating an ontological multiverse), the Past-Hypothesis response to the arrow of time (denying the explanatory burden by postulating an inexplicably low-entropy initial state), the ER = EPR response to the locality-versus-entanglement tension (denying the apparent non-locality by postulating Planck-scale wormholes), and one direction of orthodox accommodation across many paradoxes. The cost is the same as (i).*

*(iii) **Live with the paradox by treating it as a feature rather than a bug.** This is the response of the operational and instrumentalist traditions ("shut up and calculate"), of Copenhagen-school accommodation that treats complementarity as primitive rather than derived, and of much foundations-of-physics work that treats paradoxes as objects of philosophical contemplation rather than as impasses to be resolved. The cost: the framework remains incomplete; the principles continue to recede.*

*The failure mode of all three responses is the same: none of them recognizes that the simultaneous relatedness-and-disjointness of X and Y is itself a demand for a source-with-dual-readings architecture. The single-channel framework has only one channel; the paradox is asking for two. The mismatch between the two-channel demand of the paradox and the one-channel supply of the orthodox framework is the source of the postulate-accumulation pattern: each new postulate is a desperate attempt to simulate the missing second channel using machinery added by hand.*

*Proof.* By exhaustion of the options available to a single-channel framework. A framework with one channel can either obscure X (option i), obscure Y (option ii), or accept the paradox without resolution (option iii). None of these options produces a derivation that supplies both X and Y as theorems of the framework's foundational principles. The only mechanism that supplies both X and Y as theorems is a framework with two channels — a principle from which X descends through one derivational pathway and Y descends through a separate derivational pathway, with the two pathways being disjoint at the intermediate level but converging on the same source. This is the architecture that the dual-channel account of $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies (Definition IX.26.2's Dual-Channel Disjointness Predicate). ∎

## XIX.5 The Heroic-Scientific-Philosophical Tradition of Finding the Simple Truth

**Theorem XIX.5 (The Heroic-Scientific-Philosophical tradition: the philosophical commitment to seeking the simple source from which apparent contradictions descend as dual readings).** *The Western scientific tradition has, from its origins in Euclid's $\textit{Elements}$ (~300 BCE) through Wheeler's $\textit{Law Without Law}$ (1983) and the present, exhibited a specific methodological-philosophical commitment that is part of its living inheritance and that the McGucken framework inherits and serves: when two claims about physical reality appear contradictory, the response is to seek the underlying source from which both claims descend as dual readings. This is the philosophical move that distinguishes the Heroic-Scientific-Philosophical tradition from the postulate-accumulation tradition that has dominated foundational physics since the mid-twentieth century. The tradition's instances exhibit a consistent pattern of one-principle-with-multiple-readings commitment:*

*— **Euclid** (c. 300 BCE) made this move when his five postulates, twenty-three definitions, and five common notions supplied a source from which both the algebraic relations (the Pythagorean theorem, the parallelogram law, the regular-solid theorems) and the geometric constructions (the angle-bisector, the perpendicular dropped from a point to a line, the inscribed-and-circumscribed-circle theorems) descended as dual readings of the same axiomatic foundation. Algebra and geometry were dual readings of the axioms.*

*— **Newton** (1687) made this move when his three laws of motion plus the inverse-square law of gravitation supplied a source from which both the celestial-mechanical theorems (Kepler's three laws, the motion of the planets, the precession of the equinoxes) and the terrestrial-mechanical theorems (the parabolic trajectory of a projectile, the period of a pendulum, the tides) descended as dual readings of the same axiomatic foundation. Celestial and terrestrial mechanics were the same science under one set of laws.*

*— **Maxwell** (1873) made this move when his four equations of the electromagnetic field supplied a source from which both the electrical phenomena (Coulomb's law, Ohm's law, capacitors and resistors) and the magnetic phenomena (Ampère's law, the magnetic deflection of compass needles, electromagnets) descended as dual readings of the same field-theoretic foundation. Electricity and magnetism, treated as separate phenomena throughout the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries, were unified by Maxwell as dual readings of the same electromagnetic field.*

*— **Einstein** (1905, 1915) made this move when his special-relativity postulates (the constancy of $c$, the relativity principle) supplied a source from which both the mechanical phenomena (time dilation, length contraction, $E = mc^2$) and the electromagnetic phenomena (the Lorentz transformation of fields, the invariance of Maxwell's equations under Lorentz boosts) descended as dual readings of the same kinematic foundation. Mechanics and electromagnetism, separately understood since Newton and Maxwell, were unified by special relativity as dual readings of the same kinematic axioms. The 1915 general relativity then supplied gravitation as the curvature of the same spacetime that special relativity had established as the kinematic substrate, with both terrestrial gravity and cosmological dynamics descending from the equivalence principle as dual readings.*

*— **de Broglie** (1924) made this move when his single relation $\lambda = h/p$ supplied a source from which both the particle phenomena (the photoelectric effect, Compton scattering, the discrete energy levels of atoms) and the wave phenomena (electron diffraction, Davisson-Germer 1927, the interference of matter) descended as dual readings of the same matter-wave duality. Wave and particle, treated as contradictory throughout the early years of quantum mechanics, were unified by de Broglie as dual readings of $\lambda = h/p$. The Bohr complementarity that followed was the philosophical articulation of this dual-reading structure.*

*— **Wheeler** (1983) made this move when his call for the single principle from which the laws of physics descend was the methodological articulation of the same tradition; Wheeler's "$\textit{Omnibus ex nihil ducendis sufficit unum}$" (quoting Leibniz) was the explicit invocation of the one-principle-with-multiple-readings commitment as the form of the program of physics.*

*The McGucken framework's $dx_4/dt = ic$ is offered in this Heroic-Scientific-Philosophical tradition. The principle is one equation. The principle has two disjoint readings (the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel algebraic-symmetry, the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel geometric-propagation), with the disjointness established at Definition IX.26.2's Dual-Channel Disjointness Predicate and the convergence on identical physics established by the 47-theorem dual-channel architecture of [3]. The seeming-contradictions of orthodox foundational physics — unitarity-versus-randomness, determinism-versus-Born-statistics, locality-versus-entanglement, information-conservation-versus-Hawking-radiation, time-symmetry-versus-arrow-of-time, and the eight others in Table XIX.A — are pairs of dual readings of the same source, each pair related (by sharing the source $dx_4/dt = ic$) and disjoint (by sharing no intermediate machinery between source and conclusion).*

*The simultaneous relatedness-and-disjointness that every paradox demands is exactly what one-principle-with-two-channels supplies. ## XIX.6 The Methodological Commitment the Framework Inherits

**Remark XIX.6 (The methodological commitment to finding the Simple Truth, in the spirit of the Fathers of science, physics, and philosophy).** *The Heroic-Scientific-Philosophical tradition's central methodological commitment — finding the simple source from which apparent contradictions descend as dual readings — is what Wheeler called $\textit{the Noble in physics}$ and what the present author received from Wheeler as the moral charge of a student. The commitment is the recognition that the paradoxes and contradictions of foundational physics are demands for the dual-reading architecture that one principle with multiple readings supplies. The orthodox postulate-accumulation pattern is in this sense a methodological-philosophical departure from the tradition: it patches when the tradition asks for derivation; it accumulates when the tradition asks for unification; it accommodates when the tradition asks for resolution at the source.*

*$dx_4/dt = ic$ is offered as my attempt to serve the tradition's methodological commitment at the level of contemporary foundational physics. The principle is simple — one equation, three symbols of physics ($x_4$, $c$, $i$) plus the calculus of derivatives. The principle is adequate to the paradox-resolution task — the dual-channel architecture supplies the simultaneous relatedness-and-disjointness that every paradox demands, with the four-step pattern of Theorem XIX.3 instantiated across the eight worked dissolutions of Table XIX.A and the further dissolutions documented in [Companion 2026]. The principle is in the line of inheritance — it sits in the tradition initiated by Euclid's five postulates, continued by Newton's three laws, advanced by Maxwell's four equations and Einstein's two postulates of relativity, articulated for the contemporary period by Wheeler's call for the single principle in $\textit{Law Without Law}$.*

*Wheeler said to me at Princeton in 1989, in words I have carried as a charge for the thirty-seven years since: the search is for the simple truth, and the duty of the student is to honor the tradition by continuing the search with the rigor the Fathers established and the courage the Fathers exemplified. The framework is offered in that spirit, with the dual-channel architecture as the form the search has identified, the paradox-dissolutions of Table XIX.A as the claim the search has produced, and the explicit retractions of overclaimed content (Remark IX.13.10.B.10, the channel-non-commutativity identity retraction, the signature-lock retraction) as the record that the search proceeds with the acknowledgment of what does not hold alongside the rigorous statement of what does.*

*The simple truth that the framework offers: one equation, two channels, many paradoxes dissolved through the same four-step pattern. The empirical claims of the universe is preserved (every theorem of the framework is anchored to a century or more of experiment); the philosophy is transformed (the paradoxes that the orthodox tradition has treated as features rather than bugs are dissolved by the recognition that they are demands for the dual-reading architecture that $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies). This is the Heroic-Scientific-Philosophical contribution at the level — the contribution that the tradition asks of every generation: faithfulness to the search for the simple truth that the Fathers built and that Wheeler called us to continue.*

# XX. Engagement with Chiara Marletto's Constructor Theory Program: What the Diagnostic Names, and Why dx₄/dt = ic's Dual-Channel Architecture Supplies the Superior Physical, Mathematical, and Ontological Solutions

Chiara Marletto, working with David Deutsch at Oxford, has developed Constructor Theory as a contemporary meta-theoretic program responding to the same orthodox failure $dx_4/dt = ic$ addresses: the inability of the dynamics-plus-initial-conditions paradigm to dissolve the paradoxes of physics. Marletto's diagnostic work — articulated across her 2014 paper with Deutsch ("Constructor theory of information", *Proc. R. Soc. A* 471), her 2021 book *The Science of Can and Can't*, and recent expositions such as the Apple Finch Pudding episode 39 — names the problems with precision. Constructor Theory's contribution is the meta-theoretic insight that **counterfactual (possibility/impossibility) statements carry foundational explanatory power that dynamical-laws-plus-initial-conditions cannot supply**. This insight is real; this paper honors it.

The McGucken framework's relationship to Constructor Theory is one of respect for the diagnostic combined with physical disagreement about the destination. Marletto correctly identifies what is wrong with the orthodox framework. Constructor Theory's response is a meta-theoretic constraint catalog above dynamical laws. The McGucken framework's response is a single physical principle from which the dynamical laws, and the impossibility statements Constructor Theory takes as primitive — descend as theorems through the dual-channel architecture. Where Marletto's program ends in commitment to the Many-Worlds ontological multiverse as the metaphysical cost of taking quantum theory seriously, the McGucken framework preserves the universality Marletto correctly requires while dispensing with the multiverse through the algebraic structureS that distinguishes the 4D wavefunction on $\mathcal M_G$ from its 3D cross-section reading at the apparatus event. The McGucken framework supplies the **superior physical solution** (a derived foundational principle rather than a meta-theoretic constraint), the **superior mathematical solution** (the dual-channel derivational architecture rather than the constructor-theoretic principle-catalog), and the **superior ontological solution** (one principle with two channels rather than the ontological multiverse), while preserving everything Constructor Theory gets right at the diagnostic level.

I formalise this through seven numbered statements (Theorem XX.1. Marletto's diagnostic content honored; Theorem XX.2 — physical-level superiority; Theorem XX.3 — mathematical-level superiority; Theorem XX.4 — ontological-level superiority; Remark XX.5 — the relationship between the two programs as parallel contributions to the same target problem; Theorem XX.6. Marletto's robust-principles bridge with all twelve survivability-robust principles derived from dx₄/dt = ic; Remark XX.7 — dx₄/dt = ic as the bridge Marletto's methodological insight asks for) and two detailed left-justified 10pt tables (Table XX.A — the comparison; Table XX.B — the robust-principles derivation routes).

## XX.1 Marletto's Diagnostic Content Honored

**Theorem XX.1 (Marletto's diagnostic work identifies real problems with the orthodox foundational-physics framework; the McGucken framework agrees with her diagnostic and supplies the response that Constructor Theory does not yet supply).** *Across the Constructor Theory literature and the Apple Finch Pudding 39 exposition, Marletto identifies six diagnostics of the orthodox framework's foundational failures:*

*(i) **The mode-of-explanation must shift.** Orthodox foundational physics has been using the dynamical-laws-plus-initial-conditions paradigm since Newton, and the paradigm has limitations the foundations-of-physics community treats as features rather than bugs. Marletto verbatim: "if there is some problem that in that context seems to be problematic and not solvable, it's always possible to change the mode of explanation."*

*(ii) **The reversibility-irreversibility tension cannot be resolved within the orthodox framework.** Time-symmetric fundamental dynamics cannot account for the empirically real arrow of time. Marletto verbatim: "we know it's difficult to incorporate something like irreversibility in this framework of laws of motion dynamical laws in initial conditions because they are reversible."*

*(iii) **The GR-QM clash is diagnosable as a classical-bit vs qubit information-theoretic incompatibility.** Marletto verbatim: "if you look at the information theory structure of these two theories, the classical laws of physics that Newton formalized in his laws and general relativity's laws. They are all classical from the point of view of information theory. That's not not allowed by general relativity or by special relativity. This is the main reason that's the fundamental reason why these two theories clash with each other."*

*(iv) **Counterfactuals (possibility/impossibility statements) carry foundational explanatory power.** Marletto verbatim: "things that don't happen have have an explanatory power and they are the reason why other things do occur or at least can occur."*

*(v) **Interpretations of quantum mechanics cannot discriminate one another because they are designed to agree on empirical outcomes.** Marletto verbatim: "if you talk about interpretations, it's very difficult to discriminate one interpretation against another because they're all designed to agree on the actual outcomes."*

*(vi) **Quantum mechanics is universal: there is no fudge-line where it stops applying.** Marletto explicitly belongs to the universality camp.*

*The McGucken framework agrees with all six diagnostics. The dual-channel architecture of dx₄/dt = ic is the mode-of-explanation shift Marletto advocates (the active-expansion principle replacing dynamics-plus-initial-conditions on a static-coordinate spacetime, with $x_4 = ict$ as the integrated coordinate shadow of the active expansion). The reversibility-irreversibility tension dissolves into the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's reversibility (Stone-theorem unitary group with $U(-t) = U(t)^{-1}$) and the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's irreversibility (+ic orientation with no -ic counterpart). The GR-QM information-theory clash dissolves because the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel's geometric-propagation account produces the classical-bit structure of GR and the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel's algebraic-symmetry account produces the qubit structure of QM, both as dual readings of one principle. Counterfactual-explanatory power is preserved as theorems of the framework: the impossibility of -ic orientation (no real algebraic counterpart), the no-cloning theorem (from the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing), the Pauli 1933 absence of self-adjoint time operator (at Tier II of the channel-perpendicularity hierarchy), Noether's energy conservation theorem (from $x_4$-translation invariance). Interpretive landscape discrimination is achieved at the level by operating one level upstream of QM, with the Hilbert space co-generated from dx₄/dt = ic via the four-level cascade (Theorem IX.13.10.B.7) rather than presupposed. QM is universal because dx₄/dt = ic applies at every event of $\mathcal M_G$, with no scale at which the principle stops applying.*

*The diagnostic content is honored at every point. The physical disagreement is about the form of the response, which is what Theorems XX.2 through XX.4 address.*

## XX.6 The Relationship Between the Two Programs

**Remark XX.5 (Constructor Theory and the McGucken framework as parallel responses to the same orthodox failure, with Constructor Theory diagnosing and the McGucken framework solving).** *Constructor Theory and the McGucken framework are not in opposition; both diagnose the same orthodox failure of the dynamics-plus-initial-conditions paradigm; both propose the mode-of-explanation shift that Marletto names as the methodological response; both honor counterfactual-explanatory power as important; both require universality of quantum mechanics; both reject the postulate-accumulation pattern that the orthodox tradition has used to patch over the paradoxes.*

*The relationship between the two programs is hierarchical. Constructor Theory's diagnostic content, the six diagnostics catalogued at Theorem XX.1, characterizes the problems with precision and is honored throughout the McGucken framework. Constructor Theory's response, a meta-theoretic constraint catalog above dynamical laws, operates one level removed from where the physical principle would sit; it constrains the laws without generating them; it takes the impossibility statements as primitive rather than deriving them. The McGucken framework occupies the foundational-physical-principle level that Constructor Theory does not yet occupy: dx₄/dt = ic is a specific physical principle from which the dynamical laws and the impossibility statements descend as theorems through the dual-channel architecture.*

*scholarly position is that Constructor Theory characterizes the problems well, and that the McGucken framework supplies the superior physical, mathematical, and ontological solutions. The Marletto-Deutsch program deserves credit for the diagnostic precision, the methodological insight about counterfactuals, and the rejection of the postulate-accumulation pattern. The McGucken framework supplies what Constructor Theory's diagnostic identifies as needed: a single physical principle, observable in every empirical fact of physics, generating the empirical claims of QM and GR through disjoint channels, with the impossibility statements Constructor Theory takes as primitive supplied as derived theorems, with the universality preserved without the Many-Worlds ontological multiverse, and with Newton's Rule I satisfied at the level.*

*The framework is offered to the foundations-of-physics community — including Marletto and Deutsch as the most prominent contemporary practitioners of the constructor-theoretic program — as the foundational-physical-principle response to the diagnostic Constructor Theory has correctly articulated. The two programs are parallel contributions to the same target problem; the McGucken framework's contribution is at the principle from which the diagnostic content Marletto identifies descends as derived fact. Where Constructor Theory points correctly at what is wrong with the orthodox framework, the McGucken framework supplies what is needed to replace it.*

The active-expansion account dx₄/dt = ic appears in the priority record across six eras of my work, beginning with my Princeton undergraduate junior-year projects of 1989–1990 under John Archibald Wheeler (fall 1989, general relativity) and Joseph H. Taylor (spring 1990, quantum measurement and Bell's theorem) and continuing to the present.

## Era 0. Princeton Junior Year (1989–1990): Two Independent-Work Projects under Wheeler and Taylor

The conceptual foundation of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic was laid in two Princeton University junior-year independent-work projects I conducted under two of the figures of 20th-century theoretical physics: **John Archibald Wheeler** (Fall 1989, on general relativity) and **Joseph H. Taylor** (Spring 1990, on quantum measurement and Bell's theorem). The Princeton requirement that the second junior project be supervised by a different advisor from the first placed me under Taylor for the Spring 1990 quantum-foundations work, while the Fall 1989 general-relativity work had been supervised by Wheeler. At the time of the second project (Spring 1990), **Taylor had not yet received the Nobel Prize** — that recognition would come in 1993, three years later, awarded jointly with Russell Hulse for the discovery of binary pulsar PSR B1913+16 and the first indirect detection of gravitational waves through the observed orbital decay matching Einstein's quadrupole-radiation formula to better than 0.3% accuracy. I was enrolled in Taylor's experimental-physics course in Spring 1990 — a hands-on laboratory course in which physics was grounded in the *physical*, as the discipline must always be grounded in the physical. The two junior-year projects, taken together, constitute the foundational documents of the McGucken Principle's intellectual lineage: Wheeler's relativistic-geometry and Taylor's empirical-quantum-measurement content, brought together a decade later in the active-expansion account of x₄ = ict as dx₄/dt = ic.

Taylor's experimental-physics orientation traces back through the Einstein-Galileo lineage. Albert Einstein, in his essay *On the Method of Theoretical Physics* (the Herbert Spencer Lecture, Oxford, 10 June 1933), placed Galileo at the origin of modern physics in the following verbatim terms: *"Propositions arrived at by purely logical means are completely empty as regards reality. Because Galileo saw this, and particularly because he drummed this into the scientific world, he is the father of modern physics — of modern science altogether."* This Einsteinian commitment, that physics must be grounded in the physical, that propositions arrived at by purely logical means are empty as regards reality, that experimental-physical confirmation is the foundational ground of theory — is the methodological commitment Taylor embodied as the advisor of the Spring 1990 quantum-measurement project and the author of the binary-pulsar empirical confirmation of gravitational radiation. The McGucken framework's emphasis on *experimental* verification — on the Bayesian-likelihood-ratio $\gtrsim 10^{141}$ confirmation of the dual-channel architecture against the entire confirmed empirical claims of GR + QM (Theorem IX.26.11 of [3]), on the McGucken Cosmology's first-place finishes across twelve independent observational tests with zero free dark-sector parameters [5], and on the seven post-1998-dissertation precision tests of §Era 1.A — is the -methodological descendant of the Galileo–Einstein–Taylor commitment to *grounding physics in the physical*. The McGucken Principle is the active expansion of a fourth dimension at velocity c relative to the three spatial dimensions, with the entire confirmed empirical claims of modern foundational physics (the 47 GR + QM theorems of [3], the twelve cosmological tests of [5], the seven post-1998-dissertation precision tests of §Era 1.A) descending from this single fact about the manifold.

The Spring 1990 Junior Paper documents the framework's origin. The Spring 1990 junior-year independent-work paper **"Within a Context: A Discussion of Paradoxes in Quantum Theory between Curiosity and Perseverance"** [68], submitted to Princeton's Physics Department under Taylor as advisor of record (with Wheeler acknowledged as advisor of the prior Fall 1989 general-relativity project), exhibits in its title page, table of contents, twenty-one-page body, four figures, and supplementary additional-references page the formal mathematical and conceptual content of the paradoxes from which the McGucken framework subsequently emerged. The paper opens with R. P. Feynman's verbatim epigraph on the Einstein-Rosen-Podolsky paradox (*Physics Today*, Vol. 38, No. 4, p. 47): *"We have always had a great deal of difficulty, understanding the world view, that quantum mechanics represents. Every new idea, takes a generation or two, until it becomes obvious that there is no real problem."* The body is a Socratic dialogue between two figures — *Curiosity* and *Perseverance*. Modelled on the Bohr-Einstein epistolary tradition and on Wheeler's own dialogue style in *Geons, Black Holes, and Quantum Foam*. The Table of Contents lists five sections: **I. The EPR Paradox; II. Bell's Theorem; III. Delayed Choice; IV. Wigner's Friend; V. Conclusion.** Five additional references on the supplementary page: Clauser–Shimony 1978 (*Bell's Theorem: Experimental Tests and Implications*, Reports on Progress in Physics 41, 1881–1927); d'Espagnat 1979 (*The Quantum Theory and Reality*, Scientific American 241(11), 128–66); Mermin 1985 (*Is the Moon Really There When Nobody Looks?*, Physics Today 38(4), 38); Rae 1986 (*Quantum Physics: Illusion or Reality?*, Cambridge University Press); Redhead 1987 (*Incompleteness, Nonlocality, and Realism*, Clarendon Press, Oxford).

**§I The EPR Paradox.** §I opens with Einstein's foundational commitment from the Bohr-Einstein exchange — *"Physics is an attempt to grasp reality as it is thought independently of its being observed"* — against Bohr's reply that *"these conditions (of measurement) constitute an inherent element of any phenomenon to which the term 'physical' reality can be attached. This requires a final renunciation of the classical ideal of causality and a radical revision of our attitude towards the problem of physical reality."* The singlet state $|\Psi\rangle = (1/\sqrt 2)(|+\!-\rangle - |-\!+\rangle)$ is introduced on page 5. The EPR-locality argument is presented verbatim — *"Einstein's locality postulate, based on his laws of relativity, asserts that a measurement at some point in space can help us to find out about the real features existing at some distance $\Delta x$, but it cannot modify them before the time $\Delta x/c$ needed for light to cover that distance"* — together with the EPR criterion of physical reality and the EPR conclusion that *"the quantum-mechanical description of physical reality given by wave functions is not complete."* Bohr's reply on page 6 — *"an influence on the very conditions which define the possible types of predictions regarding the future behavior of the system"* — sets the stage for the central question Curiosity poses: *"Bohr refers to some type of an 'influence' which must result from an action at a speed greater than that of light. Suppose we adhere to Einstein's locality postulate, based on relativity, which asserts that there can be no influence that is propagated faster than light. Is there some type of resolution to this apparent paradox?"* The Princeton paper does not resolve the apparent paradox; it formalizes it.

**§II Bell's Theorem — the full Bohm-Bell mathematical apparatus.** §II supplies the formal mathematics. Page 7 states Bell's two statements verbatim — *"1. Einstein's locality postulate imposes constraints on the predictions of spin correlations in the form of inequalities. 2. The predictions of quantum theory for the EPR-Bohm experiment violate these inequalities implied by Einstein's locality."*, and announces the *Quantum Probability* and *Hidden Variable Probability* parallel computations. Pages 8–12 carry out the full Bohm spin-1/2 reformulation: single-particle eigenstates of $\sigma_z$ with $\Psi_{z+} = (1, 0)^T$; the Pauli-matrix rotation operator $U_x = \exp(-i\theta s_x/\hbar) = \exp(-i\theta\sigma_x/2) = \cos(\theta/2) - i\sigma_x\sin(\theta/2)$ derived from the Pauli identity $\sigma_x^2 = 1$; the rotated single-particle state $|\Psi_{b+}\rangle = \cos(\theta_{ab}/2)|+\rangle + i\sin(\theta_{ab}/2)|-\rangle$ verified as the +1-eigenvector of $\sigma_b = \sigma_x\cos\theta_{ab} - \sigma_y\sin\theta_{ab}$; the two-particle extension via commuting spin operators $s = s(1) + s(2)$; the two complete sets of commuting observables (Set A: $s(1)^2, s_z(1), s(2)^2, s_z(2)$; Set B: $s^2, s_z, s(1)^2, s(2)^2$); the lowering-operator construction $|s=1, m=0\rangle = (1/\sqrt 2)(|+\!-\rangle + |-\!+\rangle)$; the singlet $|\Psi\rangle = (1/\sqrt 2)(|+\!-\rangle - |-\!+\rangle) = |s=0, m=0\rangle$ as the orthogonal complement; the rotation of particle 2 by $\theta_{ab}$ giving $|\phi\rangle = U_x(2)\Psi_{z++} = \cos\theta_{ab}|+\!+\rangle + i\sin\theta_{ab}|+\!-\rangle$; the inner product $\langle\phi|\Psi\rangle = i/\sqrt 2 (\sin\theta_{ab})$; and the closing quantum-mechanical probability, page 12, verbatim, $P_{++} = (1/2)\sin^2(\theta_{ab}/2) = P_{--}$. **Figure 1** (Spin Correlation Thought Experiment) presents the three-axis detector geometry: detectors 1a and 2b on axes $a$ and $b$, detectors 1b and 2c on axes $b$ and c, detectors 1a and 2c on axes $a$ and c.

**§II's verbatim Bell-inequality contradiction at $\theta_{ab} = \theta_{bc} = \pi/3$, $\theta_{ac} = 2\pi/3$.** The paper carries the parallel hidden-variable computation through to the explicit numerical contradiction on page 14: under the three-axis configuration with $\theta_{ab} = \theta_{bc} = \pi/3$ and $\theta_{ac} = 2\pi/3$, the hidden-variable inequality demands $\sin^2(\theta_{ab}/2) + \sin^2(\theta_{bc}/2) \geq \sin^2(\theta_{ac}/2)$, equivalently $\sin^2(\pi/6) + \sin^2(\pi/6) \geq \sin^2(\pi/3)$, equivalently $1/2 \geq 3/4$ — **a contradiction**. The Princeton paper closes the §II argument with Curiosity's verbatim line: *"So it seems that we must either abandon our view that there is an objective reality, or we must reject Einstein's postulate of locality! What should we do? This paradox is like a bolt from the blue!"* This is the formal-mathematical statement of the Bell-inequality violation by quantum mechanics — derived in full at Princeton in Spring 1990, four years after the Aspect 1982 confirmation, twenty-five years before the Hensen et al. 2015 loophole-free confirmation, and twenty-eight years before the Big Bell Test 2018.

The Bell verbatim aether quote is the cornerstone of the Princeton paper's relevance to the McGucken framework. §II of the Princeton paper, on page 14, quotes John Bell verbatim on the resolution of the Bell-inequality contradiction. Bell on his own non-resolution: *"Well, you see, I don't really know. For me it's not something where I have a solution to sell! For me, it's a dilemma. I think it's a deep dilemma, and the resolution will not be trivial; it will require a substantial change in the way we look at things. But I would say that the cheapest resolution is something like going back to relativity as it was before Einstein, when people like Lorentz and Poincaré thought there was an aether."* And Bell on the pre-Einstein aether position more formally: *"behind the apparent Lorentz invariance of the phenomena, there is a deeper level which is not Lorentz invariant. What is not sufficiently emphasized in textbooks, is that the pre-Einstein position of Lorentz and Poincaré, Larmor and Fitzgerald was perfectly coherent, and is not inconsistent with relativity theory. The idea that there is an aether, and these Fitzgerald contractions and Larmor dilations occur, and that as a result the instruments do not detect motion through the aether, that is a perfectly coherent point of view."* **Bell's verbatim 1980s call for "a deeper level which is not Lorentz invariant" is what the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic supplies a decade later in the 1998 UNC dissertation Appendix B and a generation later in the full technical-paper corpus of 2024–2026.** The McGucken Principle's deeper level is the active expansion of x₄ at velocity c relative to the three spatial dimensions, with the Lorentz-invariant phenomena emerging as the *integrated shadow* of the active expansion through the transformation x₄ = ict. The Fitzgerald-Larmor contractions and dilations of the pre-Einstein aether position become, in the McGucken framework, theorems of the active-expansion: time dilation is the rotation of a moving entity into the moving fourth dimension (1998 Appendix B p. 154–155); length contraction is the increased probability of the object's quanta residing in the time dimension (1998 Appendix B p. 155). The Princeton paper records Bell's explicit verbatim 1980s call for the resolution that the McGucken Principle subsequently delivers. The author, reading Bell's call in Spring 1990 as a Princeton junior under Taylor's advisorship, internalized the requirement for a "deeper level which is not Lorentz invariant" eight years before the dissertation appendix would articulate that deeper level as the active expansion of the fourth dimension at velocity c.

**§III Delayed Choice. Wheeler's signature thought experiment.** §III presents Wheeler's delayed-choice experiment formally on pages 15–18. Wheeler verbatim on the delayed-choice content (page 15): *"a choice made in the here and now has irretrievable consequences for what one has the right to say about what has already happened in the very earliest days of the universe, long before there was any life on earth."* **Figure 3** presents the full Mach-Zehnder geometry: source S, half-silvered mirror $M_1$, totally-reflecting mirrors $A$ and $B$, "Delayed Choice Region" at the location of the optional second half-silvered mirror $M_2$, and photomultipliers $P_1$ and $P_2$. Pages 16–17 carry out the full delayed-choice analysis: without $M_2$, photons exhibit corpuscular behavior and are counted by $P_1$ or $P_2$ along path $rAr$ or path $tBt$; with $M_2$ inserted, destructive interference at $P_2$ forces all photons to $P_1$, exhibiting wave behavior. The Carrol Alley experiments at the University of Maryland are cited (page 17). Bohr verbatim via Wheeler (page 17): *"In actuality, we have no contradiction. As Bohr said, we have no right to talk about what the photon is doing during its long travel from the point of entry — from the first half-silvered mirror to the point of registration. When you analyze this language that the physicists have fallen into, that physics is about the results of observations — you find that on analysis it evaporates"* (page 18) close §III with the foundational observer-question content. **The Princeton paper's verbatim treatment of Wheeler's delayed-choice content places me in direct intellectual contact with Wheeler's foundational thought-experiment programme one year after Wheeler's call for the *Noble* in physics (autumn 1989 in Jadwin Hall) [27] and eight years before the 1998 UNC dissertation Appendix B's articulation of dx₄/dt = ic.**

**§IV Wigner's Friend — the measurement problem at full Hamiltonian rigor.** §IV presents Wigner's Friend formally on pages 19–21. Mr. Observer state $|A,a\rangle$ with quantum numbers $A$ (observer's readiness state) and $a$ (system's spin component). Time-evolution operator $U = \exp(-iHt/\hbar)$ with Hamiltonian decomposition $H = H_{Mr} + H_s$ before observation, factoring as $U = U_{Mr} U_s$ where $U_{Mr} = \exp(-iH_{Mr}t/\hbar)$ and $U_s = \exp(-iH_s t/\hbar)$. Bell verbatim on quantum mechanics as a "dirty theory."** §V opens with Bell's verbatim statement on the status of quantum mechanics (page 21): *"I am a professional theoretical physicist and I would like to make a clean theory. ### Era 0.C. The Jadwin Hall Conversations, the Photon-as-Tracer Argument, and the Eureka Moment

The autobiographical narrative of the Princeton afternoons during which the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic was conceived is recorded in my published Medium memoir of December 17, 2023 [13]. I discussed the framework with Wheeler in Jadwin Hall in Fall 1989. One fine afternoon in autumn 1989 of my Princeton junior year, just before going running through the Institute for Advanced Study's pastoral fields and the woods that I had made my oasis of peace and quiet in New Jersey, I decided to visit my advisor John Archibald Wheeler. Princeton's Joseph Henry Professor of Physics — in his third-floor Jadwin Hall office. The fall junior project on general relativity that became the basis of Wheeler's later recommendation letter [32] was the immediate context. Wheeler was standing at the window watching the brilliant autumn foliage when I walked through his always-open door, his book-filled, paper-strewn office harkening of the swirling, falling leaves outside as if the same wind arranged both systems. The distinguished Wheeler slowly turned, dressed in his classic suit and tie, his hand gently clenched in a fist holding a piece of chalk, and stated, in his quiet, raspy voice with his blue eyes smiling: *"Today's physics lacks the Noble, and it's your generation's duty to bring it back"* [27]. This was the Wheeler call for the *Noble* in physics — the rhetorical-philosophical seed that animates the entire McGucken corpus. I then asked Wheeler the question I had come to ask, continuing a conversation from a week earlier: *"So a photon doesn't move in the fourth dimension? All of its motion is directed through the three spatial dimensions?"* Wheeler: *"Correct."* I asked: *"So a photon remains stationary in the fourth dimension?"* Wheeler: *"Yes."* The Wheeler verbatim affirmation of the photon-stationary-in-x₄ result is the first foundational result on which the McGucken Principle subsequently rests. In the active-expansion account made precise at Proposition VI.2, the photon's x₄-stationarity content is the pair $\{d\tau = 0,\; \omega_{C} = 0\}$: (i) proper-time degeneracy $d\tau = 0$ along the null worldline (no aging from emission to absorption) and (ii) zero Compton-clock content $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar = 0$ for $m = 0$ (no rest-mass-driven internal x₄-oscillation, in contrast to massive particles whose Compton clock oscillates at $\omega_{C}\tau$); the photon adds no independent x₄-motion beyond the universal expansion, while universal $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ applies at every event of the photon's worldline as at every event of $\mathcal M_{G}$. Notational conventions for the three quantities that appear along a worldline are collected at Appendix N.

I discussed the framework with P. J. E. Peebles in Fall 1989. That same afternoon, I went on to visit P. J. E. Peebles. Princeton's Albert Einstein Professor Emeritus of Science — in whose quantum mechanics class I was then enrolled, using the galleys of Peebles's then-forthcoming textbook *Quantum Mechanics* (now in print as a treatise on the structure of QM). Many had argued that Peebles should have been awarded the Nobel Prize in physics for predicting the cosmic microwave background radiation shortly before Penzias and Wilson accidentally discovered it with the Holmdel Horn Antenna; Peebles did subsequently receive the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics for his theoretical contributions to physical cosmology. The photon-as-tracer argument runs as follows. The synthesis of the Wheeler result (photon stationary in x₄) and the Peebles result (photon distributed on a spherically-symmetric wavefront expanding at velocity c) gives, by purely physical reasoning, the active-expansion result dx₄/dt = ic. The argument is the *photon-as-tracer* argument: a small GPS tracer attached to an eagle remains stationary relative to the eagle as it soars through the air, thusly tracking the eagle's motion in flight; analogously, a photon, which remains stationary relative to the fourth dimension (Wheeler), must track the fourth dimension's motion. Because the photon is distributed on a spherically-symmetric wavefront expanding at velocity c (Peebles) while remaining stationary in the fourth dimension (Wheeler), **the fourth dimension itself must be expanding at velocity c.** This is the active-expansion result. The photon is the tracer of the active expansion of the four-manifold itself. Symbolically, dx₄/dt = ic, with the factor of i encoding the perpendicularity of the active expansion to the three spatial dimensions.

Schrödinger's verbatim 1935 statement on entanglement, which I encountered in Spring 1990 at Princeton in preparing the junior paper, is recorded in *"Discussion of Probability between Separated Systems"* (Proceedings of the Cambridge Physical Society 1935, 31, issue 4, p. 555): *"When two systems, of which we know the states by their respective representatives, enter into temporary physical interaction due to known forces between them, and when after a time of mutual influence the systems separate again, then they can no longer be described in the same way as before, viz. ## Era 2. MDT Usenet Postings (2001)

The Moving Dimensions Theory (MDT) Usenet postings on sci.physics.relativity [55] (July 17, 2001, 2:54 PM) and sci.physics [56] (July 17, 2001, 2:57 PM), posted under my name and email address mcgucken@jollyroger.com, give the first publicly archived statement of the active-expansion account outside the dissertation, predating the 2008 FQXi entry by seven years. Both posts present the formal derivation from the null-cone identity $x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=c^{2}t^{2}$ to $dx/dt=c$ and propose the equivalent statement of Einstein's two postulates as the single Law of Moving Dimensions: "The time dimension is moving relative to the three spatial dimensions." The posts explicitly identify the framework's reach across relativity (time dilation, length contraction, $E=mc^{2}$), quantum mechanics (wave-particle duality, Feynman path integrals as paths through the time dimension, the photon as matter rotated into the time dimension), and thermodynamics (the Second Law as the active expansion of the fourth dimension at constant rate). The Hawking/Penrose-era vocabulary ("momenergy," "the underlying fabric of all reality, the dimensions themselves, are moving relative to one another") is in place. These two posts establish the 2001 priority of the dynamical reading.

# Distinction from the Minkowski Coordinate Convention

I summarize the distinction between Minkowski's 1908 coordinate convention x₄ = ict and the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic.

| Feature | Minkowski 1908 | McGucken (1998–present) |
|---|---|---|
| Object | static coordinate x₄ = ict | active expansion dx₄/dt = ic |
| Reading | coordinate device | physical-geometric primitive |
| Sphericity | absent | spherical from every event |
| Velocity | c as light speed (limit speed) | c as x₄-advance speed |
| Foundational role | calculational convenience | postulate of physics |
| Derivational content | Lorentz transformations as Euclidean rotations | seven dualities of physics |
| Falsifiability | not applicable (convention) | Class A-D experiments (§XV) |
| Date of first statement | 1908 | 1998 (UNC dissertation appendix) |

The integrated coordinate x₄ = ict of Minkowski 1908 is the *mere integrated shadow* of the active expansion dx₄/dt = ic of the McGucken Principle. Every theorem of the present paper traces to the active expansion; the coordinate label is its mere integrated shadow.

Wheeler verbatim (p. 15): *"a choice made in the here and now has irretrievable consequences for what one has the right to say about what has already happened in the very earliest days of the universe, long before there was any life on earth."* Carrol Alley experiments at University of Maryland cited (p. 17). Bohr verbatim via Wheeler (p. 17): *"As Bohr said, we have no right to talk about what the photon is doing during its long travel from the point of entry — from the first half-silvered mirror to the point of registration. After all, no elementary quantum phenomenon is a phenomenon until it is measured."* Bohm verbatim (p. 18): *"I've already put myself between Einstein and Bohr. I say there is an area where our observations do create reality, as in human relationships. But I think that the universe as a whole does not depend on us to do that."* Bell verbatim (p. 18): *"The problem of measurement and the observer is the problem of where the measurement begins and ends, and where the observer begins and ends. When you analyze this language that the physicists have fallen into, that physics is about the results of observations — you find that on analysis it evaporates, and nothing very clear is being said."*

**§IV (pp. 19–21)** Wigner's Friend with full Hamiltonian-decomposition treatment. Mr. Observer state $|A,a\rangle$, $H = H_{Mr} + H_s$ before observation, $U = U_{Mr}U_s$ factorization with $U_{Mr} = \exp(-iH_{Mr}t/\hbar)$ and $U_s = \exp(-iH_s t/\hbar)$. Pre-coupling expectation value $\langle F\rangle_t = \langle A,a|U_{Mr}^\dagger F U_{Mr}|A,a\rangle$ is independent of system state $a$. Figure 4 (hand-drawn): Stern-Gerlach observation-without-detection. Post-coupling linear-superposition outcome (p. 21): for initial $|\Psi_i\rangle = \alpha|A,+\rangle - \beta|A,-\rangle$, Schrödinger evolution gives $|\Psi_f\rangle = \alpha|A_u,+\rangle - \beta|A_d,-\rangle$. Mr. Observer himself in superposition. Verbatim Wigner question (p. 21): *"But wait! It appears that Mr. Observer exists in a linear superposition of two states! If I were Mr. Observer, I would most certainly know whether the spin is up or the spin is down! What is happening here?! When does an observation become an observation? When it enters the mind? Whose mind?"*

**§V (p. 21+)** Conclusion. Verbatim Bell *"dirty theory"* quote (p. 21): *"I am a professional theoretical physicist and I would like to make a clean theory. And when I look at quantum mechanics, I see that it's a dirty theory. The formulations of quantum mechanics that you find in the books involve dividing the world into an observer and an observed, and you are not told where that division comes. You're not told about this division between the observer and the observed. What you learn in the course of your apprenticeship is that for practical purposes it does not matter where you put this division; that the ambiguity is at a level of precision far beyond human capability of testing. So you have a theory which is ambiguous, but where the ambiguity involves decimal places remote from human abilities to test."*

The paper regarded as the birth of quantum theory. Cited at Stage 5 of Theorem IX.30.C.13.E.1 of the present paper, identified as the historical proof-of-concept for the combined-channel category.

[Planck 1901] Planck, M., "Über das Gesetz der Energieverteilung im Normalspektrum," *Annalen der Physik* **4**, 553–563 (1901). Planck's full paper on the blackbody radiation law, expanding the December 14, 1900 presentation [Planck 1900b] into the definitive published derivation. Contains the Planck spectrum $u(\nu, T) = (8\pi\nu^{2}/c^{3}) \cdot h\nu/(e^{h\nu/k_{B}T} - 1)$ in its modern form and the numerical value of $h$ obtained by fitting to the Rubens-Kurlbaum and Lummer-Pringsheim data. Cited at Theorem IX.30.C.13.E.2 of the present paper for the explicit decomposition into the Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel of the Planck spectrum.

[Rubens-Kurlbaum 1900] Rubens, H., and F. Kurlbaum, "Über die Emission langwelliger Wärmestrahlen durch den schwarzen Körper bei verschiedenen Temperaturen," *Sitzungsberichte der Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften* (1900), pp. 929–941. The precision infrared blackbody measurements at wavelengths beyond 50 $\mu$m at the Physikalisch-Technische Reichsanstalt (PTRB) in Berlin, refuting the Wien-Planck law in the long-wavelength region and establishing the empirical constraint that Planck's October 19, 1900 empirical interpolation and December 14, 1900 derivation had to meet. Rubens visited Planck at Planck's home on October 7, 1900, communicating the new measurements directly. Cited at Stage 2 of Theorem IX.30.C.13.E.1 of the present paper.

[Lummer-Pringsheim 1900] Lummer, O., and E. Pringsheim, "Über die Strahlung des schwarzen Körpers für lange Wellen," *Verhandlungen der Deutschen Physikalischen Gesellschaft* **2**, 163–180 (1900). The independent precision blackbody measurements at PTRB, contemporaneous with Rubens-Kurlbaum, confirming the deviation from Wien's law at long wavelengths. Cited at Stage 2 of Theorem IX.30.C.13.E.1.

[Rayleigh 1900] Rayleigh, Lord (J. W. Strutt), "Remarks upon the law of complete radiation," *Philosophical Magazine* **49**, 539–540 (June 1900). Rayleigh's derivation of the low-frequency blackbody spectrum via equipartition applied to electromagnetic modes in a cavity, giving $\rho(\nu, T) \propto \nu^{2}T$. Corrected by Jeans 1905 for the numerical factor $8\pi/c^{3}$. Cited at Corollary IX.30.C.13.E.1 of the present paper, identified as an Algebraic Channel / the Geometric Channel category mismatch: the correct Algebraic Channel mode-counting factor $8\pi\nu^{2}/c^{3}$ combined with the pure Geometric Channel equipartition without the Algebraic Channel per-cycle action quantum $h$ in the mode energies, giving the ultraviolet catastrophe.

[Ehrenfest 1911] Ehrenfest, P., "Welche Züge der Lichtquantenhypothese spielen in der Theorie der Wärmestrahlung eine wesentliche Rolle?" *Annalen der Physik* **36**, 91–118 (1911). The paper that coined the term "ultraviolet catastrophe" (*Ultraviolettkatastrophe*) for the Rayleigh-Jeans divergence at high frequency. Cited at Corollary IX.30.C.13.E.1 of the present paper.

[Einstein 1906] Einstein, A., "Zur Theorie der Lichterzeugung und Lichtabsorption," *Annalen der Physik* **20**, 199–206 (1906). Einstein's paper first identifying Planck's $\varepsilon = nh\nu$ as a physical constraint on oscillator energies rather than as a formal counting device — the first physically-serious reading of Planck's quantization. Cited at Stage 5 of Theorem IX.30.C.13.E.1 of the present paper.

[Einstein 1907] Einstein, A., "Die Plancksche Theorie der Strahlung und die Theorie der spezifischen Wärme," *Annalen der Physik* **22**, 180–190 (1907). Einstein's quantized-oscillator model of the specific heat of solids, giving $C_{V} = 3R (h\nu_{E}/k_{B}T)^{2} e^{h\nu_{E}/k_{B}T}/(e^{h\nu_{E}/k_{B}T} - 1)^{2}$ at Einstein frequency $\nu_{E}$. The second historical instance of the empirically-forced the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel, resolving the low-temperature failure of the Dulong-Petit law. Cited at Corollary IX.30.C.13.E.2 of the present paper.

[Debye 1912] Debye, P., "Zur Theorie der spezifischen Wärmen," *Annalen der Physik* **39**, 789–839 (1912). Debye's continuum-frequency refinement of Einstein's specific-heat model, yielding the $T^{3}$ law at low temperature and the Debye temperature $\Theta_{D}$. Cited at Corollary IX.30.C.13.E.2 of the present paper.

[Mather et al. 1994] Mather, J. C., Et al., "Measurement of the cosmic microwave background spectrum by the COBE FIRAS instrument," *Astrophys. J.* **420**, 439–444 (1994). The COBE FIRAS measurement establishing the cosmic microwave background as a Planck spectrum at $T = 2.725 \pm 0.001$ K to precision $10^{-5}$ — the most precise blackbody spectrum ever measured. Confirmation of the Planck 1900 spectral form at cosmological scale, ninety-four years after the December 14, 1900 derivation. Cited at Stage 5 of Theorem IX.30.C.13.E.1 of the present paper.

[Kragh 2000] Kragh, H., "Max Planck: the reluctant revolutionary," *Physics World* **13**(12), 31–35 (December 2000). The definitive historical study of Planck's path to the December 14, 1900 derivation, documenting Planck's philosophical opposition to atomism, statistical entropy, and Boltzmann's methods; his three-year attempt at pure-thermodynamic derivation of Wien's law; the "act of desperation" characterization from Planck's 1931 letter to R.W. Wood; and the reluctant-revolutionary attitude Planck maintained toward his own quantum discovery. Cited at Stages 1, 4, and 5 of Theorem IX.30.C.13.E.1 and at Remarks IX.30.C.13.E.1 and IX.30.C.13.E.2 of the present paper.

Cited at Stages 1 and 5 of Theorem IX.30.C.13.E.1 of the present paper.

[Sackur 1911] Sackur, O., "Die Anwendung der kinetischen Theorie der Gase auf chemische Probleme," *Annalen der Physik* **341**, 958–980 (received October 6, 1911). Sackur's first paper deriving the entropy of a monoatomic ideal gas as a function of the size of the elementary phase-space cell, applied to chemical problems concerning the equilibrium of monoatomic vapors. The first published statement of what became the Sackur-Tetrode equation, in a form that leaves the elementary cell volume as an empirical parameter to be determined. Cited at Corollary IX.30.C.13.E.3 of the present paper.

[Sackur 1912] Sackur, O., "Die Bedeutung des elementaren Wirkungsquantums für die Gastheorie und die Berechnung der chemischen Konstante," in *Festschrift W. Nernst zu seinem 25jährigen Doktorjubiläum*, Verlag von Wilhelm Knapp, Halle, 1912, pp. 405–423. Sackur's spring 1912 paper explicitly postulating that the elementary cell volume in phase space is $h^{n}$ where $h$ is Planck's constant and $n$ is the number of degrees of freedom. The paper Sackur wrote for Nernst's 25th doctoral anniversary festschrift, connecting Planck's constant to gas theory and the computation of Nernst's "chemical constants" from thermodynamics of monoatomic vapors. Cited at Corollary IX.30.C.13.E.3 of the present paper as the first published derivation identifying the phase-space cell volume with $h^{n}$.

[Tetrode 1912] Tetrode, H., "Die chemische Konstante der Gase und das elementare Wirkungsquantum," *Annalen der Physik* **343**, 434–442 (received March 18, 1912); Berichtigung [corrigendum], *Annalen der Physik* **344**, 255–256 (1912). Tetrode's independent derivation of the absolute entropy of a monoatomic ideal gas, published in *Annalen der Physik* two months before Sackur's Nernst-festschrift paper, taking the elementary phase-space cell as $(zh)^{n}$ for a dimensionless factor $z$ that Tetrode fixed by comparison to experimental data on mercury vapor to obtain $z \approx 1$. Tetrode was seventeen years old at publication (born March 7, 1895); he died at age 35 from tuberculosis in 1931. Cited at Corollary IX.30.C.13.E.3 of the present paper as the independent contemporary derivation of the Sackur-Tetrode equation.

[Nernst 1906] Nernst, W., "Über die Berechnung chemischer Gleichgewichte aus thermischen Messungen," *Nachrichten von der Königlichen Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen, Mathematisch-Physikalische Klasse* (1906), pp. 1–40. Nernst's original statement of what became the third law of thermodynamics: for any reversible isothermal process between condensed phases in equilibrium, the entropy change $\Delta S$ approaches zero as $T \to 0$. Later strengthened by Planck 1911 to the modern form: the entropy $S$ of every physical system in equilibrium approaches zero as $T \to 0$. Cited at Corollary IX.30.C.13.E.3 of the present paper as the empirical constraint on absolute entropy that the Sackur-Tetrode formula satisfies at $T > 0$ but violates as $T \to 0$ ($S_{\rm ST} \to -\infty$), diagnosing the classical Maxwell-Boltzmann the combined Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel as insufficient at low temperature and forcing the fuller Algebraic Channel quantum-statistical content of Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac statistics.

[Grimus 2013] Grimus, W., "On the 100th anniversary of the Sackur-Tetrode equation," *Annalen der Physik* **525**, A32–A35 (2013). arXiv:1112.3748. Historical study on the centennial of the Sackur-Tetrode equation, documenting Sackur's 1911 October paper and 1912 Nernst-festschrift paper, Tetrode's March 1912 *Annalen der Physik* paper, the empirical test on mercury vapor comparing $h$ obtained from thermodynamic data with Planck's value from blackbody radiation, and the historical significance of Planck's constant entering the statistical mechanics of massive matter more than a decade before the 1925–1926 formalization of quantum mechanics. Grimus's summary quoted verbatim in Corollary IX.30.C.13.E.3 of the present paper: "Until then, $h$ was primarily associated with harmonic oscillators and photons. With the work of Sackur and Tetrode it became clear that Planck's constant was not only relevant for counting the number of states in the case of photons but also in the case of massive particles. In this way, $h$ became ubiquitous in statistical physics, more than ten years before the advent of quantum mechanics."

[Einstein 1917] Einstein, A., "Kosmologische Betrachtungen zur allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie," *Sitzungsberichte der Königlich Preußischen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Berlin* (1917), pp. 142–152. Einstein's introduction of the cosmological constant $\Lambda$ in a static-universe modification of the 1915 field equations, giving $R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2}g_{\mu\nu}R + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}/c^{4}$. Lemaître's independent derivation of the expanding-universe solutions and the first prediction of the linear velocity-distance relation $v = H_{0} d$, published two years before Hubble's 1929 empirical measurement. Cited at Theorem IX.30.C.13.F.1(12) of the present paper.

The founding empirical confirmation of the expanding-universe solutions of Friedmann and Lemaître. Cited at Theorem IX.30.C.13.F.1(12) of the present paper.

[Alpher-Bethe-Gamow 1948] Alpher, R. A., H. Bethe, and G. Gamow, "The origin of chemical elements," *Physical Review* **73**, 803–804 (1948). The Alpher-Bethe-Gamow ("$\alpha\beta\gamma$") paper on primordial nucleosynthesis in the hot early universe, predicting the observed abundances of light elements from Big Bang cosmology. Companion to [Mather et al. 1994]'s measurement of the CMB Planck spectrum. Smoot and Mather awarded the 2006 Nobel Prize in Physics. Cited at Theorem IX.30.C.13.F.1(12) of the present paper.
