[Compton 1923] Compton, A. H., "A Quantum Theory of the Scattering of X-Rays by Light Elements," *Physical Review* **21**, 483–502 (1923). Compton's derivation and experimental confirmation of the wavelength shift in X-ray photon scattering off electrons, $\Delta\lambda = (h/mc)(1 - \cos\theta)$, establishing particle-like behavior of light (photon carries momentum $p = h/\lambda$). Cited at Remark IX.30.C.13.F.1 as founding empirical demonstration of the particle character of the photon.

[Davisson-Germer 1927] Davisson, C. J., and L. H. Germer, "Diffraction of Electrons by a Crystal of Nickel," *Physical Review* **30**, 705–740 (1927). The electron-diffraction experiment demonstrating the wave-like behavior of matter, confirming de Broglie's 1924 matter-wave hypothesis $\lambda_{\rm dB} = h/p$. Cited at Remark IX.30.C.13.F.1 as founding empirical demonstration of matter-wave duality.

[Young 1801] Young, T., "On the Theory of Light and Colours" (The 1801 Bakerian Lecture), *Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London* **92**, 12–48 (1802). Young's introduction of the principle of interference of light and the two-slit experiment demonstrating that overlapping light waves produce alternating bright and dark fringes rather than uniform illumination. The founding empirical statement of phase-coherent interference in classical optics — the first addition of the Algebraic Channel phase-carrying content to the pure Geometric Channel geometric-envelope tradition of Huygens 1690. Cited at Theorem IX.30.C.13.F.1(2) of the present paper as the century-later arrival of the Algebraic Channel content in classical optics, one hundred and eleven years after Huygens' the pure Geometric Channel *Traité de la Lumière*.

[Fresnel 1815] Fresnel, A.-J., "Premier mémoire sur la diffraction de la lumière" (1815), and subsequent memoirs collected in *Œuvres complètes d'Augustin Fresnel*, edited by H. de Sénarmont, É. Verdet, and L. Fresnel, Imprimerie Impériale, Paris, 3 vols., 1866–1870. Fresnel's mathematical formulation of the wave theory of light combining Huygens' envelope construction with Young's interference principle, yielding the Huygens-Fresnel principle in which each wavefront point emits a spherical wavelet with definite amplitude and phase, and the envelope-plus-interference sum gives the next wavefront. Cited at Theorem IX.30.C.13.F.1(2) of the present paper as the formal integration of the Algebraic Channel phase-coherent content with the Geometric Channel geometric-envelope content in classical optics, completing the pre-quantum wave theory of light.

[Misner-Thorne-Wheeler1973] Misner, C. W., K. S. Thorne, and J. A. Wheeler, *Gravitation*, W. H. Freeman, San Francisco, 1973. ISBN 0-7167-0334-3 (cloth); ISBN 0-7167-0344-0 (paperback). The canonical graduate-level general-relativity textbook of the past half-century, training two generations of theoretical physicists. Particularly relevant to the present paper is **Box 2.1, *"Farewell to 'ict',"* p. 51**, in which the authors explicitly execute the coordinate x₄ = ict from the textbook tradition of special relativity, on the sociological ground that *"no one has discovered a way to make an imaginary coordinate work in the general curved spacetime manifold. If '$x^{4} = ict$' cannot be used there, it will not be used here."* The McGucken framework demonstrates that the extension MTW said did not exist is the active-expansion account dx₄/dt = ic, with the imaginary unit functioning as the perpendicularity marker of the fourth dimension's active expansion at velocity c relative to the spatial three. **MTW's textbook execution of x₄ = ict is the canonical historical document of the post-Minkowski concealment of the McGucken framework**; see §XIII.2.A and §XIII.B Entry 26.A of the present paper for the full historical treatment. The textbook is also a standard reference for tensor analysis, differential geometry, the Riemann curvature tensor, the Einstein field equations, geometrodynamics, black holes, gravitational waves, cosmology, and experimental tests of GR; the geometric formalism developed in Chapters 8–15 (differential geometry, parallel transport, geodesic deviation, Riemann curvature) is inherited and extended by the McGucken framework in §§IX.0.A, IX.13, IX.14, IX.16 of the present paper. Wheeler's role as third author of MTW (the senior figure of the three, my Princeton advisor, and the figure who in 1989 would issue the call for the *Noble* in physics [Wheeler1989]) is a poignant : Wheeler in 1973 helped eliminate the very feature that, in 1998–99, I as his Princeton student would identify as the physical reality answering Wheeler's later call [McGucken1998Dissertation]. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is therefore not a rejection of Wheeler's legacy but the *completion* of it.

Peebles, Joseph Taylor, and the entire Princeton physics environment of the late 1980s. Contains: (i) the verbatim Jadwin Hall conversation with Wheeler in autumn 1989. Wheeler standing at the window watching autumn foliage, dressed in his classic suit and tie, a piece of chalk in his clenched fist, stating *"Today's physics lacks the Noble, and it's your generation's duty to bring it back"* [27], followed by my exchange with Wheeler that established the photon-stationary-in-x₄ result: *"So a photon doesn't move in the fourth dimension? All of its motion is directed through the three spatial dimensions?" Wheeler: "Correct." "So a photon remains stationary in the fourth dimension?" Wheeler: "Yes."*; (ii) the verbatim P. J. E. Peebles (Albert Einstein Professor Emeritus of Science, Princeton) conversation establishing the spherically-symmetric-wavefront result: *"So in the simplest case, when a photon is emitted from a source, it has an equal chance of being found anywhere upon a spherically-symmetric wavefront expanding at the rate of c?" Peebles: "Yes."*; (iii) the verbatim Joseph Taylor quote from Taylor's office in Spring 1990: *"Schrödinger said that entanglement is the characteristic trait of quantum mechanics. Figure out the source of entanglement, and you'll figure out the source of the quantum, as nobody really knows what, nor why, nor how ℏ is."*; (iv) the verbatim Erwin Schrödinger statement on entanglement that I encountered in Spring 1990 at Princeton (*"Discussion of Probability between Separated Systems"*, Proceedings of the Cambridge Physical Society 1935, 31, issue 4, p. 555): *"When two systems, of which we know the states by their respective representatives, enter into temporary physical interaction due to known forces between them, and when after a time of mutual influence the systems separate again, then they can no longer be described in the same way as before, viz. By endowing each of them with a representative of its own. I would not call that one but rather the characteristic trait of quantum mechanics, the one that enforces its entire departure from classical lines of thought. By the interaction the two representatives (or ψ-functions) have become entangled."*; (v) the verbatim eureka-moment narrative — the windsurfing-trip late-lunch break during which I was leafing through Einstein's 1912 Manuscript on Relativity and saw, *"like a bolt from the blue,"* that the Minkowski-inspired equation x₄ = ict had physical meaning: *"It told of the expansion of the fourth dimension relative to the three spatial dimensions, thusly providing for quantum entanglement, time's radiative arrow, and the second law of thermodynamics! Have you ever wondered why x4 is the only coordinate related to t in the spacetime metric? It is because the fourth dimension is expanding relative to the three spatial dimensions, or dx4/dt=ic!"*; (vi) the verbatim photon-as-tracer argument that establishes the active-expansion result from the Wheeler and Peebles results in combination: *"As the photon remains stationary in the fourth dimension, it provides the ideal tracer for the motion of the fourth dimension. In the same way that a small GPS tracer tagged to an eagle remains stationary relative to the eagle as it soars through the air, thusly tracking the eagle's motion in flight, a photon, which remains stationary relative to the fourth dimension, must track its motion. Thus, because a photon is described by a spherically-symmetrically wavefront expanding at the rate of c while remaining stationary in the fourth dimension, the fourth dimension must be expanding at the rate of c."*; (vii) the verbatim text of the Wheeler recommendation letter [32] reproduced in the Medium piece, including Wheeler's account of asking me to derive the *time* part of the Schwarzschild factor by "poor-man's reasoning" — *"I gave (Dr. E) the proofs of my… A Journey into Gravity and Space Time… the space part of the Schwarzchild geometric is worked out by purely geometric methods. 'Can you, by poor-man's reasoning, derive what I never have, the time part?' He could and did, and wrote it up in a beautifully clear account. His second junior paper. Was done with another advisor (J. Taylor), and dealt with… the Einstein-Rosen-Podolsky experiment and delayed choice experiments… this paper was so outstanding…"*; (viii) the original Moving Dimensions Theory (MDT) name for what became the McGucken Principle, as the Spring-1990 to 1998 working name of the active-expansion; (ix) the connection of the active-expansion account to Huygens' Principle (the 1678 *Treatise on Light*) and to the Wheeler-Feynman absorber theory's time-reversal-symmetry question, with dx₄/dt = ic identified as the resolution of the MathPages directionality question (*"Why does an expanding spherical wave continue to expand outward from its source, rather than re-converging inward back toward the source?"*). The Medium piece is the published autobiographical priority document of the Princeton-afternoons origin of the McGucken Principle, predating the present synthesis paper by approximately two and a half years and predating the 2008 FQXi essay by approximately fifteen years. It is also the published source from which the Spring 1990 conversation with Taylor on Schrödinger's *"characteristic trait of quantum mechanics"* is recorded for the priority chain.

**[14 = MG-Dissertation]** McGucken, E. *Multiple Unit Artificial Retina Chipset to Aid the Visually Impaired and Enhanced Holed-Emitter CMOS Phototransistors*, Ph.D. Dissertation, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, 1998. Copyright ©1998 Elliot McGucken. UMI Dissertation 9840958. 179 pages. Google Books record: https://www.google.com/books/edition/Multiple_Unit_Artificial_Retina_Chipset/M9eEGwAACAAJ. Appendix B: "Physics for Poets: The Law of Moving Dimensions," pp. 153–156. The first written statement of the McGucken Principle, four years prior to the July 17, 2001 Usenet posts [55], ten years prior to the 2008 FQXi essay [33], twenty-eight years prior to the 2026 technical-paper corpus, and a quarter-century prior to the modern precision tests (GW170817, Hensen et al. 2015, Big Bell Test 2018, electron $g-2$ 2023, FLRW twelve-test cosmology 2023–2025) that empirically verify it at Bayesian likelihood ratio $\gtrsim 10^{141}$ per Theorem IX.26.11 of [3]. The Appendix B text opens with Einstein's two postulates of relativity and proposes their equivalent reformulation as the single Law of Moving Dimensions: *"The time dimension is moving or expanding relative to the three spatial dimensions."* The proof proceeds from Einstein's second postulate written as the null-cone identity $\sum_{j=1}^{3} x_{j}^{2} - c^{2}t^{2} = 0$, equivalently $\sum_{j=1}^{3} x_{j}^{2} = c^{2}t^{2}$, which for one spatial dimension reduces to $x^{2} = c^{2}t^{2}$, hence $x = ct$, hence $dx/dt = c$. Appendix B then derives, from this single Law, the canonical content: time dilation (as an object's rotation into the moving time dimension catches up with the dimension's propagation), relativistic length contraction (as the object's probability is rotated into the time dimension and appears shorter from the three spatial dimensions), mass-energy equivalence (E = mc² "holds true because radiative energy, consisting of photons, is merely matter rotated fully into the time dimension," Equation AB.1, p. 156), wave-particle duality and quantum probability (the relative motion between dimensions in which both particles and waves exist), Feynman's many-path integrals (the particle has a chance of existing as a pure wave completely independent of the spatial dimensions until interaction), and the Second Law of thermodynamics (the law of increasing entropy accounted for by that all particles have a chance of existing in a dimension expanding at a constant rate equally in all directions, with the spherical symmetry of a photon's wavefront viewed as the result of matter rotated into the time dimension). Figure AB.1 on p. 154 — *"A space-time diagram with a null vector. Because space and time are moving relative to one-another, the only way to have zero length or interval is to travel at the speed of light"* — is the dissertation's geometric statement of the active-expansion account of x₄ = ict. The closing sentence, p. 156, gives the 1998 verbatim form of the McGucken Principle's animating claim: *"As physics concerns itself at all levels with changes relative to both space and time, it makes sense that all physics, time, motion, reality, life, and consciousness itself are founded upon a stage which is endowed with intrinsic motion. The underlying fabric of all reality, the dimensions themselves, are moving relative to one another."* This verbatim closing line reappears identically in the 2001 Usenet posts [55], establishing direct textual continuity from the 1998 dissertation appendix through the 2001 Usenet record to the 2008–2013 FQXi essay series. The dissertation's principal content is the artificial-retina chipset (Chapters I–VI, pp. 1–130) and the patent for the Holed-Emitter Phototransistor (Appendix A, pp. 133–151); Appendix B's status as the priority document for the McGucken Principle has been established and reaffirmed across the entire subsequent priority record [8].

**[Ritz 1908]** Ritz, W. *"On a new law of series spectra,"* Astrophysical Journal 28, 237-243, 1908. Formulated the observed regularity of atomic emission spectra now known as the Ritz combination principle: certain pairs of spectral-line frequencies $\nu(i,j)$ and $\nu(j,k)$ add to give another spectral-line frequency $\nu(i,k)$ of the same atom. Connes 2000 [Connes-2000-NCG] identifies this experimental regularity as the observational origin of the noncommutative-algebra structure Heisenberg extracted in 1925 (Connes verbatim: "quantum mechanics showed that indeed the parameter space, or phase space of the mechanical system given by a single atom fails to be a manifold... this conclusion is indeed dictated by the *experimental findings of spectroscopy*"). Cited in Remark P.3.3.1 and Remark IX.30.C.1.3 above as the primary empirical starting-data of Heisenberg's matrix mechanics.

**[Heisenberg 1925]** Heisenberg, W. *"Über quantentheoretische Umdeutung kinematischer und mechanischer Beziehungen"* ("Quantum-theoretical re-interpretation of kinematic and mechanical relations"), Zeitschrift für Physik 33, 879-893, July 1925. The founding paper of matrix mechanics. Written on the North Sea island of Helgoland during Heisenberg's hay-fever recovery. Targets spectroscopic quantities (frequencies and intensities of atomic emission spectral lines) as "observable" and dismisses electron orbits as "unobservable." Constructs a multiplication rule for quantum-theoretical Fourier series that respects the Ritz combination principle of Ritz 1908 — the rule that later Born and Jordan recognized as matrix multiplication. Heisenberg himself did not know matrix theory when writing this paper (per Connes 2000 verbatim, "Heisenberg didn't know about matrices, he just worked it out, but he was told later by Born, Jordan and Dirac that the algebra he had worked out was known to mathematicians as the algebra of matrices"). Cited in Remark P.3.3.1, Remark IX.30.C.1.3, and §P.1.4.D above as the founding QM instance of the Algebraic Channel.

**[Born-Jordan 1925]** Born, M., and Jordan, P. *"Zur Quantenmechanik"* ("On Quantum Mechanics"), Zeitschrift für Physik 34, 858-888, September 1925. First systematic mathematical formalization of Heisenberg's July 1925 multiplication rule as matrix algebra, following Born's recognition that Heisenberg's "sets of numbers" were matrices (recognition based on Born's earlier training under Jakob Rosanes in matrix algebra and familiarity with Hilbert's spectral theory of integral equations). Establishes the canonical commutator $PQ - QP = -i\hbar\mathbb{1}$ (the reversed sign convention relative to modern usage) and derives the quantum equations of motion. Cited in Remark P.3.3.1 and Remark IX.30.C.1.3 above.

**[Born-Heisenberg-Jordan 1926]** Born, M., Heisenberg, W., and Jordan, P. *"Zur Quantenmechanik II"* ("On Quantum Mechanics II"), Zeitschrift für Physik 35, 557-615, November 1925 (published February 1926). The "Drei-Männer-Arbeit" ("Three-Man Paper"). Extends Born-Jordan 1925 to arbitrary systems, establishing matrix mechanics as a general quantum theory. Contains the systematic treatment of angular momentum, perturbation theory, and identical-particle statistics in matrix form. Cited in Remark P.3.3.1 and Remark IX.30.C.1.3 above.

**[de Broglie 1924]** de Broglie, L. *"Recherches sur la théorie des Quanta"* ("Researches on the theory of Quanta"), Doctoral thesis, Faculté des Sciences de Paris, 1924. Published in Annales de Physique 3, 22-128, 1925. Postulates that material particles possess wave properties analogous to the particle properties Einstein 1905 had attributed to electromagnetic radiation. Introduces the matter-wave relation $\lambda = h/p$. Cited in Remark P.3.3.1 and Remark IX.30.C.1.3 above as the primary theoretical starting-data of Schrödinger's wave mechanics.

**[Schrödinger 1926a-d]** Schrödinger, E. *"Quantisierung als Eigenwertproblem"* ("Quantization as an Eigenvalue Problem"), four communications: Annalen der Physik 79, 361-376 (Part I, January 1926); 79, 489-527 (Part II, February 1926); 80, 437-490 (Part III, March 1926); 81, 109-139 (Part IV, June 1926). The founding papers of wave mechanics. Constructs the wave equation $-(\hbar^2/2m)\nabla^2\psi + V(x)\psi = E\psi$ by Hamilton-Jacobi analogy from de Broglie's matter-wave hypothesis of 1924, following Debye's Zurich-seminar prompt "if there is a wave, there should be a wave equation." Correctly reproduces the Bohr hydrogen spectrum by solving the eigenvalue problem for the Coulomb potential. Schrödinger's collaboration with the mathematician Hermann Weyl at ETH Zurich is documented in Schrödinger's own acknowledgments. Cited in Remark P.3.3.1, Remark IX.30.C.1.3, and §P.1.4.D above as the founding QM instance of the Geometric Channel (wave-mechanical / geometric-wave branch).

**[Schrödinger 1926e]** Schrödinger, E. *"Über das Verhältnis der Heisenberg-Born-Jordanschen Quantenmechanik zu der meinen"* ("On the Relation of the Heisenberg-Born-Jordan Quantum Mechanics to Mine"), Annalen der Physik 79, 734-756, 1926. The formal equivalence paper. Establishes correspondence between matrix elements of Heisenberg-Born-Jordan matrix mechanics and integrals of wave functions over configuration space in Schrödinger's wave mechanics. Opens with the verbatim statement of derivational disjointness: "Considering the extraordinary differences between the starting-points and the concepts of Heisenberg's quantum mechanics and of the theory which has been designated 'undulatory' or 'physical' mechanics, and has lately been described here, it is very strange that these new two theories agree with one another with regard to the known facts, where they differ from the old quantum theory... starting-points, presentations, methods and in fact the whole mathematical apparatus, seem fundamentally different." Cited in Remark IX.30.C.1.3 above as the first historical instance of a convergent-overdetermination proof for a QM theorem. Muller 1997 argues this proof was ontologically-specific to the hydrogen atom case rather than a general Hilbert-space isomorphism.

**[von Neumann 1932]** von Neumann, J. *Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik*, Springer, Berlin, 1932. English translation: *Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics*, Princeton University Press, 1955. First rigorous Hilbert-space formulation of quantum mechanics. Establishes matrix mechanics as the $\ell^2$ realization and wave mechanics as the $L^2$ realization of the abstract separable complex Hilbert space, providing the general isomorphism between the two formulations that Schrödinger 1926e had only established ontologically for the hydrogen atom case. Cited in Remark P.3.3.1 and Remark IX.30.C.1.3 above.

**[Stone 1930 / von Neumann 1931]** Stone, M. H. *"Linear transformations in Hilbert space III: operational methods and group theory,"* Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA 16, 172-175, 1930; and von Neumann, J. *"Die Eindeutigkeit der Schrödingerschen Operatoren"* ("The uniqueness of Schrödinger's operators"), Mathematische Annalen 104, 570-578, 1931. The Stone-von Neumann uniqueness theorem: any two strongly continuous unitary representations of the Weyl form of the canonical commutation relations for finitely many degrees of freedom are unitarily equivalent. Establishes rigorously that Heisenberg's matrix mechanics and Schrödinger's wave mechanics are the same theory in the finite-degree-of-freedom case. Cited in Remark IX.30.C.1.3 above.

**[Haag 1955]** Haag, R. *"On quantum field theories,"* Kongelige Danske Videnskabernes Selskab Matematisk-Fysiske Meddelelser 29, no. 12, 1955. Haag's theorem: in relativistic quantum field theory with infinitely many degrees of freedom, the Stone-von Neumann uniqueness theorem fails — the interaction picture does not exist as a proper Hilbert-space representation, and inequivalent representations of the canonical commutation relations exist. Established that the equivalence of Heisenberg-picture and Schrödinger-picture QFT is more delicate than the finite-dimensional case. Cited in Remark IX.30.C.1.3 above.

**[Johnson-Freyd 2021]** Johnson-Freyd, T. *"Heisenberg-Picture Quantum Field Theory,"* in Alekseev, A., Frenkel, E., Rosso, M., Webster, B., and Yakimov, M. (eds), *Representation Theory, Mathematical Physics, and Integrable Systems: In Honor of Nicolai Reshetikhin*, Progress in Mathematics Vol. 340, pp. 371-409, Birkhäuser/Springer, 2021; DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-78148-4_13; arXiv:1508.05908. Verbatim from the abstract: "Atiyah–Segal-type axioms do a good job of capturing the 'Schrödinger picture': these axioms define a 'd-dimensional quantum field theory' to be a symmetric monoidal functor from an (∞, d)-category of 'spacetimes' to an (∞, d)-category which at the second-from-top level consists of vector spaces, so at the top level consists of numbers. This paper argues that the appropriate parallel notion 'Heisenberg picture' should also be defined in terms of symmetric monoidal functors from the category of spacetimes, but the target should be an (∞, d)-category that in top dimension consists of pointed vector spaces instead of numbers; the second-from-top level can be taken to consist of associative algebras or of pointed categories. The paper ends by outlining two sources of such Heisenberg-picture field theories: factorization algebras and skein theory." Establishes the two pictures as categorically inequivalent at the axiomatic level, extending the finite-dimensional equivalence of Stone-von Neumann to a genuine categorical inequivalence in the QFT case. Cited in Remark P.3.3.1 and Remark IX.30.C.1.3 above.

**[Connes 2000]** Connes, A. *"Noncommutative Geometry Year 2000,"* arXiv math/0011193, 2000. Also published in Alon, N., Bourgain, J., Connes, A., Gromov, M., and Milman, V. (eds.), *Visions in Mathematics: GAFA 2000 Special Volume, Part II*, Birkhäuser, 2010, pp. 481-559. §III "Quantum mechanics" contains the primary-source identification of the Ritz-Rydberg combination principle of Ritz 1908 as the observational origin of the noncommutative-algebra structure Heisenberg extracted in 1925. Verbatim: "quantum mechanics showed that indeed the parameter space, or phase space of the mechanical system given by a single atom fails to be a manifold. It is important to convince oneself of this fact and to understand that this conclusion is indeed dictated by the *experimental findings of spectroscopy*." And: "Heisenberg didn't know about matrices, he just worked it out, but he was told later by Born, Jordan and Dirac that the algebra he had worked out was known to mathematicians as the algebra of matrices." Cited in Remark P.3.3.1, Remark IX.30.C.1.3, and §P.1.4.D above.

**[Muller 1997]** Muller, F.A. *"The equivalence myth of quantum mechanics — Part I,"* Studies in History and Philosophy of Modern Physics 28, 35-61, 1997; and *"Part II,"* Studies in History and Philosophy of Modern Physics 28, 219-247, 1997. Argues that the 1920s consensus on Heisenberg-Schrödinger equivalence rested on an ontologically-specific proof (matching hydrogen energy levels, not general Hilbert-space isomorphism), with the rigorous general isomorphism established only in von Neumann 1932. Cited in Remark P.3.3.1 and Remark IX.30.C.1.3 above.

**[Madrid-Casado 2008]** Madrid-Casado, C.M. *"A brief history of the mathematical equivalence between the two quantum mechanics,"* Latin-American Journal of Physics Education 2, 152-155, 2008. In those cases, the matrix elements represented relationships between wave-like functions, and their eigenvalues corresponded to measurable quantities, such as frequencies or energies. He suggested, with characteristic simplicity, that they might try to find the differential equation whose eigenvalues generated those matrices — in essence, to look for the wave picture behind the algebraic symbols. To Born and Heisenberg, however, this sounded like a retreat into classical imagery... They politely dismissed Hilbert's idea. Only a few months later, Erwin Schrödinger derived a wave equation that described the same quantized energy levels as Heisenberg's matrices. When Hilbert heard of Schrödinger's discovery, he could not resist a smile. As Edward Condon recalled, the mathematician had 'a great laugh' on Born and Heisenberg, remarking that they could have anticipated Schrödinger's breakthrough six months earlier if only they had listened to him." Together with Jordan's independent parallel work (Jordan 1927), transformation theory placed both formulations as different choices of representation within a single unified apparatus. Cited in Remark P.3.3.2 and Remark P.3.3.4 above.

**[Dirac 1972 Boston Lecture]** Dirac, P.A.M. *"Projective Geometry: Origin of Quantum Equations,"* public lecture at Boston University, 30 October 1972. Roger Penrose moderator. Sound recording archived at Xavier University Library, Cincinnati, Ohio (University Archives and Special Collections, archival object 2589); also American Institute of Physics History of Physics catalog (icos-28363, "Each tape contains a recording of Dirac speaking on October 30, 1972 at Boston University. Dirac Collection, Special Collections and Archives, Florida State University Libraries, Tallahassee, Florida (which holds Dirac's own written notes for the talk). Verbatim Dirac quotation from the FSU-archived notes (transcribed at atomicprecision.com/Topics/Paul Dirac Talk - Projective Geometry.pdf and at garadinervi-repertori.blog): "There are basically two kinds of math[ematical] thinking, algebraic and geometric. A good mathematician needs to be a master of both. But still he will have a preference for one rather or the other. I prefer the geometric method. Not mentioned in published work because it is not easy to print diagrams. With the algebraic method one deals with equ[ations] between algebraic quantities. Even tho I see the consistency and logical connections of the eq[uations], they do not mean very much to me. I prefer the relationships which I can visualize in geometric terms." Xavier University Archives catalog note: "the personal announcement by Dirac that he had never published his 'secret' use of projective geometry in creating quantum mechanics." The title reclaims the term *anschaulich* (variously translated as "physical" by Wheeler-Zurek 1983, "perceptible" by the Heisenberg collected works 1984, "perceptual" by Cassidy 1992, or literally "visualizable"), redefining it operationally as qualitative-grasp-of-experimental-consequences rather than in Schrödinger's spatio-temporal-picture sense. Verbatim from the paper's operational definition (per SEP): "We believe we have gained anschaulich understanding of a physical theory, if in all simple cases, we can grasp the experimental consequences qualitatively and see that the theory does not lead to any contradictions." Cited in Remark P.3.3.1 and Remark P.3.3.4 above.

I consider Mist." The German word "Mist" is variously translated by commentators: "junk" (Miller 1982), "rubbish" (Beller 1999), "crap" (Cassidy 1992), and per de Regt 1997 more literally "bullshit." Cited in Remark P.3.3.1 above as primary-source evidence of Heisenberg's mirror position — his rejection of Schrödinger's *Anschaulichkeit* claim as the geometric-visualizable side of the dichotomy against Heisenberg's algebraic-operational side.

Cited in Remark P.3.3.4 above for scope-marking: the framework's dual-channel claim concerns derivational routes, not observational aspects, and is different from Bohr complementarity even though the two axes are compatible.

Verbatim from the paper abstract: "In quantum electrodynamics one can obtain a Hamiltonian which gives reasonable field equations in the Heisenberg picture, but which does not allow of solutions of the wave equation to represent physical states in the Schrödinger picture. The inference is that the Heisenberg picture is a good picture, the Schrödinger picture is a bad picture, and the two pictures are not equivalent. The usual proof of the equivalence of the two pictures fails because the state vector of the Schrödinger picture does not remain in Hilbert space. One can set up quantum electrodynamics entirely in the Heisenberg picture and thereby avoid the worst difficulties encountered in the Schrödinger picture. The theory takes a logical form and is not merely an assembly of working rules." The Dirac 1965 paper analyses a Hamiltonian in QED for which the Heisenberg equations of motion have solutions but the corresponding Schrödinger equation has no solutions with state vectors in Hilbert space. Verbatim from the paper abstract: "The standard claim that the Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures of quantum mechanics are equivalent rests on the fact that they yield identical empirical predictions. This equivalence therefore assumes the instrumentalist worldview in which theories serve only as tools for prediction. Under scientific realism, by contrast, theories aim to describe reality. Whereas the Schrödinger picture posits a time-evolving wave function, the Heisenberg picture posits so-called descriptors, time-evolving generators of the algebra of observables. These two structures are non-isomorphic: descriptors surject onto but do not reduce to the Schrödinger state. Hence, under realism, the pictures are inequivalent. I argue that this inequivalence marks an opening toward a richer, separable ontology for quantum theory." Contains verbatim quotation of Dirac 1965 on the inequivalence in QED. **[74 = Hodge1950]** Hodge, W. V. D. *The Topological Invariants of Algebraic Varieties*. Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Cambridge, Mass., 1950, Volume 1, pages 182-192. Published 1952 by the American Mathematical Society. The paper is the primary-source articulation of what later became known as the Hodge conjecture: on a smooth complex projective algebraic variety, every rational cohomology class of pure bidegree (k,k) in the Hodge decomposition is conjecturally a rational linear combination of cohomology classes of algebraic subvarieties. Hodge's original formulation included an integral version that was subsequently shown to be false (Atiyah-Hirzebruch 1962 supplied counterexamples) and was refined to the rational version that remains open. The paper is cited in the present synthesis paper at §IX.10.9 as the primary-source articulation of the Hodge conjecture, against which the McGucken framework's the dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel / the dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel asymmetry is analogous to but not identical with. No URL is supplied because the paper is a 1950 conference proceedings volume; it is available through the American Mathematical Society archives and standard mathematical libraries.

# Appendix N — Notation for Proper Time, the Fourth-Axis Rate, and the Photon

The McGucken Principle $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ states that the fourth dimension is physically expanding at velocity $c$ at every event of spacetime. This is the ontological content of the framework: an active, universal, forward-oriented expansion of the fourth axis, with rate fixed at $c$, occurring at every point of the manifold at every moment of coordinate time. It is not a coordinate convention, not a metric ansatz, not a formal identification — it is a physical statement about what spacetime does. Every downstream result of the framework — the Minkowski metric with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, the Lorentz and Poincaré groups, the null cone, the mass-shell condition, the McGucken Sphere expanding from every event, the Compton-clock oscillation of massive particles at $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar$, the $+ic$-oriented arrow of time, the derived Einstein field equations, the recovered quantum-mechanical apparatus, the Wick rotation as a real coordinate identification — is a theorem obtained by integration, differentiation, squaring, or pullback of this single physical statement.

$\mathcal M_{G}$ names the four-manifold on which the Principle acts. Minkowski spacetime is what descends from $\mathcal M_{G}$ once the Principle is integrated ($x_{4} = ict$) and squared ($dx_{4}^{2} = -c^{2}dt^{2}$): a static bookkeeping structure — signature $(-,+,+,+)$, null cone, Lorentz and Poincaré groups, mass-shell condition — with the rate, the $+ic$ orientation, and the oscillation flattened out. The operational diagnostic is the Wick rotation of §IX.13: $\mathcal M_{G}$'s content survives ($dx_{4}/dt = ic \to dx_{4}/d\tau_{W} = +c$, expansion persists in Euclidean signature); Minkowski's Lorentzian structure does not (signature flips to $(+,+,+,+)$, null cone collapses, $\mathrm{ISO}^{+}(1,3) \to \mathrm{ISO}(4)$).

## N.1 The Three Quantities

Three distinct quantities appear when the Principle is read along a worldline.

**(R1) $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ — the coordinate rate.** The Principle stated per coordinate time. Well-defined at every event: $t$ parametrizes every worldline (timelike, null, accelerated, at any gravitational potential), so the derivative is universal. Integrating from $(t_{0}, \mathbf x_{0})$ gives $x_{4}(t) = ict$ (with $x_{4}(t_{0}) = ict_{0}$), exact and path-independent. On massive worldlines the chain rule gives the four-velocity $u^{\mu} = dx^{\mu}/d\tau = (\gamma v^{i}, ic\gamma)$ with norm $u^{\mu}u_{\mu} = -c^{2}$; on null worldlines proper time degenerates and the affine-parameter null tangent $dx^{\mu}/d\lambda$ takes its place with $k^{\mu}k_{\mu} = 0$.

**(R2) $c\,d\tau/dt$ — the time-dilation factor.** Standard $c/\gamma$ on massive worldlines. From the Minkowski line element restricted to a worldline, $d\tau^{2} = dt^{2} - d\mathbf x^{2}/c^{2}$, hence $(c\,d\tau/dt)^{2} = c^{2} - v^{2}$ with $v = |d\mathbf x/dt|$ the coordinate spatial speed. Bounded: $0 \le c\,d\tau/dt \le c$. Values: $c$ at spatial rest, $0$ on null worldlines, $c/\gamma$ on massive worldlines. Partition: $v^{2} + (c\,d\tau/dt)^{2} = c^{2}$, exception-free.

**(R3) $\tau[\gamma] = \int_{\gamma} d\tau$ — proper time along the worldline.** The standard aging quantity: elapsed time on a clock carried along $\gamma$. Path-dependent (twin paradox: two worldlines with common endpoints generally have different $\tau[\gamma]$). Zero along null worldlines ($d\tau = 0$ pointwise). The Compton-clock phase along a massive worldline is $\omega_{C}\tau[\gamma]$ with $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar$.

## N.2 The Rest-Frame Reading

The Principle is stated per coordinate time. The reading $dx_{4}/d\tau = ic$ (Theorem 4 of [3]) is legitimate on a rest worldline where $d\tau = dt$ locally; on a moving worldline the chain rule gives $ic\gamma$; on a null worldline the ratio is undefined and (R3) is replaced by the affine null tangent. Universal-rate statements read in (R1) directly, or as "$c\,d\tau/dt = c$ on the rest worldline" in (R2).

## N.3 The Photon

On a null worldline from emission $p_{0} = (\mathbf x_{0}, t_{0})$, the photon's x₄-stationarity is the pair (Proposition VI.2): (i) $d\tau = 0$ along the null worldline, so no aging from emission to detection; (ii) $\omega_{C} = mc^{2}/\hbar = 0$ for $m = 0$, so no internal Compton oscillation. The Principle $dx_{4}/dt = ic$ applies at every event of the photon's worldline; the photon rides the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_{M}^{+}(p_{0}, t - t_{0})$ at constant Sphere-comoving angular direction $\hat{\mathbf n}$.

## N.4 The Budget Partition

Budget language attaches to the bounded pair $(v,\,c\,d\tau/dt)$ on the quarter-circle $v^{2} + (c\,d\tau/dt)^{2} = c^{2}$ (Corollary VII.1), which reads exception-free on every worldline. The signed Lorentzian norm $u^{\mu}u_{\mu} = -c^{2}$ is the equivalent invariant for massive worldlines. Two angle parameters give the same content: the Sphere angle $\theta$ with $\cos\theta = 1/\gamma$ (bounded), and the rapidity $\phi$ with $\cosh\phi = \gamma$ (unbounded), related by the gudermannian $\theta = \mathrm{gd}(\phi)$. Path-length and aging arguments run on the proper time $\tau[\gamma]$ (path-dependent); the coordinate $x_{4} = ict$ is exact and $\oint dx_{4} = 0$ around any closed curve.

## N.5 Gravitational Rate

The Principle rate is gravity-rigid: $\partial(dx_{4}/dt)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (GR-T2, §IX.15 and §IX.25). Mass and energy do not touch $dx_{4}/dt$. What varies with potential is the share (R2): $c\,d\tau/dt(r) = c\sqrt{1 - r_{s}/r}$ for the static Schwarzschild observer, vanishing at the horizon. On the infaller's own clock, $d\tau = dt$ locally and the rest-frame reading holds at the universal rate throughout — the infalling clock ticks at the universal rate on its own worldline to the end. The horizon is the locus where the *share* is extinguished, not where the *expansion* stops. The Schwarzschild metric is a curved Lorentzian shadow of the Principle, obtained by solving the Einstein field equations (themselves derived from the Principle via §IX.15 and §IX.25) with a static spherically-symmetric matter distribution; every observational prediction of GR — perihelion advance, Pound-Rebka, Eddington bending, Hafele-Keating, GW170817 — reads on the curved shadow as it always did.
